# 格林布拉特课程#1

<!--en-->
*Greenblatt Class #1*

2005年9月7日

<!--en-->
Sept. 07, 2005

# 一个关于卖口香糖的故事

<!--en-->
*A Story Selling Gum*

我的目标是教你**我从未上过却渴望能上的那门课**。我25年前开始读商学院。除了阅读财务报表外，我所知道的关于投资的知识，**都是靠自己阅读和实践摸索出来的**。希望我能把我的经验分享给你。

<!--en-->
My goal is to teach you **the course that I never had and that I wish I had.** I started in business school 25 years ago. What I know about investing other than reading financial statements, **I learned on my own reading and making mistakes.** Hopefully, I can give you the benefit of my experience.

几年前，我试图向儿子解释我的职业。他当时11岁。我提到了卖口香糖的事。我儿子班上的杰森每天在学校卖口香糖：他以25美分的价格购进一包口香糖，然后以每根25美分的价格出售。他每天卖4包，一周5天，一年约36周，年收入约为4,000美元。如果杰森现在提议把一半生意卖给你，你会出多少钱？

<!--en-->
A number of years ago I was trying to explain to my son what I did for a living. He is 11 years old. I spoke about selling gum. Jason, a boy in my son's class, sold gum each day at school. He would buy a pack of gum for 25 cents and he would sell sticks of gum for 25 cents each. He sells 4 packs a day, 5 days a week, 36 weeks or about $4,000 a year. What if Jason offered to sell you half the business today? What would you pay?

我儿子回答说：“嗯，他可能每天只卖3包，这样一年只能赚3,000美元。你会现在就付1,500美元吗？如果我得等几年才能拿到这1,500美元，我干嘛要这么做呢？”

<!--en-->
My son replied, "Well, he may only sell three packs a day so he would make $3000 a year. Would you pay $1,500 now? Why would I do that if I have to wait several years for the $1,500?"

你会付1美元吗？当然会！但不会是1,500美元。我愿意现在付450美元，以便在未来几年里收到1,500美元——这才是公平的。我告诉儿子：“现在你明白我是做什么的了。”

<!--en-->
Would you pay a $1? Yes, of course! But not $1,500. I would pay $450 now to collect $1,500 over the next few years, which would be fair. Now, you understand what I do for a living, I told my son.

**我整天都在琢磨一家企业的真实价值，然后设法用远低于其价值的价格买下它。**我想你明白我的意思了。

<!--en-->
**I sit around trying to figure out what businesses are worth, and then I try to pay a lot less for them.** I think you get the point.

# 我将教给你的技能

<!--en-->
*The Skills I Will Teach You*

我并不认为我要教给你们的技能有多么宝贵。并不是说你们无法通过这些技能赚大钱，而是你们有比这更有价值的事情可做。我认为，投资于股市的社会价值类似于擅长赛马预测——资本市场确实有其存在的意义，但其实并不需要你们参与。

<!--en-->
I really don't think the skills that I am going to teach you are very valuable. It is not that you can't make a lot of money from what I am going to teach you. There are fundamentally better things you can do with your time. My view is that the social value of investing in the stock market as being similar to being good at handicapping horses. There is a benefit to having markets for raising capital; they just really don't need you.

我认为本学期我要教给你们的内容其实是如何赚钱的方法，因此对社会产生的益处也微乎其微。如果你最终采纳我的建议并取得了成功，我希望你能想办法回馈社会。我只是中间的一环而已，我究竟做了什么呢？

<!--en-->
I think what I am going to teach you this semester is really how to make money and so whatever social benefits there are to society, it is not very large. So if you do end up following my advice and it works for you, I would ask that you find some way to give back. I am one iteration removed so what I am doing?

我真希望自己能有机会上这门课，从而以某种方式帮助他人。

<!--en-->
I truly wish that I had the chance to have this course to help out in some way.

# 价格与价值之间的偏差：

<!--en-->
*Divergence between Prices and Values:*

价格的波动幅度大于价值——这正是机会所在。

<!--en-->
Prices fluctuate more than values—so therein lies opportunity.

为什么每家公司的价格与其实际价值相比如此多变且不稳定？

<!--en-->
Why are prices of each company so variable and volatile compared to the value of companies?

如果我拿起报纸，随便挑一只大盘股如*IBM*、*Cisco*、*eBay*、*KKD*、*Google*，你会发现它们的价格差异很大。看看它们52周最高价与最低价之间的巨大差距吧。这家企业本身并没有太大变化，但股价却从35美元涨到70美元，又从7美元涨到30美元，如今又跌至20美元。再看看*ANF*和*INTL*。

<!--en-->
If I take out the newspaper and I pick out any large cap stock like *IBM*, *Cisco*, *EBay*, *KKD*, *Google*, why are the prices all over the place? Look at the wide divergence between the 52 week high/low. Here is a business that hasn't changed much but the price has gone from $35 to $70. $7 to $30 and right now to $20. Look at *ANF* and *INTL*.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情况投资课程相关问题：

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Questions:

这些都是相当不错的公司，而且这是多年来最稳定的时期，但在一两年内股价却出现了100%的波动——为何会有如此巨大的差异？市场真的有效吗？为什么MBA毕业生和其他聪明人往往在资金管理方面表现不佳？人们往往凭情绪投资，他们处理信息的方式也不同。

<!--en-->
These are all pretty good companies and this has been the least volatile period in many years, and there have been 100% moves over one to two year periods—why the huge disparity?
Are markets efficient?
Why do MBAs and other smart people not do well in money management?
People invest with their emotions. They process information differently.

这些公司的基本价值在短期内并未发生变动，而股价却如此剧烈波动，这合理吗？（价格偏离了价值。）

<!--en-->
Does it make sense that these prices fluctuate so much while the values of the underlying companies do not move around in a short period of time? (Price diverges from value).

**乔尔·格林布拉特（JG）：** 这一点非常明显——随便选哪家公司来看，其价格在短期内都极其波动。令我费解的是，公司的内在价值竟与价格一样波动剧烈，*而这恰恰就是绝佳的机会所在*。像迪士尼、波音、沃尔玛这类业务相对稳定的公司，其价值波动幅度远不及价格波动幅度。本应有巨大的机会，但市场上*真正的赢家却不多*。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt (JG):** It is very clear—pick any company you want—the price is very volatile over short periods of time. It does not make sense to me that the values are nearly as volatile as the prices and *therein lies what should be a great opportunity*. All these companies which have fairly established businesses (*Disney, Boeing, Wal-Mart*) the values are not fluctuating nearly as widely as the prices. There should be great opportunity, yet there are *not many winners* in the market.

之所以如此……归根结底……为什么在价值不可能大幅波动的情况下价格却会剧烈波动呢？我来告诉你我得出的答案：答案是**我不知道，也不在乎**。我们可以花大量时间研究心理学因素，但这种现象始终存在且持续发生。

<!--en-->
The reason why that is……in the final analysis……why do the price fluctuate so widely when values can’t possibly? I will tell you the answer I have come up with: The answer is **I don’t know and I don’t care.** We could waste a lot of time about psychology but it always happens and it continues to happen.

我不知道，也不在乎。**我只想利用这种机会。** 我们本可以坐下来把一切弄清楚，但**我喜欢简单行事**。这种现象会发生；它持续发生；机会就在那里。我不在乎原因是什么——我只想利用价格偏离价值所带来的机会。

<!--en-->
I don’t know and I don’t care. **I just want to take advantage of it.** We could sit there and figure it all out, but **I like to keep it simple.** It happens; it continues to happen; the opportunities are there. I don’t know why it happens and I don’t care—I just want to take advantage of prices away from value.

在本课程中，**我将教你如何利用这种机会。** 我现在就可以保证：如果你能做好*估值工作*并且判断正确，市场先生一定会回报你。短期内（一到两年），市场是低效的；但从长期来看，市场最终会做出正确反应——两到三年内它就会回报你。做分析时请记住这一点。如果你能做好估值工作——我们会解释具体含义以及最佳指标是什么——你无需关注下个季度或未来六个月的情况，市场先生自然会给你回报。**从长期看，市场先生最终会做出正确决策；**他其实非常理性。这一点非常强大。这就是本学期你应该秉持的思维框架。宏观来看：

<!--en-->
In this course, **I am going to teach you how to take advantage of that.** I will make a guarantee now: If you do *good valuation* work and you are right, Mr. Market will pay you back. In the short term, one to two years, the market is inefficient. But in the long-term, the market has to get it right—it will pay you back in two to three years. Keep that in mind when you do your analysis. You don’t have to look at the next quarter, the next six months, if you do good valuation work—and we will describe what that means—what the best metrics to use, Mr. Market will pay you. **In the long-term Mr. Market eventually gets it right;** he is very rational. That is very powerful. That is the context in which you should think this semester.
The big picture:

华尔街上有很多聪明人，但大多数人由于种种原因最终都失败了——他们无法创造价值。我创办了*哥谭资本*，20年来我们年均收益率达到40%。1,000美元如今已增值至836,683美元。有比我更擅长制作电子表格的人，也有比我更优秀的分析师。我认为我们之所以能取得成功，是因为**我们的思维简单且略有不同。** 我们进行分析时所依据的**背景**并非说我们的分析比他人更优越。我们并非任何行业的专家，也不比别人更聪明，分析水平也并非更佳。你能在此时此地学习，说明你具备分析能力。**真正决定差异的，是你运用分析时的背景。** 简化思路，将估值置于恰当背景中，然后付诸实践。

<!--en-->
There are lots of smart guys on Wall Street yet most of them go out and basically fail for many reasons—they are unable to contribute value. I have a firm, *Gotham Capital*; we have averaged 40% per year for 20 years. $1,000 would now be $836,683. There are lots of smarter people who can do better spread sheets than I can; there are lots of smarter analysts than me. I think the difference to how we have been able to do it is that **we think simply and a little bit differently.**
The **context in which we put our analysis**—not that our analysis is any better than anybody else’s. We are not experts in any particular industry, we are not smarter than anybody else, and we are not doing better analysis. The fact that you are here means you can do the analysis. **It is the context in which you put that analysis that makes the difference to you.**
Simplify, place valuation into context, practice.

这应该能给你带来鼓舞：你不必非得聪明绝顶，也不必花费无数小时进行复杂分析，但你必须做到出色。你必须清楚自己的知识边界——即你的能力圈。你不必成为世界上最擅长解决问题的人。我会教你这些简单的要点，然后我们会进行大量练习——在牢记简单背景的前提下练习估值。就连我自己也时常需要提醒自己什么才是重要的。你必须能够排除所有干扰。《华尔街日报》一天所载的信息量，就超过了700年前全世界的信息总量。

<!--en-->
That should be encouraging to you that you don’t have to be smart, or have to do a million hours of work or tricky analysis, but you have to be good. You have to know what you know—Your Circle of Competence. You don’t have to be the best in the world at figuring stuff out. It is the context which I will teach you thosesimple things and then we will do a lot of practicing--practice of doing valuation while keeping the simple context in mind. Even I have to remind myself to remember what is important. You must be able to cut through all the noise. The *Wall Street Journal* has more info in it in one day than the entire world had 700 years ago.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

# 如何跑赢市场

<!--en-->
*How to Beat the Market*

很多人无法跑赢市场，那么请列举一些实现这一目标的方法。

<!--en-->
Many people don't beat the market, so name some ways that you can do it.

专注于*小盘股*领域，因为那里的市场*效率更低*。分析师覆盖较少，信息流通也更少。你有机会发现价格明显高于或低于其内在价值的股票。**小盘股中更容易找到定价错误的股票。**

<!--en-->
Focus on *small caps* where the markets are *more inefficient*. There is less analyst coverage so less information flow. You have the chance to find prices more above or below value. **Small caps have more opportunity to find mis-priced stocks.**

**小盘股：** 另一个秘诀是，当基金经理掌握估值方法并专注于小盘股时，他们就能赚大钱，随后便会转向其他领域。对于初学者而言，总会有**进行独创性研究的机遇**。行业内总有人员更替。

<!--en-->
**Small Caps:** Another secret, when money managers learn their valuation work and focus on small caps, they make a lot of money, and they graduate from small caps. For a guy starting out there is always **an opportunity to do original work.** There is turnover in the ranks.

**激进型投资：** *JG*曾通过代理权争夺战获利，但过程痛苦不堪。这是他首次也是最后一次尝试激进型投资。

<!--en-->
**Activist Investing:** *JG* won a proxy fight and eventually made money but it was not worth the pain. His first and last foray into activist investing.

**特殊情况投资：** 与小盘股投资相辅相成。你要去别人不去的地方，那是市场效率更低的区域。带有催化剂的价值投资。

<!--en-->
**Special situations:** A corollary to small cap investing. You go where other people aren't. A more inefficient area of the market. Value investing with a catalyst.

**学生：** 在特定行业拥有深厚知识。*琳达·格林布拉特*专注于零售业。集中投资。

<!--en-->
**Student:** Superior knowledge in an industry. *Linda Greenblatt* focuses in retail.
Concentrate your investments.

# 哥谭资本是如何创造卓越回报的：

<!--en-->
*How Gotham generated great returns:*

*哥谭资本*始终保持小规模运作。我们退出外部资本市场，以便能尽可能多地投资于各种机会（不受规模限制）。我们的投资非常集中，通常只投资5到8只证券。**务必深入了解所投资的公司。**为何这样做比分散投资更安全？**关键在于精准把握时机。**如果你的持有期为三到五年，且只需持有4到6只证券，那么每年只需一两个好主意即可。这正是我有时间讲授这门课程的原因——这种方式既有趣又有效。

<!--en-->
*Gotham Capital* stayed small. We returned outside capital, so we could invest in as many situations as possible (not constrained by size). We are very concentrated. We invest in 5 to 8 securities. **Know your companies very well.** Why that is more safe than diversifying? **You pick your spots.** So if your holding period is three to five years and you only have 4 to 6 securities, then you only need one or two ideas a year. That is why I have time to teach this class. It is more fun and it works.

# 为何价值投资有效

<!--en-->
*Why Value Investing Works*

理查德·普泽纳：

<!--en-->
Richard Pzena:

Value Investing works because it doesn't work <u>all</u> the time</td></tr></tfoot></table>

价值投资确实有效，但它往往呈周期性运作。*普泽纳*失去了70%的投资者；如今在他管理的140亿美元资产中，仅剩下4位最初的投资人（乔尔·G就是其中之一）。

<!--en-->
Value investing works, but it tends to work in cycles. *Pzena* lost 70% of his investors. Now of the $14 billion he manages he only has 4 (Joel G. is one of them) of his original investors.

**乔尔·G：**1998年至1999年间我的投资亏损了5%，当时我担心1999年会出现泡沫破裂（一种宏观层面的担忧），但我仍能找到价格低廉的公司——看看1999年伯克希尔·哈撒韦的股价有多便宜吧。他们坚持原有的投资策略，结果在2000年我的投资回报达到了130%。市场随后也回暖了。

<!--en-->
**Joel G:** I was down 5% in 1998-1999 but worried about a bubble breaking in 1999 (a macro worry), but I could find cheap companies—look how cheap Brk.a got in 1999. They kept doing what they were doing. He was up 130% in 2000. The markets came back.

推荐阅读：詹姆斯·P·奥肖内西所著的《华尔街上的成功法则》。他于1996年至1997年间发起了一只基金，但业绩比市场平均水平低25%；在连续三年表现不佳后，他于周期底部出售了自己的公司。**写这本书的人竟然抛弃了自己提出的体系！**看似容易，实则并非如此。

<!--en-->
Read: *What Works on Wall Street* by *James P O'Shaughnessy*. He started a fund in 1996-1997 but he underperformed the market by 25% and after three years in business of underperforming he sold his company at the bottom of the cycle. **The guy who wrote the book quit his system!** It seems like it is easy to do, but it is not easy to do.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情境投资课程。《华尔街上的成功法则》一书中的智慧在此得到了印证。基于他的策略而获得专利的两只基金表现惊人：HFCGX是基于他最看好的“基石增长”理念设立的专利基金；过去五年间，其年均回报率为13.44%，而先锋500指数仅为-2.01%（2000年6月1日至2005年5月31日）。HFCVX是基于他第二看好的“基石价值”理念设立的专利基金；过去五年间，其年均回报率为6.47%，同样远超先锋500指数的-2.01%。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
This book, *What Works on Wall Street*, has born out its wisdom. The two funds that are patented that fool his strategy have been phenomenal. HFCGX is the patented fund based on his top idea of Cornerstone Growth; over the last 5 years it has had an average return of 13.44% per year vs. the Vanguard 500's -2.01% per year (6/1/00 through 5/31/05). HFCVX is the patented fund based on his 2nd to best idea of Cornerstone Value; over the last 5 years it has had an average return of 6.47% per year vs. the Vanguard 500's -2.01% per year (6/1/00 through 5/31/05).

最有趣的一点是，作者指出这些投资者往往因情感因素而无法坚持执行策略。**不仅第一位书评人在该书出版一年后因其回报策略不理想而抨击此书，而且奥肖内西先生在1999年底将基金卖给了轩尼诗基金——当时该基金未能超越不久后便破裂的股市泡沫所带来的回报。**如果该投资者在书出版七年后遵循书中的最佳策略，而非跟风追捧泡沫股，他们的财富将会更加丰厚。

<!--en-->
The most interesting point is that the author points out those investors often are to emotionally involved to have the discipline to see the strategy through. **Not only did the first reviewer bash the book because he did like the returns strategy one year after the book came out, but Mr. O'Shaughnessy sold the funds to Hennessy Funds at the end of 1999 after it failed to surpass the returns of the bubble that soon after collapsed.** Seven years after it was published an investor would be much wealthier had they followed the book's top strategy instead of the investors who dog-piled onto the stocks of the market's bubble.

# 估值：

<!--en-->
*Valuation:*

有哪些不同的估值方法？

<!--en-->
What are the different Valuation Methodologies?

**DCF：现金流折现法**（存在的问题）：你需要做出预测。由于假设的微小变化，终值可能会大幅变动。该价格隐含了怎样的盈利水平？为了得出三年后的估值，我采用了何种增长率和折现率？什么才能支撑起那个未来的价格？我通常会反向推导，代入一系列数字如增长率。我所预期的价格究竟意味着什么？我将其作为现实检验工具，来判断我的假设是否合理。这样做往往能迫使我使用更为保守的数字。

<!--en-->
**DCF: Discounted Cash Flow** (problems) you have to make projections. The terminal value can change drastically due to small changes in assumptions. What earnings does the price imply? What growth rate and what discount rate am I using to get to that valuation three years from now? What would justify that future price? I sort of work backwards and throw in a bunch of numbers like growth rate. What is this price I am expecting it to be worth imply? I use it as a reality check to decide and see if my assumptions can be justified. What it tends to do is force me to use conservative numbers.

你怎么知道自己是否采用了保守的数值？

<!--en-->
How do you know if you are conservative?

如果你无法确定增长率或折现率等指标，那就放弃吧。如果连我都难以判断，**我就会转向下一个选项。**

<!--en-->
What if you can't figure this out—like growth rate or discount rate? Pass on it. If it is hard for me to figure it out, **I go onto the next one.**

**相对价值法**：观察类似企业及其交易价格。问题在于这些企业其实并不真正相似；找到合适的可比公司可能很困难。某个行业内的所有资产或许都被高估了，因此你实际上是在比较两件被高估的资产；可比公司本身也可能存在估值过高或过低的情况。

<!--en-->
**Relative value:** look at similar businesses and what they are trading at. Problems: the businesses are not really similar. It might be tough to find a good comparable. Everything might be overvalued in a sector, so you are comparing one overvalued asset with another. Comparables might be over or under valued.

**复制价值法**——我通常不采用这种方法。共产党人制造方形的轮子，是因为其制造成本与圆形轮子相同。

<!--en-->
**Replicating value**—I don't usually do that. The communists made square wheels because they cost the same to make as round wheels.

**拆分价值法**：一家公司有两个业务部门，一个盈利3美元，另一个亏损1美元（每股收益=3-1=2美元）。该股交易价格为34美元，因此市盈率=34/2=17倍；但如果你关闭那个亏损的业务部门，其实际市盈率就变为11倍，即34/3。

<!--en-->
**Break-up value:** A company has two divisions one is making $3 and the other is losing $1 (EPS = $3 - $1 = $2). The stock trades at $34 so PE = $34/$2 = 17x but if you close down the bad business, it really trades at 11 times or $34/$3.

股票过去的价格走势只是噪音而已。它到底值多少钱？关键在于它当前的价格。

<!--en-->
Where the stock has traded in the past is noise. What is it worth? Where is it today (Price).

**收购价值**：假设你拥有一家拥有10万客户的经纪账户公司，它收购了*Brown Co.*的5万名客户，仅凭新增的客户就能让该公司支付更高的收购价。

<!--en-->
**Acquisition value:** You have a discount brokerage account with 100,000 accounts that acquires *Brown Co's* 50,000 customers, so they can pay more that company due to just adding customers to their infrastructure.

收购价值可能远高于DCF估值。

<!--en-->
The acquisition value might be much higher than the DCF value.

我不喜欢看到按订阅用户数或医院床位计算的估值。我仍希望看到从医院床位中转化出的现金流数据。我也不喜欢相对价值法。

<!--en-->
I don't like to see values per subscriber or x hospital beds. I still want to see the cash flows translated from the hospital beds. I don't like to see relative value.

## 摘要：公司估值

<!--en-->
*Summary: Valuing a Company*

我们有四种方法来对一家公司进行估值：

<!--en-->
We have four ways to value a company:

1. 现金流折现法或内在价值法，
2. 相对价值法，
3. 清算价值法，以及
4. 收购价值法。

<!--en-->
1. DCF or intrinsic value,
2. Relative value,
3. Break-up value, and
4. Acquisition value

### 资产负债表、利润表和现金流量表

<!--en-->
*Balance Sheets, Income Statements and Cash Flow Statements*

一家公司的股票交易价格为每股6美元，其每股现金储备为5美元。

<!--en-->
A company trades at $6 per share and it has $5 per share in cash.

流动资产：首先我们看现金。我们常常发现，公司的交易价格与其每股现金价值相近。以2002年的科技股为例：每股有5美元现金。你可以对这家公司手中的5美元进行估值，但这笔钱并不在你口袋里。公司会如何处置这笔现金？他们又会如何重新分配这些资金呢？

<!--en-->
Current Assets: (CA) First we look at CASH. We have often found companies are trading at close to its cash per share. Technology stocks in 2002. $5 per share in cash andYou can value the $5 in the company's pocket but it is not in your pocket. What will the company do with that cash? How will they redeploy the cash?

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程指出：公司是会挥霍掉这些现金，还是会明智地将其返还给股东？要观察管理层，判断他们是否属于“资本毁灭者”。他们的收入来源是什么？他们是持有大量公司股票，还是主要靠薪水为生？

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Will they dissipate the cash or use it wisely like returning it to shareholders? Look at management and decide if they are capital destroyers. How is their bread buttered, do they own a lot of stock or are they paid mostly in salaries.

要看这家企业的业务状况——它是否在盈利？是否在其他业务中赚取了收益？管理层是否将资金用在有益之处？如果管理层行事得当，我可能会给予这笔现金全额估值；但如果企业正在亏损，我就不会按账面价值来认定它。务必确保那是净现金。

<!--en-->
Look at where the business is—is it earning money, is it earning $ in other businesses? Is management doing good things with the money? If management is doing good things, I may put full value on that cash. Or I won't take it at face value if the business is losing money. Make sure it is net cash.

他们可能需要更多的营运资金，因此我可能会对现金数额打个折扣。我通常会对资产负债表上的现金给予一定折价。总体而言，资本主义机制是有效的。经营企业的这些人往往更具创业精神。他们是将这笔钱当作自己的钱来用，还是当作别人的钱来用呢？其中总有细微差别。如果我不确定，就会给现金设定一个非常保守的估值以应对这种不确定性。你可能会说：“这5美元其实只值3美元。”那么剩下的部分还值得我购买这家公司吗？

<!--en-->
They may need more working capital so I may have to haircut the cash figure. I usually give a discount to the cash on the balance sheet. Generally capitalism works. Are these guys' losers. People running a business are generally more entrepreneurial. Are these guys treating it like their own money or somebody else's money? There always nuances. If I am not sure, I will put a very conservative value on the cash to take care of that uncertainty. You may say you know what; this $5 should only be worth $3. Do I still want to buy the company with what is left?

那5美元实际上只值3.00美元。即便是像资产负债表上的现金这样简单的项目，也有多种评估方式。很多人只是直接接受现金的账面价值，但我会对它进行分析。我会将那5美元估值为4美元或3美元。通常这并不会阻止我投资；我只是会对现金部分给予较大折扣。或许当公司进行大规模收购时，才是卖出的时机。

<!--en-->
That $5 really is worth $3.00. Something as simple as cash on the balance sheet, there are many iterations of how do I look at cash? A lot of people just look and accept the cash value, but I analyze it. I will value that $5 at $4 or $3. Usually this won't keep me from investing; I will just put a big discount on it (the cash). Probably when the company makes a big acquisition that is the time to sell.

# 应收账款：

<!--en-->
*Accounts Receivables:*

需要考虑哪些因素呢？应收账款的数额是否合理？如果应收账款增长迅速，说明公司在增加销售并放宽信贷条件——这可能是好事，也可能是坏事。

<!--en-->
What are the considerations there? Does the receivable number make sense? If A/R is rising quickly, then they are pumping out sales and extending credit—that may be good, it may be bad.

# 存货：

<!--en-->
*Inventories:*

对此也有相应的分析方法。流动资产、预付费用。营运资本包括应付账款以及长期债务的短期部分。固定资产则包括不动产——这些资产的增值程度如何？

<!--en-->
There are ways to look at that.
Current Assets, prepaid assets.
WC: Accounts Payable, short term portion of long-term debt.
Assets: PP&E, Real Estate (how much have those assets appreciated).

无形资产：商誉——即购买资产时所支付的超过其账面价值的部分。

<!--en-->
Intangibles: goodwill—the excess paid for assets above the book value of those assets.

一个小秘密：营业利润。我通常使用40%的税率。我喜欢用的是营业利润——这一税前数字便于比较。

<!--en-->
A little secret: Operating profit. Usually I use a 40% tax rate. The number I like to use is operating profit—a pre-tax number so comparisons are easier.

折旧与摊销并非现金支出。除非注销商誉，否则不会对其计提摊销。

<!--en-->
D&A are not cash expenses. Now you don't amortize goodwill unless you write it off.

EBITDA——切勿在报告中展示这一指标。必须扣除维护性资本支出（MCX）。如果公司正在扩张，你想计算“正常化盈利”，那么资本支出才是应使用的数字。资本性支出属于现金费用，而折旧只是账面记录，并非现金流出。

<!--en-->
EBITDA—don't show this in your reports. You have to subtract out the maintenance capital expenditures (MCX). Now, if the company is growing and you want to figure out “normalized earnings.” Capital spending is the number to use. Capex is a cash expense but depreciation is a book entry not cash.

假设你现有10家门店，现在又要新开10家门店，那么资本性支出既包括维护现有10家门店的费用，也包括开设这10家新店的成本；但当年你无法从这些新店中获得收益。对于正常化盈利而言，真正重要的是维护性资本支出。这一数字如何报告？请询问管理层。需区分增长性资本支出与维护性资本支出。

<!--en-->
Let us say you are opening 10 new stores in addition the 10 stores you already have, the capex would include keeping up the ten stores you already have making capex on those stores and the cost of opening the ten (10) new stores but you won't get the benefit of those new stores in that year. For normalized earnings what you really want for normalized earnings is maintenance capex. How is this number reported? Ask the management. Break out growth vs. maint. Capex.

我会要求对方解释MCX是如何得出的。通常公司会低估MCX。当EBITDA、折旧等于资本性支出时，EBIT = EBITDA – 资本性支出。使用EBIT时这是一种简便算法。我试图获取EBITDA减去维护性资本支出的数值。

<!--en-->
I ask for an explanation for mcx and how do they get there. Usually the company understates mcx. When EBITDA, DA = capex, then EBIT = EBITDA – Capex. A quick and dirty when you use EBIT. I try to get at EBITDA – maint. Capex.

讨论维护性资本支出与增长性资本支出的区别。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：有线电视行业处于**持续**升级周期。可参考EV/销售额、EBIT/EV指标。EV/EBIT代表税前盈利收益率。为何要使用企业价值（EV）？

<!--en-->
Discussion of maint. capex vs. growth capex.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The Cable Industry is in a **continual** upgrade cycle.
Look at EV/Sales, EBIT/EV. EV/EBIT is pre-tax earnings yield.
Why you use Enterprise Value (EV)?

# 公司A

<!--en-->
*COMPANY A*

EBIT为10美元，税率为40%，净利润为6美元，市盈率为10，市值为6000万美元，即EV=60。

<!--en-->
$10 EBIT
40% tax rate
$6 in Net Income
P/E 10
$60 million Market Cap. or EV = $60

## 公司B

<!--en-->
*COMPANY B*

EBIT为10美元，利息费用为-5美元，税前营业利润为5百万美元，利息支出为3百万美元。市值为1500万美元加上5000万美元债务，因此EV为6500万美元。公司A的市盈率仅为10，而公司B的市盈率为5。公司A的EV为6000万美元，低于公司B的6500万美元。

<!--en-->
$10 EBIT
-$5 Interest Expense
=$5 million in pre-tax operating
$3 mil. in int. expenses.
$15 mil in market cap + $50 mil in debt = $65 in EV
A is cheaper with a PE of 10 while Company B has a P/E of 5. The price of the EV is lower for A at $60 vs. $65 for B.

我关注的是**EV与销售额之比**，而非市销率。这样做的目的是：当你向我展示可比公司数据并声称平均市盈率为某数值——每份分析师报告都会列出行业比率，比如行业平均市盈率为13倍，而该公司为12倍，因此认为它较便宜——但这种做法并未考虑市值、税率差异等因素。而通过EV/EBIT指标来分析则能弥补这些不足。

<!--en-->
I look at **EV to sales** not P/S. The point of this exercise is that when you show me your comparables and you say the average P/E--every analyst report shows the industry ratios where they say the industry is trading at 13x and this company is trading at 12x so it is cheap--it doesn't take into account market capitalizations, differences in tax rates and things of that nature. And looking at things through an EV/EBIT basis does.

为了进行公平比较，我们将使用EBIT/EV指标。

<!--en-->
To make apples to apples comparison we will use EBIT/EV.

# ROIC与ROE的重要性

<!--en-->
*The Importance of ROIC vs. ROE*

我在乎ROE吗？我在乎的是资本回报率（ROIC）。

<!--en-->
Do I care about the ROE? I care about the return on capital (ROIC).

我首先查看ROIC = EBIT /（净营运资本 + 设备净值）。这家企业的质量如何？

<!--en-->
The first thing I look at ROIC = EBIT/ (NWC + Net Equipment). How good a business is this?

税前回报/有形净资产。企业运营所需的资本——即净营运资本 + 设备。净营运资本（NWC）：采用应收账款数据并剔除多余现金，再减去应付账款及有息债务。

<!--en-->
Pre-tax return/Net Tangible Capital. What capital the company needs to use to be in business--NWC + Equipt. Net Working Capital (NWC): Use financial A/R and eliminate the excess cash. Subtract Accounts Payable NIB debt.

为何要剔除**商誉**？因为它反映的是**历史**成本。我当初支付了多少并不重要。你真正想了解的是该企业未来的经营性质。

<!--en-->
Why eliminate **goodwill**? Because it states **historical** costs. It doesn't matter what I paid. You want to know going forward what type of business you are looking at.

EBIT/EV代表盈利收益率。我支付的价格相对于盈利而言是否合理？需避免价值陷阱（低回报企业）。

<!--en-->
EBIT/EV Earnings yield. What price am I paying relative to earnings?
Avoid value traps (low return businesses).

# 酒店业资本支出：

<!--en-->
*Hotel Capex:*

开设一家酒店需花费1000美元，每年维护性资本支出为25美元；但到第5年，为使酒店保持竞争力，需花费400美元进行翻新。因此，我会在每年25美元的基础上再加上（400美元/5年=80美元），即每年实际维护性资本支出为105美元。

<!--en-->
Spend $1,000 for a hotel. Then spend $25 per year for MCX, but then in year 5, I need to refurbish the hotel for $400 to stay competitive. So I would add ($400/5 or $80 per year to the $25 per year and deduct $105 per year in **true** maint. capex).

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

# 《战胜市场的小书》中乔尔所讲授内容的总结

<!--en-->
*Summary of What Joel teaches in the Little Book That Beats the Market*

你将学到：

<!--en-->
You will learn:

* 如何看待股票市场。
* 为什么几乎所有的个人和职业投资者都无法取得成功。
* 如何以低廉的价格找到优质公司。
* 你如何能独自战胜市场。

<!--en-->
* How to view the stock market.
* Why success eludes almost all individual and professional investors.
* How to find good companies at bargain prices.
* How you can beat the market all by yourself.

# 关键在于理解本书中的简单概念。

<!--en-->
*The key is to understand the simple concepts in this book*

大多数学者和专业人士无法帮助你战胜市场。你必须*亲自行动*。

<!--en-->
Most academics and professionals can't help you to beat the market. YOU must *do it yourself*.

你必须相信这个观点是正确的。大多数职业投资者都学到了错误的知识，很少有人相信这一点；否则成功的投资者会更多。但事实并非如此。

<!--en-->
You have to believe that the story is true. Most professional investors have learned wrong and very few people believe or else there would be many more successful investors. They aren't.

# 比较我们的投资选项。

<!--en-->
*Compare Our investment alternatives*

我们想比较一下，从美国国债这种“稳赚不赔”的投资中能赚取多少收益，与我们其他长期投资选择相比如何。我们希望确保从其他投资中获得的收益远高于无风险情况下的收益。

<!--en-->
We want to compare how much we can earn from a safe bet like a U.S. government bond with our other long-term investment choices. We want to make sure we earn a lot more from our other investments than we could earn without taking any risk.

## 购买一家企业的股份。

<!--en-->
*Buying a share in a business*

购买一家企业的股份意味着你购买了该企业的一部分（或一定比例的权益）。随后你便有权分享该企业未来的盈利。

<!--en-->
Buying a share in a business means you are purchasing a portion (or percentage interest) of that business. You are then entitled to a portion of that business's future earnings.

* 我们必须估算该企业未来的盈利情况。
* 我们对自己的预测有多大的信心？
* 明年仅仅是一年的时间。那之后的多年呢？盈利会每年持续增长吗？
* 你从企业分红中获得的收益，必须比你把同样数额的资金投入无风险的10年期美国国债所获得的收益还要多。

<!--en-->
* We have to estimate what the business will earn in the future.
* How confident are we in our prediction?
* Next year is only one year. What about all the years after that? Will earnings keep growing every year?
* The earnings from your share of the profits must give you more money than you would receive by placing that same amount of money in a risk free 10-year U.S. government bond.

## 如何确定一家企业的真实价值？

<!--en-->
*Figuring What A Business Is Really Worth?*

如果企业的内在价值不可能发生如此大的变化，为什么这些企业的股价每年都会剧烈波动呢？

<!--en-->
Why do the prices of all these businesses move around so much each year if the values of their businesses can't possibly change that much?

为什么人们愿意在极短的时间内以截然不同的价格买卖大多数公司的股票？我只需要知道他们确实会这么做！

<!--en-->
Why are people willing to buy and sell shares of most companies at wildly different prices over very short periods of time? I just have to know that they do!

谁知道呢？谁又在乎呢？也许人们只是容易冲动罢了。

<!--en-->
Who knows and who cares? Maybe people just go nuts a lot.

*本·格雷厄姆*发现：在像“市场先生”这样的疯狂交易对手那里购买股票时，始终遵循*安全边际*原则，才是获得安全且可靠投资利润的秘诀。

<!--en-->
*Ben Graham* figured out that always using the *margin of safety* principle when deciding to purchase shares of a business from a crazy partner like Mr. Market was the secret to making safe and reliable investment profits.

# 估值

<!--en-->
*Valuation*

你怎么可能知道一家企业的价值呢？如果你无法为一家公司确定合理的估值，就无法用该数值除以发行在外的股票总数，也就无法算出每股股票的公平价值。

<!--en-->
How are you supposed to know what a business is worth? If you can't place a fair value on a company, then you can't divide that number by the number of shares that exist, and you can't figure out what the fair value of a share of stock is.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：在确定企业价值的过程中，你所做的不过是做出一堆猜测和估算。这些估算涉及对未来多年企业盈利的预测。就连专家（不管那意味着什么）也很难做到这一点。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
In the process of figuring out the value of a business, all you do is make a bunch of guesses and estimates. Those estimates involve predicting earnings for a business for many years into the future. Even experts (whatever that means) have a tough time doing that.

# 学习相关概念

<!--en-->
*Learning the Concepts*

你必须暂时放下自己的成见与怀疑。

<!--en-->
You must make a willing suspension of disbelief.

预测未来是很困难的。如果我们无法预测企业未来的盈利情况，就很难为其定价。

<!--en-->
It is hard to predict the future. If we can't predict the future earnings of a business, then it is hard to place a value on that business.

如果你只购买优质公司——那些资本回报率高的公司——并且只在低价时买入——即那些能给你带来高盈利收益率的价格——最终你会系统性地买到许多被疯狂的“市场先生”视为“白送”的优质公司。

<!--en-->
If you just stick to buying good companies—ones that have a high return on capital—and to buying those companies only at bargain prices—at prices that give you a high earnings yield—you end up systematically buying many of the good companies that crazy Mr. Market has decided to literally give away.

以低价买入优质企业是赚钱的秘诀。格雷厄姆公式：

<!--en-->
Buying good businesses at bargain prices is the secret to making money.
Graham's Formula:

他的公式要求购买股价极低、以至于买入价甚至低于关闭企业并清售其资产所能获得的收入的企业。他给这类股票起了各种名称：廉价股、流动资产净值股票，或售价低于清算价值的股票。

<!--en-->
His formula involved purchasing companies whose stock prices were so low that the purchase price was actually lower than the proceeds that would be received from simply shutting down the business and selling off the company's assets in a fire sale. He called these stocks by various names: bargain issues, net-current-asset stocks, or stocks selling below liquidation value).

格雷厄姆说：“听起来似乎荒谬地简单：只要能买入二三十家价格足够低、符合他公式严格要求的公司，无需进一步分析，结果就会相当令人满意。”事实上，格雷厄姆运用这一公式取得了巨大成功，持续了30多年。

<!--en-->
Graham stated that it seems “ridiculously simple to say that if one could buy a group of 20 or 30 companies that were cheap enough to meet the strict requirements of his formula, without doing any further analysis, the “results should be quite satisfactory.” In fact Graham used this formula with much success for over 30 years.

格雷厄姆证明，一种寻找明显廉价股票的简单系统能够带来安全且稳定的良好投资回报。格雷厄姆认为，通过购买一组这类廉价股，投资者可以安心获得高回报，无需担心少数劣质股票的影响，也无需对单只股票进行复杂分析。魔力公式的结果：在17年间，持有一组约30只兼具高资本回报率和高盈利收益率的股票组合，年化收益率可达30.8%。11,000美元在扣除税费和交易成本前就能变成100万美元。要让魔力公式发挥作用：

<!--en-->
Graham showed that a simple system for finding obviously cheap stocks could lead to safe and consistently good investment returns. Graham suggested that by buying a group of these bargain stocks, investors could safely earn a high return without worrying about a few bad purchases and without doing complicated analysis of individual stocks.
Magic Formula Results
Over the seventeen years, owning a portfolio of approximately 30 stocks that had the best combination of a high return on capital and a high earnings yield could have returned 30.8 percent per year. $11,000 would have turned into $1 million before taxes and transaction costs.
To make the Magic Formula Work:

正是你对魔力公式强大逻辑性的信念，才能使其在长期内为你效力。公式运作原理：

<!--en-->
It will be your belief in the overwhelming logic of the magic formula that will make the formula work for you in the long run.
How the Formula Works:

该公式从3,500家公司的数据库中筛选出这两个因素的最佳组合。在这种排名体系下，能在两个类别中都获得优秀排名（尽管并非排名第一）要比在一个类别中排名第一但在另一个类别中仅获较好排名更好。不存在规模效应：针对规模最大的1,000家公司，魔力公式17年间的年化收益率为22.9%，而标普500指数仅为12.4%。该公式对大公司和小公司都适用。

<!--en-->
The formula looks for the best combination of those two factors out of a 3,500 company database. Getting excellent rankings in both categories (though not top ranked in either) would be better under this ranking system than being the top-ranked in one category with only a pretty good ranking in the other.
No Size Effect
The Magic Formula Results for the top largest 1,000 companies: 22.9% vs. 12.4% for the S&P 500 over 17 years. The formula works for companies large and small.

魔力公式似乎按十分位数顺序起作用。可供选择的排名靠前的股票总是很多。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：魔力公式与市场相比表现如何？

<!--en-->
The Magic Formula seems to work in order of Deciles. There should always be plenty of highly ranked stocks to choose from
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
How does the Magic Formula fare vs. the market?

在测试的12个月中，有5个月该公式表现不佳。从年度来看，每四年中就有一次该公式无法跑赢市场。

<!--en-->
The formula fared poorly 5 out of every 12 months tested. Annually the formula failed to beat the market once every four years.

如果魔力公式总能奏效，所有人都会使用它。一旦人人都用，它很可能就不再有效。该公式并非永远奏效。

<!--en-->
If the magic formula worked all the time, everyone would use it. If everyone used it, it would probably stop working. The formula doesn't work all the time.

要让魔力公式为你所用，你必须相信它会奏效，并保持长期的投资视野。永恒的原则：为了使魔力公式在长期内为我们赚钱，其背后的原则不仅必须合理且合乎逻辑，还必须具有永恒性。否则，当短期结果不如预期时，我们就无法坚持下去。

<!--en-->
For the magic formula to work for you, you must believe that it will work and maintain a long-term investment horizon.
Timeless Principles
In order for the magic formula to make us money in the long run, the principles behind it must appear not only sensible and logical, but timeless. Otherwise, there is no way we will be able to “hang on” when our short-term results turn against us.

我们购买的是平均而言质量高于平均水平、且能以低于平均水平的价格买到的公司。

<!--en-->
We are buying on average above-average companies that we can on average buy at below-average prices.

能够以高回报率再投资利润的机会非常宝贵，因为它能推动极高的盈利增长率！

<!--en-->
The opportunity to invest profits at high rates of return is very valuable because it can contribute to a very high rate of earnings growth!

即便仅一年时间，能实现高资本回报率往往意味着该公司业务具有某种特殊性。否则，竞争早已会将资本回报率压低到更低水平。

<!--en-->
To earn a high return on capital even for one year, it's likely that, at least temporarily, there's something special about that company's business. Otherwise, competition would already have driven down returns on capital to lower levels.

简而言之，能够实现高资本回报的公司往往拥有某种特殊优势。这种特殊优势能防止竞争对手破坏其赚取超额利润的能力。

<!--en-->
In short, companies that achieve a high return on capital are likely to have a special advantage of some kind. That special advantage keeps competitors from destroying the ability to earn above-average profits.

因此，通过剔除那些资本回报率普通或较差的公司后，这套神奇公式便从一组资本回报率高的公司开始筛选。

<!--en-->
So by eliminating companies that earn ordinary or poor ROC, the magic formula starts with a group of companies that have a high ROC.

接着，该基金只会购买那些相对于其收购成本而言能产生丰厚收益的公司。为什么该基金能奏效？只有当你理解了业绩优异背后的原因，良好的过往记录才能发挥作用。

<!--en-->
Then the mf will buy only those companies that earn a lot compared to what we are paying.
Why the mf works?
A good track record only helps once you understand *why* the track record is so good.

该基金在95%的时间里跑赢了市场平均水平（在测试的169个三年期间中占160次）！最差情况下的收益率也达到了11%，而市场平均收益率则为-46%。

<!--en-->
The mf beat the market averages 95% of the time (160 out of 169 three-year periods tested)! The worst return was a gain of 11% vs. a loss of 46% for the market averages.

关于投资策略，有两件事是你必须了解的：

<!--en-->
There are two things you want to know about an investment strategy:

长期遵循该策略导致亏损的风险有多大？

<!--en-->
What is the risk of losing money following that strategy over the long term?

长期来看，你选择的投资策略表现不如其他策略的风险有多大？

<!--en-->
What is the risk that your chosen strategy will perform worse than alternative strategies over the long term?

如果一种投资策略确实合理，那么你的投资期限越长，成功的机会就越大。5年、10年或20年的投资期限最为理想。

<!--en-->
If an investment strategy truly makes sense, the longer your time horizon you maintain, the better your chances for success. Time horizons of 5, 110 or 20 years are ideal.

从长远来看，市场先生总会做出正确的判断。

<!--en-->
Over the long run, Mr. Market gets it right.

我敢保证：如果你对公司的估值工作做得出色，市场先生最终会认同你的判断。通常只需等待两到三年，市场就会为这些低价买入的股票给出公平的价格。随着时间的推移，事实与现实会占据主导。聪明的投资者寻找便宜货，公司回购自身股票，以及整个公司的被收购或潜在被收购可能性——这些因素共同作用，推动股价趋向公允价值。

<!--en-->
I guarantee that if you do a good job valuing a company, Mr. Market will eventually agree with them. Two or three years is usually all the time they'll have to wait for Mr. Market. To reward their bargain purchases with a fair price. Over time, facts and reality take over. Smart investors search for bargains, companies buy back their own shares, and the takeover or possibility of a takeover of an entire company—work together to move share prices toward fair value.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

## 自行挑选公司

<!--en-->
*Choosing Companies on Your Own*

在毫无明确目标的情况下挑选个股，就如同手持燃烧的火柴冲进炸药厂。你或许能活下来，但依然是个蠢货。

<!--en-->
Choosing individual stocks without any idea of what you're looking for is like running through a dynamite factory with a burning match. You may live, but you are still an idiot.

该基金关注的是去年的盈利情况。但公司的价值取决于它未来能为我们创造多少财富，而非过去的表现。

<!--en-->
The mf looks at last year's earnings. But the value of a company comes from how much money it will earn for us in the future, not from what happened in the past.

理想情况下，我们应该输入公司在“正常年份”的盈利估算值。

<!--en-->
Ideally, we should be plugging in estimates for earnings in a *normal* year.

> “如果去掉我们最重要的十五项决策，我们的业绩就相当普通了。这并非因为过度活跃，而是源于极大的耐心。你坚持自己的原则，一旦机会出现，便全力把握。”

<!--en-->
> "If you took our top fifteen decisions out, we'd have a pretty average record. It wasn't hyperactivity, but a hell of a lot of patience. You stuck to your principles and when opportunities came along, you pounced on them with vigor."

- 查理·芒格，伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司副董事长——

<!--en-->
- Charlie Munger, Vice Chairman, Berkshire Hathaway

## 作业：

<!--en-->
*Assignment:*

上周我给了你们那个“神奇公式”。下周*理查德·普泽纳*将讲解(*Lear Corporation*)并阅读*Haugen*的书——重点在于理解其中的概念。请提前准备好关于*Lear Corp*的资料。

<!--en-->
I left you with the magic formula last week. Next Week *Richard Pzena* will talk about (*Lear Corporation*) and read *Haugen* book—focus on the concepts. Prepare *Lear Corp*.

这是上周课程的更新版图表。价值投资的周期：2005年8月至2000年2月对价值投资者而言是一段极其艰难的时期；你们应该还记得当时的*互联网*热潮。即便你持有一家前景极佳的优秀公司，市场也不为它买单。标普500指数累计上涨163%，而价值投资者仅上涨91%——表现落后72%。如果你管理的基金跑赢了价值指数，但在BV中排名最低的20%，那么五年内的表现仍会落后70%到60%。一旦发生这种情况，投资者就会离开。就连管理着500亿美元资产的*理查德·普泽纳*，在2000年3月也面临大部分投资者撤资的局面。不过此后他的业绩表现极为出色。

<!--en-->
An updated chart from last week's class. Cycles of Value Investing Aug. 2005
Aug. 95 to Feb. 2000: a very tough time for value investors; you remember the *Internet* phase. Even if you had a great company with excellent prospects, the market didn't pay for it. S&P 500 up 163% cumulatively vs. up 91% for Value Investors—72% underperformance. If you are running a fund and you beat the value index, the lowest 20% in BV, you would have underperformed by 70% to 60% over five years. If that happens, people leave. Even *Richard Pzena*, whose firm runs $50 billion dollars, in March 2000, most of his investors had left. His performance since that time has been so phenomenal.

从2000年3月至今，价值股的表现比标普500指数高出175%，而*普泽纳*的业绩更是远超这一水平。人们还是像往常一样在错误的时间离开了。如果你坚持自己的原则而客户却不支持你，你能理解基金经理所承受的压力吗？你看着一张为期四年的图表，决定熬过这个价值投资周期，但这段时间实在太长，许多人无法坚持到底。一些价值型基金经理通过向标普指数靠拢来作弊，结果遭到重创；他们为了保住职位而作弊。即便用这种简单的价值模型进行长期投资也十分困难。

<!--en-->
From March of 2000 until today, value has outperformed the S&P 500 by 175% and *Pzena* did much better than that. People left at the wrong time as usual. If you stick to your guns and your clients don't you can understand the pressures on a manager? You are looking at a chart through four years and say you will stick it out through the value cycle, but that is an awfully long time and many don't survive. Some value managers cheated with a value tilt to the S&P, and they got clobbered. They were cheating to hang in there. Even surviving long term with this simple value model is tough.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程。这看似是个小问题，但它却揭示了整个真相。实际上，**我一直在做的是尽可能对公司进行估值。**如果给公司估值极其困难呢？**那就做别的事情。**如果你有选择其他机会的余地，这确实是一个非常强大的理念。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
This may seem like a minor point, but this is the whole story. Really what **I am always doing is valuing the company when I can.**
What happens if it is very difficult to value a company? **Do something else.** That is a very powerful concept if you have the luxury of looking at something else.

我上周做出的承诺是：**如果**你的估值正确，通常最多只需要两三年时间——有时甚至更快——*市场先生*就会认可它。**做好估值工作。**我对“价值”的定义并非低市净率或低市盈率，而是**内在价值**。可以看到，市净率作为衡量指标的效果随时间推移有所减弱，其年化收益率从6%降至3.1%。

<!--en-->
The guarantee I made last week is that **if** your valuation is right, it will usually only take *Mr. Market* two or three years at most—sometimes a lot faster—to get it right. **Do good valuation work.**
They way **I define value** is not low price to book or P/E but **intrinsic value**. You can see price/book has gotten a little less robust over time from out performing at 6% to 3.1% CAGR.

我们讨论的是业绩表现上的差异。

<!--en-->
We are talking about the disparity in performance.

与过去的工业时期相比，服务类企业的资产重要性有所降低——这或许正是**账面价值重要性下降的原因**。我会逐家公司进行自下而上的分析。我深受价值投资理念的影响，但不会预测价值周期中的超额或落后表现。

<!--en-->
The lesser importance of assets with service businesses as in the past industrial period—perhaps a reason **why book value losing its importance.**
I analyze each company from the bottom up. I am very value driven I don't predict under or out performance of the value cycle.

# 神奇公式

<!--en-->
*MAGIC FORMULAS*

1. **你的付出：**“标准化”EBIT/企业价值（即我所支付的代价或税前盈利收益率）。如果因永久性税收变动导致税收减少，你对EBIT的估值应相应提高。计算税后收益率并观察其中的差异。EBIT能否代表真实的现金流？EBIT实际上是EBITDA减去维护资本支出的简写。不同的资本化方式会影响净利润；税率的差异也会造成影响。使用EBIT是一种实现“同类比较”的方法。
2. **你所获得的收益：** EBIT/(NWC + NFA)。分母部分显示了为获得该EBIT我需要在企业中投入的资金。别忘了将一年内的投资资本进行标准化处理。这就是我所获得的收益。我曾向你们介绍过我的“神奇”公式，作为评估公司的起点。**JG：** 你提出了一个非常重要的观点。这两者完全是两码事。这是基于我为此支付的成本所计算出的收益（EBIT/EV）；而这是基于公司为了创造这些收益而在资产上所投入的成本计算出的收益（EBIT/IC或(NWC + NFA)）。它们属于两个截然不同的概念。这反映的是他们过去所创造资本的回报率。那又怎样呢？新增资金虽然能带来不错的回报，但未必能达到过去的水平。新店可能带来60%的ROIC，而老店此前能达到70%；但由于没有其他地方能带来如此高的回报，我仍会建造这家新店。不过，如果我的税前回报率在15%到20%之间，那么稍有变动就可能改变决策。请使用**标准化的EBIT**，并着眼于正常环境下的表现。**这正是其中的“艺术”所在**——我所谓“正常环境”是指公司和经济均无特殊状况时的状态。显然，确定何为“标准化”属于主观判断的范畴。以下是针对企业投资资本的标准化EBIT数据。这是我对企业类型的最佳估算。我曾经营国防业务，期间与许多推销收购案的投资银行家有过接触。他们会说：“你可以在现有盈利基础上增加20美分，通过以9倍EBIT的倍数收购一家税前利润率为11%的企业来实现非稀释性收购；该企业的债务利率为9.5%，部分为固定利率、部分为浮动利率，利差仅为1.5%。对于一家表现平平的企业来说，这值得吗？”哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资课程”指出：**他们采用了与我们之前相同的估值倍数，尽管我们的杠杆率会更高。**那些投资银行家准备了一份长达400页、封面精美的报告，但归根结底，这就是你要承担的风险。看起来像是一笔糟糕的交易。把分析简化到本质——**这是一家价格合理的好企业吗？这笔交易值得吗？**不要抛弃逻辑，只需问一个简单的问题：我需要支付多少？我能获得多少收益？如果你必须不断通过收购来扩张，那情况就完全不同了。

<!--en-->
1. **WHAT YOU PAY:** "Normalized" EBIT/Enterprise Value (What I pay or pre-tax earnings yield). You would value EBIT higher if tax revenues are lower due to a permanent tax change. Take the after-tax yield and see what the differences are. Is EBIT representative of true cash flow. EBIT is a short hand for EBITDA – Maint. Capex. Different capitalization can skew net income. Differences in tax rates. Using EBIT is a way to compare apples to apples.
2. **WHAT YOU EARN:** EBIT/(NWC + NFA) the denominator shows what I need to invest in the business to get that EBIT. Don't forget to normalize investment capital over the course of a year. What I earn.
I told you about my "magic" formula as my starting point for looking at companies.
**JG:** You bring up a very important point. These are totally two different things.
This is how much I earn based on what I paid for it (EBIT/EV).
This is what I earn based on what the company paid for the assets that created those earnings (EBIT/IC or (NWC + NFA)). Those are two totally separate concepts.
Return on the capital they made on the past. So what? Incremental dollars will make good returns but not as high as they made in the past. I may earn 60% ROIC on the new store versus 70% previously in the old store, but there are no other places to earn as high a return so I will still build that store. But if my pretax returns are between 15% and 20%, it doesn't take too much to tip the balance.
Use **normalized EBIT**. Look at the normal environment. **This is the art part.** What I think a normal environment might be. There is nothing special going on in regards to the company or the economy. Obviously it is an assessment now we are into the art part of determining "normalized".
Here is normalized EBIT over capital invested in the business. This is my best guessimate of what type of business do I have?
When I ran a defense business I had a lot of contact with investment bankers who were pitching acquisitions. They would say, "Well, you can add 20 cents to earnings and make a non-dilutive acquisition by acquiring a business at 9 x EBIT earning 11% pre-tax and that is about flat in growth while borrowing 9.5% partly fixed and partly variable. The spread is 1.5%. Is this worth it for a crappy business? No.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
**They slapped on the same multiple we had before even though we would be a lot more levered.** The investment bankers had a 400 page report with a nice cover on it, but when you get down to it, this is the bet you are taking. It looks like a bad bet.
Boil the analysis all down to its essence—**is it a good business at a good price?** Is the bet worth it?
Don't throw out logic. Ask one simple question. How much do I have to pay? How much am I earning?
If you have to continually make acquisitions to grow, then it is a different animal.

除非你需要通过收购来实现未来增长，否则你在有形资本上的回报率可达50%（2美元/4美元）。你只需替换固定资产即可；你的资本支出将仅限于此。无需不断重置商誉——商誉属于过去的成本。（参见沃伦·巴菲特在1983年伯克希尔·哈撒韦年报中关于摊销和无形资产的论述。）

<!--en-->
You are earning 50% on tangible capital ($2/$4) unless you have to add acquisitions to get future growth. All you have to replace is fixed assets. Your capital spending will be confined to replacing fixed assets. You don't have to keep replacing Goodwill. Goodwill is a past cost. (See Warren Buffett's writing in the 1983 Annual Report of Berkshire Hathaway on amortization and intangible assets).

我花了很长时间才明白这一点，但如果我早读到了巴菲特1983年的信，就会更早领悟。

<!--en-->
This took me a long time to learn, but if I had read Buffett's letter in 1983, then I would have learned this sooner.

别去管公司是如何走到这一步的。如果公司因糟糕的收购导致债务被计入EV中，商誉只是过往收购产生的沉没成本。如果管理层是个频繁进行不良收购的收购狂人，未来的盈利便无法达到他们所宣称的水平——必须对此进行调整。

<!--en-->
Forget how the company got there. If the company made bad acquisitions so debt is in the EV. Goodwill is a sunk cost in past acquisitions. If management is a serial acquirer that makes bad acquisitions then the future earnings won't be what they say it will be. Adjust.

我关心的是*今天*我需要支付多少才能产生当下及未来的回报。EBIT/EV已经考虑了我为此所支付的成本。

<!--en-->
I care about what I have to pay *today* to generate returns today and in the future. EBIT/EV takes into account for what I paid for it.

如果该公司拥有可搬迁工厂的土地，且该土地能用于更高价值的用途，那么切勿仅取土地价值而忽略搬迁成本。应计算工业用地价值与土地实际价值之间的差额。

<!--en-->
If they have land where their factory could be moved and the land used for a higher and better use, don't just take the value of the land without considering the cost of moving the factory. Do the difference between the industrial land and the value of the land.

为何我们要采用净固定资产（NFA）？这并不总是准确的。假设我们以10美元的价格购买一家酒店，其使用寿命为10年，我们将其折旧期为5年，如今其账面价值为5美元。但如果其价值归零，我可能还需再投入10美元。这样一来，由于未考虑固定资产的替换与再投资，得出的回报率（5美元）便会偏高。

<!--en-->
Why are we taking Net Fixed Assets (NFA)? It is not always right. Say we buy a hotel for $10 and it is going to last 10 years and we write it down over 5 years and now it is at $5. But if this goes down to zero, I might half to invest another $10. This would give me ($5) a skewed return (being too high) because of not considering replacement and reinvestment into the fixed assets.

假设你拥有100家酒店，它们处于不同的运营周期中，那么平均而言，使用NFA是合理的。在正常10年周期内，每年约有10%的酒店需要进行翻新。这就是我对持续性企业的简易估算方法。

<!--en-->
Say you have 100 hotels and they are all on different cycles, then on average, you will be correct in using NFA. 10% of your hotels will be refurbished each year over a 10 year normal cycle. That is my quick and dirty for an ongoing business.

我是否需要根据企业的特殊情况对数字进行调整？需警惕过度高估资本回报率的现象。

<!--en-->
Do I have to adjust any numbers based on the unique circumstances of the business. Beware of overstating returns on capital.

《证券分析》的作者胡克认为：既然你无法控制公司，那就只能接受现有的资本结构，因此应使用市盈率指标。*JG*：我强烈反对这一观点——理性的人看法各异——因为我从事这一行已久，发现EV/EBIT比市盈率更可靠；如果管理层未能合理利用资本结构，自然会有人取而代之。使用**EV/EBIT**才是正道。

<!--en-->
Hooke, author of *Security Analysis*, said that you don't control the company so you take the capitalization as is so use P/E. It is the hand you drew. *JG:* I strongly disagree with this—reasonable minds differ—because I have been doing this a long time and EV to EBIT works better than P/E because if management doesn't optimally use optimal capitalization then someone will come in and do it for you. Using **EV/EBIT** is the way to go.

收购价值与市盈率倍数并非同一概念。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程指出：若资本支出出现大幅波动，则应采用毛利润与净利润的混合指标。“整合收购往往会导致亏损。”你虽然为门店投入了资金，但尚未获得相应的EBIT，因此必须对EBIT数值进行标准化处理。

Acquisition value is not the same as P/E multiple.

"Roll-ups mean lose money."
You spent the money on the stores but you don't receive the EBIT yet, so you must normalize the number for EBIT.

<!--en-->
If you are earning 50% to 60% vs. 15% to 20% then we are looking at two different animals. Then what are their growth prospects, what is their growth rate, bargain price, good business?

20%的税前收益相当于12%的税后收益。企业的平均水平就是12%。

我赚钱并非因为自己特别聪明，而是因为我对自己要做的事有全局把握。这种全局观正是50%至60%与15%至20%之间的区别所在。

## 资本成本：我的资本所面临的机会成本。

<!--en-->
*Capital Cost: Opportunity cost for my capital*

*JG*如何比较投资项目？对于一家无杠杆公司而言，每股税后盈利1美元时对应的市盈率是多少？

<!--en-->
How *JG* compares investments.
For a $1 of earnings per share after tax what P/E for a non-leveraged company?

如今我有了其他资金运用选择，10年期债券的无风险回报率低于6%，因此我采用6%作为基准。

<!--en-->
Now I have alternatives for my money, the risk-free return is the 10-year bond is less than 6%, I use 6%.

即便利率只有4.5%，也绝不会低于6%。巴菲特也确认过这一点：当利率低于6%时，我仍采用6%作为基准。

<!--en-->
Never lower than 6% even if the rates are 4.5%. You know Buffett confirmed that when rates are below 6%, I use 6%.

如果10年期债券收益率为7%，我就以7%作为基准。市盈率为16.66时，1美元对应的收益率即为6%（无风险利率）。如果我的1美元能在两年内增长到1.40美元的每股收益，那么我更倾向于选择这种增长型投资而非固定的6%收益。

<!--en-->
Now if the 10 year bonds are 7%, then I use 7% as my bogie.
$1 at a 16.66 price earnings ratio is equivalent to 6% yield (risk free rate). If my $1 is going to grow to $1.40 EPs in two years, then I prefer growth vs. a static 6%.

如何解释20倍市盈率或1美元对应5%的收益率？前提是该公司确实在成长，且我对这种增长充满信心。

How do you justify 20x or 5% yield on $1? If it is growing and I am confident of that growth.

## 我将这里的投资机会与其他选择进行比较：把具有5%收益率的成长型资产与6%的无风险利率相对照。我获得的资金是来自公司的税后利润，而债券提供的是税后现金流。先看EBIT/EV部分，再看ROIC部分。以两家企业为例：*Jason’s Gum Store*：需投入40万美元建设，运营利润为20万美元，因此ROIC为50%；*Jimbo’s Just Broccoli*：收益40万美元，但利润仅1万美元，ROIC仅为2.5%。与6%的政府债券收益率相比，Jimbo实际上每年亏损3.5%（2.5% - 6%）。这简直荒谬，除非他坚信利润会大幅增长。虽然看似赚了点钱（2.5%），实则是在浪费资金（-3.5%）。这就是我评估每家企业的方式——它们究竟在做什么。我不会为价值毁灭者买单。切勿陷入只买低市盈率股票的“价值陷阱”。WEB称其为“烟蒂股”。

<!--en-->
Compare the opportunities here versus my other choices. I compare a growing 5% yield to a 6% risk-free rate. When I get the money it is after-tax from the company compared to the after tax stream from the bond. EBIT/EV portion. Then I look at the ROIC portion. Two businesses: *Jason's Gum Store:* $400,000 to build and $200,000 in operating profit so 50% ROIC. *Jimbo's Just Broccoli:* $400,000 earnings $10,000 = 2.5% ROIC. But compared to the 6% government bond yield, Jimbo is actually losing (2.5% - 6%) 3.5% a year. This is crazy unless he thinks the profits will grow tremendously. Though it seems he is making a little bit of money (2.5%), he is actually throwing money away (-3.5%). This is how I evaluate each business—what are they doing. I won't pay for a value destroyer. Stay out of Value Traps of just buying low P/E stocks. WEB calls them “cigar butts.”

## 我想探讨两件事：哥伦比亚大学商学院的14门特殊情境投资课程。我支付的费用是否能带来**良好的回报**，资本的**增量回报**（*MROIC*）又是多少？要获得这种回报需要投入何种资本？我究竟支付了什么代价，这是否是一家**优质**企业？我希望避开*价值陷阱*。我主要关注的是未来三到四年的标准化EBIT与去年的EBIT对比情况。我所赚取的收益中，有多少能以同等比率进行再投资？资本的增量回报会影响我的增长率，进而影响美元资产随时间的增值幅度，最终决定标准化的增长率和盈利水平。

<!--en-->
I want to look at two things: 14 Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School Am I getting a **good return based on what I am paying** and what are the **incremental returns** (*MROIC*) on capital? What kind of capital do I have to put in to earn that type of return? What am I paying and is this a **good** business? I want to stay out of the *value traps*. I am really looking at normalized EBIT three or four years out vs. last year's EBIT. How much of the money that I earn can I reinvest at the same rate. The incremental return on capital will affect my growth rate. It will affect how much my dollar will grow over time, then it will what normalized growth rates and earnings will be. Generally, the way I solve any issues like that are...I look for what things in three years will be worth $50 and I pay $25 for them. If it is $45 or $55, I don't care; I am not smart enough to fine tune it over time. I am picking my spots. There are not that many companies are trading at that discount. It is $38 going to $58 in three years—24% per year. Depending upon how confident I am in that return that may be a great rate of return. Some times I need a higher rate of return depending upon my confidence. I may take a 15% to 20% rate of return despite I like to make more than that. If I am wrong how much can I lose? If I have a lot of room to be wrong and still not lose money. The risk is low. If the cost of hanging in there is dead money for three years and the $25 goes to $30 or wherever, I get an OK return. Generally, if I am good and I get 4 out of 6 right or how many I get. I look out three years. I take my best shot; I look for a wide disparity. I always looking for a catalyst or the market will realize what I see. What will make people see what I see? This is a special situations class so I would love to have a catalyst on everything I do. Eventually, in three years or more you don't even need a catalyst. There are a lot of things that can happen. **The efficient market people are right but only long term.** But eventually the facts come out. Whatever people were uncertain about now over the next two or three years, they find the answer to. There are a lot of people out there trying to figure out what something is worth. **So I think the flaw with the efficient market theory is that it often takes a lot more time.** There is often a lot of emotion in the short term and there is much more uncertainty involved, and people take the discounts for uncertainty but there is more opportunity if you have a longer term horizon. In the short term I don't think a stock can trade at $20 and $35 and nothing happens and they both can't be right. The economy doesn't change that much. **In the short term, the market may not be efficient, but in the long term the market eventually gets it right.** Other times a company may buy back stock if they think it is cheap. These little pieces of paper represent the whole company. Eventually all those things work together to get the right price. We will talk about *Duff & Phelps*. I learned from that. Break......... *(See case study material on Duff & Phelps *before* reading this section)* EXERCISE: *Duff & Phelps....Buy, hold or sell?* *Students reviewed the annual report of Duff & Phelps without looking at the subsequent price.* The best section is to look at the front section where they summarized five years of financial and operating history. This is a **great** business, it is growing, and it requires low capital intensity. Every dollar they make is spent to buy back shares. You want to see how the management's bread buttered. How much of their salary vs. share ownership? If they are giving themselves egregious option packages then I will take that into account. Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School Income grew but total assets did not grow. Their incremental return on capital is infinite. They can grow without reinvesting their capital. Did anyone attempt to value this? *Duff & Phelps* was spun off at $7. EBITDA is 31.25 and EBIT is $28.8. EBITDA of $31.25 minus capex of $2.5 = $29.535 EV/(Ebitda – capex). There are negative working capital businesses like *MacDonald's*. Anyone see a problem with using a normalized earnings? Look at the fast growth rate of earnings. Do you think that is sustainable? I took a normal growth rate over five years. Three different EBIT growth rates: 8%, 13%, 20%. I chose a conservative 8% growth rate. EBIT of $43.72 x .6 for taxes = $26.23 x 13 P/E = $341. I shrank the number of shares due to the buy backs down to 3.5 million outstanding shares. I assumed that they were buying back shares with the shares increasing in price by 8% a year. Don't forget to make assumptions about what they would do with their excess cash. $341/3.5 = about $95 to $100 per share. So at $52 today at 8% the stock price was $99; at 13% the price was $122 and at 20% the price was $164. If I go out five years expecting to earn 20% per year, how could I earn the return sooner? Time compressed? How could I make 50% in a year? The market figures it out sooner. I make 76% if pension funds wake up and discount the earnings at 9%. *Duff & Phelps* was a small cap stock with low liquidity. **I am always looking at value and where it is now.** This spin off was a good learning tool for *(Joel's interest and work to analyze and invest in) Moody's*. *Duff & Phelps* was taken over by *Fitch* at $100. Compare the multiple to the bond rate. I will take a 5% earnings yield with a great business and with growth vs. 6% bond yield that is flat. Quality of Earnings Example: *Commodore*. Work in Process Inventory (WIP) growing faster than Sales. *Sunbeam* Article in *Barron's*. *Chain Saw Al* stuffed the channels with inventory. Another trick is to write down inventory to 0. 490 million to $0. If there are any sales in future periods then sales will be inflated and there will be extra profits. $92 million in PP&E removes D&A so earnings are overstated. Drop in allowance for doubtful accounts is less conservative accounting. Sunbeam still lost money after all these adjustments. *Perelman* took stock at $40 but the company was worth $7 per share. **Each mistake leads to better insights and subtleties.**

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

# 格林布拉特课程 #3

<!--en-->
*Greenblatt Class #3*

理查德·普泽纳先生于2006年9月21日的演讲

<!--en-->
Presentation by Mr. Richard Pzena
Sept. 21, 2006

# 三个目标：

<!--en-->
*Three objectives:*

(1) 我想谈谈价值投资的一般原理：它为何有效？哪些特征可能让你相信某资产具有价值？又是什么导致这些股票或公司价格低廉？

<!--en-->
(1) I want to talk about value investing in general: why does it work, what are the characteristics that might make you believe there is value, and what makes them (the stocks or the companies) cheap.

(2) 如何实际分析一家企业？首先从宏观层面讲——什么才是好企业？我会花些时间讨论好企业与坏企业之间的区别。

<!--en-->
(2) How do you actually analyze a business? First generically—what makes a good business? I will spend a little bit of time talking about the difference between a good business vs. a bad business.

(3) 接着我会以Lear Corp为例，说明它是否可能属于价值投资标的。我们将尝试判断它究竟是不是价值投资。

<!--en-->
(3) Then I will use an example, *Lear Corp*, as something that might be a value investment. We will try to understand whether it is or is not a value investment.

随时欢迎提问打断。

<!--en-->
Feel free to interrupt with questions any time.

## 1. 让我从价值投资开始讲起。

<!--en-->
*1. Let me start with value investing.*

我假定你们都读过关于价值投资的学术研究成果。它们基本都指出同一结论：如果你进行投资时关注所付价格与账面价值、销售额、盈利或现金流等价值指标之间的关系，往往能取得不错的成绩。法玛和法国的研究表明，只要时间跨度足够长，按账面价值计量的低价股表现会优于指数。

<!--en-->
I assume you have all read the same things, the academic studies on value investing. They all say basically the same thing that if you do invest and you are sensitive to the price you pay relative to some metric of value like book value, sales, earnings, cash-flow, you tend to naively do well. *Fama & French* studies show price relative to book value metrics outperforming an index as long as they have a pretty long period to work with.

这类研究被反复验证。事实上，我敢说找不到任何一个连续20年买入市盈率、市销率或市净率最低十分位股票的时期，其表现会不如买入指数基金。但长期来看，这确实是一种有效的策略。我不必局限于账面价值；销售额、现金流和盈利——任何能反映企业规模的有形指标同样适用。如果你以低于该指标所反映价值的价格买入股票，就能跑赢市场。**请注意价值指标带来的显著超额收益，不过也存在表现不佳的时期（阴影区域）。***既然如此简单，为什么不是人人都这么做呢？** 这就是我的困惑所在。即便你研究这些数据已有数十年之久。上世纪90年代末曾出现罕见的十年期，价值投资似乎失效了——当时我们身处“新世界”。如今我们又面临另一种“迷你新世界”论调：工业商品和能源将长期短缺，价格也会永远居高不下。几乎可以肯定，最终结果仍会是价格下跌。你永远无法预知何时会发生，但世界就是如此——人们喜欢某些事物，也会厌恶另一些事物。

<!--en-->
Those studies are repeated over and over again. In fact, I don't believe you can find a single 20-year period of buying the lowest deciles P/E, P/S or P/Book stocks where you wouldn't do better than buying an index. There are none. But over the long term it is a strategy that works. I don't have to use book value, the same thing works with sales, cash flow and earnings--any tangible metric of the size of the business. If you buy a stock at a low price relative to that metric, you outperform the market. *Note the large out-performance of the value metrics, however there are periods of underperformance (shaded areas).***So why doesn't everyone just do it, if it is so simple?** That is the dilemma for me. Even recently where you could study this data for decades. In the late nineties, you had the rare ten-year period that showed that value investing didn't work. We were in a "new world". Now we are in another "mini-new" world thesis where we will be perpetually short of industrial commodities and energy and those prices will stay high forever. Almost certainly that will end the same way (badly with price declines). You never know when, but this is what happens in the world. People love things; people hate things.
