哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资课程”：这些投资曾带来不错的回报，但2001年形势突变。究竟发生了什么？他们未能预见销售下滑——即技术行业的放缓。人们以为增长会持续，却没看到需求的下降。这是互联网泡沫破裂之后的情况。当时涌现了大量可能成为网络设备客户的企业。它们筹集了大量资金并进行了巨额资本支出。这导致对某些网络设备的需求远远超出了正常水平。

<!--en-->
42
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
There were nice returns and then came 2001. So what happened? They didn't foresee the sales—the technology slowdown. People thought growth would continue while not seeing the decline in demand. This is post the Internet bubble. Lots of companies were created who were or could be customers for networking equipment. There was a lot of money raised and a lot of capital expenditure. It really got above trend line for demand for some of this equipment.

如果看看这里的营业利润表现……1997年至2000年间，营业利润率从最低的8%上升至最高的11%。因此，如果你认为该公司能持续保持10%的营业利润率，那可就错了——我最初买入股票时并未这么想。我们原以为公司会在销售额触底后重新回到其原有的商业模式。问题在于：*销售额的底线究竟在哪里*？这家公司的营收曾达到7亿美元，那么底线会是5亿美元还是3.5亿美元呢？他们能否扭转局面？我在股价5美元时买入该股票；而购买*MIPS*股票时股价仅为1.10美元，我当时倾尽全力加仓。这种情况确实令人心惊。

<!--en-->
If you look at the operating income performance here...the years from 1997 to 2000 the operating margins went from a low of 8% to a high of 11%. So if you think the business will keep earning operating margins of 10%, but we were not thinking that initially when I started buying the stock. We thought the company could get back to their business model once they had reached the bottom of their sales. The question was *where was the bottom of their sales*? This was a business that has done $700 million so would it be $500 or $350 million? Were they going to be able to right the ship? I bought the stock at $5 while I made that *MIPS* purchase at $1.10, and I was buying with both hands while I was tripling down. This was something that can be very scary.

**学生：** 你永远无法精准判断底部。那你如何决定愿意投入多少资金？具体分配多少呢？

<!--en-->
**Student:** You never pick the bottom. How do you make the decision as to how much capital you are willing to pour in? How much do you allocate?

**BN：** 在这种特定情况下，我不断反复核实事实，与管理层沟通，试图彻底了解他们的扭亏为盈计划。本质上，你必须权衡风险与回报；有时市场在股价2美元时就已揭示了企业的价值及风险回报比。而在1.10美元时，你不得不问自己：“我是否判断错误？这家企业能否生存下去？”在1.10美元时我的判断是：只有公司倒闭才会让我蒙受损失。好消息是，以1.10美元买入55万股仅需约50万美元，这一仓位规模远不及在*MIPS*上投入的250万美元——当然，谁也不希望亏掉这笔钱。

<!--en-->
**BN:** In this particular situation I kept going back and double checking, triple checking my facts, checking with management and really trying to understand what the plan was in how they were going to turn it around. Basically you have to look at risk/reward and sometimes the market says at $2 you knew what the EV value was and the risk/reward. And at $1.10 you have to say, “Am I wrong? Will this business not be able to survive?” The way I was looking at it at $1.10—the company going out of business was the only way I was going to lose. The good news was that buying 550,000 at $1.10 was only about ½ million dollars so it was not as big a position as $2.5 million in *MIPS* though you do not want to lose the money.

**学生：** 如果你发现了其他更具吸引力的机会，你会投入同样多的资金吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** If you had found another opportunity that was compelling would you have put this much money into it?

**BN：** 我认为总有办法评估眼前的投资机会：既要看上行潜力，也要看下行风险。顺便说一句，没有哪位投资者比你的教授*乔尔·格林布拉特*更擅长分析上行与下行风险，这是他最出色的技能之一。对于这类小盘股，资金的分配取决于你可实际购买的份额。这可不是*微软*——如果你想给微软分配资金，几秒钟内就能完成任何规模的交易。但此类情况则截然不同。

<!--en-->
**BN:** I think there is always a way to look at the opportunity sets in front of you. Look at the upside and downside. By the way, there is no better investor who understands the upside and downside as your professor, *Joel Greenblatt*. That is one of his greatest skills. And for some of these small stocks, you allocate capital based on what is available for you to be able to buy. This is not *Microsoft*. If you want to allocate money to *Microsoft*, you can be filled in five seconds for whatever you want allocated. In something like this, it is different.

**学生：** 您能介绍一下您如何集中管理投资组合吗？换手率如何？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Can you give us an understanding about how you concentrate your portfolio? Your turnover?

**BN：** 集中投资？我曾持有占比超过20%的股票。至于换手率，如今与过去有所不同。我很难再找到具有同等机会的投资标的；能找到的虽价格低廉，但上行潜力有限。因此，我喜欢预留资金以应对这些能带来超额回报的机会。

<!--en-->
**BN:** Concentration? I have had 20% + positions. In terms of turnover, today is different than the past. I am having trouble finding ideas with the same opportunity. I can find ideas that are cheap but with not the same upside potential. So I like to have dry powder for these opportunities for real outsized returns.

我的盈利并非平稳产生——有些年份收益丰厚，有些则不然。现阶段的关键在于*保护资本，而非冒险行事*。

<!--en-->
I have made my money in a lumpy way—some years were big and others were not. The key thing at this point is *preservation of capital and not striking out at this point*.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**学生：** *ASTN*公司有现金来偿还债务吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Did *ASTN* have cash to offset the debt?

**BN：** 是的，他们有。他们经历了许多波折：原本有银行信贷额度，后来被可转换债券取代。当股价从40美元跌至5美元又回升至10美元时，他们与一家韩国公司合作发行了可转换证券（转换价为每股10美元），我原以为那家公司会收购他们。短期内并无偿债压力。最终他们进行了再融资，请来了*Deltec*的人参与，并发行了公开可转换债券。我想这发生在2003年，当时股价约为6美元中段。

<!--en-->
**BN:** Yes, they did. They went through a lot of different things. They had a bank line and they replaced it with a convertible. When the stock went from $40 to $5 and back to $10 they did a convertible security (convertible at $10/share) with a company in Korea that I thought would buy them. There was no near term problems. They ended up refinancing. They took out the guy from *Deltec* and they did a public convertible. I think they did it during 2003 when the stock was trading at the mid-$6's.

我可以详细讲述当时发生的情况。你必须善于随机应变。**这其中涉及大量的判断。** 资本分配、业务评估、人员判断以及风险判断——这里涉及诸多判断。我哥哥恰好是这家公司CEO的挚友。我没有内部消息，但我确实认为他是个诚实的人。正如你过去五年在新闻中看到的那样……在《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》出台前，人们行事比现在更随意、更草率。我认为这是今天值得记住的重要一点。

<!--en-->
I can walk through what happened. You have to be resourceful. **There is a lot of judgment involved.** Judgment involved with allocation of capital, judgment about the business, about the people and about the risk—there is a lot of judgment involved here. My brother happened to be best friends with the CEO of this company. I got no inside information, but I did think he was an honest man. And as you have seen in the news for the past five years...before Sarbanes-Oxley people played it a little faster and looser than they do today. I think that is an important thing to remember today.

**你必须保持独立。** 别人会告诉你各种信息，但仅仅因为管理层说了X、Y、Z，并不意味着这些就是事实。作为投资者，你的职责是反复核实这些信息，四处打听，去问问客户、竞争对手。打个电话，听听其他人的观点。

<!--en-->
**You have to be independent.** People will tell you things and just because management tells you X, Y and Z, it doesn't mean X, Y, & Z are true. Your job as an investor is to double and triple check it and go around this way and talk to a customer, talk to a competitor. Get on the phone and check out other points of view.

**学生：** 您是如何发现这家公司的？

<!--en-->
**Student:** How did you find this company?

**BN：** 该公司的企业价值与历史EBITDA比率很低。它之前就在我的关注范围内。

<!--en-->
**BN:** This was a low Enterprise Value to historical EBITDA valuation. It was on my radar screen before.

**学生：** 您用什么工具来筛选股票？

<!--en-->
**Student:** What serves as the screen?

**BN：** 我使用*彭博终端*。筛选只是起点而已。它主要用来找出具有某些特征的公司，以便我进一步深入研究。如今互联网的优势在于获取和处理信息的能力比以往任何时候都强。

<!--en-->
**BN:** I use *Bloomberg*. The screen is just a starting point. Basically, it identifies companies with certain characteristics to make me drill down further. The great thing about the Internet today is the ability to get information and manipulate it is greater than it has ever been.

**学生：** 您偏好的股票筛选方式是什么？

<!--en-->
**Student:** What is your preferred way to screen stocks?

**BN：** 我的筛选标准相当基础。很多时候，我会查看*创新低股*列表，看看是否有我了解其情况的公司。要知道，我从事这一行已有25年（自1980年起）。25年间，你会逐渐掌握一两点规律；于是你会关注估值指标，留意那些股价创新低的公司，从而大致判断哪家公司的业务前景较好、属于周期性行业。筛选方法有很多种。

<!--en-->
**BN:** I screen with pretty basic criteria. A lot of times, I will look at the *new low* list. I want to see if there is some company that I know something about. You know I have been doing this for 25 years (since 1980). In 25 years, you probably figure one or two things and so you look at valuation metrics, you look at companies hitting new lows and you sort of have a sense of somebody who has a good business, a cyclical business. There a lots of ways to screen.

*乔尔·格林布拉特（JG）：* 我们会开设关于如何筛选股票的课程，但实际上这只是个*起点*。我会给你提供很多并不光鲜但价格低廉的投资标的。

<!--en-->
*Joel Greenblatt (JG):* We will have a class on how to screen, but really it is just a *starting* point. I will give you plenty of places to go that are not that pretty but that are cheap.

**学生：** 您的筛选范围有多大？

<!--en-->
**Student:** How big a universe do you screen for?

**BN：** 你可以按市值或国家来限定筛选范围。在*彭博终端*上有多种筛选方式。我的考虑因素是：我能投入多少资金？5%的仓位又意味着什么？从这点出发来判断是否值得进一步深入调研。有时你无法预知某个投资想法会走向何方。你开始买入某只股票，却不确定它是否会继续下跌。因此你必须建立一个关于价值的数据库——这就是一切。**了解公司的价值是一项极其宝贵的数据库建设成果。它是你的智力资本。**

<!--en-->
**BN:** Well, you can cut it off by market cap or you can cut it off by country. There a lots of different ways to screen on *Bloomberg*. The way I look at it is: how much capital can I commit to it? And what is a 5% position? Look at it that way to decide if that will be meaningful enough to do the further work and drill down on the potential idea. Sometimes you don't know where the idea will go. You start buying something and you don't know if it is going to get cheaper. You sort of have to have a data base of where values are--that is everything. **Understanding the values of companies is a really, really valuable database to build. It is your intellectual capital.**

**学生：** 您凭什么认为这家公司的销售额已经触底？

<!--en-->
**Student:** What allowed you to think that this company's sales had hit bottom?

**BN：** 当时所有产品都在海外制造，人们认为中国会挤垮所有这些公司。所有订单都会流向成本最低的生产商。但实际情况并非如此。如果你能因为对方缺少零部件就迫使其中断生产线，那你就不仅仅是普通的商品生产商。如果客户是*戴尔*——他们本就不想与成千上万家供应商打交道。因此人们担心中国公司会抢走所有业务。我们与一些公司交谈，了解它们与供应商的合作方式，我其实并不担心那种情况。但这家公司必须确定哪里的生产成本最低，以及如何腾出部分产能。

<!--en-->
**BN:** Everything was being made overseas and that China was going to kill all these companies. Everything was going to the lowest cost producer. But that is not really it. If you are in a position where you can shut down somebody's production line because they do not have a part, then you are not just a commodity producer. If you are selling to *Dell*—first of all they don't want to deal with thousands and thousands of vendors. So the fear was that China companies were going to take all the business. We spoke to companiesand how they like to deal with their vendors and I was not really concerned about that situation. But what this company had to do was figure where they could manufacture the cheapest and how to get out of some of their capacity.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情境投资课程：当时根本不会有那种程度的需求。所以他们承受了打击，关闭了工厂和设施，重新回归到合理的核心业务。我可以向你展示当时发生的一切。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
There just wasn't going to be the type of demand. So they took their hit. They closed down plants and facilities. They got back to their basic business that made sense. I can show you what had happened.

销售额确实大幅下滑。2002年1.08亿美元的净亏损中包含了巨额的固定资产减值。这并不等同于现金损失。实际上他们仍在产生现金流，因为应收账款在减少。他们只是对业务进行了精简。过去13个月里有人提交了13-D表格，据说该公司正在出售中。目前股价为9美元。

<!--en-->
Sales really did fall away. The $108 m in net income loss in 2002 was including significant fixed asset write downs. It was not the equivalent of a cash loss. Actually they were generating cash because their receivables were going down. So what happened was that they right sized the business. And a guy filed a 13-D in the last 13 months. The company is supposedly for sale. The stock is at $9.

之前有人问及安全边际的问题——虽然这里可能没有体现S（安全边际），但风险/回报比显然很不错。因为如果你相信销售额会在3.5亿美元左右触底，且公司能恢复10%的经营利润率，那么税前每股收益将达到70美分至80美分。不难看出这样就能盈利。所以……

<!--en-->
Somebody asked a question before about the margin of safety—the M of S might not have been here, but the risk/reward was certainly great. Because if you believed that sales were going to bottom at $350 million or near there and they got back to a 10% operating margin business, then you would generate $70 cents to $80 cents EPS pre-tax. It was not hard to see that you were going to make money. So.........

**学生：** 戴尔公司难道不能外包吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Couldn't *Dell* outsource?

**BN：** 他们可以，但戴尔希望找到可靠的供应商来提供准时交货的服务。戴尔虽然可以围绕这些供应商进行产品设计，但他们仍倾向于外包。戴尔本质上是一家组装与营销公司；他们希望供应商能提供优质零部件，以便组装电脑并出售。他们是一艘庞大的营销巨轮。Power-One也是类似的竞争对手。

<!--en-->
**BN:** They could but *Dell* wants dependable people (suppliers) as outsourcers to supply them with just in time delivery. *Dell* could design around them, but *Dell* wants to outsource. *Dell* is an assembly and marketer. *Dell* wants suppliers who can provide good parts so they can assemble the computers and sell them. They are a huge marketing ship. *Power-One* was a similar competitor.

当戴尔的股价跌至1.10美元时，首席执行官乔·麦克唐纳不得不亲自出面安抚员工，告诉他们自己两年内仍会留在公司。戴尔不想放弃这项业务；他们希望从ATSN获得价格合理且质量可靠的产品及优质服务，从而专注于自身擅长的领域。

<!--en-->
When *Dell* saw the stock trade at $1.10, *Joe McDonnell*, the CEO had to go to *Dell* and hold their hand and tell them that he was still going to be around in two years. They did not want to give that business out. They wanted dependable goods from *ATSN* at a fair price and good service while they focused on what they were good at.

**学生：** 您是否遇到过情况恶化的情形？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Did you have situations where the situations deteriorated.

**BN：** 当然有。我遇到过几次。好消息是成功的案例远多于失败的案例。其中一个例子就是Vlasic——它曾是金宝汤公司的拆分企业。该公司的负债率极高。他们生产多种食品，但由于过度负债导致经营不善，而我当时并未正确评估其价值。我以为这些资产的实际价值会比实际情况更高，结果失败了，我因此亏了钱。杠杆是一把双刃剑：正如学习企业价值时所知，顺境中它能为你创造巨额财富。

<!--en-->
**BN:** Sure. I have had a few. The good news is that I have had a lot more winners than losers. One that comes to mine was *Vlasic* which was a spin off from *Campbell Soup*. It was highly levered. They make a lot of different food products and basically, the company was over levered and it didn't perform, and I did not evaluate it properly. I thought the assets would be worth more than they were. And it didn't work. I lost money. Leverage is a two-edged sword. It will make you a lot of money when things go right as you would know from studying enterprise value.

如果你拥有5000万美元的股权和5亿美元的债务，那么当公司价值升至6亿美元时，你的股权就会翻倍；若价值跌至4.5亿美元，你则会血本无归。如果公司价值达到7亿美元，你的资金将翻四倍。这就是我的一个失误。如果重来一次，我可能会采取不同的做法。

<!--en-->
If you have $50 mm in equity and $500 mm in debt then a rise in value to $600 mm will double your equity and a drop in value to $450 mm will wipe you out. If it is worth $700 mm you will quadruple your money. So that was one of my mistakes. If I had to do it over again I might have done things a little bit differently.

**特拉华州威尔明顿，2005年9月13日**——特拉华州的一家联邦法院周二宣判金宝汤公司无需为拆分Vlasic Foods International一事承担欺诈罪责。

<!--en-->
**WILMINGTON, Del. Sep 13, 2005** — A federal court in Delaware Tuesday exonerated *Campbell Soup* Co. of charges of fraud in connection with its spin-off of *Vlasic Foods International*.

债权人指控这家位于新泽西州卡姆登的食品公司将亏损业务打包成新上市公司，并将其推向市场，而这家新公司几乎没有生存机会。

<!--en-->
Creditors had accused the Camden, N.J., food company of packaging its money-losing lines of business into the new public company and sending it into the market with little chance of survival.

美国地方法官肯特·乔丹驳回了他们的诉求，认定Vlasic公司在上市时具备偿付能力，因此金宝汤公司无需为该公司的后续破产负责。

<!--en-->
U.S. District Judge Kent Jordan ruled against them, finding that the *Vlasic* business was solvent at the time it hit the public market, so *Campbell Soup* isn't liable for the company's later collapse into bankruptcy.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情境投资课程指出：这场诉讼是为了筹集资金以偿还债权人（主要是债券持有者）的款项；这些债权人在Vlasic业务被拆分成立独立公司一年多后，购买了价值2亿美元的债券。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The lawsuit was part of a continuing effort to raise money to pay creditors, mainly bondholders, who bought into a $200 million debt offering more than a year after the Vlasic businesses were launched into a separate company.

除了泡菜业务外，金宝汤公司还将Swanson冷冻食品及其他业务并入这家新公司。

<!--en-->
In addition to the pickle line, *Campbell Soup* pushed its Swanson's frozen food and other businesses into the new company.

尽管金宝汤公司承认这些业务表现不佳，但与Vlasic相关的人员认为该公司仍有成功的可能，乔丹法官如此裁定。

<!--en-->
While *Campbell Soup* admitted the businesses were poor performers, those associated with Vlasic thought the company had a chance of succeeding, Jordan ruled.

根据周二的裁决，金宝汤公司拆分Vlasic并非出于欺骗债权人的目的。

<!--en-->
According to Tuesday's ruling, *Campbell Soup* didn't launch *Vlasic* with an eye toward defrauding the company's creditors.

作为拆分的一部分，金宝汤公司向Vlasic转让了5亿美元的债务，最终Vlasic于2001年1月申请了第11章破产保护。

<!--en-->
As part of the spin-off, *Campbell Soup* transferred $500 million in debt to Vlasic, which wound up filing for Chapter 11 protection in January 2001.

债权人原本希望借此案从金宝汤公司追回超过5.44亿美元的资金。

<!--en-->
Creditors had hoped to recover more than $544 million from *Campbell Soup* in the case.

在破产期间，Vlasic、Swanson及其他品牌以3.35亿美元的价格出售给Pinnacle Foods Corp.，而其他业务的出售则额外筹集了约2000万美元现金。

<!--en-->
During the bankruptcy, Vlasic, Swanson and other brands were sold to Pinnacle Foods Corp. for $335 million, while sales of other lines raised about $20 million in additional cash.

**JG：** 如您所见，布鲁斯确实是一位了不起的投资人。有情况时我会找他商量，他经验丰富。有一点值得注意——你们都足够聪明，能成为优秀投资人——那就是“实践”的重要性。我仍在学习中；我想布鲁斯也会说他仍在学习。好的一点是，你不必成为理查德·普泽纳或布鲁斯·纽伯格那样的人……

<!--en-->
**JG:** As you can see *Bruce* really is an amazing investor. He is the guy I call to go over a situation. He has seen a lot over the years. One of the things that helps—you are all smart enough to be good investors—that there is a lot to be said about *practice*. I am still learning. I would say *Bruce* would say he is still learning. The good thing is you don't have to be *Richard Pzena* or *Bruce Newberg* but

* 但你必须非常深思熟虑。
* 你必须做好功课。
* 你确实需要合适的框架。我要感谢*Bruce Newberg*的到来。掌声…… 结束。*Bruce Newberg*：课间与学生交谈…… **BN：** 我认为对冲基金中流通的资金太多了。这涉及资本配置问题——太多资金被分配给那些无法创造附加值的人。资金已从大盘股中流出。如果你查看养老基金的配置情况，比较六年前与如今分配给多空对冲基金的资金量，我敢保证现在分配给这些策略的资金要多得多。此外，更多资金流向了私募股权领域，用于资助企业收购。所有这些吸引资本的策略都会产生乘数效应。但你要知道市场存在周期性；你不会想涉足1970年至1975年的市场。会有某些时期这类业务表现优异，也有时期则不然。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程。可转换债券套利市场呢？我认为该市场现状是……过去一年里利率上升且波动性降低。通常而言，可转换债券套利者会押注高波动性和高利率；因此当利率上升时债券远期价值会下跌，而波动性减弱也会导致期权部分价值缩水。但如果资金从可转换债券中流出，你反而应趁机进入——去往资金正在撤离的领域。**学生：** 您认为调整已经足够了吗？**BN：** 或许尚未结束。真正的问题是：如果某指数出现大幅波动会怎样？比如大盘股表现强劲，而对冲基金回报率却比其低400至500个基点（净值计算）？那时会发生什么？因为人们往往依据过往经验来投资。正确的做法是根据未来趋势做判断，尽管你不可能永远准确。

<!--en-->
* You do have to be very thoughtful
* You do have to do your homework
* You do have to have the right framework
I want to thank *Bruce Newberg* for coming. Applause............
END
*Bruce Newberg:* talking to students between the break............
**BN:** I think there is just too much money floating around in hedge funds. I think it is allocation of capital. Too much capital has been provided to people who do not think they can provide value added. Money has moved out of the big cap stocks. If you look at pension fund allocation and you see how much money was allocated to long/short hedge funds six years ago versus today I can guarantee that there is so much more money allocated to these different strategies. And the other thing is that more money has gone to private equity. There is moremoney to fund buyouts. There is a multiplier effect for all of these different strategies that have attracted capital. But you know you go through cycles. You don't want to be involved in the markets from 1970 to 1975. There will be different cycles where this will be a great business and where it won't be a great business.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The Convertible Arbitrage market? I think that the market is ...well what you had happen in the past year: Interest rates have gone up and volatility has decreased. Typically, convertible arbitrage guys are long volatility and they are long the interest rate. So the bond forward value goes down when interest rates go up. The option portion is worth less as the volatility comes in. But if money floods out of converts, you want to go into it. Go to the area where money is flowing out of it.
**Student:** Do you think there has been enough of a correction?
**BN:** It is probably not over. The real question is what happens if we get a big move in some index? Like large cap stocks do really well and hedge fund returns under perform that by 400 to 500 basis points net? Then what will happen? **Because people tend to invest in the rear view mirror.** The right thing to do is think about what is going to happen though you won't always be right all the time.

*Second half of Class*

**JG：** 你可能会说现在对冲基金资金充裕，但机会不多；我在浪费时间，派对已经结束。1998年、2000年以及2002/03年，小盘股领域曾存在巨大机遇——那并不久远。如今我认为机会存在于大盘股中。我称之为“规模较大、上行空间有限但质量更佳的企业”。

<!--en-->
**JG:** You might say that there is a lot of hedge fund money out there and there might not be much opportunity now. I am wasting my time. The party is over. In 1998 and 2000 and 2002/03 there were huge opportunities in small caps. That was not too long ago. Right now I think the opportunities are in the large caps. I would call the opportunities larger cap with smaller upside and better quality businesses.

我不认为风险回报比发生了太大变化，但预计回报会更低而风险更小。现在你可以以诱人价格投资于更优质的企业，必须据此调整策略。

<!--en-->
I don't think the risk rewards have changed all that much, but I think the rewards will be lower but less risky. Now you have better businesses to invest in at attractive prices. You have to adjust for that.

在*Bruce*提到的*ATSN*案例中，他虽没有大量现金作为安全边际，却能下注1美元以期赚取5至7美元——这是一笔划算的风险/回报交易。你会接受这种风险/回报交易，但根据自身承受损失的能力来调整仓位大小。首次投资*MIPS*时属于安全边际型交易；他评估局势后选择了风险/回报型交易。

<!--en-->
In *Bruce's* example of *ATSN*, he did not have the pile of cash as a margin of safety but he could bet a $1 to make $5 or $6 or $7. It was a good risk/reward bet. You would take that risk/reward bet but adjust your position size based on your ability to take the hit on that. In the first bet, in *MIPS*, was a margin of safety bet. He fell into the situation, he assessed it and chose the risk reward bet.

显然，你希望追随自己尊敬的人学习。如果可能的话，将其视为一次学习经历。希望修完本课程后你能以特定视角看待世界。这不是唯一的世界观，却是富有成效的一种。我肯定会努力积累投资组合经验。

<!--en-->
Obviously, you want to work under somebody you respect. If you can I would look at it as a learning experience. Hopefully by the end of this course you will look at the world through a certain lens. This is not the only way to look at the world but it is one productive way to look at the world. I would certainly try to get myself into a position where I have some portfolio experience.

你必须犯过多次错误并从中吸取教训。如果你能评估某资产价值并以低于其实际价值的价格买入，事情其实没那么复杂。

<!--en-->
You have to screw up a bunch and learn from it. If you can value something and buy it for cheaper than it is worth it doesn't have to be a whole lot more complicated than that.

我带来了这本1959年出版的书，书名是《如何利用股市特殊情况获利》，作者为Maurece Schiller。书中讲述了如何通过超额认购和配股获得巨额利润。我的意思是：人们从事此类活动已有悠久历史。

<!--en-->
I brought this book published in 1959 and it is called, *How to Profit from Special Situations in the Stock Market* by Maurece Schiller. Big profits from oversubscriptions and rights offerings. My point is that people have been doing this for a long time.

今天我在报纸上看到关于麦当劳的对冲基金经理报道。内容涉及一位对冲基金投资者想收购麦当劳持有的房地产，再通过售后回租释放现金流。相关文章如下：

<!--en-->
I was looking in the paper today about the hedge fund manager in *McDonald's*. It is about a HF investor who wants to take over the real estate owned by *McDonald's* and then sale/lease back to free up some cash. Article below:

## 麦当劳的对冲基金经理：Pershing Square的20亿美元赌注在于该连锁店能否成功转型；但进展并未如预期迅速。2005年9月28日；C1版

<!--en-->
Hedge-Fund Man at *McDonald's* Pershing Square's $2 Billion Bet Is That the Chain Can Revamp; Time Frame Hasn't Been Fast. September 28, 2005; Page C1

1997年，一位年轻气盛的对冲基金经理设想：麦当劳公司应出售旗下所有餐厅，以便为股东奉上一份丰厚的“价值大餐”。八年后，比尔·阿克曼已持有了这家美国标志性企业的大量股份；当他驾车驶入得来速窗口时，简直垂涎欲滴——没错，他还要搭配薯条一起享用。哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资课程”指出：自9月中旬披露阿克曼旗下的潘兴广场对冲基金已积累足够多的股票和期权、可使其投资者获得价值20亿美元的4.9%股权以来，麦当劳股价便持续动荡。这堪称对冲基金有史以来最大的单股持仓之一。

<!--en-->
In 1997, a brash, young hedge-fund manager envisioned *McDonald's* Corp. selling off all its restaurants to give shareholders a huge value meal. Eight years later, Bill Ackman has amassed a super-size stake in the great American icon and is salivating as he pulls up to the drive-through window.
And, yes -- he wants fries with that.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
*McDonald's* stock has been roiled since it emerged in mid-September that Mr. Ackman's Pershing Square hedge funds had accumulated stock and options that could give his investors a 4.9% stake valued at $2 billion. That is one of the biggest single-stock positions ever taken by a hedge fund.

阿克曼将麦当劳视为三家独立的企业：其一为特许经营业务，占其全球3万多家餐厅中的约75%；其二为直接拥有并运营剩余餐厅的餐饮运营商；其三则为房地产公司，持有近40%门店所占用的土地。

<!--en-->
Mr. Ackman sees Mickey D's as three separate businesses: a franchising operation that accounts for about 75% of its 30,000-plus restaurants world-wide; a restaurateur that owns and operates the rest of the outlets; and a real-estate company that owns the land beneath nearly 40% of all of them.

上世纪90年代，他曾持有少量股份，并建议麦当劳将餐厅业务与房地产业务分拆上市。据知情人士透露，如今他的想法略有不同：他仍希望麦当劳保留最核心的特许经营业务，同时将公司自有餐厅的大部分股权作为一家独立的上市公司出售，该实体将成为大型麦当劳特许经营商；但他要求麦当劳保留这些房地产，利用其中未被开发的价值进行借贷，并将所得资金分给包括他本人在内的股东。

<!--en-->
Back in the 1990s, he had a small stake and suggested that *McDonald's* spin off both its restaurants and the real-estate business. Now, he has a slightly different idea, says a person familiar with it. He still wants *McDonald's* to retain the crown-jewel franchise operation and to sell off a majority stake in the company-owned restaurants as a separate, publicly traded entity that would be one big *McDonald's* franchisee. But he wants *McDonald's* to keep its real estate, borrow against its untapped value and give the money to him and other shareholders.

阿克曼希望麦当劳保留的两类业务堪称理想之选：它们回报率高且资本成本低，使得公司能够通过贷款和股票发行以较低成本筹集运营资金。特许经营商向门店业主收取其营业额的4%作为费用；房地产公司则额外收取9%至10%的租金。

<!--en-->
The two businesses Mr. Ackman wants *McDonald's* to keep are as close to ideal as possible: They have high returns and low cost of capital, allowing it to raise money to run the business cheaply via loans and stock sales. The franchisee business charges outlet owners 4% of whatever they generate in revenue. The real-estate company gets an additional 9% to 10% in rent.

第三类业务则不尽如人意：其利润率低，且运营餐厅需要巨额资本支出。创始人雷·克罗克最初甚至并不想拥有餐厅，他更愿从每个汉堡中赚取微薄利润。麦当劳后来才涉足自营餐厅业务，当时公司现金流充裕到不知如何处置。

<!--en-->
The third business isn't as good: It has low profit margins and demands huge capital spending to run the restaurants. Founder Ray Kroc originally didn't even want to own restaurants, preferring to collect all those pennies on every burger. *McDonald's* ownership of its own joints came later, when it was throwing off so much cash that it didn't know what else to do with it.

这些房地产仅躺在麦当劳的资产负债表上，并未为股东创造太多现金。据熟悉其分析的人士称，阿克曼对麦当劳房地产的估值为600亿美元，这一数值基于其产生的现金流计算。相比之下，该公司目前的股市总值与净债务之和还不到500亿美元。

<!--en-->
The real estate is just sitting on the *McDonald's* balance sheet without producing much cash for shareholders. Mr. Ackman values *McDonald's* real estate at $60 billion, based on the cash it produces, says the person familiar with his analysis. By comparison, the entire company right now has less than $50 billion in stock-market value and net debt.

对许多投资者而言，这一切或许显得大胆甚至离谱。若分拆出的强大特许经营商日后与其原东家抗衡，可能会适得其反；而给母公司增加债务同样充满风险。

<!--en-->
All this may come off to many investors as audacious, if not farfetched. Spinning off a powerful, gigantic franchisee could backfire if it decides to flex its muscles against its former owner. And adding debt to the parent would be risky, too.

不过，公司实际上可能正在认真考虑这些提议。上周，在公司定期举行的分析师与投资者会议结束后，阿克曼与麦当劳高管进行了会面。

<!--en-->
But the company might actually be giving the proposals a sympathetic hearing. Mr. Ackman and *McDonald's* executives met after one of the company's periodic meetings with analysts and investors last week.

“我们非常看重麦当劳——包括公司本身、品牌以及管理层，”阿克曼在邮件中表示，“管理层以股东价值为导向的举措尤其令我们鼓舞。简而言之，我们简直爱死它了！”

<!--en-->
"We have a very high regard for *McDonald's* -- the company, the brand, and the management," Mr. Ackman says in an email. "We are particularly encouraged by management's shareholder-value focused agenda. Bottom line, we're lovin' it!"

“麦当劳始终在寻求进一步提升股东价值的方法，”公司投资者关系副总裁玛丽·凯·肖在邮件中称。

<!--en-->
"*McDonald's* is always looking for ways to further increase shareholder value," says Mary Kay Shaw, the company's vice president of investor relations, in an email.

阿克曼此前曾与麦当劳接触。1997年末至1998年间，他向麦当劳的一名董事及包括现任首席财务官马修·保罗在内的一些高管提交了提议。根据阿克曼于1999年3月写给对冲基金投资者的信函，麦当劳对此颇感兴趣，甚至聘请了格林希尔咨询公司来分析各业务板块的价值。但随后股价自行强劲上涨，采取行动的紧迫性便随之减弱。

<!--en-->
Mr. Ackman has met with *McDonald's* before. In late 1997 and 1998, he presented his proposals to a *McDonald's* director and some executives, including Matthew Paull, now chief financial officer. *McDonald's* was intrigued enough to hire boutique investment firm Greenhill & Co. to analyze the divisions' value, according to a letter Mr. Ackman wrote to his hedge-fund investors in March 1999. But the stock rose strongly on its own and the urgency to do something faded.

此后，麦当劳已蜕变为一家截然不同的公司，尤其是过去两年间。公司缩减了扩张计划，更加重视股东利益，削减资本开支，并通过提高股息和股票回购向股东回馈资金。它刚刚宣布将部分分拆旗下子公司——墨西哥风味连锁餐厅Chipotle。然而，这些举措仍未使公司达到最高效状态：回购股票意味着公司拥有了更多资产，其中包括那些盈利能力较弱的餐厅运营商。

<!--en-->
Since then, *McDonald's* has become a dramatically different company, especially in the past two years. It pulled back on its growth plans and became more shareholder-focused, cutting capital expenditures and returning money to shareholders with increased dividends and stock repurchases. It just announced it would partially spin off one of its subsidiaries, the Chipotle Mexican food chain. But these initiatives haven't made the company as efficient as possible. Buying back stock increases its ownership of everything, including the less-profitable restaurant operator.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资”课程：阿克曼先生有着激进的股东维权记录。他持有温迪餐厅10%的股份，起初该公司拒绝了他关于分拆旗下Tim Hortons甜甜圈业务的要求。由于他的持股比例足以触发信息披露义务，他便通过公开信向管理层施压。温迪餐厅最近采纳了他的建议，其股价也随之上涨。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Mr. Ackman has a track record of fast-food activism. Wendy's, in which he has a 10% stake, initially resisted his calls that the company spin off its Tim Horton's doughnut division. In that case, his position was big enough to require public disclosure, and he pressured management with public letters. Wendy's just recently took his suggestion, and its stock is up.

他对麦当劳并未采取类似举措，这表明他认为麦当劳管理层更易沟通。这可能是因为麦当劳股价目前比上世纪90年代末的峰值低了约25%。不过该公司现在的价值其实更高：现金流有所改善，房地产资产也增值了。当然，这正是杠杆收购公司或潜在收购方所看重的。

<!--en-->
He hasn't taken those steps with *McDonald's*, a signal that he perceives management as more receptive. That may be because the stock is roughly 25% lower than where it was at its peak in the late 1990s. But the company is worth even more now: Cash flow has improved and the real-estate portfolio has appreciated. Of course that happens to be what leveraged buyout firms or potential acquirers hunt for.

这意味着麦当劳可能必须更加重视股东利益，否则就有被收购的风险。阿克曼的行动已经引发了猜测：大型房地产投资公司Vornado Realty Trust可能会试图收购麦当劳的土地。仅仅是这种可能性就对麦当劳构成了压力。

<!--en-->
That means *McDonald's* may have to become even more shareholder-friendly or risk becoming takeover bait. Already, Mr. Ackman's play has prompted speculation that **Vornado Realty Trust**, the big real-estate investment company, will make some sort of bid to get a hold of *McDonald's* land. Just the possibility puts pressure on *McDonald's*.

阿克曼的提议让人想起1986年可口可乐的分拆案：当时公司将盈利能力惊人的糖浆业务与需要大量资本支出的瓶装业务分开。这一举措创造了巨大的股东价值，但部分原因在于瓶装商被视作独立公司这一会计上的错觉。可口可乐最初只出售了瓶装业务49%的股份，实际上多年来仍对其拥有控制权。

<!--en-->
Mr. Ackman's proposals are reminiscent of the split that Coca-Cola underwent in 1986, when it divided its syrup business, which had astonishing profitability, from its bottling operation, which demanded heavy capital spending. That created immense shareholder value, but was, in part, built on an accounting illusion that the bottler was an independent company. Coke initially sold only 49% of the bottling operation and, effectively, still controlled it for years.

无论如何，阿克曼确实玩了一招妙棋：他管理的基金规模仅为13亿美元，却成功增持了麦当劳股份。对于单一基金而言，这一持股比例过于集中，因此上个月他邀请投资者将资金投入一个专门投资于单只股票的特殊独立基金——他起初并未透露该股票名称。三天内他便筹集了约2.5亿美元。加上从其主要基金中调拨的约1.5亿美元，他共购买了6200万股股票及期权；据知情人士称，若这些期权全部行权，他的持仓价值将达到20亿美元。

<!--en-->
If nothing else, Mr. Ackman has pulled off a neat trick: He eked out his stake while only having $1.3 billion under management in his funds. The stake would be too much concentration for one fund, so last month, he invited his investors to put money into a special separate fund to invest solely in a single stock, the name of which he didn't disclose initially. He raised about $250 million in three days. Along with about $150 million from his main fund, he bought 62 million shares and options that, if fully exercised, would bring his stake to the full $2 billion, says a person familiar with the matter.

对冲基金的批评者常诟病它们为伺机而动的秃鹫，只图短期利益。但阿克曼自1997年便开始从事此类活动。现在我们将看到他最终能否收获一份“开心餐”。

<!--en-->
Critics of hedge funds deride them as vultures that swoop in for short-term feasts. But Mr. Ackman has been at this since 1997. And now we will see whether he ends up with a happy meal.

**致信**Jesse Eisinger，邮箱：longandshort@wsj.com³。

<!--en-->
**Write to** Jesse Eisinger at longandshort@wsj.com³.

因此，或许存在一种在不影响运营的情况下提取现金的机会。然而一旦不再拥有这些房地产，公司就需按市场租金支付费用，因此必须对此进行调整，以计算实际净收益。这便是今日报纸上的相关内容。

<!--en-->
So there might be an opportunity to take out the cash without effecting operations. However, once you do not own the real estate anymore, you start paying market rates of rent so you have to adjust for that and see what the net gain is. So that was in the paper today.

《华尔街日报》紧接其下的下一篇文章是关于美国运通分拆的报道。

<!--en-->
The next article in the Wall Street Journal right under that is an article on the *American Express* spin-off.

《美国运通分拆必须证明自身能创造更多价值》  
作者：ERICA COPULSKY，《华尔街日报》记者  
2005年9月28日；C1版  
在整个1990年代，美国运通财务顾问公司一直是美国运通帝国的王牌业务。

<!--en-->
American Express Spin-off Must Prove It Can Create More Value On Its Own
**By ERICA COPULSKY Staff Reporter of THE WALL STREET JOURNAL September 28, 2005; Page C1**
Throughout much of the 1990s, American Express Financial Advisors was the crown jewel of the **American Express** Co. empire.

一度，这家总部位于明尼阿波利斯的理财规划部门贡献了高达40%的利润，而当时美国运通正努力改造其表现不佳的信用卡业务及小型国际银行。

<!--en-->
At one point, the Minneapolis-based financial-planning unit contributed as much as 40% of profit while American Express struggled to revamp its sagging charge-card business and small international bank.

但近年来，该部门却成了美国运通的薄弱环节，而该公司的标志性信用卡、旅游相关服务及支付处理业务却利润丰厚。雪上加霜的是，该部门还因被州监管机构指控欺诈客户——即向顾问提供未公开的激励措施以推销表现糟糕的内部基金——而蒙受公关危机；最终该部门同意向新罕布什尔州支付740万美元以解决相关指控。

<!--en-->
But more recently, the unit has been the weak link at American Express, whose signature card, travel-related services and processing businesses are highly profitable. Compounding its problems, the unit sustained a public-relations black eye when state regulators alleged that it defrauded customers by giving its advisers undisclosed incentives to push its poorly performing, in-house funds; the unit agreed to pay $7.4 million to New Hampshire to resolve the allegations.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资”课程：如今，原美国运通财务顾问公司更名为Ameriprise Financial Inc.，即将被分拆给美国运通股东。该公司的挑战在于说服投资者：它有能力独立创造更多价值。周五，美国运通股东每持有5股美国运通股票将获得1股Ameriprise股票，这些股票将于周一在纽约证券交易所上市交易，股票代码为AMP。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Now that Ameriprise Financial Inc., the new name for American Express Financial Advisors, is about to be spun off to American Express shareholders, its challenge is to convince investors that the business can create more value on its own. On Friday, AmEx shareholders are to receive one Ameriprise share for every five American Express shares they hold, and the shares will begin trading Monday on the New York Stock Exchange, using the stock symbol AMP.

Ameriprise寄希望于通过深耕其三十年前以Investors Diversified Services之名开创的财务规划业务来脱颖而出。该公司于1984年被美国运通收购。Ameriprise管理着约4000亿美元的资产，拥有超过10,500名财务顾问，客户数量达250万。它面临着富达投资（Fidelity Investments）、**嘉信理财**（Charles Schwab）Corp.以及**美林证券**（Merrill Lynch & Co.）等竞争对手的挑战。该公司希望通过为即将退休的富裕婴儿潮一代提供一站式财务规划服务来实现差异化。

<!--en-->
Ameriprise is betting it can distinguish itself by building on the financial-planning business it helped pioneer three decades ago under the name Investors Diversified Services, before it was acquired by American Express in 1984. Ameriprise -- which manages roughly $400 billion, has a network of more than 10,500 financial advisers and boasts 2.5 million clients -- faces competition from the likes of Fidelity Investments, **Charles Schwab** Corp. and **Merrill Lynch & Co.** It hopes to differentiate itself by providing one-stop financial planning to affluent baby boomers approaching retirement.

“我们会全面考量客户的整体情况，”董事长兼首席执行官詹姆斯·克拉奇奥洛表示。“通过在全面的财务规划框架下提供投资与保险产品组合，我们不仅能帮助客户增值资产，还能保护他们的财富。”Ameriprise是为数不多能提供从共同基金到年金、人寿保险等一系列产品的财务顾问公司之一。其持证财务规划师的数量也超过了所有竞争对手。该公司的目标客户群体是那些拥有10万美元至100万美元可投资资产的约2900万户美国家庭，即所谓的中高收入阶层。

<!--en-->
"We look at a client's whole picture," Chairman and Chief Executive James Cracchiolo said. "By offering a combination of investment and insurance products, within the context of a comprehensive financial plan, we help our clients not only grow but protect their assets." Ameriprise is one of the few financial-advisory firms to offer an array of products, ranging from mutual funds to annuities to life-insurance products. It has more certified financial planners than any of its rivals. And it is targeting the mass affluent -- the roughly 29 million U.S. households with $100,000 to $1 million in assets to invest.

不过，并非华尔街所有人对此都深信不疑。“该公司并未向分析师和投资者清晰披露不同产品间的盈利构成。这增加了理解公司业务模式以及股本回报率提升来源的难度，”摩根士丹利的保险行业分析师奈杰尔·达利指出。达利尚未对该股给出评级，其所在公司也与Ameriprise没有银行业务往来。

<!--en-->
So far, not everyone on Wall Street is convinced. "The company hasn't been transparent with analysts and investors on the earnings breakdown between different products. This is adding to the complexity of understanding the company's story and where the return on equity improvement will likely emerge," said Nigel Dally, an insurance analyst at Morgan Stanley. Mr. Dally doesn't yet have a rating on the stock and his firm doesn't have a banking relationship with Ameriprise.

在本月早些时候面向分析师的演示中，Ameriprise将其两大业务部门定义为资产积累业务和保护业务：前者占2004年盈利的61%，后者占39%。但许多分析师认为Ameriprise实际上是一家披着金融顾问外衣的保险公司。据Fox-Pitt Kelton的分析师约翰·纳德尔称，资产积累业务近一半的盈利来自固定及可变年金——这类产品结合了投资与保险功能。根据他的分析，保险和年金产品贡献了该公司约70%的盈利。

<!--en-->
In a presentation to analysts earlier this month, Ameriprise defined its two operating units as asset accumulation, accounting for 61% of 2004 earnings, and protection, accounting for 39%. But many analysts view Ameriprise as an insurance company in disguise. According to John Nadel, an analyst at Fox-Pitt Kelton, nearly half of the earnings of the asset-accumulation business come from fixed and variable annuities, products that combine investments with insurance. Based on his analysis, insurance and annuity products generate about 70% of the company's earnings.

华尔街已经提前窥见了Ameriprise可能的估值水平。9月15日，Ameriprise在“预发行”市场中的交易价格为38.02美元；在该市场中，投资者可以在证券正式发行前进行交易。尽管该股随后跌至37.25美元——昨日下午4点在纽约证券交易所的综合交易中下跌了50美分——但相对于部分分析师的预估而言，这一价格仍显得偏高。由于交易量相对清淡，一些分析师认为当前价格并不能准确反映该股正式上市后的估值。

<!--en-->
Wall Street already has gotten a sneak preview of how Ameriprise may be valued. On Sept. 15, Ameriprise began trading at $38.02 in the "when-issued" market, where investors can buy and sell securities before they have been issued in the primary market. Although the stock has since fallen to $37.25, down 50 cents yesterday at 4 p.m. in Big Board composite trading, it still appears to be a rich price relative to some analysts' estimates. Because trading has been relatively thin, some analysts argue that the current price isn't a good indication of how the stock will be valued when it begins officially trading.

“基于我们的基本面估值结果以及美国运通股东可能带来的短期抛压因素，我们认为该股的合理交易区间应在每股31美元至34美元之间，”尚未对该股给出评级的Fox-Pitt Kelton分析师纳德尔表示。

<!--en-->
"Based on our fundamental valuation work as well as the potential near-term selling pressure from American Express stockholders, we believe the stock should trade between $31 and $34 a share," says Mr. Nadel of Fox-Pitt Kelton, who doesn't yet have a rating on the stock.

一个重大的不确定因素是：持有大量美国运通股票的投资者在获得Ameriprise股票后是否会抛售它们。目前，美国运通的大部分股份由注重增长的投资者持有，而这类投资者可能不太愿意持有Ameriprise——后者通常被认为会更吸引注重价值的投资者。

<!--en-->
One big unknown is whether investors who own big chunks of American Express stock will dump Ameriprise once they receive the shares. Currently, a large portion of American Express shares are held by growth-oriented investors, who may be less inclined to own Ameriprise, which is generally expected to attract more value-oriented investors.

公平地说，美国运通的最大股东正是著名的价值投资者沃伦·巴菲特。巴菲特的**伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司**持有约12%的美国运通股份；他是否在分拆后继续持有Ameriprise，必将影响华尔街的判断。巴菲特拒绝就此发表评论。

<!--en-->
To be fair, AmEx's largest shareholder is one of the best-known value investors, Warren Buffett. Mr. Buffett's **Berkshire Hathaway** owns roughly 12% of American Express shares and whether he intends to stick with Ameriprise after the spin-off is certain to affect Wall Street's thinking. Mr. Buffett declined to comment.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程本周早些时候，标准普尔公司宣布Ameriprise将于9月30日收盘后被纳入其重要的标普500指数。这一举措消除了指数基金因需抛售该股而可能带来的短期压力。不过，Ameriprise被纳入标普500指数或许会让那些指望借此机会低价买入该股的一些投资者感到失望。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
At least one potential overhang on Ameriprise shares was lifted earlier this week when Standard & Poor's Corp. said Ameriprise would be added to its flagship S&P 500 Index at the close of trading Sept. 30. The move eliminates the possible near-term pressure on the stock by index funds that would have been required to sell their shares. However, Ameriprise's inclusion to the S&P 500 Index may have disappointed some investors hoping the selling pressure would enable them to buy the stock on the cheap.

“如果股价跌至34美元以下，投资者就应当考虑买入，因为该股的下行空间有限，而如果管理层能够成功提升股本回报率，其上行潜力将非常可观，”Fox-Pitt的纳德尔说道。

<!--en-->
"If the stock falls below $34, then investors should want to own it because the downside in the stock is limited and the upside could be very attractive if management could execute on improving the company's return on equity," Fox-Pitt's Mr. Nadel said.

目前，Ameriprise的股本回报率为9%至10%。公司管理层设定的目标是将股本回报率提升至12%至15%。

<!--en-->
Ameriprise's return on equity is currently 9% to 10%. Management is targeting a return on equity of 12% to 15%.

为了实现这一目标，管理层计划推出新产品，通过投资销售和能力基础设施来重新聚焦机构资产管理业务的拓展，并通过银行和经纪公司等第三方渠道扩大共同基金和年金产品的分销。不过，分析师指出，该公司的未来增长很大程度上取决于其能否持续提升旗下共同基金的业绩。

<!--en-->
To accomplish that goal, management plans to roll out new products, refocus on expanding the institutional asset-management business by investing in sales and capabilities infrastructure, and expand distribution of mutual fund and annuity products through third-party channels such as banks and brokerage firms. However, analysts say the company's future growth depends largely on whether it can continue to improve the performance of its in-house mutual funds.

虽然已有好转迹象，但资金仍在持续流出。根据加州阿卡塔的AMG Data Services数据，今年迄今为止，投资者已从美国运通的股票和债券共同基金中撤出70亿美元。目前这些股票和债券基金管理的资产规模约为555亿美元。晨星公司分析师拉塞尔·金内尔表示，尽管整个公司的共同基金业绩有所改善，但并不突出。根据晨星的数据，过去三年中，按资产加权计算，这些基金的表现逊于65%的同类基金。

<!--en-->
While there are signs of a turnaround, money is still walking out the door. So far this year, investors have pulled $7 billion out of American Express stock and bond mutual funds, according to AMG Data Services in Arcata, Calif. The stock and bond funds now have roughly $55.5 billion in assets. Overall firm wide mutual-fund performance has improved but isn't striking, says Russel Kinnel, a Morningstar Inc. analyst. On average, the funds did worse than 65% of similar funds over the past three years on an asset-weighted basis, according to Morningstar.

分析师们也担心，失去美国运通这一在金融服务行业极具知名度的品牌后，公司业务将如何发展。

<!--en-->
Analysts also are concerned about how the business will fare without the American Express name, one of the most highly recognized in the financial-services industry.

尽管存在这些风险，仍有几位投资者认为该股是值得投资的对象，因为其中蕴含价值有待挖掘。T. Rowe Price Group Inc.的金融服务分析师凯尔·塞尔米纳拉认为：“Ameriprise被视为一只相对便宜且具备提升股本回报率潜力的股票。”

<!--en-->
Despite these risks, several investors believe the stock is a good investment because there is value to extract. As Kyle Cerminara, a financial-services analyst at T. Rowe Price Group Inc., sees it: "Ameriprise is viewed as a relatively inexpensive stock that has potential for [return on equity] improvement."

**请写信给**Erica Copulsky，邮箱：erica.copulsky@wsj.com¹ 如今，*AXP*正在分拆Amer. Fin. Advisors业务，该业务此前一直管理不善。同时，独立的信用卡业务也将被剥离，这是一项拥有高股本回报率、良好市场地位及广阔发展前景的优秀业务，今后将独立交易。人们可能会说：“唉，这谁都知道，并非什么鲜为人知的情况。”

<!--en-->
**Write to** Erica Copulsky at erica.copulsky@wsj.com¹
Now *AXP* is spinning off the Amer. Fin. Advisors which has been an under managed business. It also unleashes the stand alone charge card business which is a great franchise with high ROE, good market position, good growth prospects and things of that nature. So that will trade on its own. People might say, gee, everyone knows about this. It is not obscure situation.

接下来我想详细介绍一下我书中提到的案例。封面页列出了可用于案例分析的分拆案例。你们的第一个任务是：提交一份一页纸的分析报告并附上支撑材料。请阐述你的投资逻辑。如果你经过研究后发现该公司并不便宜，那就展示你的估值过程。我希望看到你选择这家公司的初衷及研究发现。你们需要进行可比公司分析以及对未来盈利的绝对分析，估值等内容则写在背面。我想看到你们的工作成果，我不希望只看到市盈率或市销率这些数据。

<!--en-->
Now I thought I would hand out more detail on the cases that were in my book. On the front are spin-offs that you can use for your cases. Your first assignment: I am expecting a one page write-up with backup. Give me the investment thesis. If you did the work and you find that the company is not cheap, then show your valuation work. I want to see the original thesis as to why you chose this company. What you find out. You will do your comparable analysis, you will do your absolute analysis of what you think earnings will be. Valuation and things like that on the back. I want to see your work. I don't want to see P/E and Price/Sales.

本次练习的一部分是反馈我的评语。这节课之后你们只剩两节课，随后便是假期。下周我会分发一些我认为非常出色的分析报告。

<!--en-->
Part of the exercise is to get my comments back. You only have two more classes after this and then there is a vacation. Next week I will hand out some write-ups that I thought was very good.

你们面前的是一份待分拆公司的清单。下一页是*Sears*的案例。先阅读有关*Sears*的内容，然后我们再讨论。

<!--en-->
What you have in front of you is a list of pending spin-offs. The next page is the *Sear's* example. Just read about *Sear's* and then we will discuss it.

关于*Sears*分拆的讨论：*All State*和*Dean Witter*的分拆。这一想法由迈克尔·普莱斯在《巴伦周刊》中提及。分拆将于4月或5月进行，尽管我自称擅长捕捉特殊机会，却完全错过了它。*Sears*将分拆出80%的Dean Witter股份。5月5日的《巴伦周刊》刊登了关于迈克尔·普莱斯的文章。

<!--en-->
Discussion of *Sear's* Spin off. Spin off of *All State* and *Dean Witter*. This idea was explained by Michael Price in Barron's. This comes out in April or May but I completely missed it despite being a special situationguy. *Sear's* will spin off 80% of Dean Witter. Then the July 5th issue of Barron's because I read an article on Michael Price.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊机会投资课程指出，*Sears*股价54美元显然被严重低估。这54美元中包含1股*All State*股票；因此，每持有1股Sears股票，可获价值28美元的*All State*股票和15美元的DW股票，剩余仅11美元归于*Sears*本身。再扣除用于Coldwell Banker的2-3美元以及用于*Sears*墨西哥业务的3美元后，留给*Sears*的市值仅为5美元。而其销售额高达270亿美元，市值却只有15亿美元——简直太便宜了！

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
*Sear's* at $54 seems valued much too low. That $54 includes 1 share of *All State* so for 1 share of Sear you get $28 worth of *All State* and $15 worth of DW so that leaves $11 for *Sears* then take out $2 or $3 for Coldwell Banker and $3 for *Sears* Mexico and it leaves $5 for *Sears*. A market cap of $1.5 billion with $27 billion in sales. CHEAP!

该公司没有债务，因此销售额的回报率达到6%。那么可比公司的情况如何呢？我翻到*J.C. Penny*的相关内容。让我将其与另一家表现不佳的零售商——*J.C. Penny*进行比较。JC是我能找到的最接近的参照对象。当时我们使用的是纸质资料（那时还没有互联网），经计算，其销售额的变现比例仅为60美分。

<!--en-->
There is no debt here. So you get 6% on the dollar for sales. What does a comparable look like? So I turn the page on *J.C. Penny*. So let me compare it to another crummy retailer—*J.C. Penny*. JC was the closest I could find. I used the tear sheet—we didn't use the Internet in those days—and if I go through the math is trading at 60 cents on the dollar for sales.

*Sears*的销售额变现比例为6美分，而*J.C. Penny*则为60美分；此外，从利润率、盈利等角度对比，两者也较为接近。这足以作为说明价格差异的良好指标。接下来我做了什么？这一切都是由迈克尔·普莱斯为我铺好的道路。

<!--en-->
*Sears* is 6 cents on sales versus *J.C. Penny* which is at 60 cents on the dollar of sales while also going through other comparables such as margins, earnings, etc. Everything was pretty close. This was as good a metric to use to show the disparity in prices. So what did I do next? This is all laid out for me by *Michael Price*.

我发现*Sears*与*J.C. Penny*的估值相差十倍之多。你们猜我接下来做了什么？我在接下来的两周内尽可能多地买入。这篇文章发表后，他们开始发行股票，我便趁机大量购入迈克尔·普莱斯所提及的股票。实际上，我以5美元的价格“创造”出了原本价值50美元的*Sears*，其中的差距实在巨大。

<!--en-->
I am looking at a ten times difference in valuation from *Sears* to *J.C. Penny*. What did you think I did next? I bought as much as I could over the next two weeks. I did this after the article after they were giving out the shares. I bought as much as I wanted at the stocks Michael Price was speaking about. I effectively created *Sears* for $5 which could have been worth $50. The gap was huge.

他们分拆出*All State*之后发生了什么？*Sears*的股价涨到了30美元，我们就在那时卖掉了大部分股票；两个月后股价又涨到了50美元。这怎么可能呢？

<!--en-->
What happened after they spun out *All State*? The *Sears* went up to $30 where we sold most of our stock and two months later it went to $50. How can that be?

我错过了这次机会，而*Mike Price*为我详细解释了来龙去脉，我居然还能买入。这怎么可能呢？这些可都是知名公司啊。当时有10位分析师跟踪*Sears*的情况。我有点困惑：看来零售行业分析师并不涵盖保险公司和经纪公司领域，导致信息被遗漏了。

<!--en-->
I missed it and *Mike Price* lays it all out for me and I am still able to buy it. How can that be? These are well-known companies. There were 10 analysts who were following *Sears*. I am a little baffled. I guess the retail analyst does not cover insurance and brokerage companies. Things fall through the cracks.

答案是我真的不知道。我只是告诉你这事确实发生了。你可能会说这很难理解；有时候确实如此，有时候则不然。这是十年前的一个特殊情况。你或许会说如今对冲基金众多，这种机会已不复存在，这在某种程度上或许属实，但过去五年里其实仍有不少机会。比如*American Express*正在分拆业务，也许分拆后的股票会遭到抛售。市场总是充满变数。即便机会不像这次这么明显，但肯定还会有其他机会。有效市场理论认为这种事不该发生。

<!--en-->
The answer is that I don't really know. I am just telling you that it happened. You can say it is so hard. Sometimes it is and sometimes it is not. It was a special situation over ten years ago. You may claim that there are so many hedge funds today that that opportunity would not exist and that may be to some extent be true yet there have been plenty of opportunities in the past five years. *American Express* is doing a spin off. Maybe the spin off gets beat up. Plenty of stuff goes on. Even if the opportunities are not as glaring as this one, but there will be others. The efficient market theory says this shouldn't happen.

类似的公司当时交易价格与*J.C. Penny*的水平相当，而非*Sears*的水平。

<!--en-->
Comparable things were trading at *J.C. Penny*'s level not at *Sear's* level.

有人说我写关于分拆的书是愚蠢之举，因为那样机会就会消失。我写完书一年后，分拆股的整体表现并不出色，但随后回报又回来了。

<!--en-->
People said I was an idiot to write the book on spin offs because then the opportunities would disappear. A year after I wrote the book, spin offs did not do particularly well in aggregate, but then the returns came back.

**关于分拆股，我的看法是：它们是寻找定价错误机会的沃土。**有时它们因受到过多关注而定价过高；有时则因抛售压力过大而定价过低。市场会出现错配与变动，奇怪的现象时有发生。*American Express*将来能够独立交易，人们才会看清它究竟是一家多优秀的公司。

<!--en-->
**What I say about spin offs: It is a fertile ground to find mis-priced opportunities.** Sometimes they are overpriced because too many people are following or sometimes the spin offs are under priced because of too much selling pressure. There is a dislocation and change. Weird stuff is happening. American Express will be able to trade on its own so people will see how good a business they really have.

我要指出的是市场中存在的惊人错配现象。几年前互联网泡沫时期，你可以以负36美元的价格买入包含*Palm*业务的*3Com*股票。为了好玩，我们做了空*Palm*、做多*3Com*的交易。

<!--en-->
I am pointing out the amazing dislocations you could have. A few years ago during the Internet bubble you could own *3Com*, which was inclusive of *Palm*, at a negative $36 dollars. For fun, we shorted *Palm* against *3Com*.

有问题吗？我没有任何答案，只能说世事难料，值得去观察。我们并未持有任何*Wal-Mart*股票，但我们正在关注。有人问我何时该买入分拆股：该等两个月，还是立刻入手？我没有固定公式，而是独立分析每种情况。幸好没有所谓的“万能公式”。

<!--en-->
Questions? I don't have any answers but to say stuff happens and it is worthwhile to look. We don't own any *Wal-Mart* but we are looking. People ask me when they should buy spin offs. Should you wait two months, should you buy right away? I don't use a formula. I analyze each situation independently. Luckily there is no magic formula.

也许被分拆的公司规模较小，因此机构投资者不感兴趣。大盘股在5到7年间股价并无变动，但盈利却有所提升。

<!--en-->
Perhaps the company being spun off is small so the institutions won't want it. The large caps have not moved in 5 to 7 years but the earnings have moved up.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：我们最糟糕的年份是1998年至1999年，随后在2000年获得了100%的回报。当情况看似显而易见时，往往会有意外发生。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Our worst years were 1998 to 1999 then we made 100% in 2000. When things look obvious, things happen.

看看价值投资者俱乐部网站上你应提交的应用案例吧。

<!--en-->
Look at the application on the value investors club for things you should present.

请翻到第12页，了解*Viacom*收购*Paramount Communications*的案例。基本上，竞标获胜者没钱支付，于是*Viacom*向股东支付了大量纸质凭证作为补偿。

<!--en-->
Go to page 12 *Viacom's* purchase of *Paramount Communications*. Basically, the winner of the bid ran out of money so *Viacom* offered lots of paper to its shareholders as payment.

如果你是一名机构投资者，拿到这些东西后会怎么做？你会卖掉它们。机构投资者不会去研究*或有价值权利（CVRs）*。最终会导致抛售潮。我以前从未见过CVR或认股权证。

<!--en-->
So if you are an institutional investor and you get all this stuff what do you think is going to happen when you get this? You will sell it. Institutional investors won't pay read about *Contingent Value Rights (CVRs)*. There will be a fire sale. I hadn't seen a CVR or what the warrants were.

请绘制出你能获得的各种价值组合图表。

<!--en-->
Diagram the combinations of values you can obtain.

我们持有一份行权价为6美元、为期三年的认股权证。他们借了大量资金，因此*Viacom*的股权相当于一次杠杆收购。由于杠杆率很高，这些认股权证或许有价值。

<!--en-->
We have a three year warrant struck at $6. They had borrowed a ton of money so the equity stake of *Viacom* was like a leveraged buy out. There is a lot of leverage here so these warrants may be worth something.

可交换可转换债券本质上属于垃圾债，但其面值仅为60美分，我却可以用它们来购买有价值的资产。我需要凑齐价值70美元的债券：70美元×0.60=42美元，用于购买五年期认股权证。我的成本降低了40%。这些次级债券的面值超过10亿美元。

<!--en-->
The exchangeable convertible debentures are basically junk but they were worth 60 cents on the dollar but I can use them as money to buy something of worth. I had to come up with $70 worth of debentures. $70 x 0.60 = $42 for five year warrants. I lowered my cost by 40%. These subordinated debentures have over $1 billion in face value.

让债券可用于换取认股权证，使得认股权证更有价值。*Viacom*只是没钱了，所以才发行了这种可交换凭证。

<!--en-->
Making the debentures available for the warrants made the warrants more valuable. *Viacom* simply ran out of money so they created exchangeable paper.

每当你看到任何略显复杂的事物时，试着从宏观角度去理解它。市场认为*Viacom*为*Paramount*支付了过高价格；而我的看法如下：

<!--en-->
Any time you see anything remotely complicated try to take the big picture view of it. The market looked at *Viacom* as if it way overpaid for *Paramount*. The way I looked at it was like this:

他们只用了一半现金支付，其余部分则用垃圾债券偿付。如果他们没付现金，从信用角度来看我并不在乎是否溢价支付；剩下的部分他们用垃圾债券支付。而我正好排在下一顺位。

<!--en-->
They only paid half of it in cash and the rest of it with junk. If they didn't lay out cash then I don't care if they overpaid from a credit worthy standpoint. The rest they paid in junk. I was next in line.

我在*MGM*也赚了不少钱，因为*Turner*一半用现金支付，一半用票据支付。他收购了一个电影库，因此节目制作成本很低。接下来我们来看看*Host-Marriot*。总体来看：没人喜欢杠杆率过高的Host Marriot。我认为有吸引力的点是：其股权价值为4亿美元，债务为26亿美元，总价值达30亿美元。这些债务对母公司而言是无追索权的。在4亿美元的债务中，有3亿美元仅涉及旧金山Marriot酒店。20亿美元的债务由子公司担保，而非母公司。

<!--en-->
I also made a lot of money in *MGM* because *Turner* paid half in cash and half in paper. He bought a film library so he had low programming costs.
Next we will look at *Host-Marriot*.
The big picture here: No one likes the over levered Host Marriot. What I thought was potentially attractive: there is $400 million in equity with $2.6 billion in debt so $3 billion in value. The debt was non-recourse to the parent. Of the $400 million in debt $300 million was only on the San Francisco Marriot. $2 billion guaranteed by the subsidiary and not the parent.

$$ \$700 \text{ million} - \$100 \text{ debt} = \$600 \text{ million.} $$

这是一笔风险收益比不错的投资。这是一笔杠杆投资。Host的股票价格为每股4美元，但对应母公司的价值却达到每股6美元。学校里可不会教你如何去关注这类机会。这是一笔风险收益比良好的交易：我花费4美元就能获得价值6美元的资产，且无需承担债务，还有上涨空间。

<!--en-->
This was a good risk reward. This was a leveraged bet. $4 per share for Host but worth $6 per share of the Parent. There is nothing you can learn at school that says to go look at this stuff. This was a good risk reward where I lay out $4 for 6 value with no debt and some upside.

我不必做到事必躬亲。如果我有一个投资逻辑并且它持续成立，就继续下去；否则就放弃。我不在乎自己没做的事，只在乎实际做了什么。你只需等待合适的时机即可。

<!--en-->
I don't have to get to that point where I do a lot of work. If I have a thesis and it keeps holding up, you keep going or if not then drop it. I don't care what I don't do but what I actually do do. You wait for your pitch.

为自己工作的好处就是你可以无所事事。

<!--en-->
The good thing about working for yourself is that you can sit on your hands.

估值工作永远不会白费。涉足的行业越多，你的能力圈就越广。关键在于做好估值工作并保持纪律。关键在于以何种视角看待世界。重要的是把分内之事做好。我不在乎自己错过了什么。

<!--en-->
The valuation work is never wasted. The broader your circle of competence from doing different industries the better. The key is doing good valuation work and having the discipline. The key is what context to look at the world. What matters is doing well what you do. I don't care about what I missed.

第17节：乔尔·格林布拉特：我想看看你们的报告。总体而言，作为初次尝试，它们写得很好。不过从宏观角度来看，我希望看到更简洁的陈述。

<!--en-->
Track 17: Joel Greenblatt: I want to go over your papers. In general for a first attempt they were very good. I guess big, big picture, I would like a more concise pitch.

我读过一篇关于比尔·米勒的文章，他负责管理莱格梅森基金，他的业绩非常出色，过去14到15年间一直跑赢市场。他是一位有趣的价值投资者，但他管理的资金规模高达数十亿美元。

<!--en-->
I read an article about Bill Miller who runs the Legg Mason funds, and he has done tremendously and he has beaten the market for the last 14 or 15 years. He is an interesting value investor but they run billions and billions of dollars.

他希望陈述能够简洁且快速。如果你能迅速概括自己的观点，那会对你很有帮助。这家公司目前不受青睐；它的盈利较少，但如果看其 normalized earnings（ normalized earnings 指经调整后的盈利），其交易价格仅为 normalized earnings 的5倍，而 ROIC 高达50%。他们正在关闭亏损的业务部门，因此人们才忽视它。人们如此看待它，而这正是情况会好转的原因。你应该能够简明扼要地说明这一点。

<!--en-->
He wants a pitch very concise and fast. It helps you if you can summarize your pitch very quickly. This company is trading –it is out of favor now; it is earning less money but if you look at normalized earnings it is trading at 5 times normalized earnings and ROIC are 50%, they are closing their money losing division so that is why people don't see it. People see it this way and that is why it will get better. You should be able to say it.

你应该能用几句话讲清楚你的陈述以及为何认为该股估值偏低，但随后我希望看到支撑依据。这对你理解自己为何买入或不买入某只股票是非常好的练习。或者说，这是我当时的想法，而结果如何。当你被指派分析某只股票时，难度会稍大一些，因为你可能没有强有力的论据。该股票看起来定价合理；经过对 normalized earnings 的分析，其价格处于合理区间。或者我无法预测 normalized earnings 的具体数值。如果你能选择*BBI*（Blockbuster）并说“我不知道其盈利会如何变化，所以我必须回避”，并给出三种情景：如果其中一种情景发生，我将损失惨重，而我尚不确定哪种情景会成真，那也行。

<!--en-->
You should be able to spit out the pitch and the valuation portion of why you think it is cheap in a few lines but then I want to see the back up. It is just very good practice for you to understand why you are or are not buying something. Or this is what I thought and this is how it turned out. It is a little harder when you are assigned something because you might not have a strong pitch on it. It looks fairly priced. I went through normalized earnings it comes out within the range of fairness. Or I can't predict what normalized is. If you can pick *BBI* (*Blockbuster*) and say I don't know where earnings are going to be so I have to stay away. Here are three scenarios and if it hits this one, I am going to lose a lot of money and I don't have a lot of confidence which one is going to hit yet.

顺便说一下，针对有人问布莱恩的问题：“你如何评估一家三年、五年后盈利将大幅下滑的公司？其实这不过是个折现现金流问题。你只需对未来的现金流做出假设，如果能以未来可收回现金总额的一半价格买入，那就会入手。这虽不是沃伦·巴菲特会选的类型，但如果你认为能收回那些钱，这就是一种赚钱方式。它并不复杂——你只是想弄清楚所购之物的价值，然后以远低于其价值的价格买入。这就是你的目标。

<!--en-->
In answer to the question which was asked of Brian, by the way, which is: "How do you value a company whose earnings are going to drop off a cliff in three years, five years or whatever? It is really nothing more than a discounted cash flow question. You make your assumptions about future cash flows and if you can buy it at half of all the cash you would collect, then you would buy it. It is not a Warren Buffett pick but it is a way to make money if you think you will collect that money. It is not super complicated—you are trying to figure out the thing you are buying—what is it worth and pay a lot less for it. That is what you are trying to do.

我回答大多数问题的方式是：如果我搞不清楚，就说我不知道。既然如此，我就没理由投资它。

<!--en-->
The way I answer most questions is that if I can't figure it out then I say I don't know. Then I have no business investing in that.

学生：您会如何看待BBI所使用的终值计算方式？哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程。JG：你知道吗？就我个人而言，我不会把事情搞得那么复杂。他们第一年、第二年……第八年能赚多少？然后算出这对我来说值多少钱。如果我现在支付5美元，8年后能收回10美元吗？其中一些钱可能明年就能到账，之后一年再收1美元。只要我能从所投资的资金中获得不错的内部收益率（IRR），那就挺好。谁会在乎第9年的收益呢？根据我的假设，那几乎可以忽略不计。我并非在寻求精确答案，我只是觉得：嘿，我认为它值10美元，而目前交易价只有5到6美元。我觉得这是个相当不错的赌注。

<!--en-->
Student: How would you think about the terminal value used for BBI?
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
JG: You know what? Me personally, I would not get that complicated. What are they going to earn in year 1, year 2, .......Year 8 and then figure out what that is worth to me. If I pay $5 now will I get $10 within 8 years. $ of the dollars could be next year and the following year I would receive $1. If I can make an IRR (internal rate of return) on the money I have invested that might look pretty good. A. who cares what I make in year 9 because it will be next to nothing based on my assumptions. I am not looking for exact answers. I am looking for—hey, I think it is going to be worth $10 and it is trading $5 to $6. I think that is a pretty good bet there.

埃里克关于风险套利的演讲。有人有问题吗？我认为很多人对我书中所述存在误解。切勿在家尝试此法。并非说这不是个好地方，但它不适合不花功夫的业余人士。

<!--en-->
Eric's presentation on Risk Arbitrage. Does anyone have any questions? I think many have misconceptions over what I wrote in the book. Don't try this at home. Not that it isn't a bad place to be but it isn't for amateurs who don't do a lot of work.

埃里克提到，套利空间非常微小。交易者投资的标的年化回报率仅为8%或略高于无风险利率。我从未从那个角度看待这类业务。我认为这正是其缺陷所在。我把这视为一门风险与回报并存的生意：我可能赚1美元，但也可能损失10美元，而且这一切可能在三个月内发生。许多人将其视为年化回报业务。其实年化回报更高的情况更常见——比如赚10美元而仅损失1美元。

<!--en-->
What Eric said is that spreads are so thin. Traders are investing in situations with 8% annualized returns or just above the risk free rate. I never looked at the business that way. And I think that is the flaw. I look at it as a risk reward business. I can make a dollar but I can lose $10 and all this happens in three months. A lot of people set it up as an annualized return business. One annualized return can be a lot better where you make ten and lose a dollar.

人们看待此事的角度有误，这一直是我的抱怨点。追逐回报的资金太多了。我认为眼下这并不特别有吸引力，因为普通的套利机会并不理想。当局势发生变化时，总会有有趣的机会出现。布莱恩刚刚谈到了好莱坞的收购战：最初出价14美元，后来降至10.25美元，这值得深思。如果你有坚定的估值观点且了解收购运作机制，就会发现其中涉及大量讨价还价和博弈论运用，买方试图压低价格。这里的激励因素是什么？CEO并未竭力要求降价，但买方仍感兴趣。他们并未放弃，并非因为业务毫无前景；否则他们可能不会再出现。

<!--en-->
People look at it the wrong way which was always my complaint. There is too much money chasing returns. I don't think it is particularly relevant right now because plain vanilla arbitrage is not too good. There are always interesting things when something is changing. Brian just went through the takeover battle for Hollywood. There was a $14 bid and it went down to $10.25, that is an interesting one to think about. If you have a strong valuation opinion and you understand how takeovers work, there is a lot of back of forth and game theory involved as the buyer tries to get a cheap price. What are the incentives here? The CEO is not trying too hard for them to cut the price and they still are interested. They didn't walk away because the business is going nowhere. They probably wouldn't show up again.

第18类资产：那里仍有许多机会，因此仍是肥沃的土壤。我们谈到过并购证券——有时会出现竞价过高或管理层试图将其私有化的情况，其间就有赚钱的机会。我并非说要完全忽视此类机会，而是说它属于一个特殊的领域。我最初写那本书并非针对MBA学员；当时我还没教过MBA课程。我虽为MBA水平的读者写了书，但我已有15年从业经验，所以并未意识到这一点。我其实是面向普通大众撰写的。

<!--en-->
Track 18: There is a lot of stuff going on there, so it is still fertile ground. And we talked about merger securities to look at sometimes there is overbidding or management is trying to take it private. There is a chance to make money along the way. I am not saying ignore this are completely. I am saying it is its own special area. I originally did not write that book for MBAs. I hadn't taught MBAs yet. I wrote the book for MBA level readers but I had been doing it for 15 years so I didn't realize that. I really meant for lay people.

## 对学生论文的评论

<!--en-->
*Comments on Students papers*

## 以下评论并无特定顺序，我只是浏览了论文并作了点评。请勿介意。不少人随意使用了12倍EBIT的倍数。我不会轻易采用这一数值；只有相当优秀的公司才能以12倍EBIT的价格交易，而他们却给出了很高的数字。实际上，目前交易价仅为该数值的一半。或许确实如此，但这个数字还是偏高。我们曾讨论过：10倍EBIT且抽成率为40%时，税后回报可达6%，这样的公司足以与政府担保的债券相媲美。若采用12倍EBIT，你必须对业务及其增长前景有十足把握。我不建议随意使用这些数字。的确有些公司值这个价甚至更高，但它们并不便宜！再次强调：如果难以确定正常化盈利水平，最好的办法就是转向你能分析的对象。如果你无法分析正常化盈利，那你根本一无所知。

<!--en-->
*This is in no particular order, I just went through the papers and made comments. Don't take it personally. I bunch of people slapped on a bunch of 12 x EBIT numbers. I would not do that lightly; it has to be a pretty good business to trade at 12 x EBIT and people threw out pretty high numbers. Well, it is trading at half that. That might be, but that is a pretty high number. We talked about 10 x EBIT with a 40% take rate is 6% after-tax return that is a pretty good business to trade off for a government guaranteed bond. To take 12 x EBIT you would want to be pretty certain of the business and the growth. I wouldn't throw those numbers around so lightly. There are certain business that are worth that or more than that but it ain't cheap! Once again if it is tough to know what normalized earnings are, the best thing is move on to something you can analyze. If you can't analyze normalize earnings then you don't have a clue.*

## 《如何向投资组合经理做汇报》——作者：比尔·米勒，Legg Mason公司的投资组合经理

<!--en-->
*How to Make Presentations to Portfolio Managers by Bill Miller, PM of Legg Mason*

BM：我想在你们的演示中强调一点：一旦进入资本市场，就会发现投资组合经理的注意力持续时间极短。**据我所知，没有哪位成功的投资组合经理愿意听超过九十（90）秒的故事。** 彼得·林奇曾规定：当高级分析师向他推荐股票时，他会启动一个90秒的计时器。分析师必须在90秒内完成陈述并离开。

<!--en-->
BM: I want to emphasize in your presentations that if you go into capital markets, you will realize that portfolio managers have ultra-short attention spans. **And there is basically no successful portfolio manager of my acquaintance who has ever wanted to hear a story longer than ninety (90) seconds.** Peter Lynch, when a senior analyst came into a pitch him a stock, would turn on an egg timer for 90 seconds. The analyst had to complete the presentation within 90 seconds and be out of there.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：如果你无法在这段时间内用有说服力的论据吸引投资组合经理的注意，他们就会认为你要么没有令人信服的理由，要么无法清晰表达，这时你就应该回去重新准备。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
If you can't get the portfolio manager's attention within that time with a convincing case then they will assume that you either don't have a convincing case or you are not able to articulate it, and you should go back and figure it out.

## 故事而非原子

<!--en-->
*Stories not Atoms*

世界是由故事构成的，而非原子。大多数人认为应该先分析原子及其组成部分，然后确定其价值并加以描述。另一种思路则是构建一个有说服力的故事——把所有资料整合起来，形成一个令人信服的叙述。

<!--en-->
The world is made of stories, not of atoms. Most people think of the world as analyzing atoms and its constituent parts, and then I am going to figure out how to value it and then describe it. The alternative way to think about it is to construct a convincing story. Take all your material together and construct a convincing story.

如果你与投资组合经理交谈，最好的开场白是：“我想和您谈谈*Homestore*（HOM）。它目前的价格为2.25美元。过去52周的价格区间为4美元至2美元，历史最高价出现在2000年，为100美元。我认为它值得买入，原因如下：”

<!--en-->
If you speak to a portfolio manager, the best thing to say is, "I want to talk to you about *Homestore* (HOM). It is at $2.25. The 52-week range is $4 to $2 and the all time high was $100 in 2000. I think it is a buy for the following five reasons:

1. 啪
2. 啪
3. 啪
4. 啪
5. 啪：该股目前交易价格约为2美元左右。我认为它的价值应为6美元或8美元。以下是我认为它值这个价的原因，以及相关的风险。说完即可。在演示中：正面观点不超过五个，负面观点不超过三个。说明其价值后便可结束。--

<!--en-->
1. Bam
2. Bam
3. Bam
4. Bam
5. Bam
The stock is trading a $2 and change. I think it is worth $6 or $8 or whatever. Here is why I think it is worth that. Here are the risks. Then you are done.
In the presentations: no more than five positive points and three negative points. What is it worth and then you are done.
--

## *琳达·格林布拉特关于零售股投资的演讲。*

<!--en-->
*Linda Greenblatt Presentation on investing in retail stocks.*

*乔尔·格林布拉特（“JG”）：*在她发言前，先给大家介绍一下背景：琳达专注于一个领域——**消费品和零售业**。她在该领域已有10年经验，平均年化收益率高达20%以上。她在自己熟悉的细分市场中找到了大量机会。她的收益波动并不比其他专注型投资者更大。她凭借对自己所熟悉领域的深入研究取得了惊人回报。这对你们而言是个很好的启示：不一定要局限于零售业，但必须是你理解的行业。她选择了自己真正*感兴趣*的领域——这非常重要。

<!--en-->
*Joel Greenblatt ("JG"):* Before she speaks, just to give you a context, Linda sticks to one area: **consumer products and retail.** She has been in that area for 10 years and has averaged high 20's percent returns staying in that little niche that she knows well. She finds enough opportunities in that one area. Her returns have been no more volatile than other concentrated investors. She has phenomenal returns focusing on what she knows. There is a great lesson for you. It doesn't have to be retail but an industry that you understand. She picked something she really *enjoys*--that is a very important lesson.

课前有不少人来找我，说他们打算加入大公司，担心自己会被局限在某个领域。或许确实如此，但要想真正精通某个领域并仍能获得丰厚利润，这是完全可行的。随着长期投资经验的积累，你会逐渐了解更多领域。能够*精通一个领域*已经非常了不起。

<!--en-->
A number of people have come up to me before class and said they will join a big firm and they are afraid they will be pigeon holed. That may be true but to really learn an area very well and still be very profitable. As you invest over a long period of time you will come to know more areas. Knowing *one area well* is tremendous.

她将谈论她正在研究的领域……

<!--en-->
She will talk about areas she is working on......

## *一个来自长岛的女孩为何会涉足零售业？*

<!--en-->
*What is a girl from Long Island doing in retail?*

*琳达·格林布拉特（“LG”）：*那么，一个来自长岛的女孩为何会涉足零售业呢？选择一个你能够深入了解且感兴趣的领域。**我喜欢购物。**这绝对是我必须深入研究的领域。你会开始察觉到其中的*规律*。经过十年的观察，你能掌握某个行业群体的交易模式，这比那些初次接触股票、毫无背景的人具有巨大优势。

<!--en-->
*Linda Greenblatt ("LG"):* So what is a girl from Long Island doing in retail? Pick an area that you can know and that you can understand well and that you enjoy. **I like shopping.** It is definitely an area I have to come to know well. You start to see *patterns*. Over a ten-year period you learn how a particular industry group trades that gives you a big advantage over people who are first looking at the stock and coming in cold and not having the background.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：我喜欢零售业，因为信息更新频繁——每月甚至每周都会发布数据。零售商会公布同店销售数据，即年度同比销售情况。而大多数行业通常只按季度发布数据。信息越多，人们就越会在事前、事中或事后利用这些信息进行交易。因此该行业波动性很大。很多人不喜欢波动，但对我来说，只要有长期的好机会，我就能接受波动。如果我以两年为投资周期，那么这些月度数据恰恰是我最大的机遇。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
I like retail because you are constantly getting information. You get it on a monthly basis and sometimes on a weekly basis. Retailers put out same store sales numbers-Comparable sales in stores for a year-over-year period. Monthly basis but most industry groups you normally get quarterly numbers. The more information you have, the more people try to trade on the information before, after and during. You get a tremendous volatility in this sector. A lot of people don't like volatility. As far as I am concerned, I can live with volatility if there is a good opportunity over the long term. And if I am taking a two years time horizon that is actually my greatest opportunity--are these monthly numbers.

不可避免地，这些公司会因为自身过错或宏观环境的影响而表现不佳。业绩数据会不及预期，而市场往往毫不留情——于是市场会抛售这些股票。某天它的市盈率还是20倍，第二天就跌至10倍（基于盈利计算），但公司基本面其实并未改变。这种基本面上的差异正是你的机会。因此你必须忍受些许焦虑。相信我，当这些股票下跌30%到40%时，很难下定决心买入，但这通常正是最佳买入时机。波动性其实是你的朋友。

<!--en-->
Inevitably these companies are going to miss because of their fault or no fault of their own due to the macro environment. There will be a missed number and the market tends to have no mercy. So the market kills these stocks. One day it is trading at 20 times and the next day it is trading 10 times (earnings) but nothing has fundamentally has changed. That fundamentally is your opportunity. So you must live with a little bit the anxiety. Believe me when these stocks are down 30% to 40% it is hard to pull the trigger, but that is usually the best time to buy. Volatility is your friend.

我不知道如何预测下一个潮流。我真的不懂时尚。我想说的是：没人能持续精准预测时尚趋势。**这些公司能否长期经营良好？**它们能否驾驭经济周期的起伏？

<!--en-->
I don't know how to pick the next trend. I really don't know fashion. I say this: nobody can predict fashion. It is really not about hitting the next trend on a continuous basis. **Are these companies running a good business over the long-term?** Are they running a business that can weather the ups and downs?

最佳的买入时机是当它们错过一个季度的商品销售时。如果你审视公司的基本面，发现其运营良好，却因错过一个季度的销售而导致股价暴跌，那这正是长期持有的机会。它们是否紧跟热门趋势其实并不重要。

<!--en-->
The best time to get in is when they missed a season of merchandise because if you look at the fundamentals of the company and it is well-run and the stock gets crushed because they miss a season of merchandise, then it is an opportunity to own for the long term. It is really irrelevant if they pick the hot trends or not.

这很有趣：华尔街往往误解了零售业的本质。大多数分析师报告都聚焦于这家公司10月份的业绩如何？卡特里娜飓风或圣诞季取暖费上涨会对它产生什么影响？这些问题固然重要，但并不能说明这是否是一家好公司。从基本面看，它依然会存在。如果你以合适的价格买入，客户今天的行为其实并不重要——因为他们会继续存在并持续消费。

<!--en-->
It is very interesting because the Street misses the point on retail. Most analyst reports focus on how this company will do in Oct? How will this company be affected by Katrina or higher heating prices for Christmas? These are all relevant questions, but not relevant if this is a good business. Fundamentally it will be around. If you buy it at the right price it really doesn't matter what is happening to the customer today because they will be around and they will continue to buy.

去年《财富》杂志引用了一位经常投资零售业的对冲基金经理的话：“我会派人去门店查看商品打折幅度或收银台前是否有长队；如果该公司业绩超预期我就买入，若不及预期则做空。就这么简单。”

<!--en-->
A quote from Fortune last year from a Hedge Fund manager who often invests in retail, "I have my people visit stores to see how much the items are marked down or if there are long lines at the register and I buy if this company will beat numbers and short it if it misses numbers. It is that simple.

**他完全没抓住重点。**事情没那么简单。如果我必须按这种方式投资，我会为能否持续做到这一点而夜不能寐。也许我的判断正确率只有50%，期间还会充满焦虑。如果你能采取一到两年的更长投资视野，**就必须在人们厌恶这些股票时买入**，因为显然那时才是你的机会所在。所以你必须做一个逆向投资者。

<!--en-->
**He really misses the point.** It is not that simple. If I had to invest that way, I would lose sleep over whether I could consistently do that. Maybe I would get it right only 50% of the time. I would have a lot of anxiety in between. If you can take a longer time horizon for one to two years. **You have to buy these things when people hate it** because that, obviously, is when your opportunities are available. So you have to be a contrarian.

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c03ab07bdc683a20adf8ed0f095eaceb.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=5747f296b77bb5fe0457d6f43571dc143edcaf7113e74effb297beaa746e42e9)

这是两年的价格走势图，先涨后跌。你首先会注意到**这只股票中蕴藏着巨大获利空间**。两年前它的股价为7.5美元；如今股价为10美元，而其资产负债表上还有3到4美元的现金，由此可知它不会倒闭。没错，它确实错过了销售旺季——有人熟悉这个故事吗？

<!--en-->
Here is the two year price chart, it was up then down. So the first thing you notice **there is a lot of money to make in this stock.** Two years ago it traded at $7.5. Here at $10, they had $3 to $4 dollars of cash on the balance sheet, you knew they were not going under. Yes, they missed sales—is anybody familiar with this story?

基本上，它们有一段时间偏离了市场潮流。它们不确定如何在市场中定位自己。它们试图与Abercrombie、ANF等品牌竞争，但缺乏吸引力。2004年时，它们未能满足那些善变的青少年顾客的需求；2003/2004年它们错过了迎合顾客的机会，未能满足他们的需求。

<!--en-->
Basically they were off-trend for a while. They were not sure how to position themselves in the marketplace. They tried to compete against (Abercrombie, ANF) but they didn't have the cache. Back in 2004 they were not addressing their customer—the fickle teenager. Back in 2003/2004 they were missing the boat with their customer; they were not meeting their needs.

六个月后，它们控制了库存并调整了商品结构。同店销售额的回升是关键。2004年时它们的盈利潜力并不比六个月后差，只是同店销售额为负。这家公司不应被给予如此低的估值——既然同店销售额为负，其股价本应仅为潜在盈利的六倍（扣除现金后）。在我看来，这是一家能够长久存续的公司，其资产负债表健康。没错，它们确实错过了商品销售时机；同店销售额也的确下滑。但它们正在更换管理团队、加强库存管理。2004年它们确实在库存方面受挫，但显然仍有潜力。

<!--en-->
Fast forward six months, they got their inventory under control and they turned their merchandise around. Comparable store sales turned around that was key. Back in 2004 it wasn't that their earnings potential was any less than six months later, it was the fact that comps (comparable same store sales) were negative. This company doesn't deserve this multiple because they are showing negative comps so it should trade at six times potential earnings net of cash. To me this is a company that will be around. They have a healthy balance sheet. Yes, they have merchandise misses; yes their same stores sales are down. But they are making changes to their management team; they are on top of their inventories. They got hit on inventories in 2004. Certainly there is potential there.

一旦人们看到同店销售额趋于稳定，意识到公司能恢复更正常的盈利和利润率，股价便几乎翻了三倍。这就是在零售业中把握时机赚钱的一个例子。下一张图表：ANF。

<!--en-->
As soon as people saw comps stabilizing and they recognize that they could get back to more normalized earnings and margins, the stock basically tripled. This is one example how you can make money in retail if you get in at the right time.
Next Chart: ANF:

有人了解这里的情况吗？基本上发生了同样的事情：同店销售一度为负；商品供应出现失误，他们随后调整了管理团队。早在2003/2004年，尽管该公司拥有强劲的资产负债表和稳定的客户群，其股价却依然低迷。ANF拥有忠实的追随者，这些客户不会轻易离开。只要他们能稳定利润率就好了。事实上，该公司的利润率在行业内名列前茅，资本回报率也是最高的——可以说是一家运营稳健的企业。唯一的缺点是同店销售为负，正因如此股价才被压低到那种水平。从2003年12月到2005年7月，该股股价几乎翻了三倍——从25美元涨至75美元。

<!--en-->
Does anyone know the story here? Basically the same thing happened. Comps were negative for awhile; there were merchandise misses, they tweaked their management team. Back in their 2003/2004 area, despite the fact that they had a strong balance sheet and strong customer base, the stock was depressed. ANF has a loyal following and they were not going away. If they could just stabilize their margins. Again, they had the highest margins in the business; they had the best ROC in the business—a solidly run business. The one caveat was that their comps were negative. That is why people knocked the stock down to those levels. The stock was basically a triple from December of 2003 to July of 2005—the stock went from $25 to $75.

JG：顺便说一下，琳达曾在课堂上推荐这些低价股票。

<!--en-->
JG: By the way, Linda was here in class touting these stocks at the lower prices.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
