## Aeropostale

有人对这家公司略知一二吗？有人去过*ARO*门店吗？你有没有遇到过商品打折却不买的情况？如果某件商品标价30美元，马上就会打八折。你会立刻觉得捡到了便宜。这当然与*ANF*的经营策略截然不同。大多数零售商只有在必要时才会降价促销；如果看到没人购买，他们也不会跟风降价。

<!--en-->
Anybody know a little bit about this company? Anyone been into an *ARO* store? Have you ever not bought something on sale? If they mark something at $30 it immediately has 20% off. You immediately feel like you are getting a bargain. That is certainly different from what *ANF* is trying to do. Most retailers are only taking their mark downs when they have too. If you see people not buying, I am not going to buy too.

我们希望顾客感觉自己买到了便宜货。他们的定价比*Eagle*低约30%，而*Eagle*又比*ANR*低约30%。这样的定价策略使他们在市场上占据有利位置，不会与其他品牌直接竞争。这是一年的股票走势图：上周股价最低跌至18.5美元，几个月前曾高达35美元。或许这里存在投资机会。我们买入的价格大约在18美元左右。

<!--en-->
We want our customers to feel like they are getting a bargain. Their price points are about 30% lower than *Eagle* and *Eagle* is about 30% lower than *ANR*. It positions them very well in the marketplace. There is certainly a place for them in the marketplace so they are not going head to head with the other guys. This is a one year stock chart. The stock was as low at $18.5 last week and as high as $35 a few months ago. Perhaps there is an opportunity here. Around $18 was where we were buying it.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/18e144a2c419a05e3db81bff06ab0af1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=1d30865a215d9192eb4856255e4cd16b96b0c287ce477916188f9bcdcdc22001)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/18e144a2c419a05e3db81bff06ab0af1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=1d30865a215d9192eb4856255e4cd16b96b0c287ce477916188f9bcdcdc22001)

哥伦比亚大学商学院第59期特殊情境投资课程：我们将扩大其门店规模，并评估其在未来三到五年内的价值。我们希望确定自己的目标价位。

<!--en-->
59
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
We are going to build out their store base and figure out what we think it is worth in a three-to-five year period. We want to figure out a price target of our own.

显然，引起我兴趣的是股价的*急剧下跌*。这确实让我重新审视该公司。我知道其盈利预期在每股2美元左右，现金储备达3美元，因此估值约为15美元；若每股收益能达到2美元，市盈率则仅为7.5倍。这只股票看起来相当有吸引力，我想进一步深入研究。

<!--en-->
So obviously, what got me interested was the *precipitous fall* in the stock price. It certainly made me take a second look. And I knew estimates had been in the two dollar earnings range with $3 in cash so $15 and potential for $2 EPS gives you 7.5 xs. The stock seems pretty interesting; I want to do more work.

股价下跌的原因在于：同店销售未达预期，商品供应略有偏差；每平方英尺存货量增加了33%，而同店销售额却下降了2%，说明存货过多。他们可能需要几个月时间（并非一个季度就能解决）来清理库存。因此他们不得不大幅促销以处理滞销品、引进新货，导致期间利润率被严重压缩。这是一家非常稳定的公司，他们终将让商品供应重回正轨。他们只是需要时间度过难关。如果一家负债沉重的公司错过几个销售季，就可能破产。目前管理层正在解决问题，存货问题也在得到处理。我宁愿看到他们承受短期冲击以解决存货问题，也不愿看着问题拖延一年之久。

<!--en-->
What happened for the decline to have occurred: They missed their comp sales, their merchandise was slightly off; inventories were up 33% per sq foot while same store sales were down 2% so they were over inventoried, it will probably take them a few months (not a one quarter problem) to clear out the inventory. So they were having big sales to get rid of stale inventories to bring in fresh inventories so margins get crushed in the interim fire sales. It is a very stable company. They will get their merchandise back on track. They just needed time to weather the storm. A company with heavy debt that misses several merchandising seasons could go bust. The wheels are in motion, management issues--if there are any--are being addressed and inventory issues are addressed. I would rather see you take a hit and get your inventory problems behind you rather than stretch their problems out over a year.

一旦他们出现问题，所有人便*蜂拥而上*（投资者立即抛售；分析师纷纷下调评级）。此时不宜持有该股，因为问题会延续到下一季度。大多数分析师对其评级为“持有”或“卖出”。没人愿意过早下结论。他们看出这个问题会持续一两个季度，因此无论股价多么低廉，都不愿冒险预测其复苏。他们无法预测未来几个月的情况，但正如你所知，同店销售数据其实并不重要。**真正重要的是：该公司能否克服这些问题，恢复正常的利润率和盈利水平？一旦做到这一点，它的价值又是多少呢？** JG：琳达，请在此处停下，看看那张图表，难道不觉得世界运转的方式很*奇妙*吗？（股票图表显示股价从35美元跌至18美元。）多年来琳达一直靠此获利，而每次情况都如图表所示。

<!--en-->
They started to have these issues and everyone *piles* onto the band wagon (investors sell immediately; all the analysts downgrade the stock). You can't own it here because the problems will carry over into the next quarter. The majority of analysts either have holds on it or sales on it. Nobody wants to get ahead of themselves. They see that this will be a problem for a quarter or two so they don't want to go out on a limb and predict a turnaround no matter how cheap the company becomes. They can't predict over the next few months, but as you know, it is irrelevant what same store sales are going to be. **Because what is relevant is if this company gets past these issues, can the company be back to normalized margins and earnings and when they do, what is this company worth?**
JG: Stop Linda right here and look at that chart and say isn't it *great* that the world works like that. (Stock chart shows a collapse from $35 to $18). Linda has been making money all these years and that is what the chart looks like *every* time.

LG：你不必听信卖方分析师的意见。分析师称：当股价为19美元时，我们对*ARO*持低配观点，因为该公司会持续达不到预期（“在低位抛售”或“高买低卖”），原因是其库存过多（绝非玩笑）。这种趋势可能会持续到春季（1-2月）。或许如此，但我们采取的是一到两年的投资时间框架。我们不在乎春季会发生什么，只在乎他们解决这些问题后的情况。

<!--en-->
LG: You don't want to listen to the sell-side analysts. Analyst: At $19 we are underweighting *ARO* because they will continue to miss estimates ("sell" it at the lows or buy high and sell low) because they have too much inventory (no kidding). Those trends will likely continue into spring (Jan-Feb). Maybe so, but we are taking a one to two year time horizon. We don't care what happens into spring, we care about what happens when they get through these issues.

“我们认为，对盈利动能放缓的股票采取低配策略是合理的。”我认为这完全是错误的思维方式。盈利未达预期只是表象。真正的*买入时机*在于所有人都知道公司未能达到预期、存在库存问题之时。要知道，如果她都知道了，那其他人也必然知道。此时正是你需要以*逆向投资者*的视角审视并行动的时候。

<!--en-->
"We think it makes sense to underweight stocks with earnings momentum slowing." I think that is exactly the wrong way to think. Downside earnings miss. It is the wrong way to think about things. The *time to buy* is when everybody knows they are missing comps, have inv issues, etc. You know what, if she knows it, then everyone knows it. This is the time you have to be looking at it and thinking like a *contrarian*.

JG：她向来如此，今后也会继续这样。

<!--en-->
JG: She has always has done it that way, she is going to keep doing it that way.

LG：从彭博社的数据来看，原预计年度盈利在1.65美元左右，明年盈利预计将达到2美元左右。现在的情况是：年度盈利降至1.36美元，明年盈利预测也被下调至1.70美元。**为何要下调明年的盈利预测？**这毫无道理。如果今年盈利被下调，他们不可能维持对明年的预测不变。无论业务状况如何，他们都会自动下调明年预测。该业务明年能实现2美元盈利吗？当然可以。一旦解决库存问题，他们很有机会实现每股2美元的盈利。

<!--en-->
LG: Pulled off the Bloomberg. Earnings were supposed to be $1.65 range and the number for next year was supposed to be in the $2 range. This is now: earnings came down to $1.36 for the year and they took earnings down to $1.70 for the following year. **Why did they take the following year's earnings down?** It makes no sense. They can't keep their estimates for next year the same if they lower this year's earnings. They automatically bring next year's estimate down regardless of the business. Could the business do $2 next year? Of course, they could. I think there is a really good chance to make $2. Per share once they get through their inventory issues.

数据下调这一事实说明，你不应被误导，以为业务基本面发生了导致明年盈利下降的根本性变化。

<!--en-->
The fact that they numbers come down means that you shouldn't be fooled that something has fundamentally changed with the business that is causing numbers to come down for next year.

学生：您如何区分不同的管理团队？哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程 LG：关于管理层——我倾向于选择经验丰富的人选。我喜欢经过验证的管理团队。在研究过程中，我会考察：他们的客户群是谁？竞争对手是谁？他们存在的理由是什么？人们为何选择这家店而非竞争对手？答案是价格。ARO在价格上具有优势。他们存在的理由明确：他们与折扣店竞争，且商场中直接与之竞争的特色店并不多。这正是他们所瞄准的价格区间。

<!--en-->
Student: What do you do to differentiate among management teams?
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
LG: Management--I like to see someone who has been around for awhile. I like to see a proven management team. As I do more research, I look at: Who is their customer base? Who are their competitors? Is there a reason for their being? Is there a reason people shop at this store vs. their competitors? Yes, because of price. ARO will win on price. There is a reason for their being. They are competing with the discounters and there are not many other specialty store concepts in the malls that are competing directly with them. This is the price point they are looking to.

学生：为何您没有将*American Eagle*视为投资对象？两家公司股价都远低于高点，运营状况良好，且都有存在的理由。

<!--en-->
Student: Why didn't you look at *American Eagle* as an investment? They both are way off of their highs, they both are well run and they have a reason for being.

LG：这很有趣，因为这正是我原本打算纳入投资组合的两家公司。我研究了*Eagle*，您的看法完全正确，但主要区别在于*ARO*是一家拥有600家门店的连锁企业，凭借Jimmy's等品牌，其扩张潜力可达1000到1200家门店。增长潜力巨大。而American *Eagle*已在900家门店达到饱和状态，或许还能再开100家门店。我认为*ARO*的增长前景更好。*Eagle*要恢复增长潜力还需数年时间。AEOS虽可推出新品牌，但测试阶段需一年，真正发力还需几年。我看重*ARO*正在于此。*ARO*与其说是时尚引领者，不如说是时尚追随者。我更青睐这种定位。*ARO*无需领先于时尚潮流，稍慢一步即可。

<!--en-->
LG: It is interesting because those are exactly the two companies I was looking at to add to the portfolio. I looked at *Eagle* and you are right on all counts but the one major difference was that *ARO* is a six hundred store chain and they have more potential to grow to 1000 to 1200 stores with their concepts like Jimmy's. The growth potential is tremendous. I look at that an American *Eagle* that is fully saturated at 900 stores. Perhaps they can open another 100 stores. I believe growth will be better with *ARO*. It will be a few years before *Eagle* has any growth potential. AEOS can open a new concept but it will take a year for a test phase and a few more years to get momentum. I like *ARO* primarily for that. *ARO* was a little bit less a fashion concept than a fashion follower. I like that position a little better. *ARO* doesn't have to be in the lead on fashions, they can be a step behind.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/9a2167871790f0d4cdec4c77f1335326.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=488cdaf78c4d3a61d8a9db7025d19d5d48444a774f05c707152f395fb4482536)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/9a2167871790f0d4cdec4c77f1335326.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=488cdaf78c4d3a61d8a9db7025d19d5d48444a774f05c707152f395fb4482536)

学生：同店销售额下滑怎么办？

<!--en-->
Student: What about falling same store sales?

LG：同店销售额下滑但门店数量却在增长？这要看具体原因。如果营收增长有限但利润率有所提升，那或许值得关注。根据具体情况，我并不要求必须看到15%到20%的营收增长。

<!--en-->
LG: Same store sales falling and growth in stores? It really depends upon the issues. They didn't have much top line growth but margin growth, then that might be of interest. I don't necessarily have to see 15% to 20% top line growth depending upon the situation.

你要弄清楚同店销售额下滑的原因。询问公司如何应对这一问题，或者是否采取了措施。如果管理层将原因归咎于天气、油价等，我更喜欢那些勇于承担责任并着手解决问题的公司。要知道，虽然存在某些宏观因素，但我们已有计划来解决自身问题。

<!--en-->
You want to understand why the SSS are declining. Ask how the company is addressing the problem or if they are addressing it. If management is blaming it on the weather, oil prices etc. I like companies that take the blame and take responsibility to fix the problem. You know what, there are some macro issues but we have a plan to fix our issues.

学生：您如何判断一个零售业态是否已达到饱和？

<!--en-->
Student: How do you know when a retail concept is reaching saturation?

LG：这取决于其目标客户群以及所在的商场类型：ABC商场。你可以在A类、B类或C类商场看到AEOS门店。对于零售商而言，进入所有三类商场的最大门店数上限为1000到1200家。

<!--en-->
LG: It depends upon whom they are catering to: what malls are they in: ABC Malls. You could see an AEOS in an A or B or C mall. A 1000 to 1200 is max saturation for a retailer to go into all three mall types.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：*ANF*品牌最多只会进驻400家购物中心，因为它们仅出现在A类购物中心中。你不会在C类购物中心看到它们。正因如此，他们推出了面向质量较低的B类和C类购物中心的Hollister概念店。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
An *ANF* will max out at 400 malls because they are only in A type malls. You won't see them in a C mall. That is why they launched the Hollister concept which was for lower quality malls: B and C.

**学生：**做研究时你会和谁交谈？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Whom do you talk to when doing your research?

JG：我会和任何愿意与我交谈的人交流。我会与门店经理交谈，因为他们通常了解很多信息。我也会尝试与高级管理人员沟通。从高级商品经理那里得到的信息与从首席财务官那里得到的信息是不同的。

<!--en-->
JG: I will talk to anyone who will talk to me. I will talk to store managers because they often know a lot. I try to talk to senior managers. You will get *different* information from a senior merchandising manager than a CFO.

我们会与提着或没提着购物袋走出门店的顾客交谈，也会与门店员工交流。这取决于我们当时想要了解什么。在研究*ARO*时，我们想看看其是否有忠诚的客户群。顾客进店后却不购买吗？他们对商品有何看法？即便商品质量不佳，顾客是否仍会光顾？我们试图理解的基本问题之一是：在该公司出现商品管理失误期间，其客户群发生了什么变化。你带着对股票的预判进入研究——**为什么这只股票如此便宜？**然后深入探究下去。

<!--en-->
We talk to people who come out of the store with or without bags. We speak to store employees. It depends upon what we are trying to find out at the time. When looking into *ARO* we wanted to see a loyal customer base. Are customers coming in and not buying? What do they think of the merchandise? Are the customers still coming in despite the weak merchandise? One of the basic things we try to understand is what is happening to their customer base during this period of time when they have these merchandising missteps. You go in with a thesis on the stock. **Why is the stock cheap?** You go in and try to delve further.

零售商的好处在于你能更容易接触到他们的顾客。同样，信息越多越好。我会去购物中心，我的搭档以及一位经常泡在购物中心、二十多岁的年轻人也会一同前往，我们一起考察门店情况。

<!--en-->
The nice thing about retailers is that you have more access to their customers. Again, the more information the better. I go the malls, my partner and a person in her twenties who spends a lot of time in the malls—we all go to the malls to check out stores.

我会让我的母亲或任何我认识的潜在顾客去门店体验。在零售业方面，每个人都有自己的见解。我们身处东海岸，因此对世界的看法难免有偏差。务必注意不要把东海岸的情况推及全国。如果你在进行定性研究，应关注*整个*地区而非单一地区。

<!--en-->
I send my mother or anyone who I know is a potential customer to the store. Everybody has a valid opinion when it comes to retail. We are based on the East Coast so certainly we have a very warped perspective of the world. It is important to be careful not to extrapolate from the East Coast to the whole country. If you are out doing that qualitative research you focus on the *entire* area not just one area.

**学生：**那些可能损害零售商的宏观问题有哪些？

<!--en-->
**Student:** What about macro issues that can hurt retailers?

LG：像这类廉价零售商，由于油价上涨，其顾客受冲击最大；但另一方面，过去在*Eagle*购物的顾客现在会因为收入减少而转投*ARO*。**我不会在消费趋势上花费太多时间。** **我尽量避开宏观因素。** 我认为宏观经济的相关消息早已反映在市场中。我是否认为过去四个月读到的每篇文章内容都已被市场消化？是的。

<!--en-->
LG: When it is a cheap retailer like this, this is the customer who will be hit the hardest because of the high oil prices, but on the other side, the customer who used to shop at *Eagle* will now shop at *ARO* because they have less money. **I do not spend too much time on spending trends.**
**I try to avoid the macro stuff.** Do I think the news of the Macro economy is out there already in the market. Do I think that every article I have read for the past four months is already in the market? Yes.

我会询问这只股票如今是否便宜，以及未来两年是否会迎来正常环境。

<!--en-->
I ask whether this is a cheap stock today and do I think over the next two years there will be a normal environment.

**学生：**你们会卖空股票吗？LG：有时我会卖空。我更倾向于卖空一*篮子*股票而非单只股票。这些股票的价格在上涨时可能会达到更离谱的水平。我没有耐心等待两年才看到股票下跌，不像持有多头时那样有耐心。

<!--en-->
**Student:** Do you short stocks?
LG: Sometimes I short. I prefer to short more of a *basket* than a particular stock. These stocks can go to even more ridiculous valuations on the upside. I don't have the two-year stomach to wait for a stock to drop like I do for the long side.

如果我看到一家公司连续数月实现两位数的销售增长，且市盈率高达50倍，我会认为这种状况可持续吗？不会。我不知道它何时会逆转，但我知道这种状况不可持续。你知道那一天终会到来——*均值回归*。

<!--en-->
If I do see a company posting double digit comps for several months in a row and it is trading at 50 times earnings, do I think it is sustainable? No. I don't know when it is going to turn but I know it is unsustainable. You know the day will come. *Reversion to the mean.*

**学生：**如何评估成长性？LG：这里简单看一下数据就能发现这只股票看似便宜，或许值得我们进一步研究。你会发现其企业价值与息税前利润之比为8倍，但这只是利润率低迷的一年后的数据，因为公司在商品管理上出了差错。所以8.5倍的企业价值/息税前利润比并不具参考价值。你真的需要展望一年后的情况。那个企业价值/息税前利润比也并不重要。人们下调预测数字并非因为业务发生变化，而是因为今年受到了冲击。

<!--en-->
**Student:** How do you value growth?
LG: Here is a quick look at the numbers to say this stock looks cheap, so perhaps we want to do more work on it. If you notice it's EV to EBIT is 8 times but this is year coming off of depressed margins because they messed up on merchandise. So that 8.5 EV/EBIT is not that relevant. You really want to look out a year. That EV to EBIT is not really that relevant either. People took down their numbers not because the business is changed but because they got hurt this year.

我喜欢自己推算明年的数据。我自己的测算显示企业价值/息税前利润比为6倍，因此看起来相当便宜，所以我打算进一步研究。幻灯片：

<!--en-->
I like to put together my own numbers for next year. My own numbers show EV to EBIT of 6 times so it looks pretty cheap so I want to do more work.
Slides:

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：这张幻灯片讲的是门店潜力：ARO的前景看起来相当可观。这里有一些简单的数字可以说明为何在我看来这只股票很便宜。那些市盈率并未扣除现金，扣除现金后价格更便宜，这很有趣。你问到了成长性。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
This slide is on store potential: It looks pretty exciting for ARO. Just some Easy numbers to calculate for why the stock looks pretty cheap to me. Those P/Es are not net of cash so net of cash they are even cheaper so that is interesting. You asked about growth.

ARO有望再开400家门店，而Jimmy概念店则可能开设800家。我较为保守地估计为600家，但其门店潜力确实巨大。

<!--en-->
ARO with the potential for another 400 stores and the other, Jimmy concept could be 800 stores. I was more conservative with 600 stores, but there is a lot of store potential there.

目前的情况是，人们正在关注今年的数据，尤其聚焦于10.8%的营业利润率——这一数字正面临压力。分析师指出，利润率确实承压；在公司恢复更佳的利润率水平之前，我们持谨慎态度，不推荐买入（这属于“事后诸葛亮”式的投资判断）。就在不久前，该公司的利润率还超过14%。我认为该公司有望达到13%的利润率，而市场预期的数值仅为11.5%。考虑到其经营模式并未改变，他们重回14%的营业利润率水平真的有那么难吗？在我看来，这意味着营业利润率有400个基点的提升空间。

<!--en-->
Here is a situation where people are looking at this year's numbers and they are really focusing on that operating margin number of 10.8%--under pressure. The analysts write that the margins are really under pressure; we hesitate to recommend it until they get back to better margins (investing in the rear view mirror). It wasn't that long ago that the company did north of 14% in margins. It wasn't that long ago the company did north of 14%. I believe the company can do 13% while the street is at 11.5%. Is it difficult for them to get back to 14% op margins considering nothing in their business has changed in the way they run their business? This says to me, Wow, there is 400 basis point of operating margin improvement in operating margin here.

从11.5%到14%，该公司还有巨大的改善空间。我们应当关注**正常化利润率**，而非受抑制的利润率。鉴于去年该公司利润率曾达到14.5%，我认为其正常化利润率应在13%左右。这便引出了对股票估值的话题。关键在于，当前营业利润率为10.7%，却有望提升至14%，因此存在上涨潜力。我对此感到兴奋。大多数人却说：“该股利润率只有10.7%，我要下调其评级。”

<!--en-->
They have big room for improvement 11.5% to 14%. You need to look at **normalized margins** not depressed margins. If I look at norm in the 13% area because they did 14.5% last year. That This leads me to a valuation of the stock. But the point being is that I see 10.7% operating margin with potential to go to 14%, so there is upside here. I get excited. Most people say, "the stock is 10.7% margins, I am going to knock it down."

从10.5%的利润率提升至14.5%，这里蕴含着巨大的上涨潜力。

<!--en-->
There is huge potential upside here from 10.5 margin to 14.5 margin.

LG：我们希望看到一家企业具备一年内开设大量门店的经验。通常来说，我们不希望看到一家公司一年内从100家门店猛增到500家，因为风险太高。我们必须确保该公司拥有成熟的商业模式、规范的门店设计、对顾客需求的精准把握，并能创造具有吸引力的ROIC。只有当他们信心十足时，门店扩张才会加速。

<!--en-->
LG: You like to see that has experience opening a large number of stores in a year. Typically you don't want to see a company go from 100 to 500 stores in a year, the risk is high. You want to be sure that they have a good model, they can format the store, they know what their customer is looking for, and they are earning attractive ROICs. As they gain confidence then the store opening can accelerate.

JG：新门店的表现可能不如成熟的门店。如果公司的商品陈列不佳，那么无论开设多少门店都无法提升ROC。需要查明是否是门店数量过多导致饱和，或是存在其他原因。

<!--en-->
JG: A new store may not do as well as a more mature store. If the company has poor merchandising then it doesn't matter if they open many stores or not to help ROC. Ask if there are too many stores opening (saturation) or something else is going on.

我总是倾向于对其扩张计划打折扣。对于增长部分，合理的折价是多少？我在计算终值时会非常保守。

<!--en-->
I always want to discount their expansion. What is a fair discount for growth?
I try to be very conservative on my terminal value.

请注意，商品陈列的质量对同店销售额的影响，可能比门店数量或饱和程度更大。新幻灯片：

<!--en-->
Be aware that the quality of merchandising may affect same store sales more than the number of stores opening or the company being close to a saturation point.

JG：这张幻灯片有点令人困惑，但它有助于我们确定股票何时被低估、何处适合买入。我试图展望五年期，并对该期间股票给出22亿美元的终值评估。Arrow公司有40亿平方英尺的潜在拓展空间；Jimmy’s目前仅有8家门店。目前他们正处于测试阶段，还将继续测试6个月。我做假设时力求保守：假设他们再测试两年，之后每年缓慢开设50家门店。

<!--en-->
JG: This slide is a little confusing, but it helps you come up with a thesis as to when the stock is cheap; where you want to buy. I try to take a look out over a five year period and place a terminal valuation on the stock over that five year period
2.2 billion for arrow with pot for 400 another 1.4 billion Sq ft Jimmy's currently only has 8 stores, Now, this is a sit where they are in a test mode and they will continue to test for another 6 mos. When I make may assumptions, I want to be very conservative. So I assume they test for another two years, then they slowly open 50 stores a year.

看看Arrow公司是如何扩张门店的：一旦模式成熟，他们每年便能开设100家门店。这些都属于保守估计。我的估值假设并不激进。

<!--en-->
If you look at how Arrow opened their store base, once they has their concept down, they opened 100 stores a year. These are conservative estimates. My assumptions are not aggressive in terms of how I do my valuation.

未来五年内，他们拥有22亿平方英尺以及20亿平方英尺的潜在拓展空间。Arrow公司每平方英尺营收为525美元，这是我用于计算新增门店的数据。我并未对同店销售寄予过高期望。

<!--en-->
Over next five years they have 2.2 billion Sq. and 2 bil sq fot potential. Arrow doing $525 a square foot. That is the number I am using for the additional store openings. I am not assuming big things for comps again.

Jimmy’s的运营效率不及Arrow。其所属品类的每平方英尺营收为400美元，这一数字与其他同类零售商相当。Jimmy’s主要面向18至25岁的顾客群体。可以参考竞争对手的数据来获取相关数值。

<!--en-->
Jimmy's not as prod as Arrow. They are doing $400 per sq ft for their category which is more in line with retailers that compete in their category. Jimmy's is catering to 18 to 25 year old customer. You can take a look at competitors to get the numbers.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：未来五年内的潜在盈利能力如何？正常化利润率——历史峰值曾达14.6%。需注意的是，公司认为自己有能力超越这一水平。我假设其利润率为13%，我认为这是正常化利润率，既与其他零售商水平一致，也低于公司自身的预期。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
What is the potent earnings power over that five year period? Normal margins—peak margins were 14.6%. Mind you that the company believes it has the pot to do north of that. I assume a 13% margin which I believe is a normalized margin, certainly in line with other retailers and well below what the company thinks it can do.

按13%的利润率计算，他们可赚取1.63美元；若利润率更高，则可达1.42美元。如果Arrow公司能达到13%的利润率，而Jimmy’s利润率更高，那么五年内的盈利将达到3.05美元。基于保守假设，我给予其12倍的低市盈率估值。Jimmy’s有潜力开设800家门店，但五年结束时仅会开设150家。

<!--en-->
They are earning $1.63 on 13% margin and $1.42 with additional margins. If the Arrow can do a 13% margins and Jimmy's doing a higher margins- Earnings over that five years is $3.05 and place a low 12 multiple (based on conservative assumptions). Jimmy has the potential to open 800 stores but they will only have 150 stores opened by the end of five years.

接下来是五年内的现金积累情况。110美元加上折旧费用，再减去维护性资本支出后，可得出每股8美元的现金；目前已有每股3美元的现金，因此总计每股11美元的现金。我假设管理层既不派发股息也不回购股票，而是将现金留存起来。如此算来，37美元加上11美元，便得到5年期结束时的股价为45美元。如果你还记得Arrow的股票走势图，其实你有一一个半月的时间可以在20美元或更低的价格买入该股票。若你做了这些计算，未来五年的回报率将达到19%。这只是其中一种分析方式。

<!--en-->
Then the build up of cash over the five years. $110 then adds back depreciation and subtracts maintenance capex and it gets you to $8 per share in cash and there is $3 in cash today for a total of $11 per share in cash. I am assuming that management does not pay dividend or buy back stock, they just sit on their cash. Here you have $37 plus $11 gets you to $45 stock price at the end of a 5 year period. If you remember Arrow's stock chart, basically you had a month and a half to buy at $20 or under to buy this stock. If you had done these calculations, you have a return of 19% over the next five years. That is one way to look at it.

JG：没错。我们的看法是，一旦大家了解到*Arrow*的盈利水平，其股价可能达到48美元，那么股价重新估值的速度会更快，两年内就能达到48美元。其他投资者可能会按10%的折现率来计算，因为这是股票投资的正常回报预期。这样一来，两年内股价可能达到36美元，即实现80%的回报。虽然Linda给出的五年年化回报率为19%，但一旦大多数人意识到这一点，接下来的两三年内你就能获得大部分收益。

<!--en-->
JG: Right. The way we talk about is that when everyone figures out what *Arrow* will earn and it could be a $48 stock, you could have the stock revalued faster and within two years you could have a $48 stock. Other investors could discount that back at 10% since that is a normal return of what you expect to get from a stock. The stock could be at $36 within two years which is an 80% return. Though Linda presents the return as 19% annualized over five years, when most people start to figure it out, you could get a big chunk of your upside in the next two or three years.

我想再强调Linda提出的一个重要观点——她逐步扩展了门店网络。换句话说，大多数人会说：“他们的门店增长率是X%，因此理应享有相应的市盈率。”他们往往根据短期增长率凭空设定数字。无论增长率如何，他们只是随意选取数值——我也不知道他们怎么定的。但Linda的做法非常合乎逻辑：她构建了完整的商业模型，这很有道理。她采用了保守的利润率和开店计划；即便新概念门店仅开发了潜在规模的20%，她仍得出了惊人的数字。因此，这种测算是为了确定其真实价值，并且极其保守。如果其实际价值与当前价格之间存在较大差距，那就意味着这是一笔不错的投资。

<!--en-->
I just want to make another important point that Linda made—she built out her store base. In other words, most people say, “Well, they are growing their stores at X percent and it deserves that P/E or that P/E—people just pick numbers out of the sky based on a growth rate that will be short-term. Whatever the growth rate may be, people just pick—I don’t know what they do. But what Linda does is just so logical. She builds out the whole concept; it makes sense. She used conservative margins and store openings. She built up the new concept by only 20% of the potential but she still comes up with huge numbers. So this exercise is figuring out what it is worth and being super conservative. If there is a big gap between what it is worth and what you are paying, then you have something that is pretty good.

LG：另一种看待方式是，如果该公司能在未来几年内达到每年2美元的盈利水平，那么其他投资者一旦从单店销售转向关注盈利数据，再结合门店面积的增长情况，就会认为：“哦，他们的增长率在15%到20%之间，因此理应享有15倍至20倍的市盈率。”这样一来，未来两年股价将达到30美元至40美元。总之，我没有加入一些更激进的假设，这些假设本可以进一步提升*Jimmy's*新概念店的上升空间，比如更快速地扩张门店数量。五年后门店数可能达到500家，而不只是我假设中的150家。我假定单店销售增长持平，但实际上他们可能做得更好；他们还可能回购股票，且利润率表现优于13%。公司也会采取措施将利润率提升至14%以上。

<!--en-->
LG: Another way I look at it is that if the company can get to that $2 in earnings run rate over the next couple of years, then other investors once they get off same store sales and onto earnings and then they look at square footage growth and say, “Oh, they are growing at 15% to 20% so this company deserves a 15x to 20x multiple, so you have a $30 to $40 stock over the next two years. The bottom line is that I am not including what I could have put in additional assumptions which would imply a more aggressive upside for the new concept of *Jimmy's* which includes a more aggressive roll-out of the stores. They could have 500 stores at the end of the five years not just 150 stores like I mentioned in my assumptions. I am assuming a flattish pick-up of same store sales, but they could do better. They do a stock buy back and the margin performance is doing better than that 13%. The company takes steps to improve the margins beyond 14%.

**学生：**这些门店的ROIC是多少？商场内的门店通常能获得怎样的回报？

<!--en-->
**Student:** What are the ROIC's on the stores? What type of return do mall based stores typically have?

**用于计算企业价值（EV）的超额现金**

<!--en-->
**Calculating Excess Cash for Enterprise Value (EV)**

**JG：** 一个常被提及的问题是：是否要扣除全部现金？答案是否定的；只需扣除“超额”现金（即每年运营不需要的现金）。必须判断这些现金中是否有任何一部分是必需的。负营运资本型企业（如麦当劳，顾客用现金或信用卡付款，而应付账款周期为30/60/90天）通常会在资产负债表上体现全部超额现金，当然收银机里的零钱除外。

<!--en-->
**JG:** One of the points that always come out is do you subtract (all) cash? The answer is no; you subtract "excess" cash (cash that is not needed to run their business on a yearly basis). You have to decide whether any of that cash is needed. Negative working capital businesses (like McDonald's Restaurants where customers pay cash or credit card while payables are 30//60/90 days) usually have the total amount of excess cash on the balance sheet excepting, of course, for petty cash in the registers.

请记住，零售商需要随时在收银机中保留现金，因此不要扣除资产负债表上的全部现金。竞争对手：*Wolverine*。他们拥有一批忠实的客户群——建筑工人。

<!--en-->
Remember that retailers need to keep cash in their registers all the time, so do not subtract the full amount of cash on the balance sheet.
Competitors: *Wolverine*.
They have a loyal following of customers—construction workers.

<!--en-->

门店平均面积为300平方英尺。近年来门店面积逐年增长，过去五年的复合年增长率为2.5%。每平方英尺的销售额达到529美元。

**JG：** 他们一直在关闭部分门店，这种趋势将会停止，因此使用净面积数据可能会产生误导。我建议深入剖析这一数字，看看在关闭大型门店后小型门店的增长情况如何。

你提到他们正在关闭大型门店，而门店面积却仍以每年2.5%的速度增长。应重点关注小型门店的增长情况。**务必将不同业务模式分开分析！** 整个公司的EBIT利润率为10%，EBIT金额为5000万美元。保守估计，若按7%的EBIT利润率计算，EBIT可达3500万美元；理想情况下利润率可达到10%。我们确实认为会面临*Finish Line*的竞争。由于该业务增长乏力，我们给予8倍的估值倍数。此外，还需加上在线业务产生的4亿美元价值以及现金储备。

**把公司拆解得越细越好。** 在某些行业中，不同业务板块之间会相互带动；但在FL公司中，欧洲与美国在增长机会、利润率及竞争格局方面存在显著差异，因此必须分别分析不同业务。其利润率从18%骤降至10%，仍有很大的提升空间。关键在于最终能达到什么水平。

<!--en-->

But in FL there is enough *disparity* in the growth opportunities, the margins and the competitive landscape in Europe vs. the US where you need to pick apart the different businesses separately. There is extreme margin contraction from 18% to 10%. There is a lot of room there. The question is where it lands.

管理层认为其利润率有望达到两位数。我试图提出自己处理此类问题的方式。由于最接近的竞争对手规模仅为他们的五分之一，因此他们的竞争地位非常强大。

**分析师：** 这一点适用于两份演示文稿——营业利润率是价值投资者衡量增长的关键指标。最令人担忧的是，人们往往倾向于采用均值回归理论或管理层预测来解释盈利情况，比如FL公司便是如此。虽然这些往往是可行的答案，但最佳做法始终是*尽可能从底层数据出发来推导这一数字*。按照Joel的建议，将不同业务分开分析。你们在经营租赁方面以及FL公司的进展中便采用了这种方法。

<!--en-->
**Analyst:** This applies to both presentations--operating margins are the value investors' growth number. The scariest thing to get into earnings is that you feel the urge to go to a reversion to the mean thesis or management estimate thesis like FL. Often those are the best answers you can come to, but the best you can do in all cases is *to try to get as bottom up to that number as you can*. Do what Joel suggested which is to separate the businesses. You did that with operating leases and how they made progress at FL.

**学生：** 该如何处理经营租赁问题？

<!--en-->
**Student:** How do you treat operating leases?

**分析师：** 大多数情况下这并不重要。但在租金与市场利率存在差异的情况下，这就显得重要了，因此必须根据市场利率进行调整以得出正常化数值。

<!--en-->
**Analyst:** In most cases it doesn't matter. In some cases where rent is different than market rates, it can matter so you have to adjust for market rates to figure out normalized.

*养老金问题。* 将养老金债务计入企业价值的最重要时机是当公司未通过损益表来支付相关费用时。假设公司有3亿美元的养老金资产，而每年实际需向已退休及在职员工支付的养老金为3000万美元。有时养老金核算会出现偏差，因为它是基于滞后平滑处理的。因此，如果养老金资金不足，务必按调整后的现值重新计入养老金债务。

<!--en-->
*Pensions.* The most important time to add pension debt to the EV is when the company is not funding expense through the income statement. Say you have $300 million in pension assets and you are really paying $30 million a year into that pension for employees that are already retired and those that are in service. Sometimes pensions get screwed up because it is done on a lagged smoothed basis. So you must make sure you add back the pension debt on an adjusted present value basis if it is under funded.

**JG：** 如果管理层对其养老金计划采用了9%的不切实际的回报率假设，而你认为实际回报率应为5%或7%，那么我建议调整养老金负债并采用你调整后的数值。

<!--en-->
**JG:** If management is using an unrealistic assumption of 9% returns for their pension plan but you think the returns should be 5% or 7%, then I would adjust the pension liability and use your adjusted number.

### 交叉验证你所用的倍数

<!--en-->
*Cross Checking Your Multiple*

**JG：** 你们是否进行了现金流折现分析以确定合适的倍数？

<!--en-->
**JG:** Did you do a discounted cash flow analysis to determine an appropriate multiple?

**学生：** 没有，我们没有进行。

<!--en-->
**Student:** No we did not.

**JG：** 现金流折现分析有助于你确定合理的倍数作为交叉验证。永续5%的增长率会让大多数增长模型失效，从而得出极高的倍数。那么问题在于：永续3%或5%的增长率下会怎样呢？列出不同增长率对应的倍数矩阵或许很有意义。理论上，永续5%增长对应的倍数是多少？你们所用的12倍又处于什么位置呢？

<!--en-->
**JG:** A DCF analysis would help you determine a proper multiple as a cross check. A 5% growth in perpetuity will blow out most growth models and gets you a very high multiple. So the question is what happens at 3% or 5% growth in perpetuity? It might be interesting to have a matrix of various growth rates to judge the multiple. What multiple theoretically is 5% growth in perpetuity? Where does your 12 multiple fit into that?

你们认为税后15倍倍数（6.6%的股息率）对*Claire Stores*而言是合理价格。我认为应采用至少6%的最低门槛收益率。充其量来说，这家公司是一家不错的生意，不会亏损太多，且将来有望获得更高的倍数。你们可能过于保守了，这没关系，毕竟你们试图以极大折扣买入它。

<!--en-->
You figured a 15x multiple (6.6% yield) after tax was a reasonable price for *Claire Stores*. I say use a minimum 6% hurdle rate. At best what we will get out of here is that it is a great business, it won't lose much money and at some point it will get a higher multiple. You are probably being too conservative which is OK because you are trying to buy it at a huge discount.

(Don't just assume a multiple even if conservative—cross check it).

Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The company takes six or seven years to integrate an acquisition of a new campus. They have made 80 acquisitions in the past four years. We think the company is worth $22 while it is currently trading at $12. We assume improvement in operating margins.

**JG：**你信任这些人吗？请解释一下整体情况。他们不是从政府那里获得学费资助吗？而且该公司不是还有欺诈指控吗？

<!--en-->
**JG:** Do you trust these guys? Explain the big picture thing. Don't they get funding from the government for the tuition and aren't there claims of fraud against the company?

没有定罪记录，但我却是个好人？他们是在夸大数字吗？他们是不是太激进了呢？为什么营业利润率在下降——他们过去的行为和现在有什么不同？

<!--en-->
There are no convictions but I'm a great guy? Are they goosing the numbers, are they too aggressive, why is the operating margins dropping—what did they do in the past that is different now?

**分析师：** 72%的上涨空间？你认为它在2010年能值22美元吗？你凭什么认为它能更快达到这个价位？请解释一下你所说的“校园”具体指什么。

<!--en-->
**Analyst:** 72% upside? You think it will be worth $22 in 2010? Why do you think it will get there quicker? Explain what you mean by campuses.

**学生：** 关于收购的ROIC指标呢？商誉能否作为资本的合适替代指标——既然他们不断收购校区，商誉是否也能较好地代表资本支出？如果他们不收购校区，就不得不自己建造学校吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** ROIC regarding acquisitions? Would goodwill be a good proxy for capital—a decent proxy for capex since they are constantly buying campuses? If they didn't acquire campuses then they would have to build the schools?

**JG：**他们购买这些校区是为了利用其盈利能力，而非资产成本，以便整合这些学校。扩张难道不会给他们带来成本吗？基本上，你必须对每一所学校运用逻辑来分析。

<!--en-->
**JG:** They are buying these campuses for their earnings power not the cost of their assets to be able to put the schools together. Wouldn't it cost them to expand? Basically you have to use logic on each one.

简化一切——如果他们现在停止扩张并维持现状，那又有什么价值呢？接着，如果他们用新增的资本去购买资产，我认为他们能获得怎样的额外回报呢？通常我会把问题分为两部分来分析。他们目前拥有的资产就是如此。如果停止扩张，这些资产的价值是多少？如果他们能产生这么多现金，那他们会怎么处理这笔现金呢？他们可以派发现金（支付股息）、回购股票或收购资产。我必须假设他们会对这笔现金做何安排。一旦他们开始收购资产，我就得问：“这算是现金的有效利用吗？”然后据此来评估其价值。如果你开始假设他们会在某个时间点以某个价格购买多少资产，事情就会变得过于模糊不清；一旦这些情况发生变化，整个评估体系就会乱套。

<!--en-->
Simplify everything—what is it worth now if they just stopped and grow? Then if they take some of their incremental dollars capital and buy stuff what kinds of incremental returns do I think they are going to get on that? So I break things into two pieces generally. They have what they have now. Incrementally if they stop growing what is that worth? If they can generate this much cash, so what will they do with that cash? They can distribute cash (pay a dividend), buy back stock or acquire stuff. I have to make an assumption of what will they do with that cash. If they start acquiring stuff, I have to ask, “Will that be a good use of the cash or not?” And value it that way. It gets to be too amorphous if you start assuming if they are going to buy these many at this time or at this price? If that all changes it mucks up the whole works.

我会先看看自己手头有什么，然后判断如果他们要花些钱的话，这对他们（进行收购的公司）来说究竟是好事还是坏事。接着我会问：“我认为他们能从中赚多少钱？”这就是我拆解你的问题并尝试解答的方式。

<!--en-->
I take what I have and then if they are going to spend some cash do I think is it going to be a good thing or a bad thing (the company which is making acquisitions). And then I ask, “How much do I think they are going to earn on that?” That is the way I take apart your question and try to attack it.

用数学方法量化增长——新学校与成熟学校的增长矩阵。对于零售商而言，有一件非常重要的事：只要能量化某事物，就能从中得出有价值的信息。举个例子：三分之一的学校创办两年，三分之一的学校创办四年，而另外三分之一的学校在创办六年后达到饱和状态。仅凭这些数据，你就能推算出它们从当前状态到成熟阶段的增长率。你可以选取标准化的增长率和利润率，而非仅仅依赖现有的数据。如果我预计创办两年的学校会在未来四年内趋于成熟并提升利润率，而创办四年的学校则会在接下来两年内继续增长，那么通过矩阵分析就能预测它们在成熟时的利润率与增长率，进而算出此后的增长潜力。进行这些计算总是很有帮助的。这与分析需要时间成熟的门店类似：你可以查看过去两三年间开业的门店数量，从而预判未来的发展趋势。很多人没有这么做，其实这很简单——不过是数学运算而已，却能让你对未来的增长趋势有所把握。

<!--en-->
Quantify Growth Mathematically—Growth Matrix of New and Maturing Schools
Another thing that is very important especially with retailers—here was a situation—any time you can quantify something. Here was a question where 1/3 of the schools were two years old, a 1/3 were four years old and a 1/3 were at saturation at 6 years, you can figure out what the growth rates are going to be just from the stuff that you have until maturity. You can pick out the normalized growth rate and margins instead of taking the margins that are there now. If I really did think the two year schools would mature over the next four years and increase margins and the four year old schools will increase over the next two. You can figure out with a matrix as to where it (the margins and growth rate) will be at maturation and then how much growth from there. You can do the math and it is always helpful to it. This is similar to figuring out store bases that take a time to mature. You can see how many stores are open over the last three years or last two years and see what is going to happen in the future and you can almost project part of that. A lot of people don't do it and it is the easy stuff. It is just math and you can get a feel for the (future growth).

## 利用乔尔的小书进行投资

<!--en-->
*INVESTING USING JOEL'S LITTLE BOOK*

### 《战胜市场的小书》（精装版）

<!--en-->
*The Little Book That Beats the Market (Hardcover)*

作者：乔尔·格林布拉特。谈论他的新书《小书》……几年前，在互联网热潮期间，他的学生完全不理睬他，还称他为白痴；他们说：“看看Price-line吧！它的股价会翻一番。”这是当时《巴伦周刊》上用来吸引会员加入其价值投资者俱乐部的广告。当时价值投资理念如此不受待见，以至于我们展示了一具尸体的轮廓图。（幻灯片演示详见附录。）

<!--en-->
by Joel Greenblatt
Discussing his new book........."The Little Book"
A few years ago during the *Internet* craze, his (Joel Greenblatt's) students just ignored him and called him an idiot and they said, “Look at *Price-line*! It will double. This is the ad in *Barrons* at the time to attractmembers to his *Value Investors' Club*. Value investing was so bad back then we showed an outline of a dead man. (See appendix for slide presentation).

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：回到正题……多年来我逐渐意识到，格雷厄姆代表的是“便宜”这一面，而巴菲特则主张：“我想买入一家能持续盈利、拥有强大竞争优势且未来仍能持续赚钱的优质公司。”于是问题来了：**“能否同时找到既优质又便宜的公司呢？”**我们做了一项小测试。定义与之前相同：所谓优质公司，是指资本回报率较高的企业，即营业利润除以净营运资本和固定资产净额；我们采用的是有形资本的高回报率来界定“优质”。有形资本的高回报率能很好地表明该公司可能属于优质企业。至于“便宜”，则是指EV/EBIT（盈利收益率）——这一指标比市盈率分析更为精细，它考虑了不同的资本结构，从而能在公平的基础上比较各类公司，使资本化程度趋于一致。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Back to the story.....so over the years it became apparent to me that *Graham* was one side of the equation which was *cheap* and *Buffett* was: "I would like to buy a *good company* that could earn good money and had a good franchise that was going to stay there and be able to earn good money going forward." So the question was: **"Can you combine good and cheap at the same time?"**
We did a little bit of a test. We defined the same things I taught you. Good companies we define as having high returns on capital which is operating income divided by net working capital and net fixed assets. We use high returns on *tangible* capital. So that is how we defined good. High return on tangible capital gives a very good indication that this may be a good company. Cheap was *EV to EBIT (Earnings Yield)* which is a little more sophisticated than a P/E analysis taking into account different capital structures and being able to compare companies over a wide array on a fair basis. This equalizes capitalizations.

## 研究过程

<!--en-->
*The Study*

我们使用了去年的数据，并未采用预测值。在研究过程中，我们根据税前有形资本回报率（ROIC）对3500家公司进行排名，回报率最高的公司排名靠前。我们选取数据库中规模最大的3500只股票，直接按ROIC进行排序。接着，我们对“便宜”这一标准也做了同样处理：根据盈利收益率对3500家公司进行排名，从1到3500。我们使用的都是去年的数据。这是我们首次尝试的方法，虽然去年的数据是很实用的参考信息，但显然并非无可争议的依据。

<!--en-->
We used last year's numbers, we didn't use projections. So what we did was in the study: we ranked companies 1 to 3500 based on their Pre-tax Return on Invested Tangible Capital (ROIC). The best ROC companies we will rank the highest. So we take the 3500 largest stocks in our database and rank them on ROC just straight out. And then we did the same thing for cheap, we ranked 3500 companies on earnings yield: 1 – 3500 on earnings yield. We used last year's numbers. It was the first thing we tried. It (last year's numbers) is good information to have, but certainly it is not disputable information to have.

为了简便起见，我们采用了去年的数据，没有使用五年平均值或预测值。这是我们的初次尝试，力求简单明了。可以想象，使用去年数据会存在诸多问题，比如数据未经过标准化处理、存在异常值等。尽管这些数据很有参考价值，但确实并非绝对可靠。这些数据并非预测值，也没有采用过去五年的任意平均值。在进行回测时，这样做很危险，因为分析师的判断会随时间变化，他们有时会高估有时低估——每个人都在不断进化。因此我们避开了这一切。分析师的预测调整缓慢，所以我们直接采用最简单的数字——去年的数据。

<!--en-->
We wanted to make it easy so we used *last year's* numbers. We didn't use five-year averages or projections. This is the *first thing we tried*, we kept it simple. You can imagine all the problems with using last year's numbers, they are not normalized. There are aberrations. It is good information to have but it is certainly not disputable information. It wasn't projections. It is not using an arbitrary number or average over the past five years. When you are back testing, it is dangerous because people adjust all the time or use estimates. The question is that analysts get better over time, they over estimate, they underestimate—everyone evolves. So we didn't use any of that. Analysts' estimates adjust slowly so they change slowly. We use the simplest number—last year's numbers.

我们寻找的是ROIC高且盈利收益率也高的公司。听起来并不复杂。我们按ROIC对3500家公司排名（1到3500），再按盈利收益率排名（1到3500）。然后将这两个排名合并。如果某公司的ROIC排名第50位、盈利收益率排名第100位，那么其综合排名即为$150 (50th rank in ROC + 100th in earnings yield) = 150th ranking$。这种方法非常实用。显然，我们希望得到的是标准化后的数据而非滞后数据，但这一点并无争议。

<!--en-->
We sought companies with high ROIC *and* a high earnings yield. It doesn't sound that complicated. We ranked from 1 to 3500 on ROC and 1 – 3500 on earnings yield. We *combined* the rankings. If you had the 50th best ROC and the 100th best earnings yield your combined ranking was $150 (50th rank in ROC + 100th in earnings yield) = 150th ranking$. This is very helpful. Obviously we would rather have a normalized number than a trailing number but there was no dispute about this.

这项研究针对的是排名前3500的公司。1988年，我们运用“神奇公式”取得的收益率为27%，而市场等权重平均收益率仅为24.4%。我们选取排名最高的30只股票构成投资组合（属于前10%的股票），每只股票在组合中持有一年。具体时间为1988年1月至1989年1月、1988年2月至1989年2月，以此类推……我们在17年间共计算了193个滚动年度周期。我们使用了众多投资组合，最终取这些组合的平均值。总之，我们涵盖了大量的时间段和股票。“神奇公式”所涉及的30只股票（从3500只中选出）的收益率约为30%。我们设定的市值门槛为5000万美元以上，同时要求这些小盘股必须具备一定的交易量才能被纳入样本。我们还有最低交易量的要求，因此人们无法辩称这些结果是由于“小盘股效应”导致的——毕竟投资者能够买到这些股票。

<!--en-->
This is for the top 3500 companies. This is what we did in 1988 we did 27% using the magic formula vs. 24.4% using a market equally weighted average. In that 30 stock portfolios of highest ranked stocks (the top or 1st deciles) and each stock was held in the portfolio for one year. What we did was Jan. 1988 to Jan 1989, then Feb. 1988 to Feb. 1989 and so on..... We measured 193 periods during the 17 years using rolling one year periods. We used many, many portfolios and it was the average of those portfolios. The bottom line is that we used a lot of time periods and stocks. The magic formula stocks (30 out of the 3500 stocks) did about 30%
We used market caps above $50 million and we had criteria that those small caps had to have a certain amount of volume to be included. We had a minimum trading volume requirement also. People couldn't say that the results were because of the *small cap effect* where investors wouldn't be able to buy the shares.

所以你可以说：“你知道这些股票规模太小了。”正如你会在书中看到的——*我们*对市值在10亿美元以上的最大1000只股票也做了同样的分析。每年有80%的基金经理无法跑赢标普500指数。但这并不意味着同一位经理每年都无法超越市场。长期跑赢市场确实很难，但我们投资组合的回报率几乎是标普500指数的两倍（我们的投资组合回报率为22%，而标普500指数为12.4%）。我们根据资本回报率（1–3500）和盈利收益率（1–3500）对股票进行排名，然后采用等权重法合并这些排名。有些公司可能未上榜，是因为它们并不够便宜。最终排名取决于综合排名结果。每年我们会构建12个投资组合，再取它们的平均回报率。因此每项测试都能覆盖多年数据。这些回报并非源于某个月份的运气，而是所有月份共同作用的结果。从这张图表中可以看出几点。

<!--en-->
So you could say, “You know the stocks are too small.” So—as you will see in the book—*we* did the same thing for the largest 1000 stocks with $1 billion market cap and over. 80% of the managers each year can’t beat the S&P 500. And that doesn’t mean the same manager doesn’t beat the market each year. To beat it over time is tough but we basically doubled the return of the S&P 500 (12.4% return vs. 22% for our portfolio). We ranked stocks based on the best return on capital (1 – 3500) and earnings yield (1 3500) and then combined the rankings using an equal weighting. A company might not make the list because it wasn’t that cheap. The ranking depends upon the best combined rankings. There were 12 portfolios a year so we averaged the returns. So we got a lot of years out of each test. The returns weren’t due to just a lucky Jan. or a lucky July, it was a combination of all of those (months).

### 持有期限

<!--en-->
*Holding Periods*

也有未能跑赢市场的时候，比如2002年。当年该投资组合下跌22.7%，而市场仅下跌22%，差距为-0.7%。在大盘股表现不佳的时期，这套“神奇公式”产生的波动并不比市场更大。**坏事难免发生，这很艰难，但你必须坚持到底，因为最终一切都会好起来。** 我在此想说的是……那1000只最大市值股票中存在的缺陷是什么？共有360只股票，每只持有一年。换手期为一年，每隻股票均被持有整整一年。

<!--en-->
There were times it didn’t beat the market like in 2002. In 2002 it was down 22.7% vs. the market being down 22%—a difference of negative 0.7%. The magic formula wasn’t much more volatile than the market during the bad times for the big stocks. **Bad stuff happens which is tough but you have to stay the course because things work out in the end.** My argument here.....what would be the flaws in the largest 1000 stocks? There were 360 stocks each held for a year. Turnover was for one (1) year. Every stock was held for one year.

#### 小盘股效应

<!--en-->
*Small Cap Effect*

在这一时期，小盘股的表现既无优势也无劣势——其实并不存在所谓的小盘股效应。无论你查看哪种数据库，当你购买价值股时，**通常买到的都是规模较小的股票**，因为这些股票不受市场青睐。由于不受青睐，它们的市值较低、价格也较低。市值等于股价乘以完全稀释后的流通股数，因此价值股往往倾向于具有较小的市值。这些股票不受青睐，所以人们不会为它们支付高价；价格较高的股票则更受欢迎。销售额并无差异，但因其不受青睐且无人愿出高价，所以市值较小。

<!--en-->
Small caps in this period did no better or worse—it really wasn’t the small cap effect. When you buy value stocks no matter what databases you are looking at **you are generally buying smaller stocks** because the stocks are out of favor. The market caps are depressed because they are out of favor and they have low prices. Market cap is price x fully diluted outstanding shares so value stocks are *skewed* toward the smaller market caps. The stocks are out of favor so people are not paying a lot for them. The higher priced ones are popular. The sales are not different but the market cap is smaller because they are out of favor and people are not paying a lot for them.

你可能会认为流动性是个问题。就像格雷厄姆选中的股票逐渐消失一样——尽管乔尔·格林布拉特每年、每月都重复这一操作，在我们进行的三次测试中，总共筛选了超过4500只股票——你或许会认为这些选中的股票也会像格雷厄姆的股票那样逐渐消失。市场可能会变得更有效率等等。我认为这种看法并不十分成立。但这确实是我会予以重视的一种观点。

<!--en-->
You could argue that liquidity was a problem here. Just as *Graham’s* stocks disappeared— his (Joel Greenblatt’s) thirty favorites even though he did it every year and every month, between the three tests we did, we did over 4500 stock picks over the time—you might argue that the picks might go away like what happened to *Graham’s* stocks. The market could get more efficient, etc. I don’t think it is particularly valid. But that is one argument I would be sensitive to.

### 机会的消失

<!--en-->
*The Opportunities Disappear*

于是我们又对前2500只股票进行了另一项测试，并按排名将其分为十个等级。排名最好的为第1组；其次为第2组……直至第10组。各组的业绩表现与排名顺序几乎完全吻合：第1组回报率为18%，第2组为17.5%，第3组为15%，以此类推。我的观点是：如果前30只股票不起作用，接下来的30只股票就会表现良好。**一切是按顺序进行的。** 如果你能掌握一些信息，并预知某只股票未来的走势，那无疑是宝贵的信息。

<!--en-->
So we did another test of the top 2500 stocks and we divided them by rankings into deciles. The best ranking was deciles 1; the second best ranking was in deciles 2... to deciles 10. The performance matched the declining deciles almost perfectly. The top deciles made 18%, then the second did 17.5%, the third did 15%, etc. My argument is that if the first 30 don’t work, the next 30 stocks will do well. **It works in order.** If you know a couple of things and you know what a stock is going to do in the future, that is probably valuable information.

### 乔尔·格林布拉特的实际操作或哥谭合伙公司的投资方式与该书所述有何不同？

<!--en-->
*What JG Does or How Gotham Partners Invests vs. What the Book Suggests*

我们（*哥谭合伙公司*）所了解的情况比我书中写的要多一些。但我认为，如果能将人们的股票回报率翻一番，或将小盘股的回报率提高到近三倍，那便是值得的。**我们确实会寻找这两类指标（高ROIC和高盈利收益率），但我们使用的不是去年的盈利数据，而是经调整后的盈利数据。** 大多数人无法理解这一点。我们对大多数股票也无法确定，但对于那些我们能够确定的股票，我们寻找的是基于*经调整数据*的实物资本回报率较高、且盈利收益率也较高的公司。这其实非常合乎逻辑。

<!--en-->
We (*Gotham Partners*) know a little bit more than what I wrote in the book. But I figured if you could double people’s returns in stocks or close to triple the return in small stocks that was worthwhile. **We do look for these two things (high ROIC and high earnings yield) but instead of looking at last year’s earnings we use normalized earnings.** Most people can’t figure that out. We can’t figure it out for most stocks, but for those stocks where we can figure it out, we are looking for companies with high returns on tangible capital on a *normalized* basis and high earnings yield based on *normalized* earnings. That is just very logical.

第一个故事是关于一本书：《华尔街上的成功之道》（2005年），作者是Shaughnessy，书中探讨了投资公式。他回测了40种在市场上有效的公式，从中挑出表现最好的几种，并据此设立了一只共同基金。第一年基金表现一般，第二年业绩落后25%，第三年更是逊于所有竞争对手。三年后，他的基金表现糟糕透顶。之后他把基金卖给了别人，自己另谋出路。

<!--en-->
The first story is about a book written called, *What works on Wall Street (2005)* by Shaughnessy about investing formulas. The guy back tested 40 formulas on what worked in the market. He tested dozens of formulas and picked the ones that performed the best and started a mutual fund. The first year the fund didn't do so well, then the second year his fund underperformed by 25% and then the third year he underperformed compared to all his competitors. So after three years, he suffered terrible underperformance. After that he sold his fund to someone else and he found something else to do.

**写这本书、做了所有研究并确信其有效的人，最终却放弃了，还把基金管理公司卖掉了。** 接手Shaughnessy业务的人继续沿用该公式，结果取得了巨大成功。Shaughnessy自己却无法坚持。事情并非如此简单；它并非永远奏效。**如果它永远有效，那它根本就不会起作用。** 另一个故事是关于Richard Pzena的，他于1996年创业。头四年他业绩不佳。但他决定继续坚持自己认为有效的做法（即买入标准化盈利基础上价格最低的股票）。当所有客户都离开时，仍能坚持下来需要极大的毅力。如果他不是为自己工作，早就被解雇了。Rich使用公式选股，该公式曾多年奏效，但后来却失效了。

<!--en-->
**The guy who wrote the book, who did all the studies and who knew that it worked, he quit and sold his fund management company to someone else.** This person who purchased Shaughnessy's business continued to use the formula and has been tremendously successful. Shaughnessy couldn't take it. This is not a straight thing; it doesn't work all the time. **If it worked all the time, it wouldn't work at all.**
Another story is about *Richard Pzena*, who started his business in 1996. He was underperforming for four years. He decided to keep doing what he knew worked (*He bought the market's lowest price to earnings stocks on a normalized basis*). That takes fortitude to stick to it when all your customers are walking out the door. If he wasn't working for himself he would have been fired. Rich used a formula and picked stocks from that formula. It had worked for many, many years and it wasn't working.

五年后的今天，他已跻身所有基金经理前1%之列，管理着超过150亿美元的机构资金，拥有众多投资者。他有数百个机构投资者，但最初的投资人只剩4个，我就是其中之一——因为我是他的朋友。

## 持有期限

<!--en-->
*Holding Period*

**我们使用过去一年的业绩数据。** 如果你持有超过一年，比如两年，该策略依然有效。我选择一年是为了税务考虑——实际上这并非最佳周期。一年能提供最新的数据；若持有更久，所用的就是两年前的数据。人们当然希望用较新的数据而非过时数据，因此我们每年都会滚动更新投资组合。一旦换手频率超过一年，就会产生交易成本。你会在一年内卖出亏损股，而在一年后卖出盈利股。因此一年周期更高效，也更节税。

<!--en-->
**We are using trailing one year results.** If you hold it for more one year, say two years, it still works. I picked one year for tax purposes—it wasn't actually the best period. One year gives the freshest data because if you hold for another year, you are using two year old data. You would rather have fresher data than way outdated data, so we refresh the portfolio each year on a rolling basis. Once you have faster than one year turnover then you get into transaction costs. You sell your losers in less than a year and your winners in more than one year. So one year is more efficient and more tax efficient.

**学生：** 你会用这种方法进行卖空交易吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Would you use this to short stocks?

**JG：** 我还没准备好分享这一点。

<!--en-->
**JG:** I wasn't prepared to share that.

我对多空策略的看法是：那些利用特殊情形进行卖空的人，往往是在利用骗局或公司资金耗尽的机会。我喜欢这类卖空操作，尽管自己并不擅长。但如果是*估值卖空*，我就不赞同了。这种策略每隔七八年就会出问题——卖空股上涨而多头股下跌，每个量化投资者都会遇到这种情况。我并非说多空对冲基金没有意义。但如果我从三到四年的视角出发，并不在意短期波动，那为何要因卖空而放弃每年2.5%的回报呢？这并不能创造额外价值。因为我每年会损失2.5%，而我并不关心波动性问题。

<!--en-->
My quibble with long/shorts—the guys who do special situations in shorts where it is a scam or the company will run out of money. I like those type of shorts though I am not particularly good at them. If you are doing *valuation shorts* then I don't like that. That strategy blows up every seven or eight years—the shorts go up and the longs go down and that happens to every quant guy. I am not saying a long/short hedge funds doesn't make sense. But If I don't value short term volatility because I take a three or four year view. Then why giveup 2.5% a year in returns by shorting. I am not adding value. This doesn't add value because I am losing 2.5% a year and I don't care about volatility.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**学生：** 当你挑选前30只股票时，是从排名前十的股票开始的吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** When you pick your top 30 do you start with your top deciles?

**JG：** 当我们寻找股票时，会做各种事情，比如查看股票筛选结果。然后我们会研究目标公司的竞争对手，并进行阅读分析。我的做法没那么结构化；我更看重资本的正常化高回报——无论税前ROIC是50%还是80%，只要回报高就是好的，回报极高更是绝佳。此外还有“便宜”这一要素……这里还涉及其他考量因素。**你需要选取正常化的盈利数据，还要确定正常的增长率以及我对这些预测的信心程度。** 巴菲特追求的是那种他对正常化盈利及其增长率有十足把握的情况。这些都是判断股票是否便宜的其他要素，同时还要考虑长期增长率等因素。说白了，如果它确实便宜，那就不言而喻了（根本无需多想）。我不会急着打开电脑去计算它有多便宜。当初我们分析Aeropostale时，都认定它很便宜；我们承担的风险不大，且若新商业模式成功就能赚钱。我会遵循同样的思路，凭自己的判断来做决策。我这么做是为了给你信心。

<!--en-->
**JG:** When we find stocks, we do various things like look at stock screens. Then we look at competitors of the company we are looking at, we do reading. I would be less structured as this, I care about normalized high returns on capital though I don't care if its 50% pre-tax ROIC or 80% ROIC, but I just say good is good and really good is really good. And then cheap....there are other elements here. **You pick normalized earnings and you also want to pick a normalized growth rate and how confident I am in those projections.**
Buffett wants the certain one where he is pretty certain about normalized earnings and its growth rate. Those are other elements to decide how cheap it is taking into account the long term growth rates and things of that nature. Once again, drive a truck through it (it should be obvious; it is cheap). I am not running to a computer to see how cheap it is. When we did an analysis of Aeropostale we all came to a conclusion that it was cheap, and we weren't risking a lot and we could make money if the new concept takes off. I would go through the same thesis and use my head to figure it out. I would this for to give you confidence.

我使用“魔法公式”及对应的股票列表的目的，是在你内心确信其合理性及长期有效性时，为你提供*信心*。我在书中提到过，明白“二加二等于四”这一道理（即如何给资产估值非常重要）。无论别人怎么说、报纸上怎么报道，或者该观点多么不受欢迎，只要“二加二等于四”是真理，你就应坚持它。两周后我们会详细讲解为何这种方法在组合投资中尤其有效。当你持有的股票下跌20%时，你仍会*坚持使用它*。

<!--en-->
What I would use this (The Magic Formula and the list of magic formula stocks) for is to give you *confidence* if you know it in your gut (*that it makes sense and it works over time*). What I said in the book, knowing two plus two equals four (*how to value something is very powerful*). It doesn't matter what other people say or the newspaper says or how unpopular it is if two plus two equals four. If you know two plus two equals four, then you stick with it. In two weeks we will go over why this makes sense especially in the basket approach. You will *stick with it* when you have those down 20% years.

相信我，当你回顾17年数据并计算平均值时，任何人都会觉得这种方法行之有效。**但在实际运用过程中，当你的投资组合下跌25%时，你却很难确定它是否仍在发挥作用。** 这合理吗？情况有变化吗？明年真的能实现预期收益吗？又或者像报纸行业那样，曾经是优质生意，如今却每况愈下。

<!--en-->
Believe me, when you look over 17 years and you calculate the averages it looks like any idiot should know that this works. **But in the middle of doing it when you are down 25% you don't really know if it is still working.** Does it make sense? Have things changed? Is it really going to earn that next year? Or newspapers were a great franchise, but they are no longer a great franchise and they are running down.

*Blockbuster*去年盈利颇丰，但那毕竟是个日渐衰落的行业。我这样做真的对吗？情况会变得很棘手。刚开始运用“魔法公式”时(*遵循魔法公式*)很容易，但当你因此亏损，或他人表现更好时，情况就完全不同了。人们常指责我把事情说得过于简单——我猜是这样。（学生笑声）

<!--en-->
*Blockbuster* had high earnings last year and but that is a dying business. Am I really doing the right thing? It gets tough. That (*following the Magic Formula*) is easy to do when you first start doing it, but when you are losing money doing it or everyone else is doing much better it becomes a totally different thing. I am usually accused of making everything sound too easy—I am guessing. (Laughter from students).

我心中始终坚信：我的做法是有道理的，我的计算也是合理的。我必须反复告诉自己这一点，才能有所依托；确保你的决策是合理的。我在书中一步步解释了为何这种方法可行，为何高ROIC至关重要，你必须明白自己的做法是有道理的。

<!--en-->
I do have this in my head. What I am doing makes sense and what I am calculating makes sense. And I have to keep telling myself that a lot of times but to have things like this to cling to; that what you are doing makes sense. I go step by step in the book why this makes sense. Why high ROIC makes sense and you need to know that what you are doing makes sense.

### 最初创办对冲基金

<!--en-->
*Originally Opening Up a Hedge Fund*

在为一家对冲基金从事并购套利工作几年后，我从*迈克尔·米尔肯*那里筹集到了资金。

<!--en-->
I raised money from *Michael Milken* after working for a few years for a hedge fund doing merger arbitrage.

从*米尔肯*身上学到的教训：他能极度专注于一点。无论有多少干扰，他都能专心于手头的工作。这对我而言是一堂宝贵的课。

<!--en-->
Lesson from *Milken*: he could stay very focused on this one point. He stayed focused on what he was doing at the time no matter what the distractions. A good lesson for me.

我声名鹊起是因为27岁时在与*罗恩·佩雷尔曼*谈判时让他等了一个小时。如果第一年能赚到30%，我就算回本了。这是一笔成本高昂的业务。但我只接受了对方报价的一半，因为我知道如果我表现出色，他将提供无限的资金支持。

<!--en-->
My claim to fame was that I kept *Ron Perelman* waiting for an hour while negotiating my deal at age 27
If I made 30% in the first year was my break even. It was a high cost business. But I took half of what he offered me because I knew there was an unlimited checkbook if I did well.

**JG:** Yes, there are and I don't know if they are the ones you want to be buying but we took what we got. Companies that are always cheap, maybe there is something wrong with them.

Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The averages were calculated on a large amount of stocks so the results were more robust. We used a database from *Compustat*.

## 对魔法公式投资的质疑之声。

<!--en-->
*Arguments against the Magic Formula Investing.*

当时相关数据不可得，因此只能进行回溯测试。于是我们采用了*Compustat数据库*。因此幸存者偏差并不重要。“他们清除了数据库中破产的公司，”批评者可能会这么说。但同样，这并不重要。小公司因交易成本高而无法被买入。我们选用了1000只大盘股，而该公式依然表现良好。

<!--en-->
The data was not available at the time so you were back testing. So we used the *CompustatDatabase*. Thus survivorship bias was irrelevant. “Well they cleaned up the database by taking out the bankrupt companies,” critics could say. Again, it was irrelevant. Small companies can’t be purchased without high transaction costs. We used 1000 big cap stocks, and the formula still worked well.

*法玛与弗伦奇的研究*认为，一切都是由低市净率、贝塔系数以及小盘股效应决定的。我认为这项研究很荒谬。小盘股只是不受青睐的一种表现；低市净率恰好意味着股价便宜，但这并非其便宜的原因——它们只是碰巧便宜罢了。这才是寻找低价股票更直接的方法。它们碰巧便宜，并非因其本身具有某种特殊价值。这种逻辑在现实中并不成立，我认为该研究完全偏离了重点。

<!--en-->
The *Fama & French Study*-everything was determined by low/price to book, Beta and small cap effect. My opinion was that it was a ridiculous study. Small caps were one indication of being out of favor; low price to book happens to be cheap, but it is not why it is cheap. They just happen to be cheap. This is a much more direct way of finding cheap stocks. They happen to be cheap that is not why it is cheap. On the side it works that is really not how the market works. I think that study is completely missing the point.

但他们却声称：“我们不仅用低市净率股票跑赢了市场，而且这些股票波动性更低。并非市场无效，而是因为存在一些我们无法识别的风险。（真蠢！）”

<!--en-->
But they came out and say, “Not only did we beat the market with our low price to book stocks but they were less volatile. It is not that the market is inefficient it is because of risks we can’t find. (Stupid!)

关于*贝塔系数*的一点评论：如果你打算购买一家公司的股票，那么波动性对风险有何影响其实毫无意义。用过去六个月的股价波动来衡量风险根本站不住脚。

<!--en-->
A comment on *Beta*. If you think of owning a share of a company, how volatility makes any difference regarding risk is nonsensical. How volatile the stock price is over the past six months makes no sense in analyzing risk.

他们发现低市净率的股票波动性更低且回报更好。这种回报其实源于其他我们无法察觉或描述的风险。要想赚更多钱，就必须承担更大风险。这些公司往往是劣质企业——这正是它们能跑赢市场的原因（隐藏的风险）。

<!--en-->
They found out that the stocks with low price/book values were less volatile and had better returns. The returns have to do with other risks we can’t find or can’t describe. You take on more risks to make more money. These companies are crummy companies—that is why they beat the market (hidden risks).

*法玛与弗伦奇*无法用这一论点来反驳“魔法公式股票”。总体而言，这类股票属于优质公司。它们大多负债不多，不会破产，也不需要大量资本投入，却能创造丰厚利润。

<!--en-->
*Fama & French* can’t make this argument against the Magic Formula Stocks. On average these stocks are good companies. Many don’t have much debt, they are not going bankrupt and they don’t need much capital. They are earnings a lot of money.

即便他们是对的——其实并非如此——接下来的论点就是*数据挖掘*。即抛出大量数据，找出效果显著的因素后再展示结果。**答案是：这正是我们最初尝试的方法。** 我们的投资方式基于质量和价格，而非任何先前的研究。我们并未进行预先研究，只是好奇这种方法的效果如何。

<!--en-->
Even if they were right, which they are not, then the next argument is *data-mining*. You spit out a lot of data and find out what factors work great then show the results. **The answer to that is that this is the first thing we tried.** This is based on the way we invest not based on any previous study. We invest based on quality and price. We did no previous studies. We were just curious to see how well it worked.

我写这篇文章的另一个目的是为人们提供一个简单易用的指标。我没想到它会有如此好的效果。我仍然认为同样的论点依然适用：已有许多跑赢市场的研究，**价值投资其实很难。** 你可以设立基金，专门投资低市盈率股票以跑赢市场。确实有人这样做，甚至有人建立了包含71个因子模型的基金。但这个双因子模型却胜过了那71因子模型。虽然存在能跑赢市场的模型，但要在市场中持续盈利仍十分困难。

<!--en-->
The other answer as to why I wrote this was to come up with an easy metric for people to use. I had no idea it was going to work this well. I still think the same arguments apply which is there have been many market beating studies, **value investing is hard.** You can set up a fund to beat the market with low P/E stocks. There are guys who have set up funds to beat the market investing in low P/E stocks and nothing else. Believe me there are guys who have 71 factor models. This two factor model beats the seventy one factor model. There are models to beat the market, but it is still tough to stay in business and do that.

**学生：** 您是如何获取数据的？是通过彭博终端导出吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** How do you get the data? Do you do a Bloomberg dump.

**JG：** 我通过阅读学习。*沃顿商学院*仍在教授有效市场理论。我通过阅读格雷厄姆、德雷曼和巴菲特的作品来学习。我一直希望有朝一日能写作以回馈社会，这也是我教书的原因——我乐在其中。我在写这本书时，开始为读者寻找可用的数据库。我查看了《商业周刊》的数据库，因为BW归标普所有，而标普拥有Compustat数据，但BW网站并未使用Compustat数据——而这正是我们研究中所用的数据。我们希望避免使用那些晦涩难懂的数据库，因为*本书是为大众撰写的*。对你们来说没问题，因为你们可以动脑思考：“嗯，由于某项特殊因素，这说不通……”我不建议盲目照搬。但如果我为大众写书，就会有些担心——因为他们可能会用EBIT和有形资本回报率来编程。这相当困难，有些数据库甚至无法支持。

<!--en-->
**JG:** I learn from reading. *Wharton Business School* still teaches efficient market theory. I learn by reading *Graham, Dreman* and *Buffett*. I always thought about one day writing as a way to give back. That is why I teach also, I enjoy doing it. I was writing this book, and I started looking for databases to for readers to use. I looked at Business Week database because BW is owned by S&P which owns Compustat, but the BW site doesn’t use the Compustat data which was the data we used for the study. We wanted to avoid the gibberish of many databases because *this book was written for the masses*. For you guys it is fine because you can actually use your head and say, “Well, that doesn’t make sense because of a special item there, etc. I wouldn’t recommend blindly doing this. But if I am writing this book for the masses, I am a little worried because they are programming in EBIT and return on tangible capital. It is kind of tough to do, and you can’t really do it in some of these.

顺便提一下，哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资课程”中，有些同学正在学习低市盈率与高净资产收益率策略（冯·穆夫林课程）。事实证明，**低市盈率与高净资产收益率投资策略相当出色。** 虽然类似，但概念上略有不同。低市盈率与高净资产收益率确实很好，但我认为这个“魔法公式”显然更优——它能更好地考虑税收和资本结构的差异，数据也证明了这一点。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
By the way, some of you are in that class where low P/E and high ROE is used (Von Mueffling Class). It turns out that **low P/E and high ROE investing is pretty darn good.** This is better, but the concepts are similar. Low P/E and high ROE is great. This (Magic Formula) is obviously better, because it takes into account differences in taxes and capital structure much better in my opinion and the data bears that out.

我们的研究中排除了金融和公用事业公司。不过我认为低市盈率与高净资产收益率策略在这些行业中同样适用。

<!--en-->
We leave out finance and utility companies in our study. I would say low P/E and high ROE would work pretty well there too.

**学生：** 您有没有考虑过只投资高ROIC的公司，而不管其价格如何？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Did you take a look at just investing in high ROIC companies regardless of price:

**JG：** 如果不考虑价格，我可不称之为投资。我绝不会在不考虑价格的情况下投资，尤其是借助计算机时。或许市场确实会低估高ROIC企业，但我绝不会单独使用这一指标而不结合价格来看。这是什么样的企业？我能低价买入吗？没错，我只关注这两点。

<!--en-->
**JG:** If you don't take into account price, I don't call that investing. I would never invest without considering price especially using a computer. I guess the market could always underestimate high ROIC businesses, but I would never think of using that metric without combining it with price. What type of business is it and can I buy it cheap? OK? I am just sticking to those two things.

**确定标准化收益才是最难的部分。真正的难点在于：当市场与你意见相左时，你能否坚持自己的选择并贯彻到底。** 这才是难点所在。这就是问题的全部关键。

<!--en-->
**The hard part coming up with normalized earnings. The hard part is really living with your choice and sticking to your guns when the market disagrees with you.** That is the hard part. That is the whole ball of wax.

**学生：** 这种投资方式在欧洲行得通吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Does this type of investing work in Europe?

**JG：** 有史以来进行的每一项价值研究都证明，该策略在不同市场和时间段内均有效。从未有过与之相悖的情况。

<!--en-->
**JG:** Every value study that has ever been done has worked across all markets over time. There has never been a contradiction to this.
