3. 关于乔尔·格林布拉特的文章《商誉及其摊销：规则与现实（伯克希尔1983年年度报告）》（文中讨论了以有形资本回报率作为评判企业标准的问题）

账面价值 vs. 内在价值

我们以账面价值来衡量自身的进展，因为在我们的情况下（尽管并非所有情况都是如此），它是衡量企业内在价值增长的保守但相当合理的替代指标——这才是真正重要的衡量标准。账面价值作为记录指标的优点在于它易于计算，且无需涉及计算内在价值时所用的那些主观（但重要）的判断。然而，重要的是要理解“账面价值”和“内在价值”这两个术语的含义截然不同。账面价值是一个会计概念，记录了来自投入资本和留存收益的累计财务投入；内在价值则是一个经济概念，用于估算未来现金流折算成现值后的结果。账面价值告诉你已经投入了多少；内在价值则估计能从中获取多少。一个类比可以说明其中的差别：假设你为两个孩子上大学花费了相同的金额。从财务投入来看，每个孩子教育的账面价值是相同的。但未来回报的现值（即内在价值）可能相差巨大——从零到教育成本的数倍不等。那么，投入资金相同的企业，其最终价值也会存在巨大差异吗？

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程

在伯克希尔，1965财年初现任管理层接手时，每股19.46美元的账面价值严重高估了内在价值。这些账面价值全部由纺织资产构成，而这些资产平均而言根本无法产生适当的回报率。用前面的类比来说，对纺织资产的投资就如同对几乎毫无用处的高等教育进行投资。

如今，我们的内在价值已大大超过账面价值。主要原因有两点：（1）根据标准会计原则，我们保险子公司持有的普通股需按市场价值计入账目，而我们持有的其他股票则按成本与市价孰低者计价。1983年底，后一类股票的市场价值比账面价值高出7000万美元（税前），税后约为5000万美元。这部分差额应计入内在价值，却未被纳入账面价值的计算；（2）更重要的是，我们拥有几家具备巨大经济商誉的企业（这类商誉理应计入内在价值），而资产负债表上所记载的会计商誉远远低于实际水平。商誉无论是经济意义上的还是会计意义上的，都是一个深奥的话题，此处难以详尽解释。随信附上的附录《商誉及其摊销：规则与现实》将说明为何经济商誉与会计商誉往往存在巨大差异。

人们即便从不思考商誉及其摊销问题，也能过上充实而有意义的生活。但投资与管理专业的学生应当了解这一主题的细微之处。**我个人的观念与35年前相比已发生巨变——那时我被教导要偏爱有形资产，回避那些价值主要依赖于经济商誉的企业。**这种偏见导致我犯下了许多因疏忽而造成的重要商业错误，虽主动犯错的情况相对较少。凯恩斯一针见血地指出了我的问题：“困难不在于接受新观念，而在于摆脱旧观念。”我的转变迟迟未能实现，部分原因是同一位老师所传授给我的知识大多至今仍具有极高的价值。 归根结底，无论是直接还是间接积累的商业经验，都使我如今强烈倾向于选择那些拥有大量持久性商誉、且使用的有形资产极少的企业。

<!--en-->
1. Buffett Writing on ROIC
2. Magic Formula Slide Presentation by Joel Greenblatt
3. Article on Joel Greenblatt
**Goodwill and its Amortization: The Rules and The Realities (BERKSHIRE'S 1983 Annual Report)**
*(Discussion of using tangible return on capital as a judge of businesses)*
Book Value vs. Intrinsic Value
We report our progress in terms of book value because in our case (though not, by any means, in all cases) it is a conservative but reasonably adequate proxy for growth in intrinsic business value - *the measurement that really counts*. Book value's virtue as a score-keeping measure is that it is easy to calculate and doesn't involve the subjective (but important) judgments employed in calculation of intrinsic business value. It is important to understand, however, that the two terms - book value and intrinsic business value - have very different meanings.
Book value is an accounting concept, recording the accumulated financial input from both contributed capital and retained earnings. Intrinsic business value is an economic concept, estimating future cash output discounted to present value. Book value tells you what has been put in; intrinsic business value estimates what can be taken out.
An analogy will suggest the difference. Assume you spend identical amounts putting each of two children through college. The book value (measured by financial input) of each child's education would be the same. But the present value of the future payoff (the intrinsic business value) might vary enormously - from zero to many times the cost of the education. So, also, do businesses having equal financial input end up with wide variations in value?
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
At Berkshire, at the beginning of fiscal 1965 when the present management took over, the $19.46 per share book value considerably overstated intrinsic business value. All of that book value consisted of textile assets that could not earn, on average, anything close to an appropriate rate of return. In the terms of our analogy, the investment in textile assets resembled investment in a largely-wasted education.
Now, however, our intrinsic business value considerably exceeds book value. There are two major reasons:
(1) Standard accounting principles require that common stocks held by our insurance subsidiaries be stated on our books at market value, but that other stocks we own be carried at the lower of aggregate cost or market. At the end of 1983, the market value of this latter group exceeded carrying value by $70 million pre-tax or about $50 million after tax. This excess belongs in our intrinsic business value, but is not included in the calculation of book value;
(2) More important, we own several businesses that possess economic Goodwill (which is properly includable in intrinsic business value) far larger than the accounting Goodwill that is carried on our balance sheet and reflected in book value.
Goodwill, both economic and accounting, is an arcane subject and requires more explanation than is appropriate here. The appendix that follows this letter - "Goodwill and its Amortization: The Rules and The Realities" - explains why economic and accounting Goodwill can, and usually do, differ enormously.
You can live a full and rewarding life without ever thinking about Goodwill and its amortization. But students of investment and management should understand the nuances of the subject. **My own thinking has changed drastically from 35 years ago when I was taught to favor tangible assets and to shun businesses whose value depended largely upon economic Goodwill.** This bias caused me to make many important business mistakes of omission, although relatively few of commission.
Keynes identified my problem: "The difficulty lies not in the new ideas but in escaping from the old ones." My escape was long delayed, in part because most of what I had been taught by the same teacher had been (and continues to be) so extraordinarily valuable. Ultimately, business experience, direct and vicarious, produced my present strong preference for businesses that possess large amounts of enduring Goodwill and that utilize a minimum of tangible assets.

## 商誉及其摊销：规则与现实

<!--en-->
*Goodwill and its Amortization: The Rules and The Realities*

本附录仅讨论经济意义上的商誉和会计意义上的商誉，而非日常用语中的“商誉”。例如，一家企业可能深受大多数客户的喜爱甚至追捧，但却并不具备经济商誉。（AT&T在拆分前口碑极佳，却并未拥有任何经济商誉。）遗憾的是，有些企业虽遭客户厌恶，却可能拥有可观且不断增长的经济商誉。因此，暂且抛开情感因素，仅从经济和会计角度进行分析。

<!--en-->
This appendix deals only with economic and accounting Goodwill – not the goodwill of everyday usage. For example, a business may be well liked, even loved, by most of its customers but possess no economic goodwill. (AT&T, before the breakup, was generally well thought of, but possessed not a dime of economic Goodwill.) And, regrettably, a business may be disliked by its customers but possess substantial, and growing, economic Goodwill. So, just for the moment, forget emotions and focus only on economics and accounting.

当企业被收购时，会计准则要求将收购价格首先分配到所购可辨认资产的公允价值上。通常，这些资产的公允价值总和（扣除负债后）会低于企业的总收购价格。此时，差额会被记入名为“成本超过所购净资产权益的部分”的资产账户。为避免反复提及这一冗长的表述，我们将其简称为“商誉”。

<!--en-->
When a business is purchased, accounting principles require that the purchase price first be assigned to the fair value of the identifiable assets that are acquired. Frequently the sum of the fair values put on the assets (after the deduction of liabilities) is less than the total purchase price of the business. In that case, the difference is assigned to an asset account entitled "excess of cost over equity in net assets acquired". To avoid constant repetition of this mouthful, we will substitute "Goodwill".

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程指出：1970年11月之前收购的企业所产生的会计商誉具有特殊地位。除非在极少数情况下，只要被收购的企业继续存续，该商誉便可一直作为资产保留在资产负债表中。这意味着无需通过摊销费用来逐步冲销该项资产，从而不会影响企业盈利。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Accounting Goodwill arising from businesses purchased before November 1970 has a special standing. Except under rare circumstances, it can remain an asset on the balance sheet as long as the business bought is retained. That means no amortization charges to gradually extinguish that asset need be made against earnings.

然而，1970年11月之后进行的收购情况则有所不同。此类收购产生的商誉必须在不超过40年的期限内进行摊销，每年摊销金额相等，并计入损益表。由于40年是允许的最大期限，管理层（包括我们）通常选择这一年限。这种年度摊销费用不允许作为税收抵扣项，因此对税后利润的影响约为其他费用的两倍。

<!--en-->
The case is different, however, with purchases made from November 1970 on. When these create Goodwill, it must be amortized over not more than 40 years through charges – of equal amount in every year – to the earnings account. Since 40 years is the maximum period allowed, 40 years is what managements (including us) usually elect. This annual charge to earnings is not allowed as a tax deduction and, thus, has an effect on after-tax income that is roughly double that of most other expenses.

这就是会计商誉的运作方式。为了了解它与经济现实的差异，让我们来看一个身边的例子。我们会简化数字并大幅简化说明，以便更容易理解。同时也会提及对投资者和管理者的一些启示。

<!--en-->
That’s how accounting Goodwill works. To see how it differs from economic reality, let’s look at an example close at hand. We’ll round some figures, and greatly oversimplify, to make the example easier to follow. We’ll also mention some implications for investors and managers.

1972年初，Blue Chip Stamps以2500万美元的价格收购了See’s，当时See’s的净有形资产约为800万美元。（在本讨论中，应收账款被归类为有形资产，这一分类适用于商业分析。）这一水平的有形资产足以支撑企业运营而无需举债，仅在季节性短期时间内例外。当时See’s的税后盈利约为200万美元，这一数字似乎能保守地反映其在1972年不变币值下的未来盈利能力。

<!--en-->
Blue Chip Stamps bought See’s early in 1972 for $25 million, at which time See’s had about $8 million of net tangible assets. (Throughout this discussion, accounts receivable will be classified as tangible assets, a definition proper for business analysis.) This level of tangible assets was adequate to conduct the business without use of debt, except for short periods seasonally. See’s was earning about $2 million after tax at the time, and such earnings seemed conservatively representative of future earning power in constant 1972 dollars.

由此我们得出第一个结论：如果企业能够利用有形资产产生远超市场回报率的盈利，那么其价值显然远高于净有形资产。这种超额收益的资本化价值就是经济商誉。

<!--en-->
Thus our first lesson: businesses logically are worth far more than net tangible assets when they can be expected to produce earnings on such assets considerably in excess of market rates of return. The capitalized value of this excess return is economic Goodwill.

1972年（如今亦然），很少有企业能像See’s那样持续实现净有形资产25%的税后收益率——而且还是在不采用激进会计手段及无财务杠杆的情况下。产生高收益率的原因并非存货、应收账款或固定资产的公允市场价值，而是无形资产的综合作用，尤其是消费者对产品和员工的正面评价所形成的良好声誉。

<!--en-->
In 1972 (and now) relatively few businesses could be expected to consistently earn the 25% after tax on net tangible assets that was earned by See’s – doing it, furthermore, with conservative accounting and no financial leverage. It was not the fair market value of the inventories, receivables or fixed assets that produced the premium rates of return. Rather it was a combination of intangible assets, particularly a pervasive favorable reputation with consumers based upon countless pleasant experiences they have had with both product and personnel.

这种声誉构成了消费者特许权，使得产品对购买者而言的价值——而非生产成本——成为定价的主要决定因素。消费者特许权是经济商誉的重要来源。其他来源还包括不受利润限制的政府特许经营权（如电视台），以及在行业中长期保持低成本生产者的地位。

<!--en-->
Such a reputation creates a consumer franchise that allows the value of the product to the purchaser, rather than its production cost, to be the major determinant of selling price. Consumer franchises are a prime source of economic Goodwill. Other sources include governmental franchises not subject to profit regulation, such as television stations, and an enduring position as the low cost producer in an industry.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：让我们回到See’s案例中的会计处理。Blue Chip以比净有形资产高出1700万美元的价格收购See’s，因此需在账面上设立同等金额的商誉账户，并在40年内每年计提42.5万美元用于摊销。到1983年，经过11年的摊销后，1700万美元的商誉余额已降至约1250万美元。与此同时，Berkshire持有Blue Chip 60%的股份，因此也拥有See’s 60%的所有权。这意味着Berkshire的资产负债表上反映了See’s商誉的60%，即约750万美元。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Let's return to the accounting in the See's example. Blue Chip's purchase of See's at $17 million over net tangible assets required that a Goodwill account of this amount be established as an asset on Blue Chip's books and that $425,000 be charged to income annually for 40 years to amortize that asset. By 1983, after 11 years of such charges, the $17 million had been reduced to about $12.5 million. Berkshire, meanwhile, owned 60% of Blue Chip and, therefore, also 60% of See's. This ownership meant that Berkshire's balance sheet reflected 60% of See's Goodwill, or about $7.5 million.

1983年，伯克希尔通过合并收购了Blue Chip的剩余股份。此次合并需采用购买会计法，而非某些合并所允许的“权益结合法”。在购买会计法下，我们给予（或“支付”）给Blue Chip股东的股票的“公允价值”必须分摊到从Blue Chip收购的净资产中。这种“公允价值”的确定方式，与上市公司用股票进行收购时的惯例一致，即依据所放弃股票的市场价值来衡量。

<!--en-->
In 1983 Berkshire acquired the rest of Blue Chip in a merger that required purchase accounting as contrasted to the "pooling" treatment allowed for some mergers. Under purchase accounting, the "fair value" of the shares we gave to (or "paid") Blue Chip holders had to be spread over the net assets acquired from Blue Chip. This "fair value" was measured, as it almost always is when public companies use their shares to make acquisitions, by the market value of the shares given up.

此次“购入”的资产占Blue Chip全部资产的40%（如前所述，伯克希尔此前已持有另外60%）。伯克希尔为此支付的金额比所收到的可辨认净资产多出5170万美元，这笔差额被计入两项商誉：其中2840万美元归属于See's，2330万美元归属于《布法罗晚报》。

<!--en-->
The assets "purchased" consisted of 40% of everything owned by Blue Chip (as noted, Berkshire already owned the other 60%). What Berkshire "paid" was more than the net identifiable assets we received by $51.7 million, and was assigned to two pieces of Goodwill: $28.4 million to See's and $23.3 million to Buffalo Evening News?

因此，合并后伯克希尔持有的See's商誉由两部分组成：1971年收购时剩余的750万美元，以及1983年因购入40%股份而新产生的2840万美元。今后28年内，我们的摊销费用约为每年100万美元；2002年至2013年的12年间，摊销费用则为每年70万美元。

<!--en-->
After the merger, therefore, Berkshire was left with a Goodwill asset for See's that had two components: the $7.5 million remaining from the 1971 purchase, and $28.4 million newly created by the 40% "purchased" in 1983. Our amortization charge now will be about $1.0 million for the next 28 years, and $.7 million for the following 12 years, 2002 through 2013.

换句话说，不同的购置日期和价格导致了同一资产的两部分具有截然不同的资产价值和摊销费用。（我们重申一贯的声明：我们没有更好的会计体系可供建议。需要解决的问题极为复杂，只能依靠人为制定的规则来处理。）

<!--en-->
In other words, different purchase dates and prices have given us vastly different asset values and amortization charges for two pieces of the same asset. (We repeat our usual disclaimer: we have no better accounting system to suggest. The problems to be dealt with are mind boggling and require arbitrary rules.)

但经济现实究竟如何呢？一个事实是，自收购See's以来，每年在损益表中作为成本扣除的摊销费用并非真正的经济成本。我们之所以知道这一点，是因为See's去年在约2000万美元的有形净资产基础上创造了1300万美元的税后利润——这一业绩表明其经济商誉的价值远远超过了会计上记录的商誉初始成本。换言之，虽然会计商誉自购置之日起便不断减少，但经济商誉却以不规则但非常显著的方式增长。

<!--en-->
But what are the economic realities? One reality is that the amortization charges that have been deducted as costs in the earnings statement each year since acquisition of See's were not true economic costs. We know that because See's last year earned $13 million after taxes on about $20 million of net tangible assets – a performance indicating the existence of economic Goodwill far larger than the total original cost of our accounting Goodwill. In other words, while accounting Goodwill regularly decreased from the moment of purchase, economic Goodwill increased in irregular but very substantial fashion.

另一个事实是，未来的年度摊销费用将与经济成本并不对应。当然，See's的经济商誉有可能消失，但它不会以均匀的递减方式或类似形式缩减。更有可能的情况是，由于通货膨胀的影响，商誉的价值——即使不是按实际购买力计算——也会*增加*。

<!--en-->
Another reality is that annual amortization charges in the future will not correspond to economic costs. It is possible, of course, that See's economic Goodwill will disappear. But it won't shrink ineven decrements or anything remotely resembling them. What is more likely is that the Goodwill will *increase* – in current, if not in constant, dollars – because of inflation.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程指出：这种可能性存在的原因是，真正的经济商誉往往会随着通货膨胀按比例上升。为了说明这一点，让我们把See's这类企业与普通企业做个对比。回想一下，1972年我们收购See's时，它在800万美元的有形净资产基础上创造了约200万美元的利润（资本回报率高达25%）。假设我们设想中的普通企业当时也有200万美元的利润，但它需要1800万美元的有形净资产才能维持正常运营。由于所需有形资产上的回报率仅为11%，这家普通企业几乎不具备经济商誉。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
That probability exists because true economic Goodwill tends to rise in nominal value proportionally with inflation. To illustrate how this works, let's contrast a See's kind of business with a more mundane business. When we purchased See's in 1972, it will be recalled, it was earning about $2 million on $8 million of net tangible assets (25% ROIC). Let us assume that our hypothetical mundane business then had $2 million of earnings also, but needed $18 million in net tangible assets for normal operations. Earning only 11% on required tangible assets, that mundane business would possess little or no economic Goodwill.

因此，这样的企业很可能仅以其有形净资产的价值出售，也就是1800万美元。相比之下，我们为See's支付了2500万美元，尽管它的盈利水平并未更高，有形资产甚至不到后者的一半。难道价格较低反而意味着更好的选择吗？答案是“是的”——*即便两家企业的业务量都预计保持不变*——只要像我们在1972年那样，预见到一个持续通货膨胀的世界。

<!--en-->
A business like that, therefore, might well have sold for the value of its net tangible assets, or for $18 million. In contrast, we paid $25 million for See's, even though it had no more in earnings and less than half as much in "honest-to-God" assets. Could less really have been more, as our purchase price implied? The answer is "yes" – *even if both businesses were expected to have flat unit volume* – as long as you anticipated, as we did in 1972, a world of continuous inflation.

要理解其中的原因，不妨想象物价水平翻倍后对这两家企业会产生何种影响。为了跟上通货膨胀的步伐，两家企业都需要将名义利润翻倍至400万美元。这似乎并非难事：只需以双倍的价格销售相同数量的商品，在利润率不变的前提下，利润自然也会翻倍。

<!--en-->
To understand why, imagine the effect that a doubling of the price level would subsequently have on the two businesses. Both would need to double their nominal earnings to $4 million to keep themselves even with inflation. This would seem to be no great trick: just sell the same number of units at double earlier prices and, assuming profit margins remain unchanged, profits also must double.

但关键在于，为实现这一目标，两家企业可能都必须将有形资产的名义投资额翻倍，因为通货膨胀通常会对企业提出此类经济要求，无论企业优劣。销售额翻倍意味着必须立即投入更多的资金用于应收账款和存货。固定资产所需的资金对通货膨胀的反应虽较慢，但同样不可避免。而所有这些因通货膨胀而产生的投资并不会带来回报率的提升。进行此类投资的动机是为了企业的生存，而非所有者的繁荣。

<!--en-->
But, crucially, to bring that about, both businesses probably would have to double their nominal investment in net tangible assets, since that is the kind of economic requirement that inflation usually imposes on businesses, both good and bad. A doubling of dollar sales means correspondingly more dollars must be employed immediately in receivables and inventories. Dollars employed in fixed assets will respond more slowly to inflation, but probably just as surely. And all of this inflation-required investment will produce no improvement in rate of return. The motivation for this investment is the survival of the business, not the prosperity of the owner.

不过请记住，See's公司的有形资产净值仅为800万美元。因此，它只需额外投入800万美元就能满足通货膨胀带来的资本需求。而那家普通企业所需的额外资本则高达1800万美元，负担是See's公司的两倍多。

<!--en-->
Remember, however, that See's had net tangible assets of only $8 million. So it would only have had to commit an additional $8 million to finance the capital needs imposed by inflation. The mundane business, meanwhile, had a burden over twice as large – a need for $18 million of additional capital.

风波过后，这家每年盈利400万美元的普通企业，其价值可能仍相当于其有形资产的价值，即3600万美元。这意味着，投资者每投入1美元新资金，只能获得1美元的名义价值增值。（这一结果与他们将钱存入储蓄账户所得到的结果相同。）

<!--en-->
After the dust had settled, the mundane business, now earning $4 million annually, might still be worth the value of its tangible assets, or $36 million. That means its owners would have gained only a dollar of nominal value for every new dollar invested. (This is the same dollar-for-dollar result they would have achieved if they had added money to a savings account.)

哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资课程”指出：See's公司同样每年盈利400万美元，如果按我们收购时的估值标准来计算，其价值可能达到5000万美元。也就是说，在所有者仅追加800万美元资本的情况下，该公司就获得了2500万美元的名义价值增值——每投入1美元，就能获得超过3美元的名义价值。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
See's, however, also earning $4 million, might be worth $50 million if valued (as it logically would be) on the same basis as it was at the time of our purchase. So it would have gained $25 million in nominal value while the owners were putting up only $8 million in additional capital – over $3 of nominal value gained for each $1 invested.

即便如此，也要记住：像See's这样的企业，其所有者为了维持实际利润水平，仍被迫额外投入800万美元资本以应对通货膨胀。任何需要一定有形资产才能运营的企业（几乎全部都是如此）都会受到通货膨胀的冲击；而那些对有形资产需求较少的企业受冲击程度则最小。

<!--en-->
Remember, even so, that the owners of the See's kind of business were forced by inflation to ante up $8 million in additional capital just to stay even in real profits. Any unleveraged business that requires some net tangible assets to operate (and almost all do) is hurt by inflation. Businesses needing little in the way of tangible assets simply are hurt the least.

当然，这一事实很难被许多人理解。多年来，传统观念——徒有传统之名却缺乏智慧——一直认为，抵御通货膨胀的最佳方式是投资那些拥有大量自然资源、厂房设备或其他有形资产的企业（“我们信任实物资产”）。但事实并非如此。资产密集型企业通常回报率较低——这些回报往往仅够满足现有企业的通胀需求，根本无法用于实际增长、向所有者分红或收购新企业。

<!--en-->
And that fact, of course, has been hard for many people to grasp. For years the traditional wisdom – long on tradition, short on wisdom – held that inflation protection was best provided by businesses laden with natural resources, plants and machinery, or other tangible assets ("In Goods We Trust"). It doesn't work that way. Asset-heavy businesses generally earn low rates of return – rates that often barely provide enough capital to fund the inflationary needs of the existing business, with nothing left over for real growth, for distribution to owners, or for acquisition of new businesses.

相比之下，在通货膨胀时期崛起的众多伟大商业帝国，大多源于那些拥有持久性无形资产且对有形资产需求较小的企业。在这种情况下，名义收益会大幅上升，而这些收益很大程度上可用于收购其他企业。这一现象在通信行业尤为明显：该行业对有形投资的需求很少，但其特许经营权却能长期存续。在通货膨胀期间，商誉简直就是源源不断的财富之源。

<!--en-->
In contrast, a disproportionate number of the great business fortunes built up during the inflationary years arose from ownership of operations that combined intangibles of lasting value with relatively minor requirements for tangible assets. In such cases earnings have bounded upward in nominal dollars, and these dollars have been largely available for the acquisition of additional businesses. This phenomenon has been particularly evident in the communications business. That business has required little in the way of tangible investment – yet its franchises have endured. During inflation, Goodwill is the gift that keeps giving.

当然，这一说法仅适用于真正的经济商誉。那些虚假的会计商誉——这类情况比比皆是——则是另一回事。当狂热的管理层以离谱的价格收购企业时，就会采用前述的会计手段。由于无处可去，这种荒谬之举最终被计入商誉科目。考虑到创造这一科目的管理缺乏纪律性，在这种情况下，它或许更适合被称为“无商誉”。无论叫什么，40年的摊销惯例仍会被遵循，那些被资本化的“肾上腺素”便继续作为“资产”留在账上，仿佛这次收购是明智之举一般。

<!--en-->
But that statement applies, naturally, only to true economic Goodwill. Spurious accounting Goodwill – and there is plenty of it around – is another matter. When an overexcited management purchases a business at a silly price, the same accounting niceties described earlier are observed. Because it can't go anywhere else, the silliness ends up in the Goodwill account. Considering the lack of managerial discipline that created the account, under such circumstances it might better be labeled "No-Will". Whatever the term, the 40-year ritual typically is observed and the adrenalin so capitalized remains on the books as an "asset" just as if the acquisition had been a sensible one.

* * * * *

如果你仍坚信商誉的会计处理能最好地反映经济现实，我建议你最后思考一下这一点。假设一家公司的每股净资产为20美元，且均为有形资产；再假设该公司内部培育出了极具价值的消费品牌，或者幸运地通过FCC的原始授权获得了重要的电视台。因此，它利用有形资产创造了丰厚的收益，比如每股5美元，即25%的回报率。

<!--en-->
If you cling to any belief that accounting treatment of Goodwill is the best measure of economic reality, I suggest one final item to ponder.
83
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Assume a company with $20 per share of net worth, all tangible assets. Further assume the company has internally developed some magnificent consumer franchise, or that it was fortunate enough to obtain some important television stations by original FCC grant. Therefore, it earns a great deal on tangible assets, say $5 per share, or 25%.

凭借这样的盈利能力，该公司的股价可能达到每股100美元甚至更高，而且在整体出售时也很可能卖出这个价格。

<!--en-->
With such economics, it might sell for $100 per share or more, and it might well also bring that price in a negotiated sale of the entire business.

假设某投资者以每股100美元的价格买入该股，实际上相当于为商誉支付了80美元（与公司收购方支付的价格相同）。那么，该投资者是否应每年计提2美元/股的摊销费用（80美元除以40年），以此来计算“真实”的每股收益呢？如果是这样，新的“真实”每股收益3美元是否会让他对买入价重新考量？

<!--en-->
Assume an investor buys the stock at $100 per share, paying in effect $80 per share for Goodwill (just as would a corporate purchaser buying the whole company). Should the investor impute a $2 per share amortization charge annually ($80 divided by 40 years) to calculate "true" earnings per share? And, if so, should the new "true" earnings of $3 per share cause him to rethink his purchase price?

* * * * *

我们认为，管理者和投资者都应从两个角度看待无形资产：

<!--en-->
We believe managers and investors alike should view intangible assets from two perspectives:

1. 在分析经营成果时——也就是说，在评估某个业务单元的基本经济状况时——应当忽略摊销费用。一家企业利用无杠杆有形资产所能创造的收益（不包括因商誉摊销而产生的费用）才是衡量该业务经济吸引力的最佳指标。它也是判断该业务所蕴含的经济性商誉当前价值的最佳依据。
2. 在评估企业收购的合理性时，同样应忽略摊销费用。既不应从盈利中扣除这些费用，也不应从收购成本中扣除。这意味着要永远按照初始购买成本来核算所购商誉的价值，而非扣除摊销后的金额。此外，成本的定义应包含所支付对价的全部内在商业价值——而不仅仅是账面记载的会计价值——无论合并时相关证券的市场价格如何，也无论是否允许采用权益结合法进行处理。例如，在Blue Chip并购案中，我们为获得See's和News公司40%的商誉所实际支付的金额，远远高于账面上记录的5170万美元。这种差异源于此次合并中出让的伯克希尔股票的市场价值低于其内在商业价值，而后者才是决定我们真实成本的关键。基于视角（1）看似表现优异的业务，从视角（2）来看可能并不那么出色。**一家好企业未必就是一笔好买卖——尽管它是寻找优质标的的好去处。** 我们会试图收购那些根据视角（1）衡量具有卓越经营状况、且根据视角（2）能提供合理回报的企业。会计层面的影响将被完全忽略。哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
1. In analysis of operating results – that is, in evaluating the underlying economics of a business unit – amortization charges should be ignored. What a business can be expected to earn on unleveraged net tangible assets, excluding any charges against earnings for amortization of Goodwill, is the best guide to the economic attractiveness of the operation. It is also the best guide to the current value of the operation's economic Goodwill.
2. In evaluating the wisdom of business acquisitions, amortization charges should be ignored also. They should be deducted neither from earnings nor from the cost of the business. This means forever viewing purchased Goodwill at its full cost, before any amortization. Furthermore, cost should be defined as including the full intrinsic business value – not just the recorded accounting value – of all consideration given, irrespective of market prices of the securities involved at the time of merger and irrespective of whether pooling treatment was allowed. For example, what we truly paid in the Blue Chip merger for 40% of the Goodwill of See's and the News was considerably more than the $51.7 million entered on our books. This disparity exists because the market value of the Berkshire shares given up in the merger was less than their intrinsic business value, which is the value that defines the true cost to us.
Operations that appear to be winners based upon perspective (1) may pale when viewed from perspective (2). **A good business is not always a good purchase – although it's a good place to look for one.**
We will try to acquire businesses that have excellent operating economics measured by (1) and that provide reasonable returns measured by (2). Accounting consequences will be totally ignored.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

- 其定义为营业利润（EBIT或EBITDA – MCX（维持性资本支出））除以营运资本加上固定资产净值。股价便宜的股票则具备较高的盈利收益率。

Cheap stocks have high earnings yields
- Defined as pre-tax operating earnings divided by enterprise value

### 幻灯片4：

## 詹姆斯·博里奇所著的《百万美元魔法》

<!--en-->
*Million-Dollar Magic by James Boric*

乔尔·格林布拉特并不出名……他只是很富有而已。

<!--en-->
Joel Greenblatt is not famous...He is merely rich.

上周，我发现了他为何如此富有。我的发现或许也能让你的口袋里多几张钞票……甚至可能是数百万美元。

<!--en-->
Last week, I discovered why he is so rich. My discovery could easily put a few extra dollar bills in your pocket as well...Maybe even millions of dollar bills.

乔尔·格林布拉特是哈佛商学院的毕业生，但咱们别因此对他有偏见。他还是哥谭资本的创始人兼管理合伙人，这家私人投资公司成立于1985年。他最初依靠700万美元的外部资金起步——其中大部分来自“垃圾债券大王”迈克尔·米尔肯。在接下来的十年里，他的投资年化收益率达到了50%。即便在归还全部初始资本并扣除各项费用后，格林布拉特仍将其700万美元的本金增值至超过3.5亿美元。1995年时，仅1,000美元的投资就价值57,665美元；而10,000美元的投资则价值超过50万美元。

<!--en-->
Joel Greenblatt is a Harvard Business School graduate, but let's not hold that against him. He is also the founder and managing partner of Gotham Capital, a private investment firm established in 1985. He started with $7 million of outside capital - mostly from junk bond king Michael Milken. Over the next decade, he earned 50% a year - compounded. Even after paying back all of the original seed capital and factoring out expenses, Greenblatt grew his $7 million stake to over $350 million. A mere $1,000 investment was worth $57,665 in 1995. A $10,000 investment was worth more than a half a million dollars.

因此，当格林布拉特最近在纽约市举行的价值投资大会上登台演讲时，我聚精会神地听了起来……

<!--en-->
So when Greenblatt took the podium at the recent Value Investing Congress in New York City, I listened...intently.

格林布拉特宣称自己有一套简单的两步投资策略，其所能带来的回报远超市场平均水平。他将这一策略称为自己的“魔法公式”。我心想：“哇，这听起来挺老套的……但也许其中确有道理。”事实证明，确实如此。

<!--en-->
Greenblatt declared that he had a simple two-part investment process that could deliver far greater returns than the rest of the market. He called the process his "magic formula." I thought to myself, "Wow, that's pretty corny...but maybe there's something to it anyway." As it turns out, there is.

格林布拉特的公式基于一种“以价值为导向”的流程，根据两个变量对股票进行排序——即盈利收益率和资本回报率。

<!--en-->
Greenblatt's formula relies on a "value-oriented" process that ranks stocks on the basis of two variables — the earnings yield and the business's return on capital.

该公式的第一部分要求股票的价格相对于其盈利能力而言必须低廉（即具有高盈利收益率）。道理很简单：如果一家公司的年收益率不超过5%——也就是你从10年期美国国债中能获得的收益水平——那它就不值得投资。简而言之，相对于你所承担的风险而言，它的价格并不便宜。

<!--en-->
The first part of his formula requires that a stock trade for a bargain price relative to earnings power (or yield). The idea is simple. If, for example, a company can't earn more than 5% a year - the return you would receive from 10-year U.S. Treasury note - it isn't a business you want to be in. Quite simply, it isn't cheap relative to the risk you must take.

要计算一家公司的盈利收益率，只需用其每股年度盈利除以股价即可。例如：如果一家公司全年每股盈利1美元，而股价为10美元，那么其盈利收益率就是10%。由于10%的收益是10年期国债的两倍，因此这家公司或许值得进一步研究。但如果你在同一行业中找到另一家公司，其每股盈利为2美元且股价仍为10美元，那这可能是一个更好的投资机会——其盈利收益率高达20%！显然，盈利收益率越高，性价比就越好。

<!--en-->
To calculate a company's earnings yield, you divide its annual earnings per share by its share price. For instance...If a company earns $1 per share for an entire year and its stock price is $10, its earnings yield is 10%. Since 10% is double the return of a 10-year Treasury, it may be a company worth looking into. But if you find a company in the same industry that earns $2 per share and trades for $10, that may be an even better investment opportunity. It has an earnings yield of 20%! Obviously, the higher the earnings yield, the better the bargain.

不过，盈利收益率只是“魔法公式”的一半。投资者还必须问第二个问题：这家企业是否稳健？你最不想做的事就是买入那些因自身糟糕状况而导致股价低廉的股票——毕竟那是因为它实在不值得投资。

<!--en-->
But earnings yield is only one half of the magic formula. Investors must also ask a second question: Is the business a solid one? The last thing you want to do is to buy stock in a company that is cheap for a good reason - because it stinks.

格林布拉特通过考察企业的资本回报率来判断其是否“优秀”。换句话说，该企业是否明智地运用了资本、从而增强了盈利能力？还是说它把现金浪费在那些无法为股东创造（甚至还会损害）价值的无用投资上？例如：如果一家公司花费100万美元建造新工厂，次年就能额外产生50万美元的利润，那么其资本年回报率便达到了50%。这堪称卓越的表现——说明管理层懂得如何运用你的资金来创造附加价值。显然，资本回报率高的公司会比那些回报率低的公司发展得更快。87 哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情境投资课程 【编者注：顺便提一下，格林布拉特写了一本关于其“魔法公式”的精彩书籍，书名为《战胜市场的简单法则》。他还专门为此创建了一个网站，网址为www.magicformulainvesting.com.。需要说明的是，我们与格林布拉特没有任何业务往来；我们仅为向您提供这些信息而已。】

<!--en-->
Greenblatt determines whether a company is "good" or not by looking at its return on invested capital. In other words, is it investing its capital wisely - adding to its earnings power? Or is it wasting its cash on frivolous investments that will create no (or even negative) value for shareholders moving forward? For instance...If a company spends $1 million on a new factory and it is able to crank out an additional $500,000 in profits the next year, the result is a 50% annual return on capital. That's outstanding. It says management knows how to spend YOUR shareholder money to create added value. Clearly, companies with high returns on capital will grow more quickly than companies with low returns.
87
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
[Editor's Note: By the way, Greenblatt has authored a terrific book about his magic formula entitled, "The Little Book that Beats the Market." He has also created a Website dedicated to the process, which may be found at www.magicformulainvesting.com. For the record, we have no business association whatsoever with Greenblatt. We are merely providing this information as a courtesy to you].

于是，格林布拉特开始思考：如果你只投资于那些业绩良好（即资本回报率高）且价格低廉（即盈利收益率高）的公司，究竟能赚多少钱呢？

<!--en-->
So Greenblatt wondered how much money you would make if you invested ONLY in good companies (those with a high return in invested capital) that trade for a bargain price (companies with high earnings yields).

为了解答这个问题，他研究了按照其“魔法公式”筛选出的股票的历史表现。具体来说，他依据该公式的排名系统，对1988年至2004年间排名前3,500位的美国股票进行了分析——这些股票涵盖了从微软这样的巨头到市值仅5,000万美元的小型股。他根据盈利收益率和资本回报率对每个股票进行排名，范围从1到3,500。

<!--en-->
To answer that question, he researched the historical returns of the stocks his magic formula would have identified. Specifically, he went back and examined the top 3,500 American stocks (from your large behemoths like Microsoft on down to micro cap companies with market caps of $50 million) from 1988-2004, according to his formula's ranking system. He ranked each stock in terms of earnings yield and return on capital - from 1 to 3,500.

其思路是投资于综合得分最高的公司——即盈利收益率和资本回报率均最高的公司。因此，如果一家公司在盈利收益率方面排名第100位，在资本回报率方面排名第50位，那么它的综合得分就是150分。而另一家公司若在盈利收益率方面排名第6位、在资本回报率方面排名第10位，其综合得分则为16分。

<!--en-->
The idea was to invest in the companies with the best combined score – those with the highest earnings yield AND the highest return on capital. So if a company ranked 100th in terms of earnings yield and 50th in terms of return on invested capital, it got a score of 150. And if another company ranked 6th in terms of earnings yield and 10th in terms of return on capital, it got a combined score of 16.

为每家公司计算出得分后，格林布拉特选出了排名前30的公司组成投资组合。在他的测试中，每年年初都会重新选出新的“前30强”，然后计算投资者投资当年这些前30只股票所能获得的回报。

<!--en-->
After generating a score for each company, Greenblatt created a portfolio of the top 30 companies. Greenblatt created a new "Top 30" at the beginning of every year within his test, and then calculated the return an investor would have received by investing in each year's top-30 stocks.

从1988年到2004年，如果你每年都按照格林布拉特的公式买入排名前30的公司，17年间的平均回报率将达到30.8%。同一时期，市场的平均回报率仅为12.3%。

<!--en-->
From 1988-2004, if you had bought the top 30 companies generated every year using Greenblatt's formula, you would have averaged a 30.8% return for 17 years. During that same time frame, the market averaged a 12.3% return.

因此，采用格林布拉特的两部分公式构建的理想投资组合，其表现几乎是市场的三倍。而且情况还不止于此……

<!--en-->
So Greenblatt's ideal portfolio (using his two-part formula) beat the market by almost three times over. And it gets even better...

在1988年至2004年间，从未出现过连续三年该由30只优质低价股组成的投资组合无法盈利的情况。事实上，也从未有连续三年它的表现不如标普500指数。换句话说，1988年投入11,000美元购买遵循格林布拉特神奇公式的股票，到2004年其价值将超过100万美元。

<!--en-->
There was NEVER a three-year period between 1988 and 2004 where this portfolio of 30 solid, bargain stocks was not profitable. Indeed, there was never a three-year period in which it failed to beat the return of the S&P 500. In other words, an $11,000 investment in 1988 in Greenblatt's magic formula stocks would have been worth over $1 million by 2004.

作为小盘股专家，我特别感兴趣的是：格林布拉特体系中的小盘价值股显著提升了整体业绩。例如，当格林布拉特从3,500只股票的样本池中剔除最小的2,500只股票后，他发现其神奇公式投资组合的年回报率“仅”为22.9%。这一结果虽仍优于标普500指数，但远不及纳入中盘股和小盘股后所实现的30.8%的年回报率。

<!--en-->
As a small-cap specialist, I was particularly intrigued by the fact that the small-cap value stocks within Greenblatt's system dramatically boosted the overall results. For example, when Greenblatt excluded the smallest 2,500 stocks from his sample universe of 3,500, he discovered that his magic-formula portfolios produced an annual return of "only" 22.9%. That result was still far better than the S&P 500's, but the not nearly as good as the 30.8% annual returns that resulted when the mid- and small-cap stocks were included.

换句话说，小盘价值股是市场上最值得投资的股票之一。于是我不禁思考：当今市场中哪些小盘公司能满足格林布拉特严格的价值标准呢？我自己做了一些测算，最终找出10家资本回报率至少为25%、盈利收益率超过9%的公司。快来看看吧……

<!--en-->
In other words, small cap value stocks are some of the market's most valuable stocks of all. So I wondered, what small-cap companies in today's market would meet Greenblatt's stringent value criteria? I ran some numbers of my own, and came up with 10 companies that had at least a 25% return on capital and an earning yield north of 9%. Check 'em out...

### 一、关于《打败市场的小书》一书的提问。

<!--en-->
I. Questions about the book, *The Little Book that Beats the Market*.

**学生：**书中使用的EBIT是否等于EBITDA减去维持性资本支出（MCX）？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Does Ebit = Ebitda – Maintenance Capital Expenditures (MCX) used in the book?

**JG：**没错，我在书中为*MBA学生*附了一个小注。为简便起见，我假设MCX等于折旧与摊销（D&A）。要确定许多公司的真实MCX相当困难。出于简化目的，使用EBIT得出的结果大致相近。若由我亲自操作，我会核实真实的MCX数值，并从EBITDA中扣除该数。你可以用EBIT来校验结果是否接近。

<!--en-->
**JG:** Right, I put a little note in there for the *MBA Students* in the book. I assumed MCX = D&A for simplicity purposes. Figuring out MCX for a lot of these companies is pretty hard. On average it (using EBIT) is pretty close to being right for simplistic purposes. If I were doing it myself, I would check to see the true MCX and subtract that number from EBITDA. You might use EBIT as a check to see if you are close.

**学生：**您的妹妹*琳达·格林布拉特*来访时曾说，零售商因其价格波动较大（高波动性有利于低价买入）而非常适合投资。房地产板块也是如此。在您的数据库中，还有没有其他经常出现的行业？

<!--en-->
**Student:** When your sister, *Linda Greenblatt* was here she said that retailers were great to invest in due to their price swings (high price volatility allows for advantageous purchases). Real Estate swings. Were there any other consistent sectors in your database that kept showing up?

**JG：**并没有特定的行业侧重，但消费品行业占比很大；因为根据分类标准的不同，这类企业无需大量资本即可创造回报（属于低资本回报模式）。

<!--en-->
**JG:** There was no particular exposure, but there were a lot of consumer exposure in general because those businesses depending upon whom was doing the categorizing do not require a lot of capital to earn their returns (A low capital return model).

这里的精髓在于“无需费太多力气”的模式，对吧？你只需参考去年的盈利数据，无需做出夸张的假设，也无需运用过多因素。**这恰恰体现了这一基本概念的力量。**我对此乐在其中，因为我读了很多金融学术期刊（我是个狂热的人嘛）。四年前，他们以有效市场中的某些公司为例，一切都必须置于有效市场理论的框架下解释。学者们至今仍未跳出这一框架。令人惊叹的是，面对如此多的数据，人们竟能坚信通过如此简单的方法就能战胜市场。（正如沃伦·巴菲特所言：“尽管船只已环绕世界航行数个世纪，地平说者依然存在。”）

<!--en-->
The big picture here is the *not trying very hard model*, right? You sort of use last year's earnings and you do not make heroic assumptions, and you do not use very many factors. **It shows how powerful the basic concept is.**
I had fun with this because I read a lot of the academic journals (on finance) because I am a wild and crazy guy. Four years ago they took some firms in efficient markets. Everything has to be laid out in that context (of efficient market theory). They (academics) have never really gotten off that. It is pretty amazing how you can argue in the face of so much information that you can beat the market doing something this simple. (Though ships will sail around the world for centuries, the Flat Earth Society prevails- Warren Buffett).

我写这本书是为了面向*大众*——那就是本书的目标读者。如果你能真正填入自己对标准化收益的估算值，那就更好了。事实上，你们当中有些人会找到一些自己有把握的公司；这意味着*如果什么都不做就能取得如此好的效果*，只要在你遇到不顺时不被*情绪*所左右，这种策略实际上就能奏效。

<!--en-->
I wrote the book for the *masses*—that was the audience for this book. If you can really insert your estimates of normalized earnings that would be so much better. The fact is that some of you will find some companies that you feel confident in doing that means that *if it works this well doing nothing*, to work well actually thinking about it as long as you don't get messed up with the *emotions* when it is not working out for you.

**学生：**您每年是如何编制股票组合的？股票是如何被添加或剔除的？每年之间有什么变化？

<!--en-->
**Student:** How do you compile the stocks every year? How are stocks added or eliminated? How does that change from year to year?

**JG：**投资组合是如何刻意构建的？我故意把这一点说得模糊一些，因为它很复杂。基本思路是：*始终维持一个包含30只股票的组合*，随着时间推移逐步积累该组合，从而使*每只股票都被持有一年*。我们从1988年1月开始，尽管我们假设自己在1987年1月就开始购买股票，有些股票持有6个月，有些持有9个月等等；正如我在书中所描述的，我建议每两个月买入6只股票，直到1988年1月时组合中累计达到30只股票。

<!--en-->
**JG:** How is the portfolio purposely constructed? I left that purposely nebulous because it was complicated. The basic idea is that *there is always a 30 stock portfolio*, and you accumulate that portfolio over time so that *each stock was held for a year*. We started in Jan. 1988 and although we assumed we started buying stocks in Jan 1987 with some stocks held for 6 months and some held for nine months etc, as I described in the book, I suggested that you bought six stocks every two months until there were 30 stocks accumulated in the portfolio over the year by Jan. 1988.

正如我在书中所描述的，我们采用了循序渐进的过程。股票分别被持有三个月、六个月、九个月等。第二年你会有30只股票；从第二年开始，组合中就有三十只股票，然后你卖出六只股票并买入6只新股票。我在书中提到的关于三十只股票的组合，就是每两个月买入6只股票；随后你会卖出持有超过一年的股票。从第二年开始考虑，这就是我们衡量30只股票组合的方式。

<!--en-->
As I described in the book we used a step-by-step process. We had stocks held for three, six, nine months, etc. In year two you will have 30 stocks, starting in year two you have thirty stocks in the portfolio then you sell six stocks and bought 6 new stocks. What I described in the book for a thirty stock portfolio you would be buying 6 stocks every two months. Then you would sell stocks held for more than a year. Think of starting in year two and that is how we started measuring the 30 stock portfolio.

**学生：**您选择1988年作为起始年有什么原因吗？哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程

<!--en-->
**Student:** Was there any reason you picked 1988 for the starting year?
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**JG：**是的，我们使用了一个名为*Compustat时点数据库*的数据库，那是当时人们所能看到的*确切数据*。我在书后提到过这些数据受到攻击的原因，其中之一就是幸存者偏差——他们把破产公司从指数中剔除，从而导致业绩看起来更好，因为你去掉了表现差的股票。这里所用的正是当时*Compustat*客户拥有的*确切数据*，而且该数据只能追溯到1987年。所以我们从数据库的开端开始。你可能会说这样未必奏效，但我们不想引发争议，而且这是最容易使用的数据库，因为数据非常统一。

<!--en-->
**JG:** Yes, we used a database called *Compustat point-in-time database* which was the *exact data* that someone would see back then. I said in the back of the book these were the reasons things get attacked and one of them is survivorship bias where they just take bankrupt companies out of the index so you have a bias to do well because you got rid of the loser. Here this was *the exact data* the *Compustat* customer had at that point in time and it only goes back until then (1987). So we went to the beginning of the database. You could argue that it might not have worked, but we didn't want to have any argument and this is the easiest database to use because the data is very uniform.

存在很多问题，我们设立**www.MagicFormulaInvesting.com**.网站**的原因在于我不想写完书后还让人们使用糟糕的数据库，还要他们手动输入各种公式。人们会试图去编程计算有形资本之类的内容。我原本打算使用《商业周刊》的数据库，但它并不采用*Compustat*数据（尽管它归*标普*所有）。因此我觉得有必要这么做，因为读者没有准确且易于获取的数据来应用“魔法公式”，最终可能会买到错误的股票。我们力求让一切尽可能简单。

<!--en-->
There are many, many problems, and the reason we set up the **www.MagicFormulaInvesting.com**. Website was because I didn't want to write the book and then we didn't want people to use crummy databases and people have to plug in all the formulas. People would be trying to program tangible capital and all those kinds of things. So I had planned to use *Business Week's* data base but it doesn't use *Compustat* data (though it is owned by *S&P*). So I felt kind of obligated to do this because the readers would not have accurate or easily obtained data to use the Magic Formula and then they go buy the wrong stock. We tried to make it as simple as possible.

**学生：**您是否考虑过使用两年的数据？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Did you think of using two year's data?

**JG：**这是个好问题。换句话说，我说这是一种良好的长期策略，并且我说*每年要调整一次投资组合*——其一，一年周期很简单；其二，短期亏损可以在不到一年内被控制，而持有股票一年后可获得长期收益，尤其是对个人投资者而言。使用两年前的数据同样效果不错。

<!--en-->
**JG:** That is a good question. In other words, I say it is a good long term strategy and I say *to turn it (the portfolio) over ever year*—one, a year was simple and two, to take losses in less than a year for short term losses and two, to take profits after holding the stock for a year for a long term gains especially if you were an individual. It works well using two year old data as well.

我们使用去年的数据而非预测数据。一年后你得到的是比一年前*更新鲜*的数据，这总是比使用两年前的数据更有意义。出于税务原因和换手成本考虑，我们认为一年周期与长期（两年或更久）策略相比是一种折衷方案。我们希望保持简单。

<!--en-->
We are using last year's data instead of using projections. After a year you have *fresher* data than a year ago and that always makes more sense than using two year old data. We thought a year was as good as anything else for tax reasons and for turnover costs it was a compromise to a longer term (two years or more) strategy. And we wanted to keep it simple.

**学生：**最低十分位组的风险最大吗？您注意到在最低十分位组中有很多公司破产了吗？*最低十分位组的风险确实最大吗*？这些组别中的一些股票涨幅达三倍，而有些则破产了？

<!--en-->
**Student:** The lowest deciles were the most risky? Did you notice a number of companies going bankrupt in the lowest deciles? Are *the lowest deciles the most risky*? Some stocks in those deciles tripled and some went bankrupt?

**JG：** 不。**我们购买的是高ROIC、能赚取大量利润的股票，也就是真正能盈利的公司。我们不会选择低市净率的股票。** 他们的论点站不住脚。我们并未看到明显的效果。（*学者们可能会说，由于这类股票本身风险较高，因此“魔法公式投资法”选出的股票表现会更好*）。低市净率股票的表现也并不突出。（*学者们称*）：“这种风险并不会体现在波动性中——而他们（金融领域的学者）通常会在其他地方衡量风险——所以一定是其他某种风险，因为我们的理论不可能错。这简直荒谬至极。下课前我会告诉你们我的真实看法。（*笑声*）。我在附录中提到一点：如果我们根据未来收益来估值并折现……那为什么低市净率股票还会重要呢……（*语焉不详*）低市净率股票只是那些价格极低且已不受青睐的股票子集。这类低价股票的交易价格虽接近账面价值，但*这并不是它们价格低廉的原因*。它们只是恰好便宜罢了——这只是表明它们可能便宜而已。**因此，判断一家公司是否便宜的更直接方式是：它赚的钱是否*相对于我支付的价格而言足够多*？它是否处于*好行业*中？** 这种方法应该比单纯依赖低市净率股票更有效。

<!--en-->
**JG:** No. **We are buying high ROIC stocks earning a lot of money, companies that are earning money. We are not choosing low price to book stocks.** Their argument goes out the window. We didn't see much. (*Academics might say Magic Formula Investing Stocks will do better because of the higher risks inherent in the stocks*). And there isn't much in the low price to book results as well. (*Academics say*) "It (risk) doesn't come out in volatility where they (*Academics in finance*) measure risk everywhere else so it must be some other risk because our theory can't be wrong. It is patently ridiculous. At the end of class I will tell you what I really think. (*Laughter*). One thing I did slip in the appendix is that if we are valuing stocks based on future earnings, discounted back....why would low price to book stocks be important.....(*garbled*)
Low price to book stocks are a *subset* of stocks that are super cheap and are already out of favor. A subset of stocks that are cheap will trade close to book value but *that is not why they are cheap*. They just happen to be cheap—it is an indication they may be cheap. **So a more direct way to test whether a company is cheap: Does it earn a lot *relative to what I am paying* and is it in a *good business*?** This should work a lot better than low price to book stocks.

低市净率只是其中的一个子集；实际上，《特罗斯基研究》显示，不到一半的低市净率股票能跑赢市场，不过跑赢的那些股票表现确实突出。他试图剔除一些较差的低市净率股票以观察是否能改善结果，而他确实做到了。但他的方法对大盘股并不适用。我认为这正是该（“魔法公式”）方法的精妙之处。正因如此，我们进行了大盘股研究——在1988年至2003年的测试期内，大盘股的平均年回报率达到了22%。

<!--en-->
Low price to book is just a subset that you would tend to get and actually the *Trosky Study* show less than half of the low price to book stocks beat the market but the ones that do beat it by a lot. So what he tried to do is throw out some of the worse low price books stocks to see if he improved which he did. But his methodology did *not* work for large cap stocks. I think that is the beauty of this (*Magic Formula*) one. That was why we did the large cap stock study which worked well for us—22% average annual returns for large cap stocks over 1988 to 2003 testing period).

<!--en-->
**Student:** Do you remove cyclical (stocks) from your study? Couldn't you be buying cyclical stocks at the worst time because their earnings would be *peak earnings*, giving you a high earnings yield?

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**JG：** 我不会这么说。在大多数情况下……我们在这里尝试的做法是……这是我们*首先*测试的，而且效果显著。我们并没有测试很多方法后再挑选最有效的那种，这一点令人欣慰，因为它证明了*逻辑确实可行*。这就是所谓的“不刻意为之”的方法。

<!--en-->
**JG:** I wouldn't say that. In most cases.....What we try to do here rather than.... This is the thing that we tested *first* and it worked. We didn't test many things to pick the one that worked, which is comforting because it shows that *logic works*. This is the not trying method.

你不想在其中加入太多因素。我实际上收到了《华尔街制胜之道》的作者*奥肖内西*发来的邮件。我在书中对他颇有微词。名单上剩下的只有*豪根*，他提出了包含72个因素的模型（*需要每月调整持仓！*），但其效果还不如双因素模型。这样一来，一个被排除，还剩下一个。**学生：** 你们考虑过杠杆因素吗？

<!--en-->
You don't want to put too many factors in there. I actually got an email from *O'Shaughnessy* who wrote, *What Works on Wall Street*.” I beat up on him in my book. The only one left on the list is *Haugen* who has a 72 factor model (*requiring monthly turnover!*) that doesn't work as well as the two factor model. So one down and one left.
**Student** Did you consider leverage?

**JG：** 没有，但我没有考虑。不过**EV/EBIT已经包含了杠杆因素**。过去所有的研究——那些低市盈率研究——其实并非指低EV/EBIT。当我给你们那些阅读材料时，那个人（*胡克，《华尔街证券分析》的作者*）建议根据资本结构来选择指标，因此应使用市盈率而非EV/EBIT。我表示不同意。从统计数据来看，显然前者效果更好。这对分析很有帮助。

<!--en-->
**JG:** No I didn't, but **EV/EBIT includes leverage**. All the studies done in the past—the low P/E studies—are not low EV/EBIT. When I gave you those passages to read and that guy (*Hooke, the author of Security Analysis on Wall Street*) said take what you get regarding capital structure so use P/E as opposed to EV/EBIT. I said that I didn't agree with that. I think it is very clear through statistics that on average, this is much better. So that helps in that analysis.

我试图在书中解释为何这种方法有效，但坦白说，我对它的出色表现感到十分惊讶。

<!--en-->
I try to explain why this works in the book but I have to be frank, I was quite amazed at how well it worked.

**JG：** 谁认为我写这本书时是个*傻瓜*？

<!--en-->
**JG:** Who thinks I was an *idiot* to write this book in the first place?

**学生：** 笑声。魔法公式的效力会随时间减弱吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Laughter. Will the Magic Formula diminish over time?

投资就像节食一样：知道该怎么做容易，真正去做却很难。有充分的理由认为没多少人能坚持此法。它的效力或许会有所减弱。

<!--en-->
Investing is like dieting. It is easier to know what to do than actually do it? There is a pretty strong argument that not many people will be able to follow this. It probably might diminish somewhat.

**JG：** 低市盈率作为价值指标并未*衰退*，但低市净率却衰退了。不过低市净率对我来说本就没什么意义。我认为低市净率效力衰退的原因之一在于，过去15到20年间经济越来越依赖服务行业，而非资产驱动型产业。因此，那些账面价值高但盈利能力差的公司，正是最不值得投资的对象。低市净率带来的负面结果便是明证。这正是我所倚仗的一点。像低市盈率策略一样，这种方法不会衰退，过去40年间也从未衰退。买入高盈余收益率（低EV/高EBIT）、高ROIC（高EBIT/低投入资本）的公司这一策略，应当仍能保持强劲表现。

<!--en-->
**JG:** Low P/E hasn't (*diminished as a value metric*) but low price to book (P/B) has. But low P/B really didn't make much sense to me. I think one reason low price to book has diminished over the years is that the economy has been *less* asset based earned and more services industry oriented over the last 15 or 20 years. So that the companies that are trading closer to book value with a lot of assets to generate earnings are some of the worse companies to invest in. Negative results from low P/BV. That is one of the things that I am banking on. This method like the low P/E strategy won't diminish and hasn't diminished over the past 40 years. The strategy to buy high earnings yield (Low EV/high Ebit) companies which have high ROIC (high EBIT/Low Invested Capital) should remain robust.

我寄予厚望的另一点是：如果你看看“魔法公式股票”列表中的前列股票，*它们很难被持有*。我明白这些股票为何处于那种交易水平——近期利空消息层出不穷，愿意买入的人并不多。所以我认为只要……

<!--en-->
The other thing I am banking on is that if you look at the top of the list (of Magic Formula Stocks) *they are hard to own*. How I know *why* these stocks are trading there—bad near term news abounds. There are not too many takers to buy. So I think as long as.....

即便你看看*豪根*的研究，他提出了71个选股标准，并撰写了三部值得一读且各有裨益的书（参见第22页的阴影部分）。其中一部涉及他的71因子模型，他列出了所采用的十大关键因素，其中有六个是低市盈率和高净资产收益率。并非量化分析师没有这类关于何种可量化标准能跑赢市场的信息；只是普通人没有罢了。然后你必须决定：这种方法对与大公司合作制定价格的分析师或计算机机器人是否有效？

<!--en-->
Even if you look at the *Haugen* study where he had with 71 factors (of criteria to buy superior performing stocks) and he wrote a trilogy of books—all of them worth reading with various benefits with each. (See shaded segment on page 22). One of them had to do with his 71 factor model, and he shows you the top ten factors that he used and six of them were low P/E and high ROE. It is not that quants don't have this stuff (on what quantifiable criteria outperform the market). The average guy doesn't. Then you have to decide, does it work with the analyst working with big companies who set prices or computer robots?

量化分析师倒闭的原因是*他们必须不断重塑自己*——即不断更新量化模型。他们发现某些短期有效的异常现象，可能持续一天、一周或几周，之后便会回归常态。看看这个简单模型（魔法公式）的结果：2002年该模型下跌25%，而市场仅下跌22%，但人们无法承受这种波动。如果回归过程较快，人们还有耐心；但如果需要一两年时间且期间表现不佳，人们就没有耐心了。因此人们很难采纳这种(*魔法公式投资*)模型。

<!--en-->
The reasons that Quants go out of business is because *they have to keep reinventing themselves*—the quantitative model. They find anomalies that work for a day, a week a few weeks whatever and they may converge the way they are supposed to go. And if you look at the results here for the simple model (for the Magic Formula) and in 2002 the model is down 25% and the market is down 22%, but people can't eat that volatility. If things converge quickly, the people have patience. If things converge slowly over a year or two years and things go badly in between, people don't have that patience. It is very hard for people to adopt that model (*of Magic Formula Investing*).

**人们没有耐心等待回归常态。**这非常困难。可以想象，如果今年该方法不奏效，人们就会说这种方法也不行。

<!--en-->
**People don't have to patience to wait for convergence.** It is very hard. You can imagine if this doesn't work this year people will say this (*method*) doesn't work either.

<!--en-->

One of the ways which is what I said in the book. **Good companies at cheap prices.** I think that is certainly true for the first and second deciles and why they outperform the last two deciles. I think it is very clear on average that is what you are doing.

**当你投资于顶尖梯队（十分位数）的公司时，你更像是在经营一家保险公司（因此需要大量赌注来增大胜算）。**单独持有这些股票很难，因为它们不受青睐，或许会成功，也可能不会。但作为一个整体，平均而言有足够多的成功案例。所以你实际上是在下保险类的赌注，而非单只股票的赌注。总会有不受青睐的股票，它们的价格也会一直如此，直到量化分析师掌控世界。一旦量化分析师掌控世界，这种方法就不再有效；随后它又会重新生效，因为量化分析师会倒闭。

<!--en-->
**When you get into the top tier (deciles) of companies, you are working more as an insurance company (so you need a pool of bets to have the odds more in your favor).** Individually it is hard to own them because they are out of favor and they may work out or they may not. But as a group on average there are enough winners that work out. So you are really taking an insurance group bet rather than an individual stock bet. There will always be stuff out of favor and stocks will be priced that way until the quants take over the world. And when the quants take over the world, it stops working. Then it will work again because the quants will be out of business.

但总的来说……如果你想想量化模型是什么——对某人而言它只是一堆数字，它会在某个时刻失效，而你却无法判断是它失效了、环境变了，还是你的操作有误。**你**实际上是在分析公司。坦率地说，（确定标准化盈利）是我的日常工作，也是你的日常工作，因为你能够做到。这是为那些不干活的人准备的。**我的日常工作是确定标准化盈利并将其输入模型——而不是看去年发生了什么。**这对人们来说算是件容易的事。至于未来赚钱，总会有受青睐与不受青睐的股票。**人性不会改变。**

<!--en-->
But generally.....If you think about what a quantitative model is—it is just a bunch of numbers to somebody and it blows up at some point and then you don't know whether it blew up or things had changed or you are doing the wrong thing. **You** are actually analyzing companies. Frankly that is (figuring out normalized earnings) my day job and your day job because you can do it. This is for the guy not doing any work. **My day job is figuring out what normalized earnings are and plugging it into the model--not looking what happened last year.** This is sort of an easy thing for people to do. As far as making money in the future, there is always stuff that is in and out of favor. **Human nature doesn't change.**

### 评估管理层

<!--en-->
*Evaluating Managements*

**关键不在于死记硬背规则。** 因为整个学期人们都会问我关于管理评估的问题，但我只是试图判断某些人会如何为自身利益行事。这家伙的激励因素是什么？我尽量运用逻辑来分析：他做某事的动机是什么？如果人们没有动力把事情做好，他们通常就不会去做。世上确实有一些伟大的人，无论有无激励都会做正确的事，但总体而言人性还是占主导。你必须预料到人们会为自己的利益行事，并了解他们的激励机制。我正是基于这种预期来行动的。

<!--en-->
**The main point is not to memorize rules.** Because people ask me about this--evaluating management--throughout the semester, but I am just trying to evaluate how certain people will act in their own best interests. How is this guy incentivized? I try to use logic. What is his incentive to do this? If people are not incentivized to do a good job they generally won't do it. There are some great people in the world that will do the right thing regardless of incentives but on average human nature prevails. You must expect people will act in their best interests and know how they are incentivized. I would go in expecting that.

持有公司多少比例的股份才是最佳选择？无论管理层是否受到良好激励，这都可能是公司的优势所在。他们是否一直在尽可能多地侵占公司资产并将其挥霍掉？如果过去五年他们一直在回购股票，那我推测股价一定很便宜，否则他们不会这么做。

<!--en-->
What percentage of the company is best to own? It is either a strong point for the company whether management is incentivized well or not. Do they keep stealing as much as they can and keep blowing it out? If they are buying back stock over the last five years, I assume it is cheap or they wouldn't do that.

**学生：** 投资组合经理们不想在投资组合中持有这类股票（即那些有“负面”短期消息的神奇公式股票）吗？

**学生：** 你认为大多数人都是这么想的吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** You think the majority think that way?

不确定性太多，或者形势会恶化。不确定性实在太大了。情况很糟糕。你会说：“哦，我就知道它不怎么样，现在股价从33美元跌到了25美元。这通常不是人们愿意介入的时候。”

<!--en-->
There is too much uncertainty or things will turn down. There is too much uncertainty. It is tough. Things are down. You say, “Oh, I knew that stunk and now it is down from $33 to $25. It is not usually the time when guys say let us jump in here.

我不会去考虑别人在做什么或怎么想。**只需思考你该思考什么。** 简而言之，就是要剔除无关紧要的东西，让过程变得简单。别管别人怎么想或接下来会发生什么。**算出某样东西到底值多少钱，然后以更低的价格买入。** 先确定它的价值，再推算出未来的正常化盈利水平。不是去年、今年或明年的数据。大多数时候你无法做到这一点；也许业务本身太不确定、太复杂，或者你根本不了解。但如果能在你熟悉的公司中做到这点，那就是完整的分析过程。只要价格足够低，我们就能获得建仓机会。除非股价触底，否则我们从不抄底。通常这样做效果并不理想。

<!--en-->
I do not think about what others are doing or thinking. **Just think about what you should be thinking.** To cut to the chase the idea here is to cut out the extraneous stuff. It becomes a very simple process. Forget about what he thinks or what is happening next. **Figure out what the darn thing is worth and buy it for less.** To figure out what it is worth then figure out what are normalized earnings down the road. Not what happened last year or this year or next year? Most of the time you won't be able to do that. Maybe the business is too uncertain or too tough or you don't really know. **But if you can do that in the companies you do know, that is the whole analysis.**
It looks cheap enough, and we are getting paid to take our position. Unless the stock bottoms, we have never bottom ticked a stock. Usually it doesn't work out so well.

当你大量买入某只股票后还继续**看好它**，那就说明你手握好货。拥有这种**信心**的情况并不常见。

<!--en-->
You know you have something great when you are **rooting the stock down** after you have bought a lot. That doesn't happen that often where you have that **confidence**.

Or you can do *Scott Trade* which is $7 a trade and you can buy 20 stocks the first year which is $140 per year. The advantage **for you** is that you can do small caps.

你说得对，我也担心这一点。小盘股在研究期间（1987年至2003年）的年收益率比市场高出18%，随着账户规模扩大，这能抵消不少交易成本。（注：小盘股未必平均而言被低估，但它们更容易出现定价错误，要么被高估，要么被低估。）如今25年来首次，我在大盘股领域发现了更好的便宜货。不过小盘股的表现也很出色，因此这也是有力的论据。

<!--en-->
But you are right, and I was concerned about that. You can do **small caps** which have done 18% a year better than the market during the study period (1987 to 2003) and that will take care of a lot of the transaction costs as the account grows. *(Note: Small Caps are not necessarily on average more undervalued but they are subject to more mis-pricing of either being more overvalued or more undervalued).*
Right now the first time in 25 years I am finding better bargains in the large cap area. Though it works great for large caps so that is the best argument.

如果你有其他问题……
