## *罗伯特·豪根*的著作：他撰写的三本关于股市行为的书籍分别是：**《低效的股票市场》**、*What Pays Off and Why*。前者聚焦于预期收益因子模型，试图利用由错误驱动的波动性获利；低价股带来的正收益源于市场对成败的过度反应。中期动量带来的正收益则源于市场对个股盈利报告中的正负意外情况的反应不足。**《新金融学》** 探讨了市场的主要系统性错误：由于未能认识到市场经济中竞争力量的强度，市场高估了短期因素的作用时长；因此对市场对公司成败的反应过度，导致成功企业股价过高，失败企业股价过低。市场并不会对独特事件反应不足。**《华尔街野兽》** 聚焦股票波动性，认为其包含三个组成部分：股价对真实经济事件的理性且无偏反应构成了事件驱动型波动的来源。

<!--en-->
Books by *Robert Haugen*: The three books about the behavior of the stock market that he wrote were: **The Inefficient Stock Market.** What Pays Off and Why. This focused on expected-return factor models, which, in part, attempt to exploit error-driven volatility. The positive payoff to cheapness results from the market's overreaction to success and failure. The positive payoff to intermediate-term momentum results from the market's under reaction to positive and negative surprises in individual earnings reports. **The New Finance** focused on the market's major systemic mistake. In failing to appreciate the strength of competitive forces in a market economy, it over-estimates the length of competitive forces in a market economy, it over-estimates the length of the short run. In doing so, it overreacts to records of success and failure for individual companies, driving the prices of successful firms too high and their unsuccessful counterparts too low. The market doesn't under react to a unique event. **Beast on Wall Street** focuses on stock volatility. It contends that stock volatility has three components. Rational and unbiased responses of stock market prices to real, economic events are the source of event-driven volatility. End

### 《小书里的神奇公式》或许真的有效

<!--en-->
*Magic Formula of Little Book Just May Work*

2005年11月9日；C1版：尽管难以想象，但对冲基金巨头们和其他“宇宙主宰者”很快便会捧着一本标题俏皮的小书入睡：《战胜市场的那本小书》。

<!--en-->
November 9, 2005; Page C1
As hard as it is to envision, hedge-fund titans and other masters of the universe soon will be tucking themselves into bed with a thin tome bearing a cutesy title: "The Little Book That Beats the Market."

原因如下：作者是前对冲基金经理乔尔·格林布拉特。他于1997年出版的第一本投资指南同样标题滑稽，名为《你也能成为股市天才（即使你并不聪明）》，该书售出了约38,000册精装本和平装本。

<!--en-->
Here's why: The author is Joel Greenblatt, a former hedge-fund manager. His first investment guide, published in 1997, also sported a hokey title, "You Can Be a Stock Market Genius (Even If You're Not Too Smart)," and sold about 38,000 hardcover and soft cover copies.

作为处女作而言成绩不错，它还在封闭的对冲基金圈内成为畅销书，像地下出版物一样在基金经理之间传阅。这是一本用通俗易懂的语言写成、充满笑话的投资故事与案例集；据向我推荐此书的对冲基金经理们说，书中包含两个深刻的见解。

<!--en-->
Not bad as first books go, but it also became a cult hit in the insular world of hedge funds, passed like samizdat from manager to manager. A book of war stories and case studies written clearly and laced with jokes, it had two profound insights, say hedge-fund managers who have pressed the book on me.

其一，股市中存在一些隐蔽的角落，比如分拆和重组，那里往往隐藏着廉价股；其二，并没有充分理由去持有包含数十只股票的庞大投资组合，因为设计精良、集中的投资组合就能在不增加风险的前提下实现高回报目标。

<!--en-->
One was that there are secret hiding places in the stock market, like spin-offs and restructurings, where bargains tend to lurk. The other was there wasn't any compelling reason to have a giant portfolio of dozens of stocks when a well-designed, concentrated portfolio could accomplish the same goal of achieving high returns without adding risk.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：“他的投资类书籍是我读过的最有价值的东西，”管理着大型成功对冲基金Greenlight Capital的大卫·Einhorn说道。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
"His book on investing is by far the most valuable thing I have read," says David Einhorn, who manages a large, successful hedge fund, Greenlight Capital.

但他说：“对冲基金经理们并非我写书时所针对的弱势群体。”因此，在撰写第二本书时，格林布拉特先生希望写出一本更基础、更根本的投资书籍，以吸引华尔街以外的人群。可以想象成本杰明·格雷厄姆用通俗语言讲解投资之道。

<!--en-->
But hedge-fund managers "were not quite the underprivileged group I was shooting for when I wrote it," he says. So for his second book, Mr. Greenblatt says he wanted to write an even more basic and fundamental book on investing that would appeal beyond Wall Street. Think Benjamin Graham does Borscht Belt.

47岁的格林布拉特表示，他的目标是提供既专业又能被他6岁到15岁的五个孩子理解和遵循的建议。他们真是幸运——他即将出版的《小书》堪称市面上最优秀、最清晰的价值投资指南之一。虽然我有些小意见，但在个人投资建议领域充斥着晦涩难懂的短期主义或过于简化的指数化投资说法之际，格林布拉特的方法显得尤为珍贵。

<!--en-->
Mr. Greenblatt, 47 years old, says his goal was to provide advice that, while sophisticated, could be understood and followed by his five children, ages 6 to 15. They are in luck. His soon-to-be-released "Little Book" is one of the best, clearest guides to value investing out there. I have some minor quibbles, but in a world where individual-investor advice is dominated by jargon-filled short-termism on the one hand and oversimplified throw-up-your-hands indexing on the other, Mr. Greenblatt's approach is valuable.

这本书内容简单又可爱，以至于稍有经验的投资者可能会误以为它不值一提。格林布拉特将他的投资方法称为“魔法公式”。他虽是开玩笑，却也不全是无稽之谈。他写作时的语气宛如J.M.巴里在讲述彼得潘式的童话故事，但又带着一个虔诚信徒的热情：

<!--en-->
It is so simple and cute that an investor with a little bit of knowledge might mistakenly dismiss it. Mr. Greenblatt titles his investment approach a "magic formula." His tongue is in his cheek, but not entirely. He writes as if he were J.M. Barrie spinning a Peter Pan-esque fairy tale, but with the fervor of a true believer:

“你必须花时间理解其中的道理，最重要的是，你真的要相信这个道理是正确的。事实上，这个理论最终会归结为一个能让你随时间变富的‘魔法公式’。我可不是在开玩笑。”

<!--en-->
"You have to take the time to understand the story, and most important, you have to actually believe that the story is true. In fact, the story concludes with a magic formula that can make you rich over time. I kid you not."

什么是“魔法公式”呢？就是在股票便宜时投资好公司。正如格林布拉特可能会说的那样：看吧，我们早说过这听起来显而易见。那么，究竟什么算“好”公司？什么又算“便宜”呢？

<!--en-->
What is the magic formula? Invest in good companies when they are cheap. As Mr. Greenblatt might say: See? We told you it sounded obvious. Yeah, so what's "good"? And what's "cheap"?

他解释道，好公司能带来高额投资回报，而便宜公司则指股价较低（基于过往盈利数据）的公司。他用来衡量这些标准的指标分别是资本回报率（营业利润占营运资本与固定资产净值的百分比）以及盈利收益率（税前营业收益与企业价值之比，企业价值即市值加上净债务）。不过值得称赞的是，格林布拉特用不会冒犯专业人士但能让普通读者也能理解的术语解释了所有这些专业术语。

<!--en-->
Good companies earn high returns on their investments, he explains, while cheap companies sport share prices that are low (based on past earnings). His proxies for these criteria are return on capital (operating profit as a percentage of net working capital and net fixed assets) and earnings yield (pretax operating earnings compared with enterprise value, which is the market value plus the net debt). To his credit, however, Mr. Greenblatt explains all that parenthetical jargon in terms that shouldn't insult his peers but that will ring a bell for the unschooled masses.

为了进一步简化操作，他免费的网站www.magicformulainvesting.com,会根据他的标准筛选股票。他建议个人投资者买入一篮子优质股票，并根据它们的表现按固定时间表进行调整。（为了最大化税务优惠，可在持有满一年前卖出亏损股，满一年后卖出盈利股。）

<!--en-->
To make things simpler still, his free Web site, www.magicformulainvesting.com, screens companies using his criteria. He advises individual investors to buy a basket of top stocks and turn them over on a strict schedule, depending on how they perform. (For maximum tax advantage, sell losers just before a year's up and winners just after a year.)

听起来似乎太容易了。但实际上，这种方法之所以困难，并非因为难以理解，而是因为它需要耐心和信念——即便市场认为你错了，你也要坚信自己是对的。

<!--en-->
It sounds too easy. But in fact, his approach is difficult not because it is hard to understand, but because it requires patience and faith that you are right when the market is saying you're wrong.

这一理念源自沃伦·巴菲特的投资原则，但值得反复强调。就连像格林布拉特这样坚定的价值投资者也坦言，直到20世纪90年代他才意识到：寻找既便宜又好的公司比单纯找便宜股更为重要。巴菲特的导师格雷厄姆追求的是极度廉价的公司，而巴菲特则只青睐伟大的公司。

<!--en-->
This is based on Warren Buffett's investment principles. But they bear repeating. Even a die-hard value investor like Mr. Greenblatt says he didn't realize that trying to find cheap, good companies, rather than just cheap ones, was so important until the 1990s. While Mr. Graham, Mr. Buffett's mentor, was looking for starkly cheap companies, Mr. Buffett wants only the great ones.

格林布拉特说：“直到20世纪90年代初，我才真正被巴菲特的理念影响。真希望那能更早发生。”

<!--en-->
"I didn't get Buffettized until the early 1990s," says Mr. Greenblatt. "I wish it happened earlier."

回顾来看，“魔法公式”的回报明显优于市场。根据格林布拉特书中的数据，从1988年到2004年，市值排名前1000的公司中那些高回报/低价格的股票年均回报率为22.9%，而标普500指数仅为12.4%。

<!--en-->
Looked at retroactively, the returns of the "magic formula" beat the market handily. From 1988 through 2004, according to Mr. Greenblatt's book, the high-return/low-price stocks of the largest 1,000 companies had returns of 22.9% annually, compared with 12.4% for the S&P 500.

格林布拉特论点中最令人信服的一点是：当对2500家公司按价格和回报排名时，排名前10%的公司表现优于接下来的10%，以此类推。“这玩意儿确实按顺序排列有效，”他说。

<!--en-->
The most convincing part of Mr. Greenblatt's argument is that when 2,500 companies are ranked for price and returns (based on the formula), the top 10% outperformed the second 10%, which outperformed the third 10% and so on. "The darn thing works in order," he says.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：这种方法也存在一些局限。它似乎容易挑出那些高回报和高增长已成过去的股票。市值超过10亿美元的“魔法公式”股票中，有很多是快速增长的专业零售商和细分制药公司。其中一些最终可能会衰落。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
There are some limitations to the approach. It seems prone to tossing up stocks whose high returns and growth may be in the past. Magic-formula stocks with more than $1 billion in stock-market value include lots of fast-growing specialty retailers and niche pharmaceutical companies. Some of these will flame out.

正因如此，格林布拉特建议新手投资者至少购买20到30只此类股票。至于他自己，则会选择数量较少、他能深入了解的股票。但这需要一种书中难以传授的能力：敏锐的直觉和判断力，以区分真正的低价优质股和一炮而红后便销声匿迹的股票。

<!--en-->
That's why Mr. Greenblatt argues that novice investors buy at least 20 or 30 of them. For himself, he buys a smaller number that he can know deeply. But that requires something not easily taught in a book: good instincts and judgment to distinguish true cheap gems from one-hit wonders.

尽管他一直是一位价值投资者，但他所创立的对冲基金公司Gotham Capital并非总是遵循他的“神奇公式”来运作，尤其是在早期，当时他更倾向于复杂的套利策略。他于1985年创办Gotham Capital，为外部投资者管理该基金长达10年，在扣除费用前但计入开支后，实现了50%的复合年化收益率。他最初投入了700万美元，这笔资金主要通过垃圾债券大王迈克尔·米尔肯筹集而来。五年后，他返还了一半的外部资本；最终该基金规模超过3.5亿美元，所有剩余外部资本也都被返还给投资者。

<!--en-->
Though he always was a value investor, his hedge-fund firm, Gotham Capital, wasn't always run on his magic formula, especially in the early years, when he tended toward complex arbitrage. He started Gotham in 1985 and ran it for outside investors for 10 years, achieving compounded annual returns, before fees but after expenses, of 50%. He started with $7 million, mostly raised through junk-bond king Michael Milken. After five years, he returned half the outside capital. He finished with more than $350 million and returned all the remaining outside capital.

如今，他把时间花在哥伦比亚商学院的教学上，并协助运营面向专业人士的网站——价值投资者俱乐部。他的财富主要集中于Gotham Capital，该公司管理的资产规模达16亿美元，其中包括几年前他发起设立的一只对冲基金中的部分外部资金。

<!--en-->
These days, he spends his time teaching at Columbia Business School and helping run a Web site for pros, the Value Investors Club. His wealth is mostly tied up in Gotham Capital, which manages $1.6 billion, including some outside money in a fund of hedge funds he started a few years back.

他的家常菜不仅足以满足格林布拉特先生的口味，连他的孩子们也爱吃。他的长子按照书中的建议行事，表现不错；而一个女儿尝试了两个月，却遇到了些困难。“我不确定如果她没有我这个父亲，是否还能坚持下去，”他说。

<!--en-->
His home cooking isn't just good enough for Mr. Greenblatt. He's got his kids eating it, too. His eldest son is doing well following the book's advice. A daughter, at it for two months, is having a rougher time. "I'm not sure if she didn't have me as her daddy she'd be hanging in there," he says.

乔尔·格林布拉特特殊情境投资课程  
2005年3月23日，星期三  
斯普林豪斯资本的布莱恩·盖恩斯主讲

<!--en-->
Joel Greenblatt Class for Special Situations Investing
Wednesday, March 23, 2005
Brian Gains of Springhouse Capital

### “衰落”行业投资案例研究

<!--en-->
*Case Study of Investing in a "Dying" Industry*

*斜体：约翰·周整理的讲稿*  
乔尔·格林布拉特引言：

<!--en-->
Italics: Transcript by John Chew
Joel Greenblatt Introduction:

我们的嘉宾不会唱歌，但他非常聪明，他经营着一家名为斯普林豪斯资本的公司。该公司成立于2002年。

<!--en-->
Our guest will not sing, but he is really smart and he runs a fund called Springhouse Capital. He started in 2002.

希望你们已经看过BBI、MOVI和Hollywood的相关资料。斯普林豪斯资本创始人布莱恩·盖恩斯：我的演讲题目是：**在“衰落”行业中赚钱**。我将向大家介绍我是如何产生这一想法的、我所做的工作，以及几个有趣的案例研究——包括当时的事实和背景，以便你们能了解我的思考过程。

<!--en-->
I hope you took a look at BBI, MOVI and Hollywood.
Brian Gains, Founder of Springhouse Capital
My title is: **Making money in a "dying" industry**
I will take you through how I came up with the idea, the work I did and then a couple of different case studies, which I think will be pretty interesting along the way--the facts or the things that were going on--so you can experience what I was thinking or the thought process I was trying to go through.

正如你们从股市研究中知道的那样，常常有一些被人厌恶的行业，如果你偏向价值投资，这些行业正是值得涉足的领域。这些是我寻找投资灵感的地方。创意生成。

<!--en-->
As you know from your studies of the stock market, there are often hated industries where you want to go if you have more of a value bent. Some of the places I go to find investment ideas.
Idea Generation

- 52周最低价股票列表
- 高空头持仓比例  
哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程
* 《投资者商业日报》中的负动量指标
* 分拆上市
* 困境债务：收益率最高的领域  
人人都嘲笑《投资者商业日报》，但你可以在上面找到那些被所有人厌恶的、处于负动量状态的行业。你可以从中看出人们讨厌什么。从一些可能提供灵感的行业入手吧。我相信乔尔曾提到过分拆上市。你也能看到属于困境债务范畴的资产。显然，如果债务以面值的50%到60%的价格交易，那说明人们不喜欢它——这正是一个不错的起点。由此你便能找到寻找投资思路的方向。
* 挑战在于判断这种“厌恶”是否合理（企业被厌恶往往有其原因）。
* 公司可分为四类：
  - 不可持续的业务
    - 应回避
  - 糟糕的资产负债表（如2002年的Cellular公司）
    - 分析资本结构
    - 很多时候这类似于期权投资，而理解资本结构决定了该期权的成熟程度。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程。
  - 周期性行业（大宗商品处于下行周期）
    - normalized earnings（经调整后的盈利）
  - 夕阳产业（摄影、复印等）
    - 它还能持续多久？
    - 它真的消亡了吗？
    - 内部人员正在做什么？
    - 资金流向何处？难点在于找出一家企业被看衰的合理原因。我认为这些情况可分为四类：

<!--en-->
- 52 week low lists
- High short interest
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
* Investors' Business Daily negative momentum
* Spin-offs
* Distressed Debt: Highest yielding areas
Everyone makes fun of *Investors' Business Daily* but you can go in there and find negative momentum industries where everyone hates the industry(s). You can see what people hate. Start with some industries that may give you some ideas. I am sure Joel has spoken about spin-offs. You can see what is in the distressed area. Obviously, if debt is trading at 50 to 60 cents on the dollar, people don't like it--that would be a good place to start. This leads you to a place to look for ideas.
* Challenge is figuring out if the hate is logical (there are reasons why businesses are hated.)
* Companies fall in one of four categories:
  - Unsustainable business
    - Avoid
  - Bad balance sheet (Cellular in 2002)
    - Analyze the capital structure
    - Often times akin to an option bet and understanding cap structure determines the maturity of the option.
  - Cyclical (Commodities in down cycle)
    - Normalized earnings
  - Dying businesses (Photography, Photocopying, etc.)
    - How long will it last?
    - Is it really dead?
    - What are the people on the inside doing?
    - Where is the cash going?
The challenge is figuring out if there is a logical reason(s) a business is hated. I like to think that things fall into four different categories:

### 1. 不可持续的企业：

<!--en-->
*1. Unsustainable Business:*

* 应避开这类企业。不可持续的企业就像eToys.com、Pets.com一样，在2001-2002年便宣告崩溃。你可能会觉得它的股价很便宜——该股曾高达50美元，如今却仅售2美元。实际上，它根本算不上一家真正的企业；无论其拥有多少现金或资本结构如何，最终都无法维持下去。这就是一个例子。学生问：通用汽车（GM）呢？BRIAN GAINS回答：通用汽车的业务或许具有可持续性。虽然其债务结构存在问题，但它生产的是人们需要的汽车。

<!--en-->
* AVOID
An unsustainable business is like an eToys.com, Pets.com. Something that collapses in 2001-2002 and you are looking at it. You can say it is really cheap; the stock used to be at $50 and it is at $2 now. In reality, it is not a business--no matter how much cash it has or the capital structure, eventually it wasn't going to work. So that is one example.
Student: General Motors (GM)?
BRIAN GAINS: GM's business is probably sustainable. Sure it has problems with its debt structure, but it makes cars that people need.

### 2. 糟糕的资产负债表：（以2002年的手机行业为例）

<!--en-->
*2. Bad Balance Sheet: (Cellular in 2002)*

* 分析资本结构
* 很多时候这类似于期权投资，而理解资本结构决定了该期权的成熟程度。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程。我将“糟糕的资产负债表”归为第二类，2002年的手机行业便是典型例子。关键在于*分析资本结构*。所有人都知道手机将会继续存在，但问题在于这些公司的资产负债表上背负了过多债务。如果Sprint等公司能够偿还债务，它们显然能盈利。判断的方法就是分析其资本结构。这实际上就是一种期权投资。你必须弄清楚：“银行会接管这家公司吗？”如果能挺过这一关——比如债务五年后才到期，足以让公司存活下来——那么这可能就是一笔不错的期权投资。

<!--en-->
* Analyze the capital structure
* Often times akin to an option bet and understanding cap structure determines the maturity of the option
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Then I put Bad Balance Sheet, which I think Cellular companies in 2002 are a prime example. The important thing there is *analyzing the capital structure*. Everyone knew that cellular phones would be around, but it is a question of they had too much debt on the balance sheet. Sprint and all these different companies, if they could pay the debt, they clearly could make money. They way to look at it is to analyze the capital structure. You literally have an option bet. And you have to figure out, "Are the banks going to take this under?" And if you can survive past that point--if the debt is due in five years, which is long enough for the company to survive-- you probably have a great option bet.

### 3. 周期性行业（大宗商品处于下行周期）

<!--en-->
*3. Cyclical Business (Commodities in a down cycle)*

* Normalized Earnings（经调整后的盈利）***理查德·普泽纳***是调整周期性企业盈利数据方面的专家。这类企业有存在的理由，但你必须找到其中的平衡点。你们都经历过这种情况。

<!--en-->
* Normalized Earnings
***Richard Pzena*** *is the king of normalizing earnings for cyclical businesses. These businesses have a reason to exist, but you have to look for the middle point. You have all been through that.*

## 4. 夕阳产业（摄影、复印等）

<!--en-->
*4. Dying businesses (Photography, Photocopying, etc.)*

* 它还能持续多久？
* 它真的消亡了吗？
* 内部人员正在做什么？
* 资金流向何处？接下来我要谈谈最后一类——所谓的夕阳产业。也许它确实在衰落，也许并非如此。有人会说非数码摄影、复印、传真机等行业属于此类。我将以视频租赁业为例。关键问题是：“它真的消亡了吗？”它能持续多久？第三点至关重要：**跟随内部人员的动向，看看他们是否对自家业务有信心。**这是判断该行业是否还有潜力的关键。同样重要的还有*资金流向何处？* **因为投资这类股票时，重点不在于估值倍数，而在于它们能产生多少现金以及如何使用这些现金。**在评估回报时，考虑未来两年的情况非常重要：如果该公司每股能产生2美元的现金，而你以8美元的价格买入该股，那相当不错。不过你仍需确定这种状况能持续多久。但追踪资金流向才是关键。

<!--en-->
* How long will it last?
* Is it really dead?
* What are the people on the inside doing?
* Where is the cash going?
I will talk about the last category, the allegedly dying business. Maybe it is dying; maybe it is not. And some people would say non-digital photography, photocopying, fax machines. I will talk about video rental. And the key questions are: "Is it really dead?" How long it is going to last? Number three is key: **follow the insiders to see if they have confidence in their business.** That is a great key to see if this thing has some legs left in it. Also key is *where is the cash going?* **Because when you are dealing with these stocks, it is less about a multiple and more about how much cash they are going to generate and what are they doing with the cash.** It is really important when you are looking at the return to think about the next two years, they are going to generate $2 dollars a share in cash and if you are buying the stock at $8, well that is pretty good. You still have to figure out how long that will last. But following the cash is key.

## 分析“濒临消亡”的行业

<!--en-->
*Analyzing the "dying" business*

* 这一过程包括梳理所有负面观点，并针对每个观点的合理性构建论点。（正题 vs. 反题）——这是最耗费时间的活动。
* 在家尝试此方法前需先了解以下几点：——你的行为和直觉很可能不支持你提出的论点；——人们会说你疯了；——其他基金公司的朋友会告诉你他们正在做空该股票，并说你疯了；——有时你会认为他们是对的，而你自己确实疯了。我通常的做法是选定一个行业，列出人们讨厌它的所有理由，把该行业中所有糟糕之处一一列举出来，然后试图找到其中的合理性。也就是说，它真的有他们说的那么糟吗？有没有理由说明它并没有他们想的那么差？比如现在有人提到了通用汽车（GM）。你可以看到GM股价下跌，接着看看所有汽车零部件供应商的情况，列出对该行业的各种负面评价。然后构建一个论点，说明由于ABC因素，该行业并不像人们想象的那么糟糕。你的行为和直觉很可能不会支持你的做法。如果你在研究视频租赁行业，可能会说：“我不再租视频看了。”需要记住的关键一点是*你并非目标受众*。你与大多数美国人不同：你更年轻、更城市化，很多行为方式也更具科技感。因此，如果是传真或视频租赁这类事物，你会说“我不再用这些了”，从而忽略整个行业。你的朋友们会说你疯了。哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
* Process involves going through all the negative arguments and constructing a thesis as to the merit of each. (*Thesis vs. Antithesis*)
--Most time intensive activity
* Some things to accept before attempting this at home:
--Your behavior and gut instinct probably won't support your thesis
--People will say you are nuts
--Your friends at other funds will tell you they are short the stock and you are nuts.
--At times you will come to believe they are right and you are nuts.
The way I tend to look at things is that I pick up an industry and I go through all the reasons why people hate it. List all of the things that are really, really bad about it. Then try to find a reason. OK, is it as bad as they think? Is there a reason why it is not as bad as they think?
So right now someone pointed out General Motors (GM). You can see GM down and then you look at all the auto parts guys and list all the negative thoughts on the industry. Then construct a thesis as to why the business is not as bad as people think because of ABC.
Your behavior and gut instinct are probably not going to support what you are doing. If you are looking at video rentals, you are probably saying, "I don't rent videos anymore." The one key to remember is *that you are not the target audience*. You are not like most of America. For one thing, you are younger and moreurban. A lot of things you do will be more technologically advanced. So if it is faxing or renting videos you will say, I don't do that anymore so forget that industry. Your friends will say you are crazy.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

## 视频租赁行业有哪些弊端？

<!--en-->
*What's Bad about Video Rental?*

* 产品售罄率
  - 长期发展趋势？
  - 价格持续下跌？
* 视频点播（VOD）
  - 45天的时间窗口。
  - 附加功能/24小时限制/高清内容及选择受限
* Netflix/上门配送
  - 小众产品
  - 即时满足感
* 数字发行
  - 通过电脑观看
  - 下载时间与电影时长的比例
  - 画质/高清
* 盗版问题
* TIVO
* 娱乐选择日益丰富。Brian Gains：那么租赁业务有什么不好呢？为什么有人不喜欢视频租赁业务呢？学生们：Netflix、沃尔玛销售DVD，还有视频点播服务。Brian Gains：沃尔玛出售廉价的DVD，所以人们无需再租赁。我还要补充一点：文件共享、盗版以及数字发行。我会询问不同的人，了解他们对这项业务的不满之处，然后再做决策。售价仅为6美元的两张DVD——这种低价销售模式会持续下去吗？这是长期趋势吗？价格还能继续下跌吗？沃尔玛以亏损的价格出售DVD，以此吸引顾客；制片厂对此乐见其成。还有哪种业务的经销商会故意亏本销售产品呢？有人有什么看法吗？我认为，看待这个问题的角度应该是：这是一种风险。我们可以接受自己无法预测未来的定价走势。我们知道，目前制片厂从DVD中获利颇丰。至于定价，实在难以预料——它会不会持续走低呢？要知道，这些制片厂并不想降低价格。如果DVD销量每年都在增长，他们就没有理由降价。制作一张DVD的成本约为2美元，而新片售价却高达17至18美元。**制片厂根本没有降价的动机。** 研究显示，沃尔玛确实在亏本销售新片DVD，因此沃尔玛其实是在为制片厂帮忙。你见过哪家产品的经销商会亏本销售呢？这种情况并不常见。我们知道制片厂对此非常满意，他们目前并无降价之意。从逻辑上讲，制片厂确实没有动力降低价格。关于视频点播服务：重要的是要理解新片是如何进入影院放映的——它们会在影院上映两到三个月，之后便被搁置起来，随后才发行DVD。这个周期为45天。新片对音像店至关重要，因为80%的租赁业务都依赖于新片。制片厂不希望影片过早进入视频点播渠道；每售出一张DVD，他们就能赚15美元。这一点至关重要，因为有人会说视频点播会摧毁音像租赁店。可以说，由于制片厂从DVD销售中获利丰厚，他们不会缩短音像店销售DVD的时间窗口，以免影响到新片在视频点播前在音像店的销售。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程指出：你不能断言视频点播取代DVD和录像带的情况不会发生。**关键在于人们改变习惯的速度有多快。** 目前，只有2%的音乐通过数字方式发行，98%的音乐仍通过CD销售。我认为最终这种情况会发生，只是需要多长时间而已。另外，视频点播还需要数字有线电视支持，这意味着能享受该服务的群体较为有限；而且用户往往不在乎额外内容如删节场景等。制片厂正转向高清DVD，这又是人们不选择视频点播的另一个原因。Netflix提供上门送货服务，其客户数量约为260万；Blockbuster的客户数则为75万。这是两种不同的商业模式：Netflix有Premier会员——这类用户追求更丰富的影片类别，包括许多小众电影；这些并非同一类客户。数字发行所需的下载时间太长，对普通消费者而言实在不便。虽然TIVO已经问世，但人们仍然想看电影，尤其是新片。无论发行方式如何，人们去电影院观看电影都是为了那种体验。娱乐选择的确日益丰富。

<!--en-->
* Sell-Through
  - Long-term trend?
  - Pricing continuing downward?
* VOD
  - 45 day window
  - Additional features/24 hour limit/HD and selection constrained
* Netflix/Home delivery
  - Niche product
  - Instant Gratification
* Digital Distribution
  - Computer watching
  - Time to download relative to length of movie
  - Quality/HD
* Piracy
* TIVO
* Ever expanding entertainment options.
Brian Gains: So what is bad about the rental business? Why wouldn't you like the Video Rental Business?
Students: Netflix, Wal-Mart selling DVDs. VOD.
Brian Gains: Wal-Mart sells cheap DVDs, so people don't need to rent.
One of the things I would add is file sharing, piracy and digital distribution. I would talk to different people and ask what is not good about the business. And then sell through. Is the selling of cheap DVDs--$6 for two DVDs--going to continue. Is this a long-term trend? Can the price continue downward? Wal-Mart is selling DVD's at a loss to drive traffic. The studios love this. What other business has the distributors of their product intentionally selling the product at a loss?
Anyone have any thoughts?
So, I guess the way to look at this is that this is a risk. So we can accept that we don't know what is going to happen in pricing. We know that the studios currently make a lot of money off of DVDs and you can establish that. As to pricing it is very hard to predict. That is going to be one of those variables where you just don't know--is pricing going to steadily creep down? You know these guys (studios) don't want to cut the prices. If the DVD are growing every year, they have no incentive to cut the prices. It costs about $2 to make a DVD and they are selling new releases for $17 to $18. **They (the studios) have no incentive to cut prices.** Research will show you that Wal-Mart is selling new DVDs at a loss. So Wal-Mart is doing the studios a favor. How often do you see a distributor of your product sell at a loss? It is infrequent. We know the studios are pretty happy. They have no desire at this point to cut prices. So logically, the studios don't have an incentive to lower prices.
VOD: It is important to understand how new releases enter the theatres and they are there for two or three months, then they sit on the sidelines. Then they go to DVD. 45 days. New releases are important for video stores. 80% of their rentals are new releases. The studios don't want it to go to VOD. They make $15 every time they sell a DVD. THIS IS CRITICAL because someone can say VOD will destroy the video rental stores. You can make a case that the studios make so much money off of selling (DVDs) that they will not collapse the window of time for the video stores to sell the DVDs before the releases go to VOD.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
You can't say that it (VOD eliminating DVDs and videos) isn't going to happen. **It is a question of how quickly people change their habits.** 2% of all music sold is digitally distributed. So 98% of all music sold is through CDs.
I would say eventually it is going to happen, it is just how long will it take.
The other thing about VOD, you need to have digital cable so you are talking about a smaller portion of the country. You need to not have (or not care about) additional features like extra scenes. Studios are moving toward high definition DVD, so you have another reason not to buy VOD.
Netflix home delivery. Netflix has about 2.6 million customers. Blockbuster has 750,000 customers. It is a different business. It has Premier customers--people who want more category depth. A lot of niche films. These aren't the same customers.
Digital distribution takes too long to download. In reality it takes time too much time for the average consumer.
TIVO came out, but people still want to watch movies. People want to watch new movies. A truism no matter how distributed. People go to movies because of the experience.
Ever expanding entertainment options.

## 视频租赁业务有哪些优势？

<!--en-->
*What's Good about Video Rental?*

* 现金流状况良好。
* 新投资的回报率可观。
* 45天的时间窗口。
  - DVD的经济性。
* 比人们想象的更为稳定。
  - 请注意，大多数企业的存续时间都比人们预想的要长。
* 夫妻店仍占据40%的市场份额。
* 他们还能利用现有基础设施做些什么呢？
  - 零售/电子游戏/二手商品：布莱恩·盖恩斯——视频租赁业务有什么优势？  
学生：现金流不错。  
布莱恩·盖恩斯：现金流非常棒。他们拥有出色的零售模式。音像店还能销售其他商品。新开音像店的回报率简直惊人。因为开店所需的成本并不高（包括库存费用）。开设一家Blockbuster门店只需15万美元。其妙处在于：如果生意不景气，你可以把店搬到八英里外再试一次。这种业务很容易迁移。回报率很高，因此即便出点差错也负担得起。对音像店而言，45天的时间窗口至关重要（用于销售DVD）。这个行业其实比人们想象的更稳定。**很多企业的存续时间都比人们以为的要长得多。**未来二三十年里，人们仍会继续购买视频产品。人们仍在购买黑胶唱片，尽管已有替代品；在夫妻店中，黑胶唱片仍占据30%到40%的市场份额。这听起来有点“邪恶”，但这就是资本主义。只要小型商家还占有一定份额，像Blockbuster这样的连锁企业就能介入并取而代之。因此Blockbuster仍能继续扩大市场份额。他们还能利用现有基础设施做些什么呢？哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程——许多相关研究正是在那里进行的。研究者们会花大量时间与业内人士交谈，以弄清其中有多少是真实可行的。

<!--en-->
* Good cash flows
* Good returns on new investments
* 45 day window
  - Economics of DVD
* More stable than people think
  - Note that most businesses will last longer than people think
* Mom and Pop's still hold 40% share
* What else can they do with their infrastructure?
  - Retail/Video Games/Used
Brian Gains: What is good about the video rental business?
Student: The cash flows are good.
Brian Gains: The cash flows are great. They have a great retail box. Video stores can sell other stuff. The returns on new video stores are absolutely amazing. Because it doesn't cost much (to set up a store with inventory). It is $150,000 to open a Blockbuster. The beauty of it, is that if it doesn't work, then you can move it eight miles down the road and try again. You can move the business easily. The returns are high and you can afford to screw up a little bit. The 45-day window is critical for video stores (allowing Video Stores to sell DVDs). This is more stable than people think. **A lot of businesses last a lot longer than people think.** For another 20 or 30 years people will still be buying videos. People are still buying phonographic records and there is a replacement for records.
There still is a 30% to 40% share of the market in mom & pop stores. It is kind of evil sounding but it is capitalism. If the small business owners still have share, as a chain like Blockbuster, you can go in and you can take them out. So Blockbuster can still gain share.
What else can they do with the infrastructure?
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
So that is where a lot of the research is done. A lot of time talking to people to figure out how much of this is real.

## 从宏观到微观

<!--en-->
*Macro to micro*

要综合衡量所有这些因素并得出一个简便的视频租赁业绩指标，最直观的方式就是查看各门店的同店销售额。——不过有一些因素会干扰这一分析。那么，我该如何从中获利呢？在此之前，这一切都还只是理论上的；人们只是停留在对行业的初步思考阶段。

<!--en-->
Simplest place to look to find all these factors rolled up into one easy measure of video rental performance is the same store sales of the respective stores.
--Mitigating factors that will disrupt this analysis
OK, so how do I make money off of this? Before it was all-theoretical; before you were kind of thinking about the industry.

对于视频租赁业绩而言，同店销售额（SSS）是衡量其实际表现的关键指标。人们据此形成各种假设，然后试图找出其具体体现——即同店销售额的变化。但需要记住的是，视频行业中有许多干扰因素会影响SSS，就像其他行业一样（如天气、新片上映日程、政治事件、季度内的天数差异等）。正因如此，SSS未必能完全反映真实经营状况。答：Blockbuster的新片发行会吸引顾客进店——热门产品带来的销售波动较大。**人们只看同比数据，便说销售额下降了3%，却未考虑到这些影响因素。**天气也会影响销售；一个季度有12个周末，其中一个糟糕的周末就足以造成影响。

<!--en-->
For Video rental performance, the same store sales (SSS) statistic is key for forming how much of this is coming to life. You form all these theses. And then try to find out where it will show itself--in the video guise of same-store-sales. But the one thing to remember in the video business there are many mitigating factors that will affect SSS as any business (weather, feature presentation schedules, political events, days in the quarter). In this case why SSS may not be indicative of the business. Ans: Blockbuster releases drive customers to stores--hit driven product/sales causes lumpy sales. **People look at comps and say that comps are down 3% without adjusting for what effects the change.** Weather can affect sales. 12 weekends in a quarter--one bad weekend can have an affect.

我还要补充一点：儿童电影通常是被购买而非租赁的。孩子们倾向于反复观看同一部电影，而成年人则不会如此。

<!--en-->
I would also say, children's movies--they sell they don't rent. Kids have a propensity to watch the same movies over and over again. It would not be normal behavior for adults.

商店出租的电影类型也很重要。有时政治事件会导致人们更多看电视而非租电影。

<!--en-->
It is the *type of movie* that the store rents. Sometimes political events may cause people to watch more TV then rent movies.

Blockbuster（BBI）、Hollywood（HLYW）、MOVI等品牌正在从夫妻店手中夺取市场份额，这会让整个行业看起来表现不佳，但实际上它们正在抢占更多份额。当地音像店倒闭后，原本光顾它们的顾客便会转而去Blockbuster门店，因此这些门店的生意反而得以延续。

<!--en-->
The Blockbuster (BBI), Hollywood (HLYW), MOVI are all taking share from the mom & pop (stores), then it will make it look like the business is worse, but they are taking more share. Their business is surviving, because they opened a Blockbuster (store) but the local video store shut down. So everyone who went to that local store will go to the Blockbuster.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的第112期特殊情况投资课程：现在我们来聊聊我研究**Hollywood Video（HLYW）**的过程。Blockbuster有6,000家门店，而Hollywood有2,000家，两者选址类似，且更集中于西海岸地区。可以视为同类企业。

<!--en-->
112
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Now we will go through what I went through with **Hollywood Video (HLYW)**. Blockbuster has 6,000 stores while Hollywood has 2,000 stores but in the same kind of areas though more West coast oriented. Consider it identical.

2003年股市表现强劲，到了12月时我却觉得没什么值得关注的。于是我开始筛选各种投资机会。我想，既然大家都讨厌视频租赁行业，那我就从这方面入手吧。我做了我们之前讨论过的那些准备工作，随后参加了Hollywood Video的投资者推介会。那时我对它一无所知，只凭一些理由认为这个行业仍有存在价值。让我们具体看看Hollywood Video的情况。

<!--en-->
The (stock) market had a great 2003 and I am sitting around in Dec 2003 and there is nothing too interesting going on. So I am screening different stuff. So I say OK, everyone hates the video rental guys. So I do all that first stuff we talked about. Then I go to an investor presentation. I go to see Hollywood Video. At that point I knew nothing other than I had some arguments as to why this industry could exist. Let's look specifically at Hollywood Video.

在Hollywood Video的案例中发现，他们正在开设名为Game Crazies的游戏专卖店，这类店铺回报丰厚。首席执行官还表示每年将新开150家门店，且同样能获得可观回报。于是你会想：“也许这个行业不会长久，但HLWD的首席执行官似乎对此信心满满。他仍在不断开店，态度积极。”

<!--en-->
What you will see in the Hollywood story is that they are opening up Game Crazies, which are like a game store boutique. They are getting great returns. The CEO is also saying he is going to open 150 new stores a year and getting great returns. So you say, "Hey, maybe the business doesn't last so long, but he (CEO of HLWD) seems to think so. He is still opening stores. He is mildly positive.

首席执行官持有10%的股份，这一点在本案中将起到重要作用。虽然我们权衡了各种论据后认为可以信任他，但内部人士又是怎么说的呢？本案中，他（首席执行官）持有10%的股份，且正是他做出了开设新音像店的决定。这一点值得牢记：持有10%股份的人仍坚持要开设这些店铺。也许他很愚蠢，也许并非如此；但你必须承认他对业务的了解比你更多——因为他每天都在亲身经历业务运营，他能看到各项数据，也能看到那些证明“这种模式仍可行”的测试结果。毕竟这是他的钱，他所承担的风险可能比你大得多。

<!--en-->
The CEO owns 10% of the stock and this will come into play a lot in this case. Because we went through all the arguments and we can say, I believe him and I can get pretty comfortable, but what is someone on the inside saying? In this case, he (CEO) owns 10% of the stock and he is the one making the decisions to build the new video stores. That is important to remember, because the guy who owns 10% is saying he still wants to build these things. Maybe he is dumb, maybe he is not, but you have to give him more credit for knowing more about the business than you do because he is living it (the business) day to day; he is seeing the numbers; he is running all the different tests that say to him--this is still kind of working. And it is his money and he will probably have more money at stake than you probably will.

因此，在本案中以及许多企业中，了解内部人士的动态至关重要。如果内部人士纷纷撤离，而你认为企业正在衰落——那很可能确实如此。

<!--en-->
So really, really important in this case and in a lot of businesses that are dying to see what insiders are doing. If the insiders are bailing out and you think the business is dying--it probably is.

## 好莱坞音像店

<!--en-->
*Hollywood Video*

在参加完投资者推介会后，于2003年底开始关注该公司。

<!--en-->
Began looking at it late 2003 after attending an investor presentation

- Game Crazy（HLYW版的GameStop或Electronics Boutique）以及新音像店的回报率很高。
- 夫妻店仍占行业的40%。
- 首席执行官持有HLYW公司10%的股份，当时股价为13至14美元。以下是1月6日的新闻稿：1月6日 HLYW新闻稿——好莱坞娱乐公司公布2003年第四季度同店销售额数据。俄勒冈州波特兰——2004年1月6日，好莱坞娱乐公司（Nasdaq: HLYW），这家拥有并运营着1900多家好莱坞音像店及约600家Game Crazy游戏专卖店的企业，今日宣布第四季度同店销售额增长了12%。其中，租赁产品收入对同店销售额的贡献为负2%，而商品销售则贡献了14%。因此，公司预计该季度每股摊薄净利润约为0.36美元，全年调整后每股摊薄净利润预计约为1.40美元。2004年1月5日，公司提前偿还了2006年到期的2000万美元高级银行信贷额度。第四季度，公司还动用1600万美元回购自家普通股。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：公司预计将于2004年1月29日星期四公布2003年第四季度及全年经营业绩。那么，什么让你印象深刻呢？这家企业或许已经奄奄一息——人们都说它已无前途，别碰它。但这份新闻稿中有什么值得注意的呢？他们的商品销售表现强劲（商品销售增长14%）；他们正在回购股票、回笼资金，还在提前偿还债务。HLYW斥资1600万美元回购股票。回购高价股票或许是件坏事；但他们仍计划花费9000万美元开设新店。首席执行官的利益与股票挂钩，而非薪水。他于2003年10月停止了10B-501类型的销售——这是一个积极信号。我注意到的是那负2%的同店销售数据。人人都说这家企业已衰败，我们还谈到了天气等可能影响数据波动5%的因素。但他的同店销售仅下降2%——这看起来像是会彻底消亡的企业吗？从整体来看，其下滑幅度并不大。有些企业同店销售下降5%、7%甚至8%，人们仍认为它们是优秀企业。目前股价为14美元，在我看来，HLYW的首席执行官目标是实现1.40美元的盈利，而当前股价仅为明年预期收益的10倍。这就是2004年1月6日的情况。现在来看看2004年1月29日他们公布的全年业绩。

<!--en-->
- High returns on Game Crazy (HLYW's version of Gamestop or Electronics Boutique) and new Video Stores.
- Mom/Pop still represents 40% of industry
- CEO owns 10% of the stock
HLYW is at $13 to $14 bucks. So this is the news release on Jan 6th.
Jan 6 HLYW News Release
HOLLYWOOD ENTERTAINMENT ANNOUNCES 2003 FOURTH QUARTER SAME STORE SALES
PORTLAND, OREGON - January 6, 2004 - Hollywood Entertainment Corporation (Nasdaq: HLYW), owner and operator of more than 1,900 Hollywood Video superstores and approximately 600 Game Crazy video game specialty outlets, today announced that same store sales for the fourth quarter increased 12%. Contribution to same store sales from rental product revenue was negative 2% while contribution from merchandise sales was 14%.
As a result, the Company expects net income for the quarter to be approximately $0.36 per diluted share and expects adjusted net income for the full year to be approximately $1.40 per diluted share.
On January 5, 2004, the Company prepaid the $20 million 2006 amortization of its senior bank credit facility. During the fourth quarter, theCompany also used $16 million to repurchase shares of its common stock.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The Company expects to report its fourth quarter and full-year 2003 results of operations on Thursday, January 29, 2004.
So what strikes you? This business could be dead. People are saying this business is gone. Don't touch it. So what strikes you about this news release? They have great merchandise sales (Merch. Sales up 14%). They are buying back their stock, it is kicking off cash and they are prepaying debt. HLYW is buying back $16 million of stock. Buying back expensive stock could be a bad thing.
They are still spending $90 million to open stores. The CEO's interest lies in the stock, not his salary. He stopped in October 2003 his 10B-501 sales--a positive signal.
I go right to the negative 2% comps. Everyone says this business is dead. And we talked about the mitigating factors of weather and all this different stuff that can take your numbers up 5% or down 5%. His comps are only down 2%. Does it look like something that is going to fall off the face of the earth? It is not comping down much in the grand scheme of things. There are businesses that comp down 5%, 7%, 8% and people still think that those are great businesses.
The stock is at $14 and for me I see he (CEO of HLYW) is looking to make $1.40 and it is trading at 10 times next year's earnings. So that is Jan 6th, 2004
So now go to Jan 29th, 2004 when they come out with full year results.

布莱恩·盖恩斯：第四季度同店销售额下降1%，但2003年全年视频业务仍实现3%的增长——尽管所有人都认为该业务已经衰落。它仍然保持着3%的增长率。他在2003年新开了102家门店。

Brian Gains: So negative 1% comps for the fourth qtr. but for the full year in 2003, the video business still comped up 3% despite everyone thinking the business is dead. It is still comping up 3%. He opened 102 new stores in 2003.

具体来说，当我们观察营业利润的倍数时，关键在于Game Crazy是一家处于起步阶段的成长型业务，虽然亏损了2000万美元，但这种亏损最终会转为盈利。他可以停止开设不成熟的门店；而且他有许多已备好存货的新门店。即便情况糟糕，他也可以清算这些存货。因此，虽然他亏损了2000万美元，但这些门店中的存货具有价值，未来很可能带来正向收益。

<!--en-->
To put this into context, that when you start looking at multiples of operating income. What is key in Crazy? What strikes me there is that he lost $20 million in Game Crazy, which is a start-up. It is a growing business, comping up a lot; he is allowed to lose money. At some point that--$20 million loss (in Game Crazy) at some point will turn positive. He can stop opening new immature stores. He also has a lot of new stores with inventory in them. Even if it is a disaster, he can liquidate the inventory. So he is losing negative $20 million. When you are looking at the poor results for Hollywood, you must remember he has one division, which he can separate. He can do all sorts of different things with where he is losing $20 million. This division has inventory value. So you have negative $20 million, value of inventory and plus it is probably going positive.

在许多濒临衰落的业务中，我们需要关注其仍能盈利的其他领域。这正是业绩有望改善的原因。详见新闻稿的后半部分。

<!--en-->
In a lot of these dying businesses, you need to look at another area where they are making money. There is a reason why this could get better.

Brian Gains: There are a lot of things that the CEO can't predict.

他在Game Crazy业务上仍未实现盈利，但该业务在该细分市场的增长率达到了12%至14%，因此最终他会实现盈利。他之所以尚未盈利，是因为正在开设大量新门店。新开一家音像店时，起初不会有顾客光顾；改变人们的行为模式需要时间，该业务成熟也需要时间。他仍在继续发展Game Crazy业务。这其中很大程度与他持有超过10%的公司股票有关。令我惊讶的是他仍在开设音像店；他仍然认为投资回报可观。如果有人听说CEO仍在开设150家新门店，而他们此前认为这项业务已经衰落，肯定会说他疯了。他持有10%的股票，因此比我更有动力推动业务发展。

He is still not making money in Game Crazy but he is comping up 12% to 14% (in that segment), so eventually he will make money. And the reason he is not making money is because he is opening a lot of new stores. When you open a new video store, no one shows up. It takes time to change people's patterns. It takes time for that business to mature. He is still growing Game Crazy. A lot of this relates to his owning more than 10% of the stock. What strikes me is that he is still opening video stores. He still thinks the returns are good. If you told someone who thought the business is dead that the CEO is still opening 150 new stores, they would reply that he is nuts. He owns 10% of the stock. 哥伦比亚大学商学院的116门特殊情境投资课程。**你注意到什么了？** 极高的投入资本回报率、息税前利润、良好的营业利润率，而且它*真的非常便宜*。我掌握了营业利润数据，接下来需要确定维持性资本支出的水平。那么，运营一家这样的音像店需要多少成本呢？如果局势彻底失控，一切都将变得糟糕；他不会再花钱，会关闭Game Crazy门店，停止开设新店。维持这项业务究竟要花费多少？3.6倍的估值倍数确实很低，有人指出其资本回报率——值得注意的是，在计算ROC时，有公司整体的ROC，即用营业利润除以净营运资本、固定资产以及这里的租赁存货。此外还有新店带来的*增量*资本回报率。由于新店无需承担一般及行政费用，其增量ROC可能更高——这纯粹是增量部分。就整个公司而言，其税前ROC超过了42%，这一数字依然相当惊人。

<!--en-->
116
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
**What strikes you here?** Really high ROIC, EBIT, good operating margin and it is *really cheap*. So I have operating income and I need to set a maintenance capex level. So what does it cost to keep one of these video stores going? If all hell breaks loose, nothing is good, he is not spending any money, he stops Game Crazy; he stops building new stores. What is it going to cost him to keep this business going? And 3.6 multiple is cheap and someone pointed out the Returns on Capital--it is worth noting that when you do ROC--there is a company-wide ROC and taking operating income and dividing by net working capital, his PPE (Property, Plant and Equipment) and in this case his rental inventory. And then there is the *incremental* returns on capital (ROC) on his new stores. And the incremental ROC on his new stores may be higher because he doesn't have SG&A--it is just incremental. Here on the whole company he is doing a company-wide pre-tax ROC of greater than 42%. It is still fantastic.

*学生：* 您是如何计算投入资本回报率（ROIC）的？

*Brian Gains：* 我只是将净营运资本和净固定资产相加，这里还包括租赁存货。由于租期仅三年，我没有将租赁确认为资本化项目；我假设如果业务表现不佳，他们可以提前终止租赁。

<!--en-->
*Brian Gains:* So all I am doing is taking net working capital and net PPE. In this case (rental) inventory as well. I did not capitalize the leases because they are only for three years. I assumed they could break the lease if their business is not working.

将其计入运营成本，扣除所有租赁费用后的净额。

<!--en-->
Taking that as operating cost. Net of all rental cost.

*学生：* 如果门店需要不断补充存货，这部分会被资本化吗？

<!--en-->
*Student:* If the stores are having to constantly replenish inventory--is that capitalized?

*Brian Gains：* 不会。我将其视为费用——即营业费用。

<!--en-->
*Brian Gains:* No. I treat it as an expense--an operating expense.

有一件事你可能不知道：HLYW拥有净经营亏损资产。其净经营亏损高达7300万美元，这确实是一项资产。他很快就能充分利用这笔资产。了解他们是否缴纳现金税非常重要。目前营业利润达到1.87亿美元，因此他能迅速用完全部净经营亏损额度。**对于手握大量现金的公司而言，了解其税务状况至关重要——他们是否以现金形式缴税。** 在计算估值倍数时，应从企业价值中扣除净经营亏损。

<!--en-->
One thing you wouldn't have known--HLYW had an NOL asset. It has a net operating loss (NOL) of $73 million so that is an asset. He will realize it all pretty quickly. That is an asset. It is important to know whether they are paying cash taxes or not. Operating income is running 187 million dollars so he will realize all of his NOL right away. **With these companies with a lot of cash, it is important to understand their tax situation. Are they paying taxes in cash or not.** When you are looking at multiples, you would deduct the NOL from Enterprise Value (EV).

另一点值得注意：尽管人人都说该业务正在衰落，但门店数量却从244家增至252家，营业利润也有所上升。我还注意到其租赁业务的毛利润——也就是众人诟病的那部分业务——商品销售增长了12%，但这并不算理想的业务，因为其毛利率较低；不过他将租赁毛利润从876万美元提升至945万美元，且租赁业务毛利率也在提高。在我看来，情况并不算糟。实际上，我看到的是一家呈上升趋势的企业。以3.6倍EV/EBITDA-MCX的估值买入，可获得28%的税前回报率。

<!--en-->
Another thing to note--despite everyone saying the business is dying-- you went from 244 stores to 252; operating income was up as well. Another thing I noted was that his rental gross profit--the part of the business everyone hates--well, you can say merchandise is growing 12%, that is not a great a business because he has lower gross margins--he took rental gross profit from $876 to $945 and he grew the rental gross margin. To me this doesn't look so awful. I am actually seeing a business that is trending up. And getting it for 3.6x EV/EBITDA-MCX or for a 28% pre-tax return.

所以此刻我十分兴奋。我会在股价处于10美元至11美元之间时买入该股。情况能有多糟呢？

<!--en-->
So at this point I am excited. I am buying the stock here between $10 and $11.

## HLYW结论

<!--en-->
*HLYW Conclusion*

这是我的最终成果（如下）。我问了有多少种不同的情况能让我满意？

<!--en-->
Here is my final work (below). I said how many different ways can this turn out OK for me?

正常情况下——即CEO声称在2004年将实现的业绩——EBITDA为2.3亿美元。其资本支出为：拥有2,000家门店，每家门店需花费1万美元，总计2,000万美元，此外还有企业层面的资本支出。假设他仅关注MCX指标，再计入利息因素，经测算调整后自由现金流（FCF）为：虽然他有净运营亏损（NOL），但为稳妥起见我们暂不考虑。按全额征税计算，他的每股现金收益（EPS）为1.90美元。我给这个数值乘以8倍，得出每股价值15美元——该业务并未像人们想象的那样迅速衰落。

<!--en-->
The normal case--what the CEO is telling you he will do in 2004--$230 in EBITDA. His capex is: he has 2,000 stores and $10,000 per store so $20 million plus he has corporate capex. So let's say he just goes MCX then he has interest, so I calculate Free Cash Flow (FCF) tax adjusted is--he has a NOL but we set it aside just to be safe. Let us look at this fully taxed. He is doing $1.90 in cash EPS. I put a 8 multiple on that so you get to $15 per share--the business is not dying as quickly as people think.

接着你说在未来一年内能收回1.90美元的现金，这正是我之前提到的——你能立即拿回多少现金。你马上就能收回1.90美元。因此我说，如果情况真如这般发展，即便人们认为该业务正在衰败、情况很糟，我也能获得70%的回报。

<!--en-->
Then you say over the next year, you will get $1.90 back in cash, that is what I talked about before--how much cash you will get back right away. You will get back $1.90 right away. So I said, OK if this kind of works out in this fashion, if people look at it as if, OK, it were really dying; it is really bad, I could get 70%.

如果最终人们认定这是一家成长性企业，我可能获得更好的回报。我原本预计营收为2.25亿美元，但资本支出被低估为3,500万美元，因此我的实际回报率可能只有36%。不过通过这些数字可以看出，股价要跌至10美元需要多糟糕的业绩表现。必须将估值大幅下调才能认定其当前价值。而在某种情况下，我认为其价值可能高出70%。

<!--en-->
If the people in the end say it is really a growth business, I may get something much better. Then I said it does $225 and I am wrong on Capex and it is $35, so maybe my return is only 36%. But then you can go through these numbers and see how bad does it have to be to get to $10 where the stock is trading. And you have to take it down quite a bit to say, OK, it is worth what it is (now). And in one case I am saying it could be worth 70% more.

在最后一个例子中，我假设他每年在Game Crazy业务上亏损2,000万美元。实际上2004年的预估亏损额为1,600万美元，我们就把这笔钱加回来。假设他清算Game Crazy业务，由于仅有500家门店，利息支出会降低；同时出售存货，迅速回笼资金。在这种情况下，他最终能实现每股16美元的价值以及2美元现金；如果我以每股10美元的价格买入股票，就能以82%的比例获得每股18美元的收益。因此，有多种可能性可以实现盈利。

<!--en-->
In this last example, I am saying he is losing $20 million on Game Crazy per year. He is actually estimated to lose $16 million for 2004, so let's add that back. Let's say he liquidates Game Crazy so interest expense is not as high because he has 500 stores; he sells the inventory. So he immediately sells that down. In that situation, he ends up with $16 per share and $2 in cash and he gets $18 per share for 82% if I bought the stock at $10 per share. So there are a lot of ways this could work out.

业务状况并没有那么糟糕。即便确实不佳，只要MCX指标起作用——因为他意识到业务正在崩溃——从而停止相关操作，我可能仍会获利。此时我会说：“好吧，我愿意下注。”

<!--en-->
Businesses isn't as bad. Or if it is bad, and if MCX is what really comes into play because he realizes things are falling apart--so he stops doing it. I am still probably going to do OK. At this point I say, OK, I will take the bet.

在最坏的情况下，年底时股票价格为10美元。但我相信自己能从中赚大钱，获利几率可达80%。（下行风险为0%至10%，而上行潜力为36%至82%。）

<!--en-->
In the worse case scenario at the end of the year, I have a $10 stock. But I think, I make a lot of money on this. There is chance I make 80%. (0% to 10% downside for a 36% to 82% upside).

以上总结了我的观点：有多种途径可以获胜……

### MOVI财务数据

他在哥伦比亚大学商学院开设了120门关于特殊情境投资的课程。他的资产负债表上有现金。我没有提供任何年度对比数据，所以你无法查看这些信息。有趣的是……开设这些MOVI Gallery门店需要花费12,000美元，三年后就能实现62%的回报率。一家成熟的门店在三年后能带来62%的税前资本回报率，而且他一直在成功开设新店。目前他拥有2,000家门店，每年还会新增200家。相信你从零售业经验中知道，凭借62%的回报率，企业可以稳步发展而无需犯下重大错误。62%的资本回报率，恐怕很难找到更好的替代方案了。

Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
He has cash on the balance sheet. I am not giving you any yr/yr stuff so you can't even take a look at those. What is interesting.... So it costs him $12,000 to open these MOVI Gallery stores and three years out he makes 62%. A mature store three years out makes 62% pre-tax returns on capital and he has been opening stores successfully. He has 2000 stores now and he is adding 200 stores a year. And this, I am sure you know this from retailers, with 62% (returns) you build all day without screwing up. 62% returns on capital, you can't probably find better alternatives.

即便在第一年，在未完全成熟的情况下也能达到35%的回报率。尤其是当一家企业的交易价格仅为EBIT的6倍时，这简直是在浪费金钱吧？

<!--en-->

Now we get another piece on August 6th, 2004

2004年8月9日，俄勒冈州波特兰市——Hollywood Entertainment Corporation（纳斯达克代码：HLYW），这家拥有并运营着超过1,950家Hollywood Video连锁店的公司，今日宣布：Leonard Green & Partners, L.P.（Carso Holdings Corporation的关联公司及其全资子公司；该公司于2004年3月29日与Hollywood签署了合并协议）已通知Hollywood，由于行业和市场环境的变化，Leonard Green & Partners认为完成此次合并所需的融资条件将无法得到满足。

<!--en-->
August 9, 2004
PORTLAND, OR, August 6, 2004 — Hollywood Entertainment Corporation (Nasdaq: HLYW), owner and operator of more than 1,950 Hollywood Video superstores, today announced that Leonard Green & Partners, L.P., an affiliate of Carso Holdings Corporation ("Holdings") and its wholly owned subsidiary (the entities with which Hollywood entered into a merger agreement on March 29, 2004), has informed Hollywood that, due to industry and market conditions, Leonard Green & Partners believes that the financing condition to the consummation of the merger will not be satisfied.

好莱坞及其董事会特别委员会正在评估各种备选方案，以确定最符合好莱坞股东利益的行动方针。无法保证与Holdings的合并能够完成；即便完成，也无法确保交易条款与合并协议中的条款完全一致。

<!--en-->
Hollywood and the Special Committee of its Board of Directors are considering Hollywood's alternatives to determine the course of action that would be in the best interests of Hollywood's shareholders. There is no assurance that a merger with Holdings will be completed, or if completed, that it would be completed on terms that do not differ materially from those in the merger agreement.

表述有些模糊，但除了“如果你持有股票且属于套利者则会蒙受损失”之外，这里最重要的句子是：Leonard Green因融资条件问题而退出。这并非由于HLYW的业务状况或质量不佳。Leonard Green或许无法在高收益市场筹集到所需资金。他们声称并未退出交易，但对14美元的价格并不满意。由此可以推测接下来会发生什么——股价将回落至10美元。融资未能落实，虽然财务数据可能尚可，但公司又回到了原点。

<!--en-->
It is kind of vague, but it --what is the most important sentence here besides you lose if you are in the stock and you are an arb.--Leonard Green is bowing out because of the financing condition. It wasn't because of the conditions or quality of HLYW's business. Leonard Green probably couldn't get something done in the high yield market. They are saying, we are not leaving the deal, but we don't like it at $14. So you can guess what happens now, so the stock trades back to $10. You know the financing didn't get done, the numbers are probably OK and you are back to where you were.

### 人人都喜欢听好听的说辞。

<!--en-->
*Everybody loves a good spin*

* 维亚康姆为Blockbuster新增10亿美元债务，并说：“出门时别让门砸到你。”
* 新独立的BBI会带来哪些影响？当天MOVI股价略有下跌，与此同时BBI也呈现下行趋势。巧合的是，BBI从维亚康姆分拆后向维亚康姆支付了特别股息。HLYW的情况一团糟：维亚康姆的Summer Redstone认为BBI的估值倍数过低，他厌倦了这一切，决定甩掉它，同时支付5美元的特别股息。BBI具备分拆后常被诟病的所有特征——巨额债务、糟糕的行业环境等。如今BBI已完全独立。我错过了这一点，没能理解其中的逻辑。哥伦比亚大学商学院第121期特殊情境投资课程。

<!--en-->
* Viacom adds 1B of debt to Blockbuster and says don't let the door hit you on the way out.
* Ramifications of the newly independent BBI?
MOVI has traded down a little bit that day. At the same time as this, BBI is trending lower. Coincidentally BBI pays a special dividend to Viacom after being spun-off from Viacom. Everything is bad at HLYW, Summer Redstone over at Viacom says BBI gives me a lower multiple, I am sick of it, get rid of it and at the same timepay a special dividend-$5. They kick it off. BBI had everything to look for in a spin-off that may be hated—big debt load, bad industry, etc. Now BBI is completely independent. I missed this. I didn't get it.

## 更多获胜机会……

<!--en-->
*More Chances to win..*

* HLYW和MOVI股价下跌——MOVI资本结构的重要性何在？
* MOVI是否受到影响？
* HLYW首席执行官的看法如何？
* BBI？HLYW和MOVI股价均下跌。由于MOVI资产负债表上拥有大量现金，其股价下跌意义重大，因为它本身现金流充裕。任何价格跌幅在估值倍数层面都相当显著。MOVI是否受此事影响？并没有。HLYW的首席执行官对周围发生的一切作何感想？正是这位曾想加倍下注的首席执行官。他是否在乎合并价格？他反而希望价格更低。如果Leonard Green回来出价3美元，他会更兴奋——那将是一桩低价收购案……随后便演变成一场激烈争夺。
* 2004年10月14日，Leonard Green重新出价10.25美元。
* 11月11日，BBI确认有意以11.50美元的价格收购。
* MOVI提出以13.25美元的价格收购HLYW。Leonard Green于10月14日再次现身。他们先出价10.25美元，然后继续观望。典型的私募股权作风：既然CEO不介意更低价格，那就再压低4美元。然而计划被打破——新独立的Blockbuster出面表示愿出价11.50美元。接着MOVI也感兴趣，出价13.25美元。这些战略买家全都兴奋起来。关键事件包括BBI的分拆、Leonard Green的贪婪举动，最终引发激烈争夺。事情的发展真是耐人寻味。Leonard Green唤醒了所有人，让大家意识到情况并非那么糟糕。一切由此展开。HLYW的首席执行官提议收购一半的HLYW门店。当并购公告发布、MOVI打算以13.25美元收购HLYW时，我就指出BBI会因占据60%的市场份额而面临反垄断问题。快速计算一下MOVI的数据，会发现这简直是笔划算的交易：他们可以削减成本，效仿Leonard Green的做法。我第一次投资了MOVI，却没买HLYW。若给MOVI 3.50美元的每股收益赋予8倍的估值，股价可达28美元。因此如果MOVI成功收购，你会非常兴奋；即便没有，这类并购中往往会出现这种情况：若BBI收购HLYW，之后MOVI就能低价接手那些门店。另外，BBI的报价是现金加股票形式，而任何董事会都会更倾向于现金而非股票——现金报价显然更受欢迎。BBI处于劣势，因其债务负担过重。这与Quest和Horizon的情况类似：MCI的董事会表示更愿意选择提供现金报价的Verizon。HLYW的董事会已疲惫不堪，他们知道前景渺茫，也知道公司终将被收购。董事会成员个人也不想被起诉。不如赶紧收拾局面，抽身离去。

<!--en-->
* HLYW and MOVI trade down
  --Significance of MOVI capital structure?
* Is MOVI affected?
* CEO of HLYW's thoughts?
* BBI?
HLYW and MOVI traded down. Since MOVI has cash on the balance sheet, a trade down in MOVI Gallery is huge, because it is cash rich. Any fall off in price is pretty significant on a multiple basis.
Is MOVI affected by what happened? NO.
What is the CEO of HLYW thinking about everything that is going on around him. This is the CEO who wanted to triple down. Does he care where the merger happens--he would prefer a lower price. He is more excited if Leonard Green comes back and offers $3. A take-under.
...and then it becomes a food fight
* Leonard Green comes back on 10/14/04 and offers $10.25
* On November 11/11, BBI confirms interest to acquire at $11.50
* Movi offers to acquire HLYW at $13.25.
Leonard Green shows up again on Oct 14th. We will do it for $10.25, then they hang around. Classic private equity guys who say, the CEO doesn't care about a lower price, so let's offer $4 less. Then a wrench gets thrown in their plans, because a newly independent blockbuster comes back says they will do it for $11.50. Then MOVI gets interested to acquire at $13.25. All these strategic buyers get excited. With a key event, you had a BBI spin-off and you had L. Green get greedy and then a food fight begins. It is funny how this stuff works. L Green woke everybody up to it is not so bad. Everything transpired from there.
The HLYW's CEO offers to acquire half of HLYW's stores.
What I did when the merger announcement came out when Movi was going to acquire HLYW at $13.25, I said BBI runs into anti-trust problems because they have 60% of the market. You do some quick math on MOVI and say wow this is a home run. You can say they can cut costs, they can do the same thing as L. Green.
I am in MOVI but not in HLYW the second time around. Putting a 8 multiple on MOVI's $3.50, you could get a $28 stock. So you could get really excited with MOVI if they get it and if they don't, then a lot of time in these mergers, BBI is forced to sell off stores if BBI were to acquire HLYW, then MOVI could acquire those stores on the cheap.
Another thing about BBI's bid is that it is in cash and stock. And any Board of Directors will favor cash over stock. It is the easier to go with the cash bid. BBI is at a disadvantage because they have too much debt. This is what is happening with Quest and Horizon--MCI's Board is saying we want to go with Verizon since they are offering cash.
The HLYW's Board is tired. They know there is very little upside. They know it will be acquired. The Board personally does not want to be sued. Clean this up and get out of town.

### A. 业务总体发展情况

*A. GENERAL DEVELOPMENT OF BUSINESS*

该公司于1923年根据特拉华州法律注册成立，其前身可追溯至1886年创立的企业。公司主要行政办公室位于明尼苏达州明尼阿波利斯市西78街8000号400室，电话：612-943-5000。本文中“公司”一词除非另有说明或上下文指明，均指Munsingwear, Inc.及其子公司。截至1996年1月6日，公司仅有一家子公司Munsingwear UK Limited，该公司于1994年停止运营。

<!--en-->
The Company was incorporated under the laws of Delaware in 1923 as the successor to a business founded in 1886. The Company's principal executive offices are located at 8000 W. 78th Street, Suite-400, Minneapolis, Minnesota 55439, and its telephone number: 612-943-5000. As used in this document, the term "Company" refers to Munsingwear, Inc. and its subsidiaries unless otherwise noted or indicated by the context. At Jan. 6, 1996, the Company had one subsidiary, Munsingwear UK Limited, which was idled in 1994.

由于1989年至1990年间损失高达89,243,000美元，公司财务状况严重恶化。1991年7月3日，公司根据美国破产法第11章自愿申请破产，并提交了重组计划。1991年10月29日，公司脱离破产程序。

<!--en-->
After suffering a severely weakened financial condition, primarily due to losses of $89,243,000 during the years 1989 through 1990, the Company, on July 3, 1991, filed a voluntary petition for bankruptcy under Chapter 11 of the US Bankruptcy Code, together with a proposed Plan of Reorganization. The Company emerged from bankruptcy on Oct. 29, 1991.

在1989年至1991年期间缩减运营规模之前，公司通过多个业务部门及子公司设计、生产和分销各类男装及儿童服装。如今，公司的业务主要源自原来的男装部门，主要销售以下品牌的男士针织运动衫：Munsingwear®、Grand Slam®、Grand Slam Tour™、Penguin Sport™和Slammer®。此外，公司还授权他人使用其商标和品牌名称用于各类产品。哥伦比亚大学商学院的124节特殊情境投资课程显示：在过去两个财政年度中，公司的销售渠道销售结构发生了显著变化。1995年，面向高端/特色市场及高尔夫专卖店客户的销售额较1994年合计增长了52%。这一变化源于管理层试图减少公司对传统零售服装渠道的依赖，因为这些渠道往往需要大量的促销定价、折扣及广告投入。

<!--en-->
Prior to the reductions in operation implemented during 1989 through 1991, the Company designed, manufactured and distributed a broad range of men's and children's apparel through several operating divisions and subsidiaries. Today the Company's operations consist of what was formerly the Men's Apparel Division and sell primarily men's knit sport shirts under the following major brands or labels: Munsingwear ®,Grand Slam®, Grand Slam Tour™, Penguin Sport™ and Slammer®. In addition, the Company licenses its trade names and trademarks for use in a variety of products.
124
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
In the recent two fiscal years, the Company's sales by channel of distribution have undergone significant change. In 1995, sales to premium/special markets and golf Pro shop customers rose 52% collectively over 1994. This is the result of management's attempt to reduce the Company's reliance on sales to traditional retail apparel channels of distribution where heavy promotional pricing, discounting and advertising activities are required.

1995年底，该公司聘请了一家投资银行来探索一系列能够最大化股东价值的机遇。

<!--en-->
In late 1995, the Company retained the services of an investment banking firm to explore a range of opportunities to maximize shareholder value.

### B. 关于业务分部的财务信息

<!--en-->
*B. FINANCIAL INFORMATION ABOUT INDUSTRY SEGMENTS*

该公司仅在一个业务分部运营，即服装制造。截至1996年1月6日，该公司的海外业务并不重要。

<!--en-->
The Company operates in one industry segment, apparel manufacturing. As of Jan. 6, 1996, the Company's foreign operations were not material.

### C. 业务概述

<!--en-->
*C. NARRATIVE DESCRIPTION OF BUSINESS*

### 主要产品：

<!--en-->
*Principal Products:*

该公司主要通过四个主要品牌销售男士针织运动衫：Munsingwear®、Grand Slam®、Grand Slam Tour™和Penguin Sport™。Grand Slam®和Penguin Sport™产品主要销往百货商店、专卖店以及Sears。Munsingwear®产品主要销往高端/特殊市场客户以及Montgomery Ward等全国性连锁店。Grand Slam Tour™则主要通过高尔夫用品店销售。

<!--en-->
The Company sells primarily men's knit sport shirts under four major brands or labels: Munsingwear®, Grand Slam®, Grand Slam Tour™, and Penguin Sport™. Grand Slam® and Penguin Sport™ products are sold primarily to department stores, specialty stores and Sears. Munsingwear® products are sold primarily to premium/special markets customers and to national chain stores, such as Montgomery Ward. Grand Slam Tour™ is sold primarily through golf pro shops.

### 原材料及产品的来源与供应情况：

<!--en-->
*Sources and Availability of Raw Materials and Products:*

该公司约60%的产品在国内生产，其余40%主要通过与Associated Merchandising Corporation (AMC)的合作从远东地区的制造商处采购。该公司也通过加勒比海地区的807计划采购部分产品。国内生产所需的主要原材料为棉花、合成纤维以及棉/合成纤维混纺材料，这些材料主要来自美国。该公司从大约十个供应商处购买大部分面料。目前，原材料供应方面并无重大问题，且存在替代来源。该公司位于北卡罗来纳州费尔芒特的制造厂设有物料仓库、裁剪、缝纫及刺绣车间，以及成品分销中心。在生产高峰期，该公司还会利用位于北卡罗来纳州工厂附近的合同代工厂来满足需求。无论国内还是海外生产的产品，均从北卡罗来纳州的工厂发往客户。

<!--en-->
Approximately 60% of the Company's products are manufactured domestically. The other 40% is sourced primarily from manufacturers in the Far East through a relationship with Associated Merchandising Corporation (AMC). The Company also sources some product through the 807 program in the Caribbean Basin. The principal raw materials used in the domestic production process are cotton, synthetic and cotton/synthetic blended goods obtained principally from United States sources. The Company purchases most of its piece goods from approximately ten sources. There are currently no major problems in availability of raw materials and alternative sources are available. The Company's Fairmount, NC manufacturing facility includes a material warehouse, cutting, sewing and embroidery operations, and finished goods distribution center. The company also utilizes contract swing manufacturers in close proximity to its North Carolina facility to meet demand during peak production periods. All products, both domestically and offshore produced, are distributed to customers from the North Carolina facility.

### 商标与商号：

<!--en-->
*Trademarks and Trade Names:*

1991年，管理层启动了将授权经营作为公司发展计划重要组成部分的战略。1991年至1993年间，该公司签订了十一份许可协议；1994年，公司与Fruit of the Loom重新谈判了许可协议，其中包括将原协议期限延长二十五年。1995年，该公司又签订了四份新的许可协议。管理层打算继续拓展其授权经营项目，并认为多年来建立的广告、款式设计及品牌认知度对公司的竞争优势至关重要。该公司拥有的许可协议如下：

<!--en-->
In 1991, management initiated the strategy to actively pursue licensing as a vital part of the Company's growth plan. During the period 1991 through 1993, the Company entered into eleven license agreements, and in 1994, renegotiated its licenses with Fruit of the Loom which, among other things, extended the original agreement for twenty-five years. In 1995, the Company entered into four additional license agreements. Management intends to continue development of its licensing programs and believes that its advertising, styling and brand name identification established over many years are important to the competitive position of the company. The Company has the following license agreements:

* 与Fruit of the Loom, Inc.签订的许可协议，用于营销内衣和运动服。
* 与一家纽约实体签订的许可协议，用于营销睡衣。
* 与Montgomery Ward签订的五项许可协议，用于营销男士裤装、外套、配饰、正装及衬衫。哥伦比亚大学商学院开设的125门特殊情境投资课程
* 与一家加拿大公司签订的许可协议，用于营销针织衫。
* 与一家北卡罗来纳州实体签订的许可协议，用于营销男士及男孩袜类制品。
* 与一家中国实体签订的许可协议，用于营销各类服装及配饰。
* 与一家南卡罗来纳州实体签订的许可协议，用于营销毛衣。
* 与一家密苏里州实体签订的许可协议，用于营销外套。
* 与一家纽约实体签订的许可协议，用于营销梭织衬衫。
* 与一家南非实体签订的服装类许可协议。近年来，管理层对授权经营活动的重视使得该公司的特许权使用费收入大幅增加，从1991年的1,162,000美元增至1995年的4,609,000美元。

<!--en-->
* A license with Fruit of the Loom, Inc. to market underwear and active wear.
* A license with a New York entity to market sleepwear.

### 业务的季节性特征：

<!--en-->
*Seasonal Aspects of the Business:*

公司产品的销售额会随季节显著波动，发货高峰期通常出现在财年的第一季度和第二季度。

<!--en-->
Sales of the Company's products can vary significantly by season, with peak shipments normally occurring in the first and second quarters of the fiscal year.

### 营运资金管理：

<!--en-->
*Working Capital Practices:*

公司维持着一笔有担保的银行信贷额度以满足其营运资金需求。根据该协议，借款高峰期通常出现在年初的六个月——即发货繁忙期，以及第四季度为应对第一、二季度增加的销量而补充库存时。服装制造业出现季节性库存增加属于正常现象。该银行信贷额度也用于开具信用证，以支付公司从海外采购所需的款项。对于因发货错误、商品损坏等原因导致的退货，公司予以接受；过去两年中，退货额占销售额的比例均低于4%。

<!--en-->
The Company maintains a secured bank line of credit to meet its working capital needs. Peak borrowings under this agreement normally occur in the first six months of the year during the heavier shipping period and during the fourth quarter when inventories are increased to meet the additional first and second quarter sales volume. Seasonal increases in inventory are normal for the apparel manufacturing industry. The bank line of credit is also used for letters of credit that are required for generally all of the Company's purchases from offshore sources. The Company allows returns of merchandise as a result of shipping errors, damaged merchandise and for other reasons. Returns have been less than 4% of sales in each of the past two years.

<!--en-->
*Customers:*

公司拥有约4,500名客户。1994年和1993年，向山姆会员店（沃尔玛公司旗下部门）的销售额分别占净销售额的16%和21%。1995年，没有任何单一客户的销售额占比超过公司总销售额的10%。

<!--en-->
The Company sells to approximately 4,500 customers. Sales to Sam's Club (a division of Wal-Mart Stores, Inc.) in 1994 and 1993 were 16% and 21%, respectively, of net sales. In 1995, no single customers represented more than 10% of total Company sales.

### 订单积压情况：

<!--en-->
*Backlog of Orders:*

截至1996年1月6日，公司未完成的订单金额约为15,600,000美元，而去年同期则为18,800,000美元。这一减少主要是由于管理层致力于减少对传统零售服装客户的依赖。未完成的订单并不必然直接反映未来的销售情况。

<!--en-->
The Company's backlog of unfilled orders at January 6, 1996 was approximately $15,600,000 as compared to $18,800,000 a year ago. The decrease was due primarily to management's emphasis on reducing reliance on traditional retail apparel customers. The unfilled order backlog does not necessarily relate directly to future sales.

## 竞争格局：

<!--en-->
*Competition:*

美国服装行业竞争激烈，市场上只有少数综合性企业，而专业制造商数量众多。此外，还有无品牌及贴牌竞争对手，以及众多小型专业制造商与公司竞争。服装行业的主要竞争手段包括定价、款式设计、质量（包括材料和生产工艺）、库存补充计划以及客户服务。公司通过运用所有这些手段来维护其在所处市场的竞争优势。

<!--en-->
The apparel industry in the United States is highly competitive and characterized by a relatively small number of broad line companies and a large number of specialty manufacturers. In addition, there are unbranded and private label competitors as well as numerous, small specialty manufacturers competing with the Company. The principal methods of competition in the apparel industry are pricing, styling, quality (both in material and production), inventory replenishment programs and customer service. The Company seeks to maintain its competitive position in the markets in which it operates through the use of all these methods.

#### 关于本公司

<!--en-->
*ABOUT THE COMPANY*

本公司成立于1886年，是一家男式内衣制造商。20世纪初，本公司是纺织及服装制造新工艺的创新者；在1940年代和1950年代，公司扩展了产品线，收购了一家女性内衣公司，并于1955年推出了带有知名Penguin®标志的Gran Slam®系列高尔夫服饰。1960年代和1970年代，公司增设了生产设施，成立了纺织研发部门，并签署了多项关于使用其商号和商标的许可协议。

<!--en-->
The Company was founded in 1886 as a manufacturer of men's underwear. Throughout the early 1900's, the Company was an innovator of new textile and apparel manufacturing processes and, during the 1940's and 1950's, expanded its product lines, acquired a women's intimate apparel company and, in 1955, introduced the Gran Slam (R) collection of golf apparel bearing the well-known Penguin ® emblem. During the 1960's and 1970's, manufacturing facilities were added, textile research and development departments were established and the Company entered into numerous licensing agreements for the use of its trade names and trademarks.

如今，该公司的主要收入来源为男士运动服装的销售，以及男士内衣、运动服及其他相关服饰的授权业务。该公司的产品主要通过高端/特色市场、百货商店、高尔夫用品店、全国性连锁店、专卖店、体育用品店和批发俱乐部进行销售。公司负责设计、生产、进口、营销并授权以Grand Slam®、Grand Slam Tour®、Munsingwear®和Penguin Sport™为品牌的男士休闲服饰。公司总部位于明尼苏达州明尼阿波利斯市，全公司共有343名员工。

<!--en-->
Today the Company derives its revenues primarily from the sale of men's sportswear apparel and the licensing of men's underwear, active wear and other related apparel. The Company's products are sold primarily through premium/special markets, department stores, golf pro shops, national chain stores, specialty stores, sporting goods stores and wholesale clubs. The Company designs, manufactures, imports, markets and licenses branded men's lifestyle apparel under the Grand Slam ®, Grand Slam Tour®, Munsingwear ®, and Penguin Sport ™ labels. The Company is headquartered in Minneapolis, MN and has 343 employees in company-wide operations.

## 致股东信

<!--en-->
*LETTER TO STOCKHOLDERS*

1995年的营收达到5610万美元，较去年增长34%。高端/特色市场及高尔夫用品店业务的销售大幅增长，足以抵消传统客户（如百货商店、专卖店、全国性连锁店和批发俱乐部）业务小幅下滑的影响。高端/特色市场的销量增长了七倍，高尔夫用品店的销量则增长了52%。1995年，这两类业务占到了公司总销量的40%，预计在1996年将占据公司总销量的50%以上。通过过去两年的转型，公司对竞争激烈的零售服装市场的依赖程度显著降低。

<!--en-->
Revenues for 1995 were $56.1 million, a 34% increase over last year. Dramatic sales growth in our premium/special markets and golf pro shop businesses more than offset a small decline in business with our traditional customers, such as department and specialty stores, national chain stores and wholesale clubs. Premium/special markets volume increased seven-fold while golf Pro shop volume increased 52%. In 1995 these two businesses represented 40% of our total sales volume and are expected to exceed 50% of total Company sales in 1996. As recent transition the Company has undergone over the past two years, significantly reducing our exposure to the difficult retail apparel marketplace.

特许权使用费收入略微上升至460万美元。需要提醒的是，1994年的特许权使用费收入增长了25%，这得益于新增的许可协议以及Fruit of the Loom许可期限的延长（延长至25年）；不过从1996年起，现有许可协议带来的现金收入将会减少。Munsingwear的商号与商标在许可市场上向来代表着高品质，公司将继续积极寻求更多的许可协议。

<!--en-->
Royalty income was up slightly to $4.6 million. As a reminder, 1994 royalty income had increased 25% as a result of additional license agreements and a twenty-five year extension to the Fruit of the Loom license, which will also lead to lower cash receipts from existing licensing agreements starting in 1996. The Munsingwear trade names and trademarks have always signified quality to the licensing market and we will continue to actively pursue additional license agreements.

尽管1995年公司实现了显著的营收增长，但未能实现盈利。230万美元的亏损相当于每股1.13美元，其主要原因在于：面向百货商店渠道的季节性积压商品被迫大幅降价出售；涉足“周五休闲装”领域未获成功造成的损失；为支持百货商店业务而增加的广告费用；以及因人员裁减和办公空间缩减而产生的重组成本。此外，PGA巡回赛赞助计划的费用也有所增加，但我们认为该计划对于提升Munsingwear品牌在消费者中的知名度至关重要。公司成功地将销售、一般及行政费用占销售额的比例从1994年的32%降至1995年的27%。由于为满足高端/特色市场业务的爆发式销售增长而囤积了大量存货，利息支出显著增加。全年内，面向百货商店渠道的存货水平也高于预期，未能达到销售预测目标；最终，这些存货只能以大幅折扣出售。

<!--en-->
While we achieved significant revenue growth in 1995, we were not successful in becoming profitable. The loss of $2.3 million, $1.13 per share, was primarily the result of deep markdowns on excess end-of-season merchandise related to the retail department store channel of distribution, losses related to an unsuccessful entry into "Friday-wear", increased advertising expenses in support of the retail department store business and restructuring costs related to completed staff reductions and reduced office space requirements. In addition, costs associated with our PGA Tour endorsement program increased, yet we feel this program is necessary to give Munsingwear brands consumer exposure. We were successful in reducing selling, general and administrative expenses as a percent of sales – from 32% in 1994 to 27% in 1995. Interest expense was up significantly due to inventory build-up required to service the explosive sales growth in the premium/special markets business. Throughout the year we also experienced higher than planned levels of inventory for the retail department store business, which did not meet sales forecasts. Ultimately, we sold this inventory at deep discounts.

展望1996年，公司计划继续发展在过去两年中取得卓越业绩的高端/特色市场业务。Munsingwear强大的品牌认知度、Penguin标志、优质产品以及跨产品线灵活 merchandising的能力，构成了公司的竞争优势。我们坚信，凭借以下措施，公司必将实现营收增长并重新扭亏为盈：

<!--en-->
Looking ahead to 1996, we plan to continue to grow the premium/special markets business which has achieved exceptional results the past two years. Munsingwear's strong consumer brand recognition, the Penguin logo, quality product and the agility to merchandise across a broad product line give us a competitive advantage. We are confident that increased revenues and a return to profitability will be achieved due to the following:

- 高端/特色市场及高尔夫用品店业务持续强劲的销售增长。
- 成本削减计划。
- 持续聚焦核心产品——男士短袖针织高尔夫衬衫，且定价适中。（LOWELL M. FISHER的照片）哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程
* 所有产品线均采用创新设计与面料。
* 持续升级管理信息系统。
* 通过新增三名董事来加强董事会实力：托马斯·D·格里森于今年1月被任命为董事会非执行主席；凯文·S·摩尔和威廉·J·摩根则分别代表公司最大的两位单一股东。1995年底，我们聘请了一家投资银行协助探索各种能够最大化股东价值的机会，预计此类活动将在1996年加速推进。有关进一步的财务分析以及前瞻性信息说明，请参阅本年报中的管理层讨论与分析部分。尽管1995年对零售业而言是艰难的一年，但公司在两个最盈利的业务领域——高端/特色市场及高尔夫专卖店——仍取得了极为可观的营收增长。这些成果再次印证了我们继续推进公司转型决策的正确性：拓展市场、提升产品质量、增加消费者价值并加大基础设施投入。因此，我们如今处于更为强劲的战略地位；我期待与汤姆·格里森及董事会携手，继续为确保公司的长期成功与盈利能力而努力。最后，我要感谢在公司的转型过程中始终给予支持的客户、供应商及贷款方。此外，我想借此机会感谢所有Munsingwear员工，他们的辛勤付出促成了1995年惊人的销售增长，也让我们对1996年充满信心。诚挚地，/s/ 洛厄尔·M·费舍尔 洛厄尔·M·费舍尔，总裁兼首席执行官。

<!--en-->
- Continued strong sales growth in premium/special markets and golf pro shop businesses.
- Cost reduction programs.
- Continued focus on core capability – men's, short sleeve, knit, and moderately priced golf shirts.
(Picture of LOWELL M. FISHER)
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
* Innovative designs and fabrics throughout all product lines.
* Continued upgrading of management information systems.
* Strengthening of our Board of Directors by the addition of three new members, Thomas D. Gleason, who was named non-executive Chairman of the Board in January of this year, and Kevin S. Moore and William J. Morgan, who represent the Company's two largest single stockholders.
In late 1995 we retained the services of an investment banking firm to help us explore a range of opportunities to maximize shareholder value, and we expect this activity to accelerate in 1996. Please refer to the Management's discussion and analysis section in this annual report for additional financial analysis and a statement regarding forward-looking information.
Although 1995 was a difficult year for retailing, the Company achieved extremely promising revenue growth in our two most profitable businesses—premium/special markets and golf pro shops. These results reaffirmed our decision to continue the Company's transition – expanding markets, enhancing product quality, increasing consumer value and investing in infrastructure. As a result, we are now in a much stronger strategic position and I look forward to working with Tom Gleason and the Board in continuing our efforts to ensure the long-term success and profitability of the Company.
In closing, I would like to thank our customers, suppliers and lender, who have continued to support us throughout the Company's transition. Finally, I would like to take this opportunity to thank all Munsingwear employees for their hard work and effort which led to spectacular 1995 sales growth and reinforces our optimism for 1996.
Sincerely,
/s/ Lowell M. Fisher
Lowell M. Fisher, President and CEO.
