### 对价值投资者乔尔·格林布拉特的访谈

<!--en-->
*Interview with Value Investor Joel Greenblatt*

作者：比尔·曼（TMF Otter） 2005年12月21日 《战胜市场的小书》。*标题大胆？也许吧，但乔尔·格林布拉特确实具备相应的实力与业绩支撑。他的投资回报在业内堪称惊人，过去20年间年均回报率超过40%。* 132节哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
By Bill Mann (TMF Otter) December 21, 2005
The Little Book that Beats the Market. *Audacious title? Maybe, but Joel Greenblatt has the chops and the record to back it up. His investment returns are amongst the most incredible in investing, with returns exceeding 40% per year over the last 2 decades.*
132
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**比尔·曼：**你在本书开头提到，你认为自己的第一本书《你也能成为股市天才》的内容比预期要深奥一些。因此你为孩子们写了《战胜市场的小书》。能为我们描述一下创作这本书的过程吗？

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** One of the things that you talked about in the beginning of this book is that you felt like your first book, *You Can Be a Stock Market Genius*, was a little more advanced than you had intended it to be. So you wrote *The Little Book that Beats the Market* with your kids in mind. Describe for us some process that you went through in creating the book?

**乔尔·格林布拉特：**当然可以。实际情况是，我在哥伦比亚大学授课已有十年之久，期间一直教授一些简单的理念。我的学生们总说我讲得太简单了，于是我们把过去二十年在哥谭资本所采用的方法提炼成几个重要概念。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Oh sure. Well, the way it really happened was that there are a few simple things I have been teaching for ten years over at Columbia. My students are always accusing me of making things sound too simple, so we sort of boiled down to what we have done for the last twenty years at *Gotham Capital* to a couple of important concepts.

这些概念就是：以低廉价格购买优质公司。我们定义“优质公司”的标准是那些能产生高资本回报率的公司。举个例子，如果一家公司开设门店，每家门店成本为40万美元，而每家店能带来20万美元的收益，那么资本回报率就是50%。另一家公司同样开设门店，成本也是40万美元，但每年仅能盈利1万美元，其资本回报率仅为2.5%。简而言之，我们认为“年资本回报率为50%的公司显然比回报率为2.5%的公司要好得多”。这就是我们界定优质公司的一般标准——即能产生高资本回报率的公司。接着我们说：“让我们设法低价买入这些优质公司。”我们定义“便宜”的标准是：相对于支付的价格而言，公司所能产生的收益较高。我们称之为盈余收益率，它是市盈率的反向指标。也就是说，如果你能用低价买到大量盈余，那这家公司就是便宜的。

<!--en-->
What those concepts were were buying good companies at bargain prices. The way we define "good companies" was companies that earn a high return on capital. What that might mean is that if for instance a company opens stores and each store costs $400,000 and you can earn $200,000 on a store, that is a 50% return on capital. If another company opens stores that also cost $400,000 but they only earn $10,000 a year, that is a 2.5% return on capital. Simply, we said, "gee, the company that earns 50% a year on the capital invested is a lot better than the one that earns 2.5%." That is generally the course we have taken to define what a good company is, something that earns a high return on capital. Then we said, "Let's try to buy those good companies cheaply." The way we defined "cheap" was companies that earn a lot relative to the price we are paying. So we call that earnings yield, which is the inverse of P/E. So that just means that if you can buy a lot of earnings for a cheap price, that makes the company cheap.

如果我们能买到既优质又便宜的公司，在我看来这就是好事。这正是我们在哥谭资本寻找投资机会时的目标。这些概念对孩子来说并不难理解。只要这样解释给他们听——我只是想以低廉价格购买优质公司——他们通常就能明白。

<!--en-->
So if we can buy a good company that is also cheap, in combination that strikes me as being a good thing. That is what we tend to look for when we are looking for investments at *Gotham Capital*. Those concepts are not too hard for kids to understand. If you explain to them that way, that I am just trying to buy good companies at bargain prices, they tend to understand that.

重要的是你要理解自己正在做什么，而不仅仅是照搬我所说的“魔法公式”。如果你只是机械地遵循魔法公式，它并不总能奏效。但如果你理解了其中的道理，就会说：“你知道吗？以低廉价格购买优质公司确实合乎逻辑，最终这一定会奏效。”我们的一项研究表明，仅凭借这一公式，大盘股公司的回报就能达到市场平均水平的两倍；而对于小盘股，回报甚至能接近市场平均水平的三倍。

<!--en-->
It's very important that you understand what you are doing, not just following what I call the Magic Formula. If you are just following a Magic Formula, that formula doesn't always work. But if you understand what you are doing, you will say, "you know what? It just makes sense to buy good companies at bargain prices and eventually this will work." We did a study showing that large-cap companies can double the market's return just following this formula. With small caps, you could actually almost triple the market's return.

**比尔·曼：**我想强调一点：当你说“我们”时，指的是哥谭资本。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** I wanted to make this point. When you say "we", you are talking about *Gotham Capital*.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：**没错，指的是我在哥谭资本的合伙人。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** My partners at *Gotham Capital*, yes.

**比尔·曼：**需要明确的是，这正是你二十多年来在哥谭资本管理资金时所采用的方法。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** And just to be clear, this is part of the process that you have used to manage money at *Gotham Capital* for more than 20 years.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：**是的。书中的魔法公式并非我们通过大量回测、尝试40种不同公式后才找到的。这是我们最初尝试的方法，其输入参数也大致反映了我们的专业投资方式。谈到回测要素时，我们想：“还是简单点吧。看看公司的实际表现如何。如果我们根据盈余收益率和资本回报率对它们排名，并选取这两项指标综合排名最靠前的公司，这样的股票组合表现会怎样呢？”这就是我们进行的回测，也是我们最先测试的内容；正因为其简单明了，我才将其写入书中。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Yes. The Magic Formula from the book is not something that we fished around for by back tested extensively, using 40 different formulas until something looked like it worked. This is the absolute first thing that we tried, and the inputs approximate how we invest professionally. So when we talked about components for a back test we thought "Let's keep it simple. Let's look at what companies do. If we rank them based on earnings yield and return on capital and picked the companies with the best combined ranking of those two factors, how would a portfolio of stocks like that do?" That is what we back tested and that was the first thing we tested and that is what I wrote up in the book because it is so simple and obvious.

我们在哥谭资本的操作略有不同。对于我的孩子们，我认为他们尚不具备预测未来盈余的能力。在哥谭资本，我们并未采用去年的盈余数据——正是这些数据在魔法公式中创造了市场回报两倍乃至三倍的佳绩——而是使用我们认为几年后（三四年后）的正常盈余水平。

<!--en-->
There is a slight difference in what we do at *Gotham Capital*. For my kids, I did not think they were capable of projecting earnings out into the future. At *Gotham Capital* what we do is, instead of using least year's earnings, which is what we used for the Magic Formula and what got those great results of double and triple the market's returns, we used what we think normal earnings will be several years out, three or four years from now.

我们无法为大多数公司做出此类预测，但对于那些我们能够预测，或我们对预测结果有把握的公司，我们会将预测数据代入“魔法公式”，而非使用去年的盈利数据。因此，我们采用了两种截然不同的策略。其一，在使用“魔法公式”时，若参考去年的盈利数据，我们会构建一个由20或30家公司组成的投资组合；平均而言，这些公司的表现会非常出色，正如我刚才提到的结果。而对于*哥谭资本*而言，我们构建的投资组合更为集中，或许只包含五到八家公司，它们通常占我们投资组合的80%。对于这些公司，我们不会代入去年的盈利数据，而是代入对未来几年正常盈利情况的预测值，并将其用于“魔法公式”中。

<!--en-->
We can't make those projections for most companies, but for the companies that we can make those projections for, or we feel confident about our projections, then we plug those into the Magic Formula rather than last year's earnings. So there are two really different strategies that we use. One, for the Magic Formula when we are looking at last year's earnings, we buy a portfolio stock, either 20 or 30 companies because on average,they do incredibly well, were the results I just mentioned. For *Gotham Capital*, we do a much more concentrated portfolio, perhaps five or eight companies, generally are 80% of or portfolio, and those are companies that instead of plugging in last year's earnings, we plug in our projections for normal earnings several years out for the company, but we are actually plugging it in to the Magic Formula.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：正因如此，我们的投资组合更为集中，且会对所持有的每家公司进行更深入的研究。对于大多数非职业投资者来说，参考去年的盈利数据并购买由20或30家公司组成的投资组合，往往能获得极佳的平均回报。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
So we are more concentrated and we do a lot more work on each company that we own because of that. For most investors who don't do this for a living, they are better off looking at last year's earnings and buying a portfolio of 20 or 30 companies that on average will do tremendously well.

**比尔·曼：**这是一个极其重要的概念。我认为这本书的一大亮点在于：它并未谈论未来会发生什么，没有涉及激光束、牙科技术之类虽令人兴奋但当前未必能产生盈利的领域。“魔法公式”的基础在于公司已经实现的盈利，即“现实情况”。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** It is such an important concept and one of the facts that I thought was great about the book is that you are not talking about what will be. You are not talking about laser beams and dental technology and all of these things that people get excited about that may not have earnings at present. The basis for the Magic Formula rests upon what is, what earnings the company already has generated.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：**我认为这正是人们能够做到的事情。对此并无争议。你只需了解去年发生的情况，这就足够了。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** That is really I think what people can do. There is no argument about it. You know what happened last year and that is all you need to know.

我不建议人们在未做任何研究的情况下挑选个股；但如果你愿意基于这些简单概念构建由20或30只股票组成的教育投资组合，平均而言你的表现将会非常出色。

<!--en-->
I wouldn't suggest people, without doing any work, pick individual stocks, but if you are willing to own a 20 or 30 stock portfolio based on these simple concepts, on average you are going to do tremendously well.

**比尔·曼：**既然这种策略对20或30只股票的效果如此之好，为何不挑选排名前三的公司进行集中投资呢？我的意思是，如果你能确定是哪三只的话。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** What about the argument of if this works very well with the 20 and 30, why wouldn't you pick the top three and concentrate? I mean, if you could determine what they were.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：**尽管我在书中提到该公式实际上是按顺序起作用的。换句话说，我们先对低价且优质的公司分别排名，再将这两个排名合并为“魔法公式”排名。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Even though what I said in the book was the formula actually works in order. In other words, we take the combined ranking of cheap and good companies and we combine those ranks into a Magic Formula ranking.

我在书中指出，如果我们把所研究的3,500家公司分为十个等级，按“魔法公式”排名，前10%为第一等级，接下来10%为第二等级，以此类推，那么“魔法公式”确实按顺序起作用：第一等级的表现优于第二等级，依此类推。由于涉及股票数量庞大，实际上挑选前25只股票中的任何一只与挑选第22至24只股票之间并无显著的统计差异；因此，排名前三的股票并不一定比第22至24名表现更好。

<!--en-->
I said in the book that if you divide all 3,500 companies we modeled into deciles where you take the top 10% as ranked by the Magic Formula then the next 10% then the next 10%, the Magic Formula works in order. The top decile beats the second decile, and so on. That's over a large amount of stocks so there really is not much statistical difference between picking any of the top let's say, 25 stocks versus one, so the top three don't necessarily do better than number 22 to 24.

**比尔·曼：**事实上，过度集中投资会增加风险，因为你是在依赖一个公式。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** And you would in fact increase risk by being concentrated because you are trusting a formula.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：**没错，平均而言该公式效果显著。既然已经有一个平均表现良好的策略，不妨就遵循它。选择三只股票或许能带来更好的结果，但也可能表现更差。既然几乎可以确定能获利的策略摆在面前，何必放弃呢？

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Right, on average it works so to just pick a few names, if you have something on average that works, you might as well shoot for that average. You may do better with the three stocks, but you may do a lot worse. If you have almost a sure thing, why throw it away?

**比尔·曼：**你在研究中做了这样一件事：分别考察了集中于大型公司与市值低至5,000万美元的公司时的表现。那如果市值比这还小呢？

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** One of the things that you did in the study was to bifurcate what would you do if you concentrated on the largest companies and then you went down as low as $50 million. What about going smaller than that?

**乔尔·格林布拉特：**在那种情况下，该策略应该会表现惊人地好。但我不想写一本人们无法实际操作的书，同时我也想展示“魔法公式”的稳健性。它在小盘股上的表现极为出色：我们测试的由30只股票组成的小盘股投资组合，在17年间年均收益率超过了30%。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** It should work amazingly well there, but I didn't want to write a book that people couldn't execute and I also wanted to show how robust the Magic Formula was. It worked amazingly well with small caps. Using a small cap model of 30 stock portfolios that we tested over the 17 years, it earned over 30% a year.

我只是想确保人们认识到该公式的稳健性，以及它是可以实际操作的——确实能买到足够的股票。如果我们写的书能被更多人阅读，我们甚至展示了它对前1,000家公司同样有效。

<!--en-->
It is just that I want to make sure people realize that the formula was very robust and that you could actually execute, you could actually buy enough stock and if you are buying a book that hopefully a lot of people will read, we even showed how it worked for the top thousand companies.

虽然其表现不如在小盘股上那么突出（因为可選的小盘股数量远多于大盘股），但效果仍然惊人：它的回报率超过了市场两倍之多。很难被超越。

<!--en-->
It didn't work quite as well as with the small caps because there are many more small caps to choose from than large caps, but it worked incredibly well. It more than doubled the market's return. Tough to beat that.

**比尔·曼：**如果一家公司的日均成交量为50股，且出现在该名单上，对大多数投资者而言实际上并无意义，因为他们无法执行交易。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** So if a company that trades 50 shares a day and shows up on that list, that makes it functionally irrelevant for most investors because you can't execute a trade.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 嗯，我们不仅设定了最低市值要求，还规定了最低交易条件，这样你才能实际交易这些股票并将其纳入我们的模型。当然，小投资者相比大投资者有许多优势；如果你管理的资金量不至于让你无法购买小盘股，那你就拥有巨大优势——你可以从更多公司中挑选股票。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Well, we didn't just have a minimum market cap, we also had a minimum trading requirement so that you actually had to be able to trade these stocks to be put into our model. Sure, the small investor has many advantages over the large investor and if you aren't running so much money that you areprevented from buying smaller cap stocks, then you have a big advantage. You can choose from a lot more companies.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**比尔·曼：** 由于你采用的是机械性策略，人们必然会将其与吉姆·奥沙尼所著的《华尔街上的成功法则》一书相提并论。这与奥沙尼的做法有何不同呢？

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** Because you're dealing with a mechanical strategy, one of the books that people will inevitably make a parallel to is Jim O'Shaughnessy's *What Works on Wall Street*. How is this different from what O'Shaughnessy did?

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 首先，他花了很长时间测试了几十种公式，然后挑选出效果最好的那些。而我们则是根据自己实际的做法来选定一个公式并进行测试。这个公式是按照从最佳十分位到最差十分位对股票进行排序的，因此它并非只是挑选极端表现突出的股票。它实际上反映了我们认为在股市中赚钱的关键：即在股价低廉时买入优质公司。所以我们的做法确实有所不同。我个人认为吉姆·奥沙尼的书非常出色。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Well number one, he tested dozens of formulas over a long period of time and then picked the ones that worked the best. What we did is we picked a formula based on what we actually do, and we tested it. This was it. This formula ranks stocks in order from best deciles to worse and so it wasn't just picking the top outliers. It was really actually picking what we think goes into making money in the stock market, which is buying good companies when they are cheap, so it was really done somewhat differently. I actually thought Jim O'Shaughnessy's book was excellent.

**比尔·曼：** 我完全同意。Motley Fool的早期发展部分正是基于吉姆·奥沙尼的研究成果，所以我绝非在贬低他。正如你提到的，现在有一家基金公司正在运用他的一些公式，且业绩表现极为优异。[*编者注：这家基金公司是Hennessy Advisors（纳斯达克代码：HNNA），我们曾将其称为“小型瑰宝”。*]

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** I absolutely agree. The early history of The Motley Fool was built partially around Jim O'Shaughnessy's work, so I certainly am not casting aspersions. As you mentioned, there is a mutual fund company now that runs some of his formulas and does very, very well. [*Editor's Note: That mutual fund company is Hennessy Advisors (Nasdaq: HNNA), which we have highlighted as a Tiny Gem.*]

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 嗯，发生的事非常有趣。我曾写过关于基于公式的投资系统的历史：有一只基金开始采用奥沙尼的公式，但在最初三年里表现很差。该基金业绩不佳，基金经理最终卖掉了公司；接手的人继续沿用同一公式，结果随后便取得了优异成绩。自成立以来，该基金的表现一直非常出色，但最初的投资者和基金经理却因初期业绩不佳而离开。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Well, it is very interesting what happened. I actually wrote up the history of formula-based investing system where a fund did start using one of O'Shaughnessy's formulas and did very badly for the first three years. The fund didn't do well and the fund manager ended up selling the company and then the person who bought it continued with the same formula and ended up doing very well right afterwards. So since inception that fund has done incredibly well yet the original investors and the original fund manager are gone because it didn't do well in the beginning.

我认为这正是“魔法公式”的精妙之处。它并非总能奏效；如果它总是有效，人人都会采用它。确实存在一两年甚至三年时间，“魔法公式”未能跑赢市场，但从长期来看，它总能战胜市场，这一点非常强大。

<!--en-->
I think that is what so great about the Magic Formula. It doesn't always work. If it always worked, everyone would do it. There are one, two or three-year periods of the Magic Formula that we are talking about where it doesn't beat the market, but over long periods of time, it always beats the market and that is very, very powerful.

我举过这样的例子：$2+2=4$这个概念。众所周知事实就是如此，无论别人怎么说，$2+2$始终等于四。无论他们多么聪明、说辞多么动听，你都会坚持自己的判断。如果你明白自己在此处所做之事——即坚信自己是在以低价买入优质公司——你也会坚持下去，因为这样做合乎逻辑；即便市场在很长一段时间内并不认同你的观点。

<!--en-->
I used the example, the concept of $2+2=4$. Everyone knows that that is the case and no matter what anyone tells you, $2+2$ always equals four. It doesn't matter how smart they are, how long they tell you, you are going to stick to your guns. So you will also stick to your guns if you understand what you are doing here, which is if you truly believe what you are doing is buying good companies at bargain prices, you will keep doing it because it makes sense, even though the market doesn't agree with you for long periods of time.

**比尔·曼：** 我们在20世纪90年代末看到，许多盈利丰厚的公司股价却异常低廉，因为整个投资者群体似乎都被互联网泡沫所吸引。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** We saw in the late 1990s where a lot of companies that were just making a lot of money were very, very cheap because it seemed like the investor class as a whole was distracted by things that ended in dot com.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 嗯，这就是最好的例证。2000年，我们持有了许多股价低廉但质地优良的公司的股票，市场却并不重视它们，我们的投资表现也不佳。此外，我们认为互联网泡沫随时会破裂——因为股价高得离谱——这可能会拖累我们的投资，就像最终发生的互联网股崩盘一样。但我们决定：“嘿，听着，我们持有的是低价买入的优质公司。我们只需继续做我们认为正确的事。”

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Well, that is the best example. In the year 2000, we owned a lot of good companies at cheap prices that the market didn't really care about and we weren't doing very well with them. On top of that, we thought the Internet bubble was going to burst any day because stocks were at ridiculous prices and wouldn't that drag down our investments along with the crash in the Internet stocks that we eventually thought might take place, but we decided "hey, listen, we own good companies at bargain prices. We are just going to just keep doing what we know makes sense."

最终的结果是市场遭到重创：标普指数暴跌，纳斯达克指数也在2000年大幅下挫，而我们的投资组合却上涨了超过100%。如果这还不能让你坚持自己认为正确的做法，那我真不知道还有什么能做到了。市场可能表现糟糕，但只要你行事明智，长期而言你一定会取得不错的成绩。

<!--en-->
What ended up happening is the market did get crushed. The S&P got crushed. The NASDAQ got crushed in 2000, yet our portfolio was up more than 100%, so if that doesn't tell you to stick with what you think makes sense, I don't know what will. So the market could do badly but as long as you are doing smart things, over time you will do quite well.

**比尔·曼：** 我认为这正是“魔法公式”立刻吸引我的原因。它并非那种“如果你在每月第一个星期四买入，效果会更好”之类的规则。这两个投资要素极具说服力，它们正是优秀价值投资的核心。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** I think that was one of the things about the Magic Formula that immediately attracted me. It wasn't something where you said "Well, if you buy it on the first Thursday of the month, it works out better." These are two very defensible investing components. They are at the core of what good value investing is.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 嗯，我想说我学到了很多。我写这本书的原因之一是，尽管我拥有沃顿商学院的学士和MBA学位，但我实际上是个自学成才的投资者。至于投资方面，他们教给我的唯一道理就是：你无法跑赢市场。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Well, I would say that I have learned a lot. One of the reasons I wrote this book is because I am really a self-taught investor even though I got a BS and an MBA from Wharton. As far as investing, all they taught me was that you can't beat the market.

我的投资知识来自阅读，我读过本杰明·格雷厄姆的书，也读过沃伦·巴菲特的文章。这些才是真正教会我的东西。大卫·德雷曼以及格雷厄姆和德雷曼的观点都指出：买入便宜的股票是明智之举，而且从长期来看确实有效。巴菲特则补充了一点：要在股票便宜时买入优质公司。

<!--en-->
Investing I learned from reading and I was reading books by Benjamin *Graham*. I was reading the writings of Warren Buffett. Those are the things that really taught me. The readings of David *Dreman* and so *Graham* and *Dreman* taught buying cheap is a good thing to do and it works over time. Buffett added the component of buying good companies when they are cheap.

我不会妄称这是一种类似于沃伦·巴菲特的公式，但可以说两者的理念是一致的。巴菲特说：“我会坚持投资优质公司，并在价格合适时买入。”这正是“魔法公式”为投资者所做的——只不过你可以从比巴菲特现在管理的800亿美元资产所涵盖的范围更广的股票中挑选标的。

<!--en-->
I wouldn't presume to say oh, this is a formula that is similar to Warren Buffett, but what I would say is that the concepts are the same. Buffett says "I am going to stick to good companies and buy them when I can buy them at a good price." This is systematically what the Magic Formula does for you except you get to choose from a lot larger universe of stocks than Buffett does now that he is running $80 billion.

**比尔·曼：** 你提到在沃顿商学院没有学到的投资知识，这很有意思。许多个人投资者会立刻去关注一个人毕业于哪所学校；他们会说：“这个人肯定懂投资，他可是哈佛MBA。”但现实情况却大不相同，似乎只有一处例外——哥伦比亚大学。你在哥伦比亚商学院任教，因此或许能对此发表真知灼见。哥伦比亚大学的独特之处在于它有着向学生传授投资知识的悠久历史。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** It's interesting that you mention what you didn't learn about investing at Wharton. A lot of individual investors will look immediately to what schools a person has gone to or as they say, "this person obviously has to know about investing. He has a Harvard MBA." But reality is so much different, except, it seems, at one place – Columbia. You teach at Columbia Business School, so you may really be able to speak to this. Columbia is really unique in that it has a long history of actually teaching investing to students.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 我每次上课时都会对学生们说：“我希望传授给他们的是我当年读商学院时渴望学到的课程。”我想把我的经验分享给年轻人。从实际投资角度来看，这极具价值。每个投资者都会犯大量错误——无论他是沃伦·巴菲特，还是从业时间长短如何，人们都会随时间犯错。但这并非问题所在。真正的问题是能否长期坚持做那些从长远来看有意义的事情。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Well I always start each class to my students and say, "I aim to teach the class that I wish I had when I went to business school." I want to give young people the benefit of the experience that I have been through. From a practical standpoint in investing this is hugely beneficial. Every investor makes tons of mistakes. It doesn't matter whether they are Warren Buffett or how long they have been doing it or everything else, people make mistakes over time. That is not the problem. The problem is sticking to continually trying to do things that make sense over long periods of time.

我认为这是最重要的一点：什么才有意义？那就是对公司的价值进行评估，并试图以折扣价买入。当然，评估公司价值时你难免会出错——这是我对所有学生的保证。我说过，如果你能准确评估公司价值，市场最终会认同你的判断。这可能需要两三年时间，但通常最多也就两三年，只要你的评估正确，市场最终一定会认可你。

<!--en-->
I think that is the most important thing to teach people. What does make sense? You are valuing companies and you are trying to buy them at a discount. Of course you will make mistakes valuing companies. This is a guarantee I give to all of my students. I say if you do a good job valuing companies, the market will agree with you. It could take two or three years. It usually takes only at most two or three years, but eventually the market will agree with you, as long as your evaluation work is correct.

从统计上看，这正是我们运用“魔法公式”想要实现的目标：我们买入的是那些平均而言业务良好且价格低廉的公司；这类公司会在不久后回归合理定价。尤其是如果你多年坚持这一策略，只要你有耐心，从长期看几乎注定能盈利。

<!--en-->
I think statistically that is what we are trying to do with the Magic Formula, which is we are buying a group of companies that are in good businesses on average, that are cheap on average and that group of companies will go back to fairly priced within not too long a time, especially if you follow the strategy over a period of years, and you are almost guaranteed to make money over the long term, if you are patient.

**比尔·曼：** 你认为为什么大多数商学院会教授“这种折价并不存在”的观点呢？

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** Why do you suppose that most business schools teach that those discounts don't exist?

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 你知道，我认为商学院在40年前误入了“有效市场”的歧途，进而引入了大量关于波动性的统计数据和理论。当你回过头来看，投资其实就是买入一家公司的部分所有权，并在认为价格便宜时入手；那么过去六个月里股价的波动其实根本不值得关注，毕竟你买的是公司的一部分，而非单纯的证券或股票。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** You know, I think business schools 40 years ago took a wrong turn into efficient market land and through it a lot of statistics and issues about volatility and things of that nature. When you go back and you look at investing as buying a piece of a company and buying it when you think it is at a cheap price, then how much the stock bounced around over the last six months really ends up being sort of a silly thing to look at rather than thinking about it as owning a piece of company.

当你真正明白自己是在购买公司的一部分——而非证券或股票——时，商学院所教授的所有统计数据、理论等等就完全失去了意义。

<!--en-->
When you actually look at what you are doing, which is buying a piece of a company, not a security, not a share of stock, but you are actually buying a piece of a company, all the statistics and all the theory and everything else that business schools teach end up making no sense whatsoever.

**比尔·曼：** 这简直成了哥伦比亚商学院的一则绝佳广告，对吧？*(笑声)* 书中让我印象深刻的一个故事是关于你上课的第一天。你让某人随便说出一个公司名称，然后手里拿着报纸的商业版块，讨论该公司一年内的股价变动情况。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** This has become a very nice advertisement for Columbia Business School, right? *(Laughs.)*
One of the stories that I really enjoyed from the book was on your first day of class. The other thing that you did was you had someone just name a company and you had the business section of the paper in your hand and discussed the prices, how they varied within a one-year period.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 没错。每学期初，我会让学生们随便说一家公司的名字。他们通常会选通用汽车、通用电气、富乐客，或是阿贝克隆比&费奇这类公司。如果有人选中阿贝克隆比&费奇，我就会翻开报纸查看其52周的最高价和最低价。假设52周最高价为74美元，最低价为43美元。如果该公司股价在一年内一直在43美元到74美元之间波动，说明这家公司的实际价值基本没有变化。若观察过去两年的数据，价格区间甚至更宽——股价在23美元到74美元之间浮动，尽管这家公司本身在这几年里并无太大改变。这怎么可能呢？难道该公司的价值在那段时间里发生了如此巨大的变化吗？你们能解释这种现象吗？这合理吗？我的学生们会花大量时间试图找出合理的解释，实际上学术界也有专门的研究领域来阐释其中的道理。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Right. What I do is at the beginning of a semester, I call out to my students, "Just name a company." They will pick GM or GE or Foot Locker or something -- Abercrombie and Fitch, for instance. So if you pick something like Abercrombie and Fitch, I will open up the newspaper and I will look at the 52-week high and low. So the 52-week high let's say is 74. The 52-week low is 43. The company is pretty muchunchanged during the course of the year, if the stock has fluctuated between 43 and 74. If you go over the last two years, it is even a wider range. The stock has been between 23 and 74 even though this company hasn't changed very much in the last couple of years. How is that possible? Has the value of this company changed so much during that time? How do you explain that? Does this make any sense? My students spend a lot of time coming up with explanations as to why this makes sense and actually there are whole fields of academic study to explain why this makes sense.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：我会问学生：“你们认为为什么某天股价会是23美元，几个月后又变成74美元？这合理吗？”我的结论是：我不知道原因何在，而且我告诉他们我并不在乎原因是什么。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
So I ask the question I ask my students, Why do you think the stock can be $23 one day and $74 several months later? Does this make any sense? My conclusion is I don't know why it happens and I tell them I don't care why it happens.

**比尔·曼：** 我庆幸这种事确实会发生。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** I thank my lucky stars that it does happen.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 没错，这种情况确实会发生。我只需要知道：尽管股价波动剧烈，但公司的实际价值却不太可能随之大幅波动。魔法公式的目的就是挑选出那些在低价时估值被严重低估的公司。我们通过系统化的方式自动筛选出具备特定特征的公司——它们既便宜又是优质企业。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Right, it does happen. All I have to know is that even though the price is bouncing around a lot, it is unlikely that the value of the company is bouncing around nearly as much. So what the Magic Formula is trying to do is pick out those companies that are unreasonably low priced at the times when they are low priced. We are doing that automatically systematically by picking companies that have certain characteristics. They are cheap and they are still good businesses.

**比尔·曼：** 没错，我认为这正是稳健投资的核心要素——关注这两点。格雷厄姆说过，巴菲特也说过，现在你也在强调这一点。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** Yeah, and again I think that that is really the core element of sound investing is looking at those two, is looking at those two things. *Graham* said it and Buffett said it and now you are saying it.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 嗯，我喜欢追随伟人的脚步。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Well, I like to follow in good footsteps.

**比尔·曼：** 这本书名叫《战胜市场的简单法则》，现在已上市，对吗？

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** The book is called *The Little Book That Beats the Market* and it is available now, is that correct?

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 是的。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** It is.

**比尔·曼：** 太好了。祝你好运，也非常感谢你抽出时间与我们《傻瓜投资网》的读者分享心得。

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** OK, well fantastic. We wish you the best of luck and thank you so much for spending time with us here at The Motley Fool.

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 比尔，衷心感谢你所做的一切。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** Bill, thanks so much for everything.

**比尔·曼：** 保重，乔尔。*比尔·曼持有轩尼诗顾问公司的股票。* *又一个学期*

<!--en-->
**Bill Mann:** Take care, Joel.

### 格林布拉特课程 #1

<!--en-->
*Greenblatt Class # 1*

2005年1月18日：本周末，外部人士须通过邮件联系*乔尔·格林布拉特*以报名审计课程。

<!--en-->
Jan 18, 2005
This weekend outsiders must email *Joel Greenblatt* about auditing class.

*摘要：乔尔的职业——以低价买入资产。价值投资中的机会。为何聪明人并未取得更好成绩？价值投资为何有效？估值技术存在的问题。*被动投资的社会效用是什么？在乔尔看来是*零*。这类似于擅长在赛马场挑选赢家。**乔尔擅长通过分析来赚钱。**他的职业是什么？花25美分买4包口香糖，然后以每包25美分的价格卖出。他每天卖出3包。15周×36次，持续6年，计算结果为((4×0.25美元)−0.25美元)×5×36×6=810.00美元。成本为1.25美元×216=270美元。

<!--en-->
*Summary: What Joel does for a living: buying something for less. Opportunity in value investing. Why don't smart people do better? Why value investing works. Problems with valuation techniques.*
What is the social utility of passive investing? *None* that Joel can see. It is similar to being good at picking horses at the track. **Joel is good at handicapping to make money.**
What does he do for a living? Buy 4 packs of gum for 25 cents and sell one back each for 25 cents. He sells 3 packs a day. 15 weeks x 36 for 6 years or ((4 x $0.25) - $0.25) x 5 x 36 x 6 = $810.00. He pays $1.25 x 216 = $270.

**他所做的全部事情：** **找出企业的真实价值，并以低于该价值的价格买入。**这就是了解企业价值的力量。

<!--en-->
**All he does:** **He finds out what businesses are worth & buy them for less.** This is the power of knowing the value of a business.

看看这些股票：*eBay*从64美元涨至118美元；*通用汽车*从29美元涨至55美元；*苹果公司*从20美元涨至70美元；*克里斯比·克雷姆*则从50美元跌至5美元。

<!--en-->
Look at stocks: *EBay* from $64 to $118. *GM* from $29 to $55. *AAPL* from $20 to $70. *Krispy Kreme* $50 to $5.

随便说一家公司：如果市场是有效的，为何价格区间会如此（宽泛）？内在价值变化缓慢，但价格却波动剧烈且范围宽广。请注意这种差异。

<!--en-->

### 每种估值方法的缺陷

<!--en-->
*Flaws with Each Valuation Method*

1. 内在价值——现金流折现法存在缺陷，输入参数的微小变化会导致估值大幅波动。仅当企业非常稳定时才可使用该方法，且假设中的增长率和折现率应极为保守。
2. 相对价值——市盈率相近，但其他上市公司被高估。大多数收购最终失败。只需支付250倍 earnings的1/2即可。不具备可比性——行业正在整合。
3. 清算价值。其中一个业务部门每股盈利3美元，而另一个部门每股亏损1美元。因此每股盈利为2美元；若股价为33美元，则对应17倍的每股收益倍数。如果扣除亏损部门的影响后每股收益为-1.00美元，这一估值便存在缺陷。所以我们采用多种估值方法相互验证，并采用*保守*的假设，同时参考长期债券收益率。当每股收益为1美元时，16.66倍市盈率与6%的长期债券收益率相对应。比较“不断增值的美元”与“固定价值的美元”：政府债券收益率为6%，但如果美元本身能增值则更佳。若当前长期债券利率（2005年2月）为4%，至少应将其作为最低门槛利率或折现率，并预留安全边际。当每股收益为1美元时，若债券收益率为6%而股票收益率为5%，但只要公司能持续增长则更好。目前每股收益为1美元，但经调整后的盈利仅为0.50美元——你更愿意持有无风险的债券还是这只股票呢？它究竟能否实现增长？哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程。复杂的资本结构：买入相当于一半现金价值的企业以及优质业务。**价值投资者俱乐部（VIC）**：其中一半成员是专业人士，其余则是经验丰富的金融从业者。该俱乐部有不错的研报。为何价格低廉？由于每位成员每年需提交2个投资思路，数量不超过6个，因此会有一定周转。请查阅VIC的申请要求。S.CN Sherritt STM.V JEF CAH HIF-U Groupe Bull Olympia GA 股价为4.13美元，MSO BUL.FP。下周将学习损益表、现金流量及估值工作。估值时应使用EBIT而非市盈率。请阅读Hooke所著书籍的第12-13章及第17章；书中有些观点我并不认同。Duff & Phelps案例研究——估值结果为52美元。

<!--en-->
1. Intrinsic valuation – Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) has flaws, small changes in inputs lead to huge swings in valuation. Use when the business is very stable and you should be very conservative (in your assumptions of growth and discount rate).
2. Relative value - P/E similar, but other public companies are overvalued. Most acquisitions fail. Pay only 1/2 of 250 x earnings. Not comparable - industry consolidating.
3. Break-up value. One division is earning $3 per share while the other loses $1 per share. So $2 per share and if the stock is at $33, then it trades at 17 times EPS. 11 x EPS if – ($1.00 close down our loss division) has flaws.
So we use several valuation methods to cross check. Use *conservative* assumptions.
Use a long-term bond yield. $1/EPS at 16.66 xs vs. 6% long bond. Compare a growing dollar vs. a certain dollar. 6% from govt. bond, but if $1 grows then good. If the current long bond (Feb. 2005) is 4%, use 6% at least as a minimum hurdle rate or discount rate. Have a margin of safety.
$20 ----$1 EPS but the bond yields 6% while the stock yields 5%, but if it can grow, then better.
$10 ----$1 EPS now but normalized earnings show $0.50. Do you rather own a risk- less bond or this? Is it going to grow or not?

### I. 现金

<!--en-->
*I. CASH*

上周我们提到*理论上DCF是评估企业价值的最佳方式*，但很难准确预测长期内的现金流情况。问题在于如何确定这一数值。使用DCF就像操作*哈勃望远镜*一样——稍有不慎就会看到完全不同的景象。*使用DCF的例外情况除外。*

<!--en-->
We said last week that *DCF is theoretically the way to look at things*, but it is difficult to estimate the cash collected over a long period of time. The problem is figuring that out. Using DCF is like using the *Hubbell Telescope*, one small change and you are looking at another galaxy. *Exception for using DCF.*

1. 答案：一家现金流为负但拥有优质地产的糟糕零售商。其房地产价值超过了零售业务的DCF估值。这是一种*隐藏资产*，最终或许能转化为现金流，但具有不确定性。未来财富创造能力。哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情况投资课程第141讲。
2. 另一个例子：两家折扣经纪商，其一拥有20万客户，另一家拥有100万客户；后者收购了前者。收购后，经纪商2的客户数达到120万，且成本结构保持不变。对于能够推动运营改进（主要是降低成本）的收购方而言，经纪商1的价值更高。战略买家能看到更多价值。总体而言，理论上DCF是评估企业价值的常规方法。既然如此，为何还要关注资产负债表呢？
1. 资产负债表上的现金超出了必要水平，多余的现金为5美元。该如何对这部分现金进行估值和处理？投资者必须将现金产生的现金流（利息收入）与主营业务区分开来。无需考虑利息收入这一项。
2. **管理层将如何运用这笔现金？** 这$5并不在您（投资者）的口袋里。管理层有哪些投资机会？管理层过往运用现金的历史如何？资产负债表上的现金很容易看到，但这并非分析终点。由于这$5不在您的口袋中，因此您必须根据管理层的历史、公司的历史以及所处行业的机遇来判断这笔现金将会如何被使用。如果股票看起来便宜，管理层可能会用这笔现金回购股票，从而为剩余股东创造更多价值。假设股票确实被低估，这将是对现金的良好运用。公司也可能大肆收购，但您未必会赞同——因为75%的收购最终以失败告终，您可能会认为现金会被浪费掉。**您必须确定多余现金的命运。** 尽管您在资产负债表上看到现金数额为$5，但您需要判断这笔现金对作为投资者的您而言究竟价值多少。如果您认为公司能利用这笔现金拓展业务（如收购相关企业）或用于回购股票，您可能会给予其全额价值。或者公司可能只是囤积现金，每年仅产生1%或2%的收益，此时您就会对资产负债表上的现金进行折价处理。总体而言，我会审视资产负债表上的那$5，并判断它对我的价值——我可能将其估值定为$1或$2，也可能给予其全额价值。**切勿仅按表面数值看待这$5。** 如果一切真的如此简单，投资机会也不会如此诱人。使用企业价值指标时还存在另一个缺陷：$EV = 市值 + 净债务。$6的债务加上$5的现金等于$1的企业价值。假设某公司每股价格为$7，市值为$7，拥有$5现金，则企业价值 = $7市值 - $5现金 = $2。您估计该企业的价值将达到$3，即比$2高出50%（以$2为基础给予50%的折价）。如此一来，您便能以$2的企业价值投入，换取$3的价值。**这种分析有何问题呢？** 您无法立即释放多余现金的价值。回到例子：企业价值为$2，您将其估值定为$3，但若按面值计算现金价值，就等于过分看重那$5现金。您现在投入$5是为了未来的回报，而可能需要等待2到3年。因此，$5 + $2 = $7，最终却只能换来$3 + $5 = $8。这$5可能成为“死钱”，从而限制了上行空间。请注意机会成本：您可以等待2到3年，指望*市场先生*重新评估这家企业的价值。但切勿被蒙蔽——您花费$7，两年后仅获得$8的回报，实际收益率并不高，还不到7%（确切地为6.93%）。

<!--en-->
1. Answer: A crummy retailer with negative cash flow but great real estate. The property is worth more than the DCFs of the retailing operations. *Hidden Asset* that can be eventually but uncertainly turned into cash flows. Future wealth creation
141
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
2. Another example: two discount brokers: 1 has 200,000 customers and (2) another broker that has 1,000,000 customers buys it. After the acquisition Broker 2 has 1.2 mm customers with same cost structure. Broker 1 is worth more to an acquirer who can drive operational improvement--mostly cost reduction. There is more value to a strategic buyer.
In general, DCF is theoretically the normal way to value businesses. If that is the case, then why bother looking at the balance sheet?
1. More cash on the balance sheet than is necessary. The excess cash is $5. How to value and deal with the cash? CF from cash (interest earned) an investor must separate from the operating business. Forget the interest income line.
2. **How will management deploy cash?** The $5 is not in your (the investor's) pocket. What are management's investment opportunities? What is the history of the management in deploying cash?
Cash is easy to see on the balance sheet, but that is not the end of your analysis. The $5 is not in your pocket so what you have to determine, based on the history of management, the history of the company, the opportunities in their space, what is going to happen to that cash? If the stock looks cheap, one of the things management could do with the cash is buy-back stock and accrete value to the remaining shareholders. That would be a good use of cash assuming the stock was undervalued. The company could go on an acquisition binge, and you may or may not like that since 75% of takeovers end in failure, you might think that cash will be dissipated. **You have to determine what will happen to the excess cash.**
Though you see the cash--mathematically it is $5-- on the balance sheet, you need to determine what that cash is worth to me, the investor. If I think they can grow their business with that cash like buy an add-on type of business or if they are buying back stock, I may give the cash full value. Or the company may sit on the cash and only earn 1% or 2% a year, so I discount the cash on the balance sheet. Generally, I look at that $5 on the balance sheet. And how much is it worth to me. I may value it as low as $1 or $2 or at full value.
**Don't just take the $5 at face value.** If it were all mathematically simple, the opportunities wouldn't be as great.
There is another flaw when you use Enterprise Value. $EV = Mkt.Cap. + Net Debt. $6 debt + $5 cash = $1 EV. Say a company has 1 share priced at $7 per share or a $7 Mkt. Cap. $5 in cash so $EV = $7 mkt. cap - $5 in cash = $2 in EV.
You estimate that EV will be worth $3 or 50% higher (at $2 a conservative 50% discount to $3). So you can lay out $2 in EV and have something at $3 in value. **What is wrong with that analysis?** You can't immediately unlock the value of the excess cash.
Back to example: EV is $2 and you value it at $3, however if you value the cash at par you are putting a big weight on the $5 in cash. You are laying out $5 now for a future return and you may have to wait 2 or 3 years. So $5 + $2 = $7 ------going to $3 + $5 = $8. The $5 could be dead money so there is less upside. Note opportunity costs.
You can wait round for 2 or 3 years for *Mr. Market* to revalue the business. But here don't be fooled--you pay $7 for a return of $8 after two years--your return is not that high--less than 7% compounded. (6.93% to be exact).

#### 采用企业价值（EV）分析法。

<!--en-->
*USE Enterprise Value (EV) ANALYSIS*

我们应该使用市盈率还是企业价值/息税前利润比率分析法？在本课程中，**我们始终采用企业价值/息税前利润比率分析法**，因为在我从商20年的经验中，如果您不能充分利用企业价值，别人就会取而代之。

<!--en-->
Should we use P/E or EV/EBIT analysis? In this class **we will always use EV/EBIT analysis** because in my 20 years in the business--if you don't make the best of your business, someone will come in and do it for you.

从某种意义上说，在我为您指定的书籍（胡克所著的《证券分析》）中，作者指出您无法控制公司的资本结构，因此市盈率分析法尚可接受。公司有多少债务便是多少，您只需接受这一事实。

<!--en-->
So in one sense in the book I assigned you (*Security Analysis* by Hooke), the author says that you don't have control over the capital structure of the company, so P/E analysis is fine. The Company has the debt it has and you should just leave it at that.

在哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程中，我持不同观点：我认为应始终采用企业价值（EV）分析法，而非市值和每股收益（EPS）分析法。应使用息税前利润或（EBITDA - 维持性资本支出）指标。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
I disagree and think you should always use Enterprise Value (EV) analysis not market cap and Earnings per Share (EPS) analysis. Use EBIT or (Ebitda - maint. Capex).

总体而言，我认为私人市场价值（PMV）最为理想。先算出整个企业对某人的价值，然后再以大幅折价购入。

<!--en-->
In general, I think the Private Market Value (PMV) is the best. Figure out what the whole business is worth to somebody then pay a big discount for it.

Refer to Chapter 8 of *Thorton O'Glove's Book, Quality of Earnings*.

需关注的问题：信用质量和收款能力。在制品与产成品。应将其视为风险。若采用赊销方式，销量可能会更大。存货——可售性。

Concerns: credit quality and collectivity. Work in Process (WIP) vs. Finished Goods. Look at them as risks. If you sell on credit, you can sell more stuff.

Ask if receivables and inventories growth is in line with sales growth. **Look for Aberrations and divergences.**
Determine if inventories are good--should I give the A/R and Inventory a haircut?

Could be an industry in distress. Future sales shoved into inventory. Work in Process Inventory (W.I.P.) up 50% while finished goods are up 10% - big boom in sales. Check the divergence out.

存货和应收账款是否与销售增长同步？了解存货的具体构成。要把握整体情况。

Are inventories and receivables in line with sales growth? Know what inventories are made up of.
Keep the big picture in mind.

## 三、商誉

<!--en-->
*III. Goodwill*

现在部分一般商誉不再进行摊销。有形资产价值5美元，而企业价值达10美元，因此账面价值中的10美元里包含5美元的商誉。或者说：5美元商誉（收购时支付的溢价）+ 5美元有形资产 = 10美元账面价值。

<!--en-->
Now some general goodwill is not being amortized. $5 Tangible Assets with $10 EPV so purchase price of $10 in book value has $5 in goodwill. Or $5 in goodwill (premium paid in acquisition) + tangible assets $5 = $10 book Value.

我最初支付了10美元，但现在其价值仅为7美元，因此需核销3美元（10美元-7美元）。这构成了3美元的商誉减值。哥伦比亚大学商学院开设的143门特殊情境投资课程：公司1：流动资产3美元，固定资产2美元，商誉5美元——流动负债1美元。

<!--en-->
I originally paid $10, but now the value is $7, so $3 written-off ($10 - $7). There is a Goodwill impairment of $3.
143
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Company 1:
Current Assets of $3
Fixed Assets of $2
Goodwill of $5
-Current Liabilities $1

$$ \text{Book Value} = \$9 $$

公司2：流动资产3美元，固定资产7美元（固定资产越多，通货膨胀期间的重置成本就越高），商誉0美元——流动负债1美元。

<!--en-->
Company 2:
Current Assets of $3
Fixed Assets of $7 (more fixed assets means more replacement cost during inflation)
Goodwill of $0
-Current Liabilities $1

$$ \text{Book Value} = \$9 $$

两家公司每股现金收益均为2美元。**对于公司1而言，无需替换有形资产，因此你会更青睐拥有商誉的企业。** 有形资产越少，为维持企业运营所需进行的资产替换投资就越多。我（投资者）因该企业较高的盈利价值而支付了超出有形资产价值5美元的溢价。一旦支付该溢价，我便拥有了该企业；更高的回报将使我能够以较少的固定资产投资实现增长。**我无需持续支付超出有形净资产价值的溢价。**（WEB在其1989年年度报告中对此进行了说明。）

<!--en-->
Both companies earn $2 per share in cash. **With company 1, you don't have to replace tangible assets so you would prefer the business with goodwill.** Less tangible assets means more investment to replace those assets in order to keep the business running as is. I (investor) paid a premium over the tangible assets of $5 because of the high Earnings Power Value of the business. Once I have paid that premium, I own the business and the greater returns will allow me to grow with less investment in fixed assets. **I don't have to keep paying the premium over tangible net assets.** *(WEB explained this in his 1989 annual report).*

$$
\text{Current Assets} - \text{Current Liabilities} = \text{Working Capital} \quad (\text{CA-CL} = \text{WC}).
$$

**投入资本：** 营运资本 + 固定资产。因此**公司1：** 营运资本=2美元 + 固定资产=2美元——共计4美元资本。ROIC=2美元/4美元=50%。税前现金收益2美元/总投资资本=2美元/4美元=50%。

<!--en-->
**Capital employed:** NWC + FA. So **Company 1:** WC = $2 + FA = 2 ---$4 in capital. ROIC = $2/$4 = 50%. $2 in cash earnings pre-tax/total investment capital = $2/$4 = 50%.

每投入1美元，该企业可赚取50美分。该企业无需大量固定资产即可实现增长。与其公司2相比，它所需的固定资产投资更少。（再投资的资本支出较少。）

<!--en-->
For every $1 invested, the business earns 50 cents. This business doesn't need a lot of Fixed Assets to grow. You would have to buy less FA to grow than Company 2. (Less capex reinvested).

**公司2：** 营运资本=2美元 + 固定资产=7美元——共计9美元资本。ROIC=2美元/9美元=22%。每投入1美元，可赚取22美分。

<!--en-->
**Company 2:** WC = 2 + FA = $7 ---$9 in capital. ROIC = $2/$9 = 22%. For every $1 invested, it earns 22 cents.

资产负债表上存在商誉，是因为此前有人支付的价格低于我。该公司属于资产密集型。

<!--en-->
There is goodwill on the balance sheet because before, someone paid less than me. Asset heavy.

会计记录的是你或他人在*过去*支付的数额。

<!--en-->
Accounting records what you or someone else paid in the *past*.

**务必查看税前回报率。** EBIT：息税前利润或营业利润。EBIT允许对不同公司进行*同类比较*，因为各公司的税率和利率各不相同。它反映了企业无论税率或利息支付情况如何所创造的收益。企业到底赚了多少钱？

<!--en-->
**Always look at pre-tax return.** EBIT: Earnings before Interest & Tax or Operating Income. EBIT allows an *apples-to-apples comparison* between companies because firms have different tax and interest rates. How much the business is earning regardless of the tax rate or interest paid or owed. How much is the business earning?

企业进行收购所需的盈利水平是多少？销售额中有多少能转化为营业利润——即最终净利润。

<!--en-->
How much is the business earning to make an acquisition? How much of a dollar of sales drop to operating earnings--the bottom-line.

EBIT/（净营运资本）+ 净固定资产，或 EBIT/投入资本。

<!--en-->
EBIT/(Net Working Capital) + Net Fixed Assets or EBIT/investment capital.

EBIT是你产生税前回报所动用的资本。

<!--en-->
EBIT is your pre-tax return/what capital that had to be employed to generate that EBIT.

营运资本 = 应收账款 - 流动负债 - 应付账款（无息贷款）。假设没有多余现金；或者先扣除多余现金，分析后再加回。你需要为这些应收账款融资，但要减去通过应付账款获得的无息贷款部分。

<!--en-->
CA -----A/R - CL -------A/P (FREe loan). Assume no excess cash or take out the excess cash and add back after your analysis. You have to finance these receivables minus the money that is lent to you FREely through A/P.

在分母中，我们采用净营运资本——即运营企业所需的资金，再加上用于购置固定资产或厂房设备的资金。忽略商誉及其他因素。在哥伦比亚大学商学院的144门特殊情境投资课程中，产生EBIT所需的资金体现在净营运资本与固定资产之和中——这就是投入资本回报率（ROIC或ROC）。即 EBIT /（净营运资本 + 固定资产），或营业利润/投入资本。

<!--en-->
On the denominator we take the Net Working Capital--what you need to run your business plus you need to finance your fixed assets or your plant and equipment. Forget goodwill and everything else.
144
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
What you need to generate EBIT is in your NWC plus Fixed Assets — Return on Invested Capital (ROIC or ROC). EBIT / (NWC + FA) or operating income/invested capital.

## 哪种业务更好？

<!--en-->
*Which is the Better Business?*

### 口香糖店

<!--en-->
*GUM STORE*

杰森花费40万美元开设一家口香糖店，这笔费用包括营运资本、存货、固定资产以及店面装修。每年他可创造20万美元的EBIT。其资本回报率（ROC）为20万美元/40万美元 = 50%。

<!--en-->
Jason opens a gum store for $400,000 which includes WC + Inventories + FA and building-out the store. Every year he makes EBIT of $200,000. He makes $200,000/$400,000 = 50% Return on capital (ROC).

### 纯西兰花店

<!--en-->
*JUST BROCCOLI*

他的朋友吉姆博开了一家名为“纯西兰花”的店铺，每家店每年仅能赚1万美元。其ROC为1万美元/40万美元 = 2.5%。

<!--en-->
Now he has a friend named Jimbo who opens a store, Just Broccoli, and he made $10,000 for each store he opens. $10,000/$400,000 = 2.5% ROC.

你会把钱给谁用于扩张？由于ROC更高，应选择支持杰森。

<!--en-->
Who would you give money to expand? Give $$ to Jason because of higher ROC.

你想知道扩张成本是多少，以及投资能带来多少回报？

<!--en-->
You want to ask how much it costs to expand and how much will you make on the investment?

要投资于ROC较高的企业。借入10%的资金以创造50%的回报——这是笔划算的交易。为简化计算，可参考税前利率。比较税前回报与税前回报即可。

<!--en-->
Be in a business earning high ROC. Borrow 10% to make 50%—that is a good deal.
Look at pretax rate to simplify. Compare pretax return to pretax return.

吉姆博的ROC仅为2.5%，而政府债券的无风险利率高达6%。他不仅没赚到2.5%，反而亏损了3.5%（6%无风险利率 - 店铺产生的2.5%回报）。这就是机会成本。

<!--en-->
Jimbo is really throwing money away earning a 2.5% ROC vs. a 6% risk FREe rate from govt. bonds. He is not earning 2.5% but losing 3.5% (6% Risk FREe Rate - 2.5% return earned from his store). Opportunity Costs.

**作为投资者，你的目标是寻找那些资本回报率较高且高于资本成本的企业。** 无论固定资产的融资方式如何，都应关注资本的使用效率。这家企业有多好？（并非基于股权衡量）如果我投入资金，能从中获得多少回报？

<!--en-->
**Your goal as an investor: you want businesses that are earning high returns on capital and returns above your cost of capital.**
Using capital regardless of how fixed assets are financed. How good a business is this (not measuring equity)? If I put in $, how much do I earn on it?

分母是净营运资本 + 固定资产——为何使用净额而非总额？总体而言，这样做是正确的。因为固定资产会随时间折旧，导致其价值下降；为维持资产状态，必须持续进行资本支出。折旧与资本支出相互抵消（假设折旧额=维护性资本支出）。若资本支出超过折旧，固定资产就会相应增加，数据也会随之更新。在扩张阶段，新店开业会导致固定资产膨胀，而在这些资产产生收益前，ROC会下降——因此必须对其进行标准化调整。我之所以使用净额，是因为固定资产减去折旧再加上维护性资本支出。

<!--en-->
Denominator is NWC + FA—why using net and not gross working capital? On average that is the right thing to do. Because in general what happens to your fixed assets, you buy something and you depreciate the assets so the value of your asset goes down, but to maintain your asset, there has to be on-going capex. Depreciation and Capex cancel out (assume Deprec = Maint. Capex). If capex is more than depreciation, then FA will increase accordingly and you will be updated. If you are in expansion mode, you build new stores and the FA balloon before you earn on those assets, so your ROC will decline—so you must normalize or adjust for that. Fixed Assets minus depreciation plus Maint. Capex is why I use a Net number.

因此我关注的是净固定资产 + 净营运资本。这是一种简便的分析方法。我们只会挑选少数投资机会；可能要考察50到100个案例才能选中一两个。剔除或评估后进一步研究。对少数标的进行深入调研。哥谭合伙公司在投资上非常挑剔。

<!--en-->
So NFA + NWC is what I look at. A quick and dirty analysis. We only buy a few situations. We may have to look at 50 to 100 situations to buy 1 or 2. Drop or evaluate to study further. Do intensive research on a few things. Gotham Partners are very selective in our investments.

**解释整体图景。** 你的前辈们（MBA）长期未能取得成功。这与他们制作电子表格的能力无关，更多在于对整体图景的理解。我专注于整体图景。

<!--en-->
**Explain the big picture.** Your predecessors (MBAs) failed over a long period of time. It has nothing to do about their ability to do a spread sheet. It has more to do with the big picture. I focus on the big picture.

**要理解逻辑，而不仅仅是公式。** 索顿·奥格洛夫最近接受了采访，他著有《盈利质量》一书。我看了书中的附注，但它们并非整体图景。不要忽视整体视角。听着，我曾忽略了整体图景。精明的人会说附注很重要，**但要思考这是否是一家好企业，以及价格是否合适。**

<!--en-->
**Think of the logic, not just the formula.**
Thorton O'Glove was recently interviewed and he wrote the book, Earnings Quality. I looked at the footnotes but they are not the big picture. Don't lose the perspective of the big picture. Listen, I lost the big picture. Savvy guys say the footnotes are important, **but think of whether it is a good business and am I getting it at a good price.**

### 达夫与菲尔普斯案例

<!--en-->
*DUFF & PHELPS Example*

EBIT/资产 = 28.4美元/44.2美元 = 64%。这有什么问题呢？扣除2170万美元的商誉后，EBIT/有形资产比率达到126%。真是惊人的回报率！

<!--en-->
The problem with EBIT/ASSETS = $28.4/$44.2 = 64%. What is wrong with that? Take out goodwill of $21.7 million. EBIT/Tangible Assets = 126%. Fantastic returns!

**需要关注的重点：**

<!--en-->
**What to Focus on:**

1. 首先，我要寻找优质企业。关注EBIT/(营运资本+固定资产)或EBIT/有形资产。这些指标反映了企业在缴税、支付利息前后的盈利水平。
2. 其次是低价买入：即EBIT/企业价值比率或我的收益收益率。这代表了我为这些税前盈利所支付的价格。比如支付100美元却能获得9美元的收益，那么收益率就是9%。
3. 盈利趋势是在增长、下降还是保持不变？我对这一点的把握有多大？我更关注未来两到三年的常态化盈利，而非短期内的种种小问题。预测两年后的EBIT——它是否会面临风险？是会增长还是萎缩？这很难判断。预测两三年后的EBIT时，你的能力圈就显得尤为重要。
4. 相对于常态化盈利而言，我支付的价格是否合理？如果9%的收益率能快速增长，那可能值得买入。如果这是一家ROIC较高的企业，那就更好了。我是否得到了好价格？我付出了多少？能否获得良好回报？
5. 如果我无法确定常态化盈利水平，那就放弃或搁置该机会。**最难的部分在于确定“常态化数值”以及该数值的变化趋势。** *回归均值现象*。如果能算出三年后的常态化EBIT，我对这一结果的把握有多大？这是否是一家优秀的特许经营型企业？我的资本回报率是多少？我对未来的信心有多强？这取决于进入壁垒、竞争优势和管理层等因素。然后我愿意为它支付多少？**我就是用这么简单的方式来思考问题的。**大多数时候我无法预测常态化盈利，但一旦能做到，我就会对这家企业充满信心。该业务领域正在扩张，新店将创造可观收益。这家企业拥有特许经营权。简化来说，只需学会先问：

<!--en-->
1. First I am looking for good businesses. EBIT/(NWC + FA) or EBIT/Tangible Assets. This is what the business is earning pre-tax or pre interest cost or benefit.
2. Then a bargain price: EBIT/EV or my earnings yield. This is what I am paying for those pre-tax earnings. $100 paid but earning $9, so the yield is 9%.
3. Is the earnings stream growing, declining or staying the same? How confident am I of this? I focus on normalizing earnings two to three years out instead of all the little problems in the near-term. Project my EBIT two years out--will it be at risk, will it be growing or shrinking? Hard stuff. Project my EBIT two or three years out. This is where your circle of competence is important.
4. How much am I paying relative to my normalized earnings? If the 9% yield is growing quickly--it could be a good buy. If it is a business with high ROIC then good. Am I getting a good price? How much am I paying? Am I getting a good return?
5. If I am unable to normalize earnings, then pass on the opportunity or set aside.
**The hard part is determining the **normalized number** and what is happening to that number.** *Regression to the mean.*
If I can figure the normalized EBIT three years out, how confident am I of that? Is this a good franchise or not. What is my ROC? How confident can I be of the future? This depends on the Barriers to Entry, competitive advantages and management, etc.
Then how much will I be paying for that?
**I look at things in that simple way.** Most of the time I can't project normalized earnings. But when I can, then I have confidence in the business. The space is growing, their new stores will be earning a lot. The business has a franchise.
Simplify

## **评估管理层：**

<!--en-->
**Assessing Management:**

关键在于：如果CEO年薪为50万美元，那么每增加1美元薪酬就扣0.5分。他们的利益点在哪里呢？*格林布拉特教授*希望管理层持有的股份能与其薪资水平相匹配。要想更换或改造管理层，除了通过代理权争夺战外，能做的并不多。

<!--en-->
The trick is that if a CEO is being paid $500,000 a year, then 1/2 million point for every $1 up. Where is their bread buttered? *Prof. Greenblatt* wants mgt. to be large stakeholders relative to their salary. To fight or change management, there is not a lot you can do except by a proxy fight.

*Duff & Phelps*的管理层在1996年花费450万美元回购股票，1997年花费1390万美元，1998年花费1670万美元。1996年净利润为900万美元，1997年为1070万美元，1998年则达到1670万美元。

Mgt. of *Duff & Phelps* spent $4.5 mm buying back stock in 1996, $13.9 mm in 1997 and $16.7 in 1998. Net Income of $9 mm in 1996, $10.7 mm in 1997 and $16.7 in 1998.

## 你能否将EBIT标准化呢？6%（美国长期债券收益率）是需要超越的基准。16.66倍的市盈率对比6%的美国债券收益率。10倍的EBIT是我的初步基准。业务是在增长还是萎缩？*Gotham Capital*投资于由3到9个标的构成的高度集中的投资组合。应持有高度集中的投资组合，只做自己感到得心应手或非常了解的事情。如何针对特殊情形等新领域调整这一框架？又该如何创造机会并拓展我们的投资范围呢？6%相当于：16.66美元/1.00美元。***Duff & Phelps*案例的意义在于该分析的简洁性以及需要考虑的不同因素。**如果你查看附注，会发现他们每年将停止支付200万美元。他们在做什么——回购股票。管理层持有公司25%的股份，因此他们是利益相关者。这家企业拥有特许经营权和进入壁垒。哥伦比亚大学商学院开设了148门特殊情形投资课程。7.8%的税后收益率（8倍市盈率）与6%的债券收益率相比，我宁愿选择持有*Duff & Phelps*。在投资生涯中很难找到如此优质的企业。事实上，我发现的另一家类似企业是穆迪公司；它在分拆上市时市盈率为20倍，收益率为5%，其盈利曾暂时受挫。**我之所以能发现这个机会，是因为我此前对该行业有过深入研究。**最终，*Fitch*以100美元的价格收购了*Duff & Phelps*。一年内我们便获得了100美元回报，股价与价值之间的差距迅速缩小。**这一领域的所有知识都是累积性的。**讲座结束。*讲义* www.sherlockinvesting.com **股本回报率与资本回报率：哪个更能衡量业绩？作者：John Price。**兄弟俩*Abe*和*Zac*各自继承了1万美元，并决定分别创办复印机业务。一年后，由*Abe*创办的*Apple*公司税后利润为4,000美元，而*Zac*创办的*Zebra*公司利润仅为3,000美元。谁才是更出色的管理者呢？为简化起见，假设年底两家公司的股本数额并未发生变化。这意味着*Apple*的股本回报率为40%，而*Zebra*为30%。显然*Abe*表现更好？真的是这样吗？事情没那么简单。创业时，*Abe*申请了一笔1万美元的长期贷款，*Zac*则申请了2,000美元的类似贷款。由于资本定义为股本加上长期债务，因此两家公司的资本额分别为2万美元和1.2万美元。计算得出*Apple*和*Zebra*的资本回报率分别为20%（=4,000美元/2万美元）和25%（=3,000美元/1.2万美元）。因此按这一管理指标衡量，**Zac的表现优于Abe。**你会选择投资谁呢？或许两者都不选。但假设那位给*Abe*和*Zac*留下资金的恩主也给了你100美元，并要求你必须将其投资于兄弟俩所拥有的公司，你会选哪家呢？大多数分析师在讨论完每股收益后，往往会转向股本回报率。对于上市公司而言，股本通常指清偿所有负债后在资产负债表上剩余的金额。作为股东，股本代表你的资金，因此了解管理层对其的运用成效至关重要。据此，分析人士认为应查看股本回报率。让我们来看看你的100美元：如果借给*Abe*，他的资本总额将变为20,100美元，他可用这笔资金继续经营。假设他能保持同样的回报率，你的100美元将产生20%的收益。**另一方面，如果借给*Zac*，你的资金将产生25%的收益。**从他的角度看，*Zac*是更出色的管理者，因为他能让每一额外投入的美元产生25%的收益，而*Abe*只能达到20%。总资本运用的回报率为25%对比20%。 归根结底，这两个比率都很重要，且能告诉你略有不同的信息。**一种理解方式是：ROE反映了一家公司利用现有资金的表现，而ROC则反映了它利用新增资本时的表现。**（在后续文章中，我会更详细地解释如何利用ROC来估算盈利增长情况。）不过，就像你必须在投资*Abe*和*Zac*之间做出选择一样，如果让我在了解ROE还是ROC之间做选择，我会选后者。正如我所说，它能让你更清楚地了解一家公司利用其利润所能取得的成果，以及其盈利可能增长的速度。当然，如果长期债务较少，那么这两个比率之间的差异就微乎其微。

How to create opportunities and expand our universe? 6% is equivalent to: $16.66/$1.00 **The point of the *Duff & Phelps* example is the simplicity of the exercise and the different things you need to think about.** If you looked at the footnotes, you see they would stop paying $2 million a year. What are they doing--buying back stock. Mgt. owned 25% of the company so they were stakeholders. The business had a franchise. There were barriers to entry. 148 Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School 7.8% after-tax yield (8 P/E) or 6% bond? I would rather own *Duff & Phelps*. Rarely will you find a business this good in your travels. In fact, the only other business I found was Moody's when it was spun off when it was selling 20 x earnings or yielding 5%. Their earnings were temporarily depressed. **I saw this opportunity because of my prior study of this industry.** Ultimately, *Fitch* took over *Duff & Phelps* at $100. In one year we got $100. The gap between price and value closed quickly. **All knowledge in this business is cumulative.** End of lecture. *Hand-Out* www.sherlockinvesting.com **Return on Equity or Return on Capital: Which is the better guide to performance? John Price.** Two brothers, *Abe* and *Zac*, both inherited $10,000 and each decided to start a photocopy business. After one year, *Apple*, the company started by *Abe*, had an after-tax profit of $4,000. The profit from *Zebra*, *Zac's* company, was only $3,000. Who was the better manager? For simplicity, suppose that at the end of the year, the equity in the companies had not changed. This means that the ROE for *Apple* was 40% while for *Zebra* it was 30%. Clearly *Abe* did better? Or did he? There is a little more to the story. When they started their companies, *Abe* took out a long-term loan of $10,000 and *Zac* took out a similar loan for $2,000. Since capital is defined as equity plus long-term debt, the capital for the two companies is calculated as $20,000 and $12,000. Calculating the return on capital for *Apple* and *Zebra* gives 20% (=$4,000/$20,000) for the first company and 25% (= $3,000/$12,000) for the second company. So for this measure of management, **Zac did better than Abe.** Who would you invest with? Perhaps neither. But suppose that the same benefactor who left money to *Abe* and *Zac*, also left you $100 with the stipulation that you had to invest in the company belonging to one or other of the brothers. Who would it be? Most analysts, once they have finished talking about earnings per share, move to return on equity. For public companies, it is usually stated along the lines that equity is what is left on the balance sheet after all the liabilities have been taken care of. As a shareholder, equity represents your money and so it makes good sense to know how well management is doing with it. To know this, the argument goes, look at return on equity. Let's have a look at your $100. If you loan it to *Abe*, then his capital is now $20,100. He now has $20,100 to use for his business. Assuming that he can continue to get the same return, he will make 20% on your $100. **On the other hand, if you loan it to *Zac*, he will make 25% on your money.** From his perspective, *Zac* is the better manager since he can generate 25% on each extra dollar whereas *Abe* can only generate 20%. 25% return vs. 20% on total capital employed. The bottom line is that both ratios are important and tell you slightly different things. **One way to think about them is that ROE indicates how well a company is doing with the money it has now, whereas ROC indicates how well it will do with further capital.** (In a later article, I will explain in more detail how to use ROC to estimate the growth of earnings.) But, just as you had to choose between investing with *Abe* or *Zac*, if I had to choose between knowing ROE or ROC, I would choose the later. As I said, it gives you a better idea of what a company can achieve with its profits and how fast its earnings are likely to grow. Of course, if LT debt is small, then there is little difference between the two ratios. *Warren Buffett* is well known for achieving an average annual return of almost 30% over the past 45 years. Books and articles about him all say that he places great reliance on ROE. In fact, I have never seen anyone mention that he uses ROC. Nevertheless, a scrutiny of The Essays of Warren Buffett and Buffett's Letters to Shareholders in the annual reports of his company, Berkshire Hathaway, convinces me that he relies primarilyon ROC. For example, in one annual report he wrote, "To evaluate (economic performance), we must know how much total capital--debt and equity--was needed to produce these earnings." When he mentions ROE, generally it is with the proviso that debt is minimal. Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School If your data source does not give you return on capital for a company, then it is easy enough to calculate it from ROE. The two basic ways that LT debt is expressed are as LT debt to equity (DTE) and as LT debt to capital DTC. (DTC is also referred to as the *capitalization ratio*.) In the first case, ROC is calculated from ROE by $\text{ROC} = \text{ROE}/(1 + \text{DTE})$, and in the second case by $\text{ROC} = \text{ROE} \times (1 - \text{DTC})$. For example, in the case of *Abe* we saw $\text{DTE} = \$10,000/\$10,000 = 1$ and $\text{ROE} = 40\%$ so that, according to the first formula, $\text{ROC} = 40\%/(1+1) = 20\%$. Similarly, $\text{DTC} = \$10,000/20,000 = 0.5$ so that by the second formula, $\text{ROC} = 40\% \times (1 - 0.5) = 20\%$. You might like to check your understanding of this by repeating the calculations with the results for *Zac's* company. If you compare ROE vis-a-vis ROC for a company like *General Motors* with that of a company like *Gillette*, you will see one of the reasons why Buffett includes the latter company in his portfolio and not the former. END

### 为何价值投资有效

<!--en-->
*Why Value Investing Works*

以下是一些证明这种投资方式为何有效的证据。我试图用人们作为真正价值投资者不得不投资的真实案例来说明。或许这能让你了解创造价值机会的人性本质与行为心理学，以及为何这种现象会永远持续下去。

<!--en-->
Some of the evidence for why does this style of investing work. I try to use real examples of the kind of things that people are forced to invest in to be true value investors. And maybe it will give you a sense of the human nature and the behavioral psychology that creates value opportunities. And why they will continue forever.

数据相当有说服力。长期以来，许多学术研究都在试图找出股市中真正有效的因素。《华尔街的制胜之道》一书测试了所有可用的指标。无论是低股价与现金流比率、账面价值比率、销售额比率，还是低企业价值/息税前利润比率，这些价值指标往往能很好地预测未来表现。这听起来似乎很荒谬，因为你会认为这些机会早就被套利消除了。

<!--en-->
The data is fairly compelling. There have been many academic studies over the course of time trying to find the best things that work in the stock market. *What works on Wall Street* is a book that tests every available metric. Value metrics, whether they are low price to CF, BV or sales or low EV/EBIT, tend to be a good predictor of future performance. That seems silly as you can get because you would think these opportunities are arbitraged away.

如果我从1960年代（45年间）到2004年进行观察，*标普500指数*年均回报率为11.5%。如果你采用某种简单的估值指标——最低的市净率五分位数——并买入最便宜的那一组股票，那么45年间你的年化回报率将达到约17%，即每年超出基准5.5%，业绩表现几乎是基准的8倍。

<!--en-->
If I were going to look from the 1960's (45 years) to 2004. The *S&P 500* performed 11.5% a year. If you took some simple metric of valuation--lowest price to book value quintile--and bought the cheapest quintile. You would make about 17% or 5.5% out-performance per year for 45 years or 8 times as better.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：这怎么可能呢？有几种解释：人们在市场中的投资行为往往符合人类特性。那么，这意味着什么？通常，他们的预测方式是简单外推趋势：好公司会继续表现优异；坏公司会继续表现糟糕；稳定状态则会保持稳定。人们通过回顾过去来预测未来（就像开车时只看后视镜一样——*沃伦·巴菲特*）。他们利用历史数据来推断未来。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
How can that be? There are a couple of explanations: The tendency of people investing in markets is to act like human beings. Well, what does that mean? Typically, this is how they forecast: they simply extrapolate trends. Good businesses continue to do well; bad businesses continue to do poorly; and stability stays stable. People forecast by looking at the past (driving while looking through the rear-view mirror—*Warren Buffett*). People use that history to extrapolate into the future.

但公司的实际行为，尤其是在极端情况下，并非如此。实际行为是**回归均值**。请注意高净资产收益率公司的衰退以及低净资产收益率公司的崛起。

<!--en-->
But the actual behavior of companies especially at extremes does not look anything like that. The actual behavior is **regression to the mean**. Note decline of high ROE companies and rise of low ROE companies.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/b61a117c881f12b51d637ce2227cec63.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=ab986280ba91c5c9358641564bcf3a612983f8e3c6e8064debab854aee4bbfec)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/b61a117c881f12b51d637ce2227cec63.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=ab986280ba91c5c9358641564bcf3a612983f8e3c6e8064debab854aee4bbfec)

如果你使用任何盈利指标，如ROIC、利润率或ROE，你会发现最佳公司最初都位于最高五分位组（基于盈利能力），我会追踪它们随时间的盈利变化。我会发现……它们的盈利能力会逐渐向均值靠拢。人们以为盈利能力会持续，因此给这些公司定下很高的市净率——比如5倍账面价值，而它们的平均净资产收益率达到30%；而最低五分位组的公司市净率可能仅为1倍，净资产收益率为2%。许多人会说，那些净资产收益率为30%的公司显然更优秀。所以花5倍账面价值购买这类公司，得到的回报是（30%/5）=6%，而另一组仅为（2%/1）=2%，因此认为净资产收益率为30%的公司更好。

<!--en-->
If you use any profitability metric like ROIC, Margins or ROE, you would find that the best companies start in the top quintile (based on profitability), and I will track their profitability over the course of time. What would I find......I would find a slow deterioration to the mean. People assume that the profitability will continue so they price these companies at very high price to book so they might be priced at 5 x book value but earning on average 30% ROE while the lowest quintile might be priced at 1 times book value with a ROE of 2%. Many people would say well these companies with the 30% ROEs are just better. So paying 5x times book for 30%. I get (30%/5) or 6% vs. (2%/1) 2% return so those companies (30% ROE companies are better.

我们使用的数据不存在幸存者偏差，因此包含了那些破产的公司。最低五分位组中有多少公司会破产呢？仅有1%。

<!--en-->
The data we use does not have a survivorship bias so it includes the companies that go bankrupt. What percentage of the lowest quintile companies go bankrupt? Only 1 percent.

<table><thead><tr><th>长期以来的可靠统计数据</th><th>1年</th><th>5年</th><th>10年</th><th>20年</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>17%对比11.5%的超额表现</td><td>65%的概率</td><td>85%</td><td>95%</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th>A Solid Statistic over time</th><th>1 year</th><th>5 year</th><th>10 year</th><th>20 year</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>17% vs. 11.5% out-performance</td><td>65% probability</td><td>85%</td><td>95%</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table>

这是回顾过去的情况。显然，这并不能保证未来会如何，但这种现象似乎不会随时间而改变。每一代人中似乎都会出现所谓的“热门股”或“互联网泡沫”。尽管历史已经给出了数百年的教训，但仍有人会制造出令人难以置信的估值差异。为什么呢？

<!--en-->
That is looking back over time. Obviously that doesn't guarantee what the future will be, but it doesn't seem to change with time. With every generation there seems to be a *Nifty Fifty*, the *Internet Bubble*. There is something that gives rise to unbelievable valuation spreads, despite the lessons of history for 100s of years. Why?

你读过《新时代》系列书籍吗？其中一本书提到，传统的供需法则已被废除：供给越多，价值反而越高。供给增加会导致价格下降，但价值却上升。人们当时就是读着这类书并深信不疑。现在回过头看，真让人疑惑他们当时在想什么？

<!--en-->
Have you read books from the *New Era*? One book said that the historical rules of supply demand had been repealed. The greater the supply, the higher the value. The greater the supply, the lower the price but the higher the value. Those were the books that people were reading and believing. You look back on that and say what were they thinking?

如今我们几乎又走向了另一个极端：人们开始追捧那些明显属于劣质行业的商品类企业，这些企业数十年来投资回报率一直很差。如今唯一受重视的，就是对钢铁、石油或木材等实物资产的持有。

<!--en-->
Today we have gone almost back to the other extreme. Today people are looking at commodity businesses that are clearly bad businesses with decades of history of lousy returns on investment. The only thing today that counts is physical possession of steel, oil or lumber.

选择价值投资策略的成功几率更高，因为**你是在更好的“赛场”上竞争**。所以即便我水平一般，也能跑赢市场。

<!--en-->
You have better odds in the value camp, because **you are playing in a better field**. So if I was mediocre, I would beat the market.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/a0510776ea5c7597819ef0592865fcda.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2c9bcdcafd306fc36a81057019f78d61c9f793544c813a274555bd0a29447379)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/a0510776ea5c7597819ef0592865fcda.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2c9bcdcafd306fc36a81057019f78d61c9f793544c813a274555bd0a29447379)

哥伦比亚大学商学院开设的151门特殊情境投资课程：**但要成为卓越者，必须能够区分**——最低五分位数的数据表明，这些公司正面临问题；有些是暂时性问题。**创造价值的途径就在于区分暂时性与永久性难题。**通过避开高负债公司，就能避免破产风险。

<!--en-->
151
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
**But to be great one must distinguish**--what this tells you (lowest quintile) is that those companies are experiencing problems; some are experiencing temporary problems. **The way you can add value is to distinguish between temporary and permanent problems.** You can avoid the bankruptcy issue by avoiding the companies with debt.

不过，那17%的回报中有一部分来自承担破产风险。有多少基金经理能宣称自己40年间年均回报达到17%？40年后，按17%计算的资产规模将比按11.5%计算的资产规模多出8倍之多。

<!--en-->
But some of the 17% return comes from taking that bankruptcy risk. How many managers can claim for 40 years to have returned 17%? You would have 8 times as much money returning 17% vs. 11.5% after 40 years.

### 周期性股票分析

<!--en-->
*Analyzing Cyclical Stocks*

**学生**：如何对周期性股票进行估值？房地产类股票的市净率较低，但净资产收益率却很高。这算是两全其美吗？

<!--en-->
**Student:** How to value cyclical stocks? Housing Stocks have low price books with high ROE's. Is that the best of both worlds?

**Pzena**：我认为那些房地产股票*根本无法维持这种盈利能力*，这会让我感到担忧。如果你相信房屋建筑商的故事——即所有小型企业都退出市场、行业正在整合——那么这些盈利或许可以持续。这是一种可能的解释。

<!--en-->
**Pzena:** I would believe that those housing stocks have *no chance of maintaining that profitability*. That would scare me. If you bought into the home builder story--all the mom and pops are out of businesses and the industry is consolidating--those earnings will be sustainable. One possible explanation.

对于高度周期性的公司而言，其利润率波动剧烈——需求会出现繁荣与萧条交替的现象。以钢铁为例：价格从每吨200美元涨至600美元，于是人们便声称这是一个“新世界”。中国需求巨大，会导致原材料短缺。这种说法完全忽视了人类千百年来的行为模式。人们会大量兴建钢铁厂，却忽视了供给端的问题。决定价格的是供给量（以及新建工厂的数量）。一旦供给增加，规模会非常庞大，从而导致供给的突然变化。

<!--en-->
Any problem with highly cyclical companies with a profit margin swing--you get booms and busts in demand--let's use steel--the price goes from $200 a ton to $600 ton and now you hear it is a "new" world. China had huge demand, there will be shortages of material. It ignores 1000 years of human behavior. You build a lot of steel plants. You can't ignore the supply side issue. What sets the price is the amount of supply (and the number of plants built). When supply comes on, it comes on in huge amounts. There is a sudden shift in supply.

电力市场也曾出现供给问题：*Calpine*公司的净资产收益率极高，但由于环境问题，新电厂根本无法建成。因此*Calpine*的估值达到了电厂重置成本的两倍。该公司拥有价值10亿美元的电厂，但估值却是其两倍。那么*Calpine*的商业策略该是什么？一年内他们的供给量就增加了20%。由于供给端会对高价做出反应，因此很难出现持续的商品价格高峰。*供需法则永恒不变*。房屋建筑商的股本回报率历来较差，如今却突然表现出惊人的盈利能力。

<!--en-->
The electricity market had a supply problem: *Calpine* had huge (high) ROEs, power plants will never be built due to environmental issues. So *Calpine* gets valued at 2 times the replacement costs of a power plant. So they have $1 billion in power plants but they are valued at 2 times. So what should *Calpine*'s business strategy be? In one year they added 20% to supply. It is rare to find a sustained commodity peak because the supply side--the increase in supply in response to high prices. *The law of supply & demand is immutable.*
Home builders have a history of poor returns on equity and now all of a sudden they are having spectacular returns on equity.

上周我拜访了一家房屋建筑商。他们告诉我，2004年建造了37,000套住房，而2006年的计划是建造60,000套。他们已经购入了全部土地和基础设施。当被问及经济衰退时怎么办，他们的回答是无需担心，因为受影响的只是小企业。当被问及地区负责人会如何应对时，他称会迅速降价并清仓。别担心，他们会把压力转嫁给承包商。

<!--en-->
Last week I visited a home-builder. What I heard was in 2004 they built 37,000 homes and their plan for 2006 is to build 60,000 homes. They acquired all the land and infrastructure. When you ask, what about a downturn? Their response is that you do not have to worry about a downturn because the little guy will suffer. When you ask the regional guy what he will do, he says that you cut the prices quickly and move the inventory. Don't worry we will take it out on the contractors.

**价格周期的全部意义就在于改变行为。**市场无法消化新增供给。不仅他们如此，所有竞争对手都会采取同样的策略。周期终将逆转，但我不知道具体时间——可能是明年，也可能是后年，但*必然会发生*。

<!--en-->
**The whole purpose of price cycles is to change behavior.** The market can't absorb the new supply. It is not just them, but all their competitors who replicate the same strategy. It will happen (the cycle turns) but I don't know when it will happen--next year or the following year, but it *will* happen.

我并非说价格高峰不能持续一段时间，但此类投资无异于玩火。这属于动量投资。我会利用这个泡沫，在市场转向前退出。我可以给你提供统计数据证明动量投资确实有效。今天的表现与明天之间存在*序列相关性*：如果今天的盈利良好，那么明天盈利良好的概率高达80%。

<!--en-->
I am not saying that the peak can't go on for awhile, but you are playing with fire in that kind of investment. This is momentum investing. I am going to ride this bubble and get out before the market turns. I can show you statistical evidence that momentum investing works. There is a *serial correlation* between what happens today vs. what happens tomorrow. If today's earnings are good, then there is an 80% chance that tomorrow's earnings will be good.

当市场转向时，其变化会非常剧烈。那些追逐动量效应的投资者每天都会打电话给房屋建筑商，询问有多少人看过房源。

<!--en-->
When the market turns, it turns violently. The people playing momentum are spending every day on the phone with the homebuilders asking how many people looked at homes.

虽然我确实认为价值投资和动量投资是合理的策略——但我对成长型投资实在难以理解。

<!--en-->
While I do believe value and momentum investing are sensible strategies--I have a lot of trouble understanding growth investing.

如果我随机购买增长率最高的股票，我一定会亏损。增长率越高，回报反而越低——为什么呢？**因为所有人看到的情况都一样。**事实上，如果我用之前的图表，把回报率换成增长率，结果会完全相反：增长率越高，回报越低。为什么？

<!--en-->
If I randomly buy the highest growth stocks, I will lose. The higher the growth rate, the lower the returns--why? **Because everyone sees the same thing.** In fact, if I did the same graph as before substituting growth rate for returns, I would get exactly the opposite--the higher the growth rate, the lower the returns. Why?

哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资课程”：所有人看到的情况都相同，因此他们会支付高价。但这种增长持续下去的可能性有多大呢？如果你研究市值达十亿美元左右的1200家公司，根据历史分析，其中能连续十年保持15%增长率的公司还不到5%。**要实现连续十年15%的增长率真的极其困难。**人们在投资成长股时，往往将市盈率与增长率作比较，仿佛这些增长率会永远持续下去、永不改变。因此，当你试图评估思科公司的估值时，现实是思科的增长速度并未如市场所期望的那样快。投资者们必须相信这家盈利仅10亿美元的公司能创造500亿美元的估值；他们必须相信这10亿美元利润还会大幅增长。然而，这种赌注对你极为不利，尝试下这种赌注似乎并不合理。这就是其根本逻辑。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Everyone sees the same thing, so they pay a high price. But what are the odds of such growth continuing? If you were to study companies with a billion dollars of market cap, about 1200 of them, what percentage of those companies have sustained 15% growth rate for ten years based on historical analysis--less than five (5) percent. **It is really, really hard to have growth rates of 15% for ten (10) years.**
People, when they do growth stock investing, are comparing P/E to growth rates as if those growth rates would continue forever, as if the growth rate will never change. So when you try to understand the valuation of *Cisco*, the reality is that *Cisco* stopped growing as fast as the market hoped. They (investors) had to believe to put a 500 billion valuation on a company that was earning $1billion. They had to believe that $1 billion will grow a lot. Yet, the odds are so heavily stacked against you in that kind of a bet, it doesn't seem reasonable to try to make that bet. That's the fundamental underpinning.

让我们实际看看那些市净率较低的上市公司吧。

<!--en-->
Let us actually take a look at companies trading at low price to book.

They are doing it using options, but they are giving a lot of the economics away to the land-owners. They will do fine as long as they are bailed out by rising prices.

它们在计算经济效益时假设房价不会上涨，且只承接回报率在20%以上的项目。**Pzena**问该公司：“按这个标准，你们长期表现会如何？”对方回答：“如果没有房价上涨带来的支撑，我们连一个开发项目都做不成。”我相信这话，因为20%的回报率实在高得离谱。它们无法达到预期数字的原因是房地产开发难度大，且进度常常延误。因此当房价上涨时，它们就能获得意外之财。

The reason they don't make their numbers is because developing properties is difficult and they don't happen on the time schedule they expect. So when housing prices are rising, they have windfall profits.

## 搜索条件

<!--en-->
*SEARCH CRITERIA*

我看重三点：

<!--en-->
I look for three things:

1. 估值低廉
2. 业务状况良好，因此*理应*能产生不错的资本回报。
3. *当前*盈利低于正常水平。当你面对*高于正常水平*的盈利时——显然你需要判断何为“正常”盈利——就连普尔特这样的房屋建筑商也称其利润率高于正常水平。当前的房价环境并非常态。因此我会等待相反的情况出现，这样你不仅能从估值优势中获利，还能从盈利的改善中获益。即便估值便宜，跟随盈利的上升趋势也比跟随盈利的下滑趋势要好得多。

<!--en-->
1. Low valuation
2. The business is good so it *should* earn a decent return on invested capital
3. The *current* earnings are below normal.
When you are playing around with earnings **above normal**--and obviously you have to make some judgment about what "normal" earnings are--even the *Pulte's* (homebuilders) of the world say their margins are above normal. This is not a normal environment for housing prices. So I would wait for the opposite, then you win not only from valuation but a positive change in earnings. It is much better to be riding a positive wave in earnings vs. a negative wave in earnings even if the valuation is cheap.

What do we have on low price to book stocks?

**学生：** 我们很多人上过冯·穆夫林的课，他的选股标准是高净资产收益率股票以及低市净率或低市盈率股票。您对这一策略有何看法？

<!--en-->
**Student:** A lot of us had Von Mueffling's class and his criteria are high ROE stocks and low price to book value or low P/E. What are your comments for that strategy?

**普泽纳：** 我需要对（冯·穆夫林的策略）加以限定：当前的净资产收益率并非正确的或“正常化”的净资产收益率。如果能买到低市盈率且高正常化净资产收益率的股票，那确实不错——我也想这么做。**若以当前的高净资产收益率为指标，往往会选中处于周期性高峰期的股票。**此时盈利高于趋势水平，导致市盈率偏低且净资产收益率偏高；你会在周期性高峰期买入各类大宗商品或制造业股票（就像现在一样）。要小心那些盲目的筛选结果。

<!--en-->
**Pzena:** I would qualify it (Von Mueffling's strategy) and say that the current ROE is not the correct or "normalized" ROE. If I can buy low P/E and high normalized ROE, that combination is good. I would want to do that too. **When you do current high ROE as a metric, you will tend to pick everything at a cyclical peak.** The earnings are above trend so the P/E is low and has a high ROE. You will be buying every commodity or manufacturer (like today) at its cyclical peak. Be careful of blind screens.

你必须相信这些盈利是不可持续的，因此不应将其纳入当前的市盈率计算中。

**我们不会投资那些我们无法理解其运作逻辑的行业，比如时尚行业中的锐步公司。**我们致电该公司询问，发现问题在于门店内的时尚款式不当，明年才会改善——他们确实做到了，但我们仍无法理解其中的逻辑。

我不依据市净率来投资，只是告诉你这种方法确实有效。它确实是个简单实用的工具。**我使用的是经正常化处理的盈利数据。**我希望在分析出错时能有某种下行保护；这种保护未必体现为资产，也可能是公司的特许经营权或业务基础。我并不拘泥于市净率方法——否则会错失许多潜在机会。

I don't invest using price to book. I am just telling you that it works. OK. It is a nice simple thing to use. **I use price to normalized earnings.** I want some downside protection in case I am wrong in my analysis. That may not be assets, it may be the company's franchise or base of business. I am not wedded to P/B methodology. We miss many potential opportunities.

**学生：** 您如何定义“正常化”盈利？

<!--en-->
**Student:** How do you define "normalized" earnings?

**普泽纳：** 我所说的“正常”是指考虑到行业结构、竞争优势与劣势以及管理层能力后，企业应有的盈利水平——这是一种判断，但很大程度上基于历史数据。历史通常是预测企业盈利能力的良好指南，尤其是长期历史数据。

<!--en-->
**Pzena:** I define normal as what should the business earn given the industry structure, given the competitive strengths and weaknesses, given the management--it is a judgment but is highly a function of history. History is usually a good guide of what the business is capable of earning--especially if you take a long history.

我会查看五年内的净资产收益率数据；如果表现良好，或者该公司在竞争性极强的行业中却连续五年盈利出色，我会认为这只是运气而非行业结构带来的回报。

<!--en-->
I would look at five years of history of ROEs and if it looks good, or if I looked at the company/business and it is in an incredibly competitive business/industry, and I think they got lucky for five years. This is why I think it was luck and not returns based on the structure of the industry.
