## 描述：

<!--en-->
*Description:*

*NVR*是一家房屋建筑商。其独特的运营模式（下文将有详细说明）使其能在行业中承担最小的风险，同时创造最高的回报。

<!--en-->
*NVR* is a homebuilder. Their operating model, which is unique (and which is described later), allows them to assume the least risk in the industry and produce returns that are the largest.

房屋建筑商通常被忽视，因为它们具有周期性且对利率敏感（其实哪个行业不是呢？），经济衰退时必然导致大量未售出的房产积压——无杠杆的建筑商因此面临巨额存货减值，而有杠杆的建筑商则会破产。然而，*NVR*的模式能使其避免同样的命运；事实上，在经济衰退中*NVR*反而会因较弱的建筑商陷入困境而获益。

<!--en-->
Homebuilders are generally dismissed because they're cyclical and interest-rate sensitive (really, though, which industry isn't?) and downturns inevitably leave homebuilders holding large inventories of unsold properties -- the unlevered builders then suffer large inventory write downs while the levered builders go into bankruptcy. However, *NVR*'s model will prevent it from suffering the same fate and, indeed, *NVR* will prosper in a downturn at the expense of the weaker builders.

其运营模式有两个最重要的特点：

<!--en-->
Two of the most important facets to its operating model are:

(1) *NVR*通过期权合约来控制土地库存。这些合约赋予*NVR*从开发商处购买已完工地块的权利。*NVR*借助这些期权确保房屋建造所需的土地供应，而其他建筑商则直接购买土地并进行开发。通过避开这种投机性的购地/开发行为，转而使用期权，*NVR*能够用较少的资金控制市场上多年所需的大片土地。这种方式较低的资本需求意味着更低的存货风险和更高的资本回报率。

<!--en-->
(1) *NVR* acquires control of land inventory through options contracts. These contracts give *NVR* the right to buy finished lots from developers. *NVR* secures a supply of land for its homebuilding operations through the use of these options whereas other homebuilders purchase land outright and engage in land development. By avoiding that speculative practice of land purchase/development, and instead using options, *NVR* is able to control large blocks of land (years' worth) in its markets while employing less capital to do so. The lower capital requirements of this method translate into lower inventory risk and greater returns on capital.

(2) *NVR*几乎将所有房屋预先售出。其他建筑商通常会进行一些投机性建设，而*NVR*不会。在开工前，必须先接受订单并支付定金。这种做法降低了风险及营运资金需求，从而进一步提升了资本回报率。

<!--en-->
(2) *NVR* pre-sells nearly all of its homes. Other homebuilders typically participate in some speculative construction. *NVR* does not. Before *NVR* begins construction, an order must be placed and a deposit made. This practice reduces risk and working capital requirements, which further enhance returns on capital.

除了*NVR*的卓越模式外，还需考虑以下几点：  
-- **估值较低：** *NVR*的滚动市盈率仅为8.6倍（2001年预期每股收益为7.1倍），TEV/EBITDA比率为4.7倍（滚动数据）。TEV/(EBITDA-资本支出)比率为4.8倍（滚动数据），而TEV/自由现金流比率为7.8倍（滚动数据）。我将自由现金流定义为净利润加折旧与摊销再减去资本支出。  
-- **订单积压：** *NVR*有5,765套已订购房屋的订单积压，这些房屋可带来14.9亿美元的收入。作为参考，这相当于近三个财季的营收。此外，积压订单的房屋毛利率也高于历史水平。这一切应会转化为更高的每股收益。（管理层称2001年每股收益将略低于20美元。在该公司提供业绩指引的短暂历史中——此前他们拒绝这么做——其预测始终过于保守。第一季度业绩和订单积压表明20美元的每股收益预期仍然成立。）  
-- **高ROIC：** 由于其业务模式下的资本支出较低（过去12个月住宅建筑业务EBITDA达3.01亿美元，而同期合并资本支出仅500万美元），且营运资金需求少，*NVR*能够产生优异的资本回报率：2000年达到45.3%，五年平均ROIC为25%。补充事实：2000年*NVR*售出的房屋价值比1999年多出3.25亿美元，但存货（住宅建筑商最主要的营运资金需求项）仅增加了1,100万美元。  
-- **对多余资金的明智配置：** 高资本回报率和过剩现金流只有在管理层能明智地运用时才有价值。在*NVR*案例中，管理层选择将资金用于回购自家股票。从1993年12月31日至2000年12月31日，该公司共回购1,350万股股票；2001年第一季度又购入了85万股。作为参考，目前流通股仅有810万股（此处用流通股说明，但计算企业价值时我使用稀释后股份数）。

<!--en-->
In addition to *NVR*'s superior model, consider the following:
-- **Low valuation:** *NVR* trades at a P/E of 8.6x trailing (7.1x 2001E EPS) and a TEV / EBITDA of 4.7x (trailing). TEV / (EBITDA - Capex) is 4.8x (trailing). TEV / FCF is 7.8x (trailing). I am defining FCF as Net income plus D&A minus Capex.
-- **Backlog:** *NVR* has a backlog of 5,765 ordered homes. These homes represent $1.49 billion of revenue. To put this into perspective, this is nearly three fiscal quarters of revenue. In addition, the homes in backlog carry higher gross margins than the ones in the historical results. All of this should translate into higher EPS. (Management says 2001 EPS should be just under $20 per share. In the short history that the company has provided guidance (previously they refused to) they have consistently been ridiculousy conservative. Their 1Q results and the backlog indicate to me that the $20 EPS estimate continues to be the case).
-- **High ROIC:** The low capex nature of its business ($301 mil LTM homebuilding EBITDA versus consolidated LTM Capex of $5 mil) and the low working capital requirements of its model allow *NVR* to produce superior returns on invested capital: 45.3% in 2000, and 5-year average ROIC of 25%. Bonus fact: In 2000, *NVR* sold $325 mil more homes than it did in 1999, yet inventory (the bulk of a homebuilder's working capital requirement) increased only $11 million.
-- **Intelligent allocation of excess capital:** High returns on capital and excess cash flows are only useful if you have a management that is smart about deploying it. In *NVR*'s case, management has chosen thus far to deploy that capital to buy back its own stock. Between 12/31/93 and 12/31/00 the company reacquired 13.5 mil shares. In the first quarter of 2001, *NVR* purchased another 0.85 mil shares. For perspective, there are only 8.1 mil primary shares out today (I'm using primary shares to illustrate this but I use diluted shares for enterprise value calculations).

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**-- 住房是基本必需品：** 人们永远需要住房来居住。建房流程几十年来并未发生实质性变化。无论在未来一年、五年甚至二十年，这两点都不太可能改变。因此技术风险或产品过时风险极低。

<!--en-->
**-- Homes a basic necessity:** People will always need homes to live in. The process of building a home has not changed materially in decades. Neither of these statements is likely to change in the next year, the next 5 years, or even the next 20 years. There is minimal technological or obsolescence risk.

**-- 在市场占据主导地位：** *NVR*在18个地理市场开展业务，其中10个市场位居第一。在其余8个市场中，它通常排名第二或第三（至少位列前五）。其余市场是*NVR*近期才进入、未来有望主导的领域。

<!--en-->
**-- Dominant in its markets:** *NVR* competes in 18 geographic markets. It is the #1 player in 10 of them. As for the remaining 8, it is usually #2 or #3 (always at least in the top 5). The rest are markets that *NVR* has just recently entered and will dominate with time.

**-- 税收因素：** 该行业间接受益于政府以抵押贷款利息抵税形式提供的补贴。此外，近年来购房者无需对房屋出售所得的前50万美元资本利得征税。这降低了消费者的实际购房成本，提升了住房作为投资的吸引力，进而略微刺激对*NVR*产品的需求。

<!--en-->
**-- Tax factors:** The industry has indirectly enjoyed the benefits of a government subsidy in the form of tax deductible mortgage interest. Additionally, in the last few years, homebuyers no longer have to pay tax on the first $500k of capital gains on a home. This lowers the effective purchase price of a home for a consumer, increases the relative attractiveness of a home as an investment, and adds a little boost to demand for *NVR*'s product.

若考虑到*NVR*是在未进行土地开发的情况下取得这些成果，其利润和市场主导地位就更令人惊叹。尽管其他住宅建筑商能在通胀环境下通过投机性开发获得更高的毛利率，但*NVR*的利润率仍优于竞争对手。

<!--en-->
*NVR*'s profits and market dominance are all the more amazing when you remember that the results have been achieved without land development. *NVR* has margins better than its competitors despite the fact that other homebuilders benefit from the gross margin boost of speculative development in an inflationary environment.

## **催化剂：**

<!--en-->

流通股数量较少有时会导致股价出现大幅跳空下跌。*NVR*近期25%的跌幅正是此类机会。此外，股票回购将持续推动股价上涨。回购的规模及其出色的回购记录实在不容小觑：

<!--en-->

我理解你的例子，但认为你的结论有误。我将证明：在稳定或通胀环境下，*NVR*的模式实际上产生的绝对利润低于竞争对手（作为换取更高资本回报率的代价）；但在通缩环境下，其绝对利润却优于其他建筑商。鉴于过去七年我们一直处于通胀环境，*NVR*仍能实现与采用风险更高（但在通胀环境下本质上更盈利）模式的同行相当的利润，实在令人惊叹。

<!--en-->
**To:** elan19 **From:** charlie479 **Subject:** elan
I understand your example but I think your conclusion is incorrect. I'll show that *NVR*'s model actually produces *inferior* absolute profits versus the competition in a stable or inflationary environment (as a tradeoff for better returns on capital) but produces superior absolute profits versus other builders in a deflationary environment. Given that we have been in an inflationary environment for the last 7 years or so, it is all the more amazing that *NVR* has been able to produce profits consistent with operators which are using a riskier (but, in an inflationary environment, inherently more profitable) model.

让我用一个与你所用数字略有不同的例子来说明：

<!--en-->
Let me use an example with slightly different numbers than you did:

1. *NVR* 以当前市场价值10万美元的价格购买了一块土地的两年期权。该期权费用为5,000美元，赋予其以10万美元的价格购买该土地的权利。（我认为这些数字更符合现实——平值土地期权的费用约占土地价值的5%。）
2. 房屋建筑商“RVN”以10万美元的价格购买了同一块土地。我们来看三种情景：价格上涨、价格稳定以及价格下跌。价格上涨：一年后，如果土地价格涨至11万美元，且*NVR*与*RVN*都在该土地上建房并出售，那么*RVN*在这块土地上获得的潜在利润为1万美元，而*NVR*的潜在利润则为5,000美元。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程指出，RVN和NVR会以相同价格将房子卖给消费者，但RVN实现的利润会更高。价格稳定：如果土地价格维持在10万美元，结果类似。RVN没有潜在利润，而*NVR*则会有5,000美元的潜在亏损。同样，RVN实现的利润会比*NVR*高出5,000美元。价格下跌：如果土地价格跌至9万美元，RVN将面临1万美元的潜在亏损，而*NVR*的亏损则被限制在5,000美元的期权费用内。*NVR*只需放弃行使期权，转而按9万美元的市场价购买该土地即可。（注：我认为你在例子中错误地暗示在这种情况下RVN的情况并不比*NVR*更糟，因为它也可以按9万美元的市场价购买土地而不产生亏损。这是不正确的。RVN已经购入了该土地——它无法重复购买。即便RVN能找到一处同样价值9万美元的相似房产，也无法改变其在第一处房产上已有1万美元潜在亏损的事实。）还有两点值得注意：
1. 在通缩环境下，买家可能对*NVR*和RVN所购的那处特定房产根本不感兴趣！买家可能想要下镇上的房产、靠近高速公路的房产，或是某种特定颜色的房产。*NVR*可以放弃对该房产的期权，然后去购买下镇上靠近高速公路且颜色为蓝色的地块。而RVN则会陷入困境：它必须等待有人来购买其房产，同时还要承担进一步降价的风险。
2. 从理论上讲，RVN也可以尝试购买下一个城镇中的那块蓝色地块来满足买家需求。不过，当RVN翻找自己的资金储备以购置第二块地块时，很可能会面临资金短缺的问题。请记住，RVN为了购买第一块存于库存中的土地已经背负了10万美元的债务；它不太可能再借到另外9万美元。（RVN或许在最初几次交易中拥有足够的现金来完成此类交易，但一旦将这些数字乘以建筑商库存中成千上万块地块的数量，就会发现债务规模将变得极为庞大。值得注意的是，目前大多数建筑商的负债都相当严重，而NVR的净债务几乎为零。）相比之下，NVR仅背负了5千美元的债务，因此具备购买土地所需的财务灵活性。

管理层表示，期权通常相当于土地价值的6%到7%。这一比例虽略高于我在示例中采用的5%，但我同意你的看法，认为它仍然相当便宜。我会设法再次确认这些价格。你提出了一个很好的后续问题：既然期权定价如此合理，为何其他建筑商不介入竞标呢？对此我有两个推测：（1）由于在经济通胀或市场上涨环境下利润空间更大，其他建筑商仍更倾向于直接购买土地而非选择期权；因此，对土地的竞争向来激烈，但对期权的竞争却未必如此。（2）住宅建筑行业存在地方性寡头垄断现象。建筑商需要在某一地区达到一定的建设和销售规模，才能通过批量采购材料、建造样板房以及雇佣销售人员等方式实现规模经济。如果某建筑商已经控制了该地区大部分土地（甚至足以使用数年），那么另一建筑商就很难获得足以支撑其销售规模的足够库存（即区域销售经济规模）。因此，即便偶尔有价格低廉/合理的期权可供获取，竞争也仅限于那些在该地区具备足够规模的现有建筑商。需要注意的是，NVR在其超过一半的市场中都是最大的建筑商，在其余市场中也位居第二或第三。你的问题值得更详尽的回答，因此我会试图征求管理层的意见，了解为何其他建筑商不积极争夺这些期权，以及开发商为何愿意以如此低价出售期权。我承认这或许正是管理层不愿与外界沟通的原因之一。另一种传言是，NVR一直热衷于回购自家股票，管理层希望以尽可能低的价格增加其相对于流通股的持股比例；但我从未完全相信这一说法（听起来太像阴谋论了）。我认为最有可能的原因是：他们只是不喜欢与外界打交道，更愿意专注于业务运营而非股票推广。

我们之前使用的示例过于简单化，忽略了资本成本因素。因此，该示例得出的结论是：如果开发商选择走NVR的期权路线，便无法获得与其资本成本或开发努力相匹配的补偿。实际上，开发商理应得到资本成本及开发努力方面的补偿。例如，对于两年后价值10万美元的一块地块，NVR如今只需支付5千美元定金；开发商或许现在就能出售这块土地，但其售价不会达到10万美元——差价部分正是开发商在持有并开发该地块期间所获得的利润。这并不会改变我们此前示例得出的结论。 在稳定或上涨的市场环境中，其他建筑商的单位产品毛利会高于*NVR*，但为此他们需要占用更多资本（且产生的回报较低）。显然，其他建筑商承担了更大的风险，这一点在价格下跌的环境中表现得尤为明显。*NVR*在经济衰退期间不会占用大量资本，其存货损失也会低于其他建筑商。当这些建筑商试图出售多余的土地时，很可能会背负巨额债务。尽管在最近的通货膨胀环境下*NVR*存在固有的毛利劣势，但近年来其毛利率仍能与其它建筑商相媲美。我重复一下之前帖子中说过的话：我认为这是其运营效率以及市场主导地位带来的结果。

<!--en-->
1. *NVR* buys a two year option on a piece of land with a current market value of $100k. The option costs $5k and entitles them to buy the land for $100k. (I believe these figures are closer to reality - it costs about 5% of land value for an at-the-money land option).
2. Homebuilder "RVN" buys the same piece of land for $100k.
Let's consider 3 scenarios: an environment of rising prices, stable prices and falling prices.
Rising prices. In one year, if the land price rises to $110k and *NVR* and *RVN* build a house on the land and sell it, *RVN* will have an embedded profit of $10k on the land whereas *NVR* will have an embedded profit of $5k.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
RVN and NVR will sell the house to the consumer at the same price, but RVN will realize a higher profit.
Stable prices. If the land price stays at $100k, the result is similar. RVN has no embedded profit, while NVR has an embedded loss of $5k. Again, RVN will realize a profit that is $5k higher than NVR's.
Falling prices. If the land price falls to $90k, RVN will have an embedded loss of $10k but NVR's loss will be limited to the $5k value of the option. NVR will simply not exercise its option and instead purchase the land at the current market price of $90k. (NOTE: I think you incorrectly imply in your example that RVN is no worse off than NVR in this case because it can also purchase the land at the current market price of $90k and incur no loss. This is not correct. RVN has already purchased the land - it cannot purchase it twice. Even if RVN finds an identical property that it can buy for $90k, it does not eliminate the fact that it has an embedded loss of $10k on the first property).
There are two additional observations that can be drawn:
1. In a deflationary environment, buyers may not at all be interested in the specific property that NVR and RVN bought! Buyers may instead want a property in the next town, or something near the highway, or something in blue. NVR will be able to respond by walking away from their option on the property and then buying the lot in the next town near the highway with the color blue. RVN will be stuck. It will have to wait for a buyer to show up for its property, risking further price decreases in the meantime.
2. Theoretically, RVN could also try to buy the blue property in the next town to satisfy the buyer. However, RVN will likely face capital constraints when it looks in its piggy bank for funds to buy the second property. Remember, RVN has already incurred $100k of debt to buy the first piece of land that it holds in inventory. It's unlikely they'll be able to borrow another $90k. (RVN may have enough cash to do this the first dozen times, but multiply these figures by the thousands of lots that builders have in inventory to see why the debt amounts would be too large. Note that most builders currently have significant debt. NVR has almost zero net debt). NVR, meanwhile, has only incurred $5k of debt, so it has the financial flexibility to purchase the land.

To: elan19 From: charlie479 Subject: elan
Management has said that options are typically 6% to 7% of land value. This is not quite as cheap as the 5% I used in my example, but I agree with you that it's still fairly cheap. I will try to confirm these prices again.
You raise a good follow-up question: if the options are so reasonably priced, why don't the other builders go in and bid on them? I have two theories on this: (1) The other builders still prefer outright land purchases instead of options because of the greater profit potential in an inflationary or rising environment. Therefore, competition for land is always intense, but not necessarily for options. (2) There are local oligopolies in the homebuilding industry. Builders need a certain threshold level of construction and sales activity in an area to reach economies of scale for purchasing materials, showcasing model homes, having sales agents, etc. If there is a builder that already controls most of the land in a locality (years' worth, even), it is difficult for another builder to get enough inventory to support a critical level of sales (regional economy of sales). Therefore, even if there are options here and there to acquire at cheap/reasonable prices, competition for them is limited to existing builders in the area with enough scale. Note that NVR is the largest builder in over half its markets, and is number 2 or 3 in almost all the rest.
Your question deserves a more thorough answer, so I will attempt to get management's opinion about why other builders don't compete vigorously for these options, and what motivates developers to sell options at such prices.
I agree that this could be one reason management does not like to communicate with the street. The other rumored reason is that NVR has been an eager acquirer of its stock and management is interested in increasing its stake relative to the public float at the cheapest price possible. I've never quite believed this (sounds too much like a conspiracy theory). I think the most likely answer is they just don't like the Street and prefer to focus on the operating the business than promoting the stock.

**To:** charlie479 **From:** charlie479 **Subject:** follow up for elan
The example we were using was a little too simplified and ignored cost of capital. Therefore, the example produced a result that showed the developer was not being compensated for his cost of capital (or his development efforts) if he went down *NVR*'s option path.
In reality, the developer would be compensated for cost of capital and their development efforts. For example, for a lot worth $100k in 2 years that *NVR* would pay a $5k deposit for today, a developer might be able to sell that same land now but they wouldn't get $100k for it. The sale price would be something lower -- with the difference being the profit that the developer gets in return for holding and developing the property over that time period.
This does not alter the conclusions of our previous example. Other builders will enjoy higher embedded gross profits per unit than *NVR* in a stable to rising environment but they will tie up more capital (and produce lower returns) to do so. Obviously, the other builders assume more risk and it shows up in the falling price environment. *NVR* will not have large amounts of capital tied up in a recession and its losses on inventory will be lower than the other builders. The other builders will likely be left with large amounts of debt while they try to liquidate excess land.
Despite this inherent gross profit disadvantage in the recent inflationary environment, *NVR* has in recent years been able to generate gross margins that compare favorably to other builders. I am repeating what I've already said in previous posts but I believe this is a result of their operational efficiency and dominant position in its markets.

which companies in the space do you feel are most overvalued? - is there a paired trade opportunity that makes sense?
I generally **discourage a paired trade in this industry.** This is not because I disagree with your assessment that most of the companies in the sector are bad businesses, but because many of these companies already trade for extremely low P/Es. The potential downside of shorting something with a low P/E (even in a paired trade) can be massive.
That said, if you insist on shorting something as part of a pair, I'd do a simple screen and pick out the most **leveraged lenders.** These are the ones run by aggressive management who have been unable to resist accumulating inventory. Centex pops up at the top my screen.

## 描述：

<!--en-->
*Description:*

NII Holdings的前身是Nextel International，这是我一年多来发现值得分享的首个投资标的。

<!--en-->
NII Holdings, which was formerly named Nextel International, is the first investment idea in over a year that I have found worth posting.

NII Holdings于1996年作为Nextel Communications（NXTL）的全资子公司成立，负责持有NXTL所有的国际无线资产。1996年至2002年间，NXTL向NII投资超过5亿美元，债券持有人又额外投入20亿美元用于建设NII的无线网络。

<!--en-->
NII Holdings was incorporated in 1996 as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Nextel Communications (NXTL) to hold all of NXTL's international wireless assets. Between 1996 and 2002, NXTL invested over $500 mil in NII and bondholders invested an additional $2 bil. in the company to finance the build-out of NII's wireless network.

由于背负巨额债务，该公司于2002年2月1日决定不向债券持有人支付利息，随后于2002年5月24日在特拉华州申请破产。此后数月，公司与顾问公司（Houlihan Lokey和Bingham Dana）共同与债权人协商重组计划；2002年11月12日，NII Holdings在破产保护程序结束后以大幅去杠杆的资本结构重新运营。

<!--en-->
Struggling under the weight of its massive debt load, the company decided not to pay a coupon due to bondholders on February 1, 2002 and the company then filed for bankruptcy in Delaware on May 24, 2002. In the ensuing months, the company and its advisors (Houlihan Lokey and Bingham Dana) worked with creditors on a plan of reorganization and on November 12, 2002, NII Holdings emerged from Chapter 11 with a substantially de-leveraged capital structure.

以下是当前投资该公司的核心理由：

<!--en-->
The following are the main arguments for investing in the company now:

1. **研究不足、被忽视的股票**——刚从破产中复苏的NII股票几天前开始在OTC公告板交易。目前没有分析师跟踪该股情况，许多财务细节隐藏在百余页的披露文件和计划文档中。
2. **估值低廉**——该公司的企业价值仅为当前年化EBITDA的2.8倍。由于公开文件中的信息不易解读，我会在后续文章中详述具体数据。
3. **频谱使用权**——频谱使用权如同有线电视特许经营权或广播无线电许可权一样，是企业的“护城河”。NII拥有巴西、墨西哥、阿根廷和秘鲁地区800 MHz频段的频谱使用权。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程。
4. **差异化的无线服务**——NII提供传统无线运营商具备的所有通话功能，但还独有竞争对手无法提供的Direct Connect功能（除非进行昂贵的网络改造）。Direct Connect类似于对讲机功能，可让用户与指定通话组内的其他人即时联系。例如，现场主管可通过该功能同时向多名员工传达工作指令变更。该功能有两大优势：（1）深受许多企业用户青睐，其人均收入往往高于传统无线用户；（2）一旦用户加入通话组，便很难转向其他运营商（以上文中的员工为例，离开Nextel后他将无法接收组内消息）。事实上，所有Nextel子公司的ARPU值更高、客户流失率更低。
5. **资本结构已得到修复**——根据重组计划，24亿美元的债券被转为股权。此外，多项信贷额度得以偿还，其中一笔1亿美元规模的阿根廷贷款仅以500万美元结清。
6. **可比公司估值更高。**虽然我不推崇同类公司分析法，但值得注意的是：投资者愿意为NXTL的股权支付6.9倍于2003年EBITDA的价格，而对Nextel Partners股权则支付超过10倍的估值（NXTP）。传统无线运营商的平均估值为6.7倍。（注：我采用2003年EBITDA数据作为同行参照，而计算NII估值时则使用当前营收水平。）若NII的估值达到5倍EBITDA，其股价将达到28.10美元。
7. **未纳入估值的非核心资产**——除了在巴西、墨西哥、秘鲁和阿根廷这4个主要市场拥有的120万订阅用户外，*NII*还在智利和菲律宾拥有无线资产。后两者无法产生现金流，且*NII*正在出售其在菲律宾的股份。
8. **对Nextel Communications的战略重要性。** *NXTL*的客户可以在*NII*的国际网络上漫游。为了说明这对*NXTL*（尤其是毗邻的墨西哥地区）有多重要，*NXTL*在破产期间同意向*NII*支付5000万美元，以确保*NII*在特定地区完成网络建设。*NXTL*还对重组后的*NII*进行了额外投资。如今，*NXTL*持有*NII* 36%的普通股。

<!--en-->
1. **Under-researched, neglected equity** – Having just emerged from bankruptcy, NII's shares began trading on the OTC Bulletin Board a few days ago. There are no equity analysts following the situation. Much of the financial detail is buried in hundred-plus pages of disclosure statements and plan documents.
2. **Low valuation** – The company's enterprise value is 2.8 x current annualized EBITDA. The valuation isn't easily discerned from the public filings so I will post the details in a follow-up post.
3. **Spectrum rights** – Spectrum rights are a source of “moat” much like cable TV franchise rights orbroadcast radio license rights. *NII* owns the rights to spectrum in the 800 MHz region in Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
4. **Differentiated wireless offering** – *NII* offers all of the wireless calling features that traditional wireless operator's offer. However, *NII* offers the Direct Connect feature that its competitors do not (and cannot without expensive network overhauls). Direct Connect is a walkie-talkie-like function on Nextel phones that provides an instant connection to other users in one's designated calling group. For example, field supervisors can simultaneously convey work order changes to multiple field agents using Direct Connect.
This Direct Connect feature has two primary benefits: (1) it is a service which is preferred by many business users (such as the above field agents) which tend to generate higher average revenue per user than traditional wireless users and (2) once users get set up into a calling group, there is a natural reinforcement against switching to other carriers (the field agent that leaves Nextel in the above example would cut himself off from Direct Connect messages from others in his workgroup). Indeed, all of the Nextel companies have shown higher ARPU and lower churn rates than the traditional wireless carriers over a sustained period of time.
5. **Capital structure has been fixed** – *NII*'s plan of reorganization converted $2.4 bil of bonds into equity. In addition, several credit facilities paid down and a $100 mil Argentina facility was settled for $5 mil.
6. **Public comps trade at higher prices.** While I'm not a fan of comparable company analysis, it's worth noting that investors are willing to pay 6.9x 2003 EBITDA for *NXTL*'s equity and over 10x for Nextel Partners' equity (*NXTP*). The average of the traditional wireless carriers is 6.7x. (Note that I am using 2003 EBITDA for the peers but current run rate in calculating the multiple for *NII*). If *NII* were to trade at a 5x EBITDA multiple, the stock price would be $28.10.
7. **Non-core assets not included in valuation** – In addition to the 1.2 million subscribers it has in its 4 primary markets (Brazil, Mexico, Peru, and Argentina), *NII* owns wireless assets in Chile and the Philippines. The latter two do not contribute to cash flow and *NII* is in the process of selling its Philippine stake.
8. **Strategic importance to Nextel Communications.** *NXTL* customers are able to roam on to *NII*'s international network. As an indicator of how important this is to *NXTL* (particularly in the adjacent Mexico regions), *NXTL* agreed during the bankruptcy to pay $50 mil to *NII* to ensure the build-out of certain regions in *NII*'s territories. *NXTL* has also made an additional investment in the reorganized *NII*. *NXTL* now owns 36% of the common stock of *NII*.

研究快报——Legg Mason给予*NII Holdings*“买入”评级
芝加哥，10月3日（路透社）——Legg Mason于周五开始覆盖在拉丁美洲提供无线服务的*NII Holdings* Inc.，给予其“买入”投资评级，并设定12至18个月内的股价目标为每股82美元。分析师*Craig Mallitz*在研究报告中指出：“与每个市场仅有三四家运营商的美国无线市场相比，*NII*拥有更好的竞争态势；它既不存在无线本地号码可携性带来的风险，也无需面对一键通业务的竞争，还能将Nextel经过验证的商业模式移植到拉丁美洲。”

NII曾是Nextel Communications Inc.的子公司，主要在墨西哥、巴西和阿根廷等国面向企业客户销售无线服务。其卖点在于独特的对讲机功能，用户只需按一下按钮即可与他人即时连通，无需拨号。在纳斯达克早盘交易中，NII股价上涨3.11美元，涨幅近5%，达到65.91美元。自去年11月该公司脱离第11章破产保护以来，其股价已上涨十多倍。

RESEARCH ALERT-Legg Mason starts *NII Holdings* with 'buy' CHICAGO, Oct 3 (Reuters) - Legg Mason on Friday started coverage of *NII Holdings* Inc., which provides wireless service in Latin America, with a "buy" investment rating and a 12- to 18-month price target of $82 per share. "*NII* offers a better competitive dynamic than the U.S. wireless market with only three to four players per market, no wireless local number portability exposure or push-to-talk competition, and the ability to transfer Nextel's proven business model toLatin America," analyst *Craig Mallitz* said in a research note.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
NII, a former unit of Nextel Communications Inc., sells wireless service in countries such as Mexico, Brazil and Argentina to primarily business customers. Its selling point is a unique walkie-talkie feature that lets users connect to others instantly with the push of a button instead of dialing a number.
Shares of NII rose $3.11, or nearly 5 percent, to $65.91 in NASDAQ morning trading. The stock has risen more than ten-fold since last November, when the company emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. ## **描述：**

<!--en-->
**Description:**

*Sportsman's Guide*的未杠杆股本回报率超过35%，其交易价格相当于自由现金流的4.85倍（自由现金流定义为经营现金流减去资本支出）。

<!--en-->
*Sportsman's Guide* has an unleveraged return on equity of over 35% and trades at 4.85x free cash flow (defined as operating cash flow minus capital expenditures).

该公司是一家体育器材及其他户外用品零售商，主要通过商品目录和网站销售产品。如果您对该公司的产品不熟悉，请查看www.sportsmansguide.com并尽情选购。

<!--en-->
The company is a retailer of sporting gear and other outdoor items. It sells its products primarily through its catalogs and web site. If you are not familiar with this company's wares, please check out www.sportsmansguide.com and spend freely.

1) 该公司拥有强大的细分市场品牌。自1970年作为面向鹿猎人的产品目录创立以来，其客户群体便逐渐壮大。多年来，创始人Gary Olen将最初的目录扩展为一家企业，通过每年发行4600万份月刊目录，创造1.8亿美元的年营收。客户忠诚度的一个体现是该公司近期推出的“买家俱乐部”计划。买家俱乐部会员需支付29.99美元的年费，即可获得仅限会员购买的限量版商品目录；会员还能享受大部分商品5%-10%的折扣。截至2002年12月31日，会员人数已达31万。去年会员数增长了22%，第一季度仍保持增长势头。
2) 对于目录营销商而言，其客户姓名数据库是一项关键的竞争优势。该公司85%的营收来自数据库中现有的体育及户外爱好者客户。Sportsman's Guide的客户档案中存有520万个包含人口统计数据和购买历史的姓名记录，其中100万个姓名在过去12个月内购买过产品。随着时间的推移，公司利用响应数据将这一数据库细分为不同的客户子集；除了主要的Sportsman's目录外，这些子集还会收到不同专题的目录，如政府剩余物资、露营、射击、狩猎等。这种细分提高了响应率，从而降低了不必要的邮寄成本并提升了经济回报。自在线Sportsman's目录上线以来，数据库还补充了电子邮件列表；电子邮件数据库中约有90万个姓名，几乎所有人都会每隔1-2周收到一封群发邮件。
3) 该公司的“低价促销”策略难以被复制。其客户群体的形成部分得益于目录中一贯提供的低价商品——这些商品的价格比零售价低25%-60%。公司之所以能向客户提供如此优惠的价格，是因为其采购人员通过1200个供应商联系人网络搜寻停产、清仓或积压商品。由于积压商品的供应并不稳定，因此具备抓住时机采购并廉价储存的能力至关重要。所有存货均存放在明尼阿波利斯的Sportsman's仓库中；目录会在印刷前临时加入这些积压商品，以尽量缩短存货持有期。凭借热衷于捡漏的顾客基础，SGDE能够比其他竞争对手更快地售出这些商品。那些无法通过常规目录和网店售出的商品，则会在bargainoutfitters.com网站及公司在明尼苏达州的一家小型零售店中清仓处理。从目录所用的低档纸张到确保高配送准确率的激励机制，一切都是为了低价销售并实现稳健的资本回报。
4) 我认为SGDE的业务正在发生根本性转变，这不仅降低了公司成本，还改善了资本回报率——这就是被称为互联网的新事物。1998年以前，公司的所有业务均通过印刷目录开展，每年需分发数百万份目录，每份都涉及运费和印刷成本；此外，通过目录做生意的生产成本更高，产品上市周期也更长。公司于1998年开通网站，并于1999年2月实现了全部产品的线上展示。从1998年到2002年，网站产生的销售额分别为100万美元、1400万美元、2400万美元、3600万美元和5300万美元。公司通过在继续发行的目录中显著标注网址来推动这一转型。2002年第四季度，互联网销售额占公司总销售额的30%。这意味着什么？除了减少资本需求外，如果公司能成功将业务转向互联网，就有机会削减大量运营费用——目前目录发行成本约为每年3000万美元，其中任何一部分费用的节省都会直接转化为净利润。鉴于公司目前的自由现金流仅为830万美元，即便微小的节省也会产生巨大影响。公司寄出的目录数量已从1999年的8000万份减少到2002年的4600万份。销售及一般管理费用（包括目录成本）也持续下降：从占销售额的34.8%降至2001年的30.8%，再到2002年的29.3%。这些正是互联网对Sportsman's业务影响的初步迹象。

<!--en-->
1) The company has a strong niche brand. Its customer following has been cultivated since *Sportsman's Guide* was founded in 1970 as a catalog of products targeted at deer hunters. Over the years, founder *Gary Olen* has broadened the original catalog into a business producing $180 mil in revenue per year through a series of monthly catalogs with a distribution of 46 million per year. Indicative of the loyalty of the customers is the success of the company's recent Buyer's Club initiative. Buyer's Club members purchase a yearly membership for $29.99 to receive catalogs with limited run items available only to members. Members also receive 5%-10% discounts on most items. The number of members was 310,000 at 12/31/02. Membership grew 22% last year and has continued to grow in the 1st quarter.
2) A key competitive advantage for a catalog marketer is its database of customer names. 85% of the company's revenues come from existing names in its database of sporting and outdoor enthusiasts. *Sportsman's Guide* has 5.2 million names with demographic data and purchasing history in its customer files. Of these, 1 million names have purchased a product within the last 12 months. Over time, the company has used response data to subdivide this database into subsets of customers. These subsets receive different specialty catalogs in addition to the main *Sportsman's* catalog. The specialty catalogs have different product focuses: government surplus, camping, shooting, hunting, etc. Subdivision improves response rates which reduces unnecessary mailing costs and improves economic returns.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Ever since the launch of the online *Sportman's* catalog, the database has also been supplemented with email lists. There are approximately 900k names in the email database and nearly all of them receive a broadcast email every 1 or 2 weeks.
3) The company's "bargain" focus is hard to replicate. The company has developed a customer following partially because of its history of value-priced bargain items in its catalogs. These items are 25%-60% off retail. The company is able to offer these prices to customers because the company's buying agents comb for discontinued/liquidation/overstock items through a network of 1200 supplier contacts. Because the supply of overstock items is irregular, it's critical to have the ability to purchase opportunistically and store cheaply.
All inventory is stocked in *Sportsman's* warehouses in Minneapolis. Catalogs are customized to include these overstock items shortly before printing so the inventory carrying period is minimized. The company's customer base of bargain hunters allows *SGDE* to move these items faster than other competing retailers. What cannot be sold via its regular catalogs and online store is liquidated through its bargainoutfitters.com site and a small retail location the company has in Minnesota. Everything from the low grade paper in the company's catalogs to the incentive systems for maintaining high shipping accuracy is aimed at selling cheaply and producing a solid return on capital.
4) I believe there is a fundamental shift in *SGDE*'s business that is reducing costs in the company and improving return on capital. It's this fancy new thing called the internet.
Up until 1998, all of the company's business was done through print catalogs. Millions of these catalogs were distributed each year with each one incurring shipping and printing costs. There's also higher production costs and longer product lead time required when doing business by catalog. The company began its web site in 1998 and by February 1999 had its full product offering on the web. Sales generated through its web site have grown each year from 1998 to 2002: $1 mil, $14 mil, $24 mil, $36 mil, $53 mil. The company is encouraging this transition by prominently mentioning the web site in the catalogs it continues to distribute. In the 4Q of 2002, internet sales generated 30% of total company sales.
So what? Well, aside from the reduced capital needs, the company has a chance to take out a major portion of its operating expenses if it can successfully transition its business to the internet. Its current cost of distributing catalogs is approximately $30 mil a year. A large portion of any reduction of this $30 mil in expenses would drop to the bottom line. Considering that free cash flow is currently $8.3 mil, even a small amount of savings would produce a large effect. The company has reduced catalogs mailed from 80 million in 1999 to 46 million in 2002. SG&A (which include the catalog costs) has been falling: 34.8% of sales to 30.8% in 2001 to 29.3% in 2002. These are the initial signs of the internet's impact on *Sportsman's* business.

I've been measuring free cash flow over calendar year periods so that may produce our difference in calculations.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程  
过去三年间，我一直在参与该课程的学习：

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
For the last 3 years, I have:

$$
\begin{array}{l}
\text{Year} \\
\text{OCF} - \text{Capex} = \text{FCF}
\end{array}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{l}
2002 \quad 9.2 - 0.9 = \quad 8.3 \\
2001 \quad 13.0 - 0.5 = \quad 12.5 \\
2000 \quad 10.2 - 1.5 = \quad 8.7
\end{array}
$$

我选择将2002年的830万美元作为计算自由现金流的数值。就企业价值而言，得出的数值为4030万美元（4630万美元的市值加上490万美元的期权价值，再减去2003年3月31日的1090万美元现金）。由此得出的EV/FCF比率为4.85倍。

<!--en-->
I chose to use the 2002 $8.3 mil for free cash flow in my calculation. For enterprise value, I get $40.3 mil ($46.3 mil market cap plus $4.9 mil for options minus $10.9 mil of cash at 3/31/03). This gives me a EV/FCF multiple of 4.85x.

我觉得无论该比率是4.85倍还是5.2倍其实并不重要；无论如何它都相当便宜。自由现金流收益率达到20%左右的公司寥寥无几。

<!--en-->
I suppose it doesn't matter much whether multiple is 4.85x or 5.2x. It's pretty cheap either way. There are few companies with free cash flow yields of around 20%.

去年的税收情况较为特殊。需考虑长期税收影响，剔除异常的税收因素，并计入不同的税率。

<!--en-->
If I am looking at an acquisition for a company, I look at pre-tax returns.

支付10%的费用来借款，然后以8.5倍自由现金流或12%的收益率来获取收益。投资银行家们会说这会对盈利产生正面影响。我可不会去读那本长达50页的投资银行家报告。我只看一点：基于我所支付的成本（12%，且非常稳定）与必须支付的10%债务成本之间的对比。我以某价格购买这些资产（8.5倍自由现金流），它们会随时间产生y金额的票息。若该票息的税前收益达到11%，而借贷成本为9.5%，那么我就能通过杠杆操作来获取差额收益。但债务利率是浮动的；我买入的是票面利率11%的资产，该利率可能会下降，而我却要支付9.5%的成本，最终仅获得1.5%的微薄差额。为一家拥有数千名员工、结构复杂的公司浪费时间，实在不值得。

<!--en-->
Pay 10% to borrow and pay 8.5 times FCF or 12% yield. Investment bankers will say this will be accretive to earnings. I will not look at the 50 page investment bankers' book. I just say look, my pretax cash flow based on what I am paying (12% and very stable) vs. what I must pay 10% debt (cost of money). I buy these assets for x price (8 ½ times FCF), they will generate a coupon over time of y. That coupon pretax equals 11% and borrowing costs were 9.5%, then I can leverage up and make the spread. But the debt is a floating borrowing rate. I am buying an 11% coupon which could shrink and I am paying 9.5 percent for a tiny spread 1.5%. I am wasting my time for a company with 1000's of employees and a lot of moving parts.

你可以看到其中的杠杆效应。**但你没有任何安全边际。**简单的分析就会得出：“你在开玩笑吧？”无论他们把情况描绘得多么美好。这看似是一种简单化的世界观，但我认为这是看清事物的清晰方式。其实并不难，只不过他们总能把事情弄得看起来很复杂。

<!--en-->
You can see how you can leverage. **You get no margin of safety.** Simple analysis says, "What are you kidding" No matter how good they make it look. This may seem like a simplistic way to look at the world, but I think it is a clear way to look at the world. It is not that hard. But they can make it look really hard.

**如果你离开课堂时能记住这些简单的思路，你就已经领先于99.9%那些只会用电子表格、编写长篇报告的人了。**巴菲特说：“把它看作一张票息。”我选择从税前角度来分析：票息是在增长还是减少？你对这家企业的信心有多大？如果你无法回答这些问题，就不该涉足其中；如果能回答，那就尽力争取最好的交易条件。设定大致范围是合理的。当我提到EV/EBIT和EBIT/ROC时，我真正想确定的是：这家企业到底有多好？三四年后的正常化盈利是多少？它的ROC是30%、15%还是50%？

<!--en-->
**If you walk out of this class thinking these simple thoughts, you will be ahead of 99.9 percent of the people who know how to use the spread sheets and put together the big books.** *Buffett* says, "Look at it as a coupon." I am choosing to look at it pre-tax. Is the coupon growing or shrinking? How confident are you of the business? If you can't answer those questions, you have no business being there. And if you can, then you try to get the best deal you could. It is reasonable to have ball parks. When I say look at EV/EBIT and EBIT/ (ROC), what I really want to determine is how good a business is this? What are normalized earnings three or four years out? Is it a 30% or 15% or 50% ROC business?

我在看什么？以及我能以多低的价格买到这家企业。这里有一个关于额外ROC价值的矩阵：**你能在该企业中再投资多少以获得更高的ROC？**无论有无新增投资，能带来多少增长？我敢打赌，当巴菲特在30秒内做出决策时，他会想：“嘿，它价值约10美元，而我能以5.5美元左右的价格买到；也许它值9到11美元，但那10美元的价值会逐年增长。现在股价是7.5美元，两年后那10美元的价值将达到13美元。如何从中获取30到60美分的利润呢？”他能在脑海中迅速算出这些。如果你拥有一家优秀的企业，它必然占据特定细分市场。

<!--en-->
What am I looking at? And then how cheaply I can buy the business. There is a matrix between what extra ROC is worth. **How much you can reinvest in that business to get the ROC.** How much growth with orwithout investment. I bet when *Buffett* makes his decisions in 30 seconds, “Hey, it is worth about $10 and I can buy it for about $5.50 so maybe it worth $9 or $11, but the $10 is going to be growing over the years. It is trading at $7.50 and the $10 is going to be worth $13 two years from now. How to get a 30 to 60 cents dollar. He is doing that in his head. If you have got a good business, you have a particular niche.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程之所以简单，是因为你可以挑选自己有见解的企业来分析，这样确实会更轻松。并非因为分析1000家公司很容易，而是因为其中的差距很大。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The reason it is simple, because you can choose the ones you do have an opinion on and then it does become easier. It isn’t easy because you pick and have to analyze 1000 companies. It is a big gap.

### 美国交易所分拆

<!--en-->
*AMEX Spin off*

有什么看法吗？总体来看：该公司有两项业务：*American Financial Advisors, AFA*是一家财务顾问业务，其资本回报率并不高。或许可以探讨为何其资本回报率偏低——是经营不善？还是价值未被充分挖掘？而在*TRS*业务中，剔除AFA业务后，资本回报率可达28%至30%（AFA业务的ROE仅为11%）。

<!--en-->
Any thoughts? Big picture: they had two businesses: *American Financial Advisors, AFA*, is a financial advisory business that isn’t earning high returns on capital. There could be an argument why aren’t they earning higher returns on capital. Is the business not being run well? There are values not being realized. In the *TRS* business those will be 28% to 30% once we strip out the *AFA* business (11% ROE).

明年AFA的估值将为56美分，他给其赋予了16倍的估值倍数（好坏与否我不确定），称其价值应为9美元。由于目前股价为55美元，而分拆将在6到7个月后发生。如果我认为AFA存在投资机会，就必须等到它开始独立交易时再评估其价值。毕竟它在整体中只占很小一部分。我需要做好准备，在其上市时立即评估其价值。

<!--en-->
56 cents next year for *AFA* and he slapped a 16 multiple on it (good or bad, I don’t know) and said it is worth $9. Since the stock is trading at $55 now and it will happen in 6 or 7 months. If I think there is an opportunity in *AFA*, then I have to wait for when *AFA* starts trading. Its value is a small part of the whole. I need to be ready when it comes out to assess the value.

另一方面，我现在就可以关注那项“优质”业务——即*TRS*业务。在这种情况下，我认为现在就可以入手，因为原本需要支付的成本因素已被消除：目前股价55美元中，有46美元属于优质业务的价值。实际上，我现在就可以买入。如果当前股价为55美元，而AFA仅值9美元，那么46美元就是优质业务的价值。我无需等待分拆，现在就能分析该业务。当然，我必须先对*AXP*进行估值，才能确定购买*TRS*业务所需付出的代价，进而判断是否存在机会。这就是我建议现在入手的原因。

<!--en-->
On the other hand, I could look at the “good” business, the *TRS* business now. In this particular case, I think I can look now because the moving piece that I have to pay for now is reversed—the $55 stock has $46 in value for the good business. I can today, in effect, buy now. If the stock is $55 now and the *AFA* is only worth $9, then $46 value is with the good business. I can analyze that business now rather than wait for the spin off. Of course, I have to value *AXP* to know what I am paying for the *TRS* business to see if there is an opportunity there. This is why I would look now.

They also said in the release, last year between stock buybacks and dividends, we paid out over 87% of our earnings. They are able to grow without much reinvestment. They pledged no less than 65%. I am guessing it is over 70% to 75%. The rest they will have to reinvest back to grow at the rate they say they will. I don't know if I am right about where the $3 goes to.

以10年期债券收益率为6%为例。假设对该业务采用20倍估值，其税后收益率为5%，且每年增长率达12%至15%，同时具备高ROC（前提是我相信这一点——你们听里奇·普泽纳说过，仅有少数公司能维持十年以上的这种增长率），与我的6%机会成本相比如何呢？

<!--en-->
Take the 10 year bond yield – 6%. Let us try a 20 multiple on the business of 5% earnings after-tax yield which is growing 12% to 15% a year with high ROC (assuming I believe that—you heard Rich Pzena saying there are only a few companies which have sustained such a growth rate over 10 years) vs. my opportunity cost of 6%?

在股息折现模型中，一旦增长率超过8%，股价就会飙升。假设三年分别为12%、8%和5%的增长率。我宁愿选择5%的增长率而非6%。这从来都不是独立存在的业务。

<!--en-->
Any growth over 8% in a dividend discount model, you get prices off the charts. Take three years of 12% then 8% then 5%. I would rather have 5% growing than 6%. This has never been a business by itself.

假设采用22倍估值（针对优质业务），假设AEFA的价格为9美元，排除其他收益及分红支出，我们还能额外获得3至4美元。按22倍市盈率计算，股价有望达到80美元。

<!--en-->
Assume a 22 multiple (for a great business) and assume *AEFA* is $9 and exclude any other earnings, net of what they pay in dividends, so we collect another $3 or $4 dollars. 22 times earnings you can make a case for $80.

22乘以3美元的每股收益等于66美元，再加上AFA的9美元，合计75美元；银行产生的1美元收益以及分红后的净收益，假设再增加3美元，那么每股价值就在79至80美元之间。这意味着从这里开始的回报率可达20%。一年内就能收回9美元本金。

<!--en-->
22 x $3 EPS = $66 then + $9 for *AFA* = $75 and the earnings from the bank $1 and add earnings net of dividend payments, let's say you collect another $3 so $79 to $80 per share. That is a 20% rate of return from here. You get back your money, $9 in a year.

这就是一个投资论点的开端。我不确定这是否足够充分。但我知道很难找到如此优秀的业务。我也不敢指望股价能达到22倍估值。穆迪公司的估值曾达到30倍，但这家公司并非穆迪。

<!--en-->
That is the beginning of a thesis. I don't know if that is fat enough for me. I do know it is hard to find a business that is as good. I don't know if I should count on the stock getting to 22x. *Moody's* went to 30 times. This isn't *Moody's*.

盈利目标合理，但并非稳赚不赔。显然，这只是投资论点的开端，我以后还有机会研究其拆分出的AEFA业务。

<!--en-->
The earnings are a reasonable target, but not a safe bet. Obviously, that is the beginning of a thesis, and I will have an opportunity to look at the spin-off—*AEFA* later.

这是一家结构复杂、变量众多的企业。通常遇到这类情况我会跳过，因为有些问题无法解答，还需设定特定指标。但我不想错过AXP，因为这是一家好公司。我也会探讨期权相关情形。

<!--en-->
A complicated business with a lot of moving pieces. Most of the time I do this, I skip it because there are questions I can't answer and I need to make certain metrics. I don't want to skip *AXP* because this is a good business. I will also discuss option situations.

AEFA公布的数据为：每位客户可贡献300美元利润。250万客户乘以每位客户300美元的净利润——这对其他人来说价值几何呢？有意以5000万美元收购AEFA的公司寥寥无几。总体而言，这是个值得关注的点。<u>看看它对其他方的收购价值吧。</u>你必须支付全额对价。

<!--en-->
*AEFA* reported numbers: $300 profit per client that they have. 2.5 million Clients x $300 net income per client—what is this worth to someone else? The list of companies with $50 million to buy *AEFA* is short. Generally, that is a good thing to look at. <u>Look at the takeover value to someone else.</u> You would have to pay a full price.

AEFA可能是一家管理不善、效率较低的公司。从其管理的资产规模来看，从这个角度衡量它是否相对便宜呢？

<!--en-->
*AEFA* is a potentially poorly, under-managed firm. How much do they have under management, is it relatively cheap from that stand point.

**学生：**您给自己设定的时间框架是多久？

<!--en-->
**Student:** What kind of time frame do you give yourself?

***乔尔：***我一完成工作就会行动。市场上此类股票数量不少。我认为竞争不会太激烈，因为这并非我见过最便宜的选项。**我的原则是：我不是交易者**，所以有机会时才会建仓。我擅长评估企业价值，却不擅长交易。我从未见过靠交易为生的人。

<!--en-->
***Joel:*** As soon as I finish my work, I move. This situation has a lot of stock out there. I don't think there will be a lot of competition because it is not the cheapest thing I have ever seen. **My general rule is I am not a trader**, so I take a position if the opportunity is there. I am good at valuing businesses but not trading them. I have never met anyone who has made a living trading.

如果你能评估企业价值且纪律严明，那这就是主要策略。

<!--en-->
If you can value businesses and are very disciplined, then that is the main strategy.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特别情况投资课程：乔尔扮演巴菲特 ***乔尔将饰演沃伦·巴菲特。你们对沃伦有什么问题吗？*** 我希望找到能带来良好资本回报的企业。我需要优秀的管理层；但如果一家好企业由平庸的管理层执掌，我可能会要求更大的折价。两三年后，市场最终会做出正确定价——**企业价值会被合理评估，价格差距也会随之缩小。** 我确实有一些同事会去拜访管理层。我更侧重数字分析，但也会观察管理层长期的行为表现。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Joel as Buffett
***Joel will play Warren Buffett. Any questions you have for Warren?***
I want a business earning good returns on capital. I want good managers but if I have mediocre managers in a great business, I may ask for a bigger discount. In two or three years out, the market will eventually get it right—**value the business correctly and the price gap will close.**
I do have people that work with me who go out and visit management. I am more of a numbers guy, but I look at the actions of management over a long time period.

我总是寻找足够大的安全边际，这样即使我判断错误，仍能盈利。

<!--en-->
I am always looking for a big enough margin of safety in case I am wrong, I will still make money.

我现在持仓最大的股票（暂不透露名称）具有极高的资本回报率，且有大股东支持。他们会将盈利再投资于回购股票。我们确信他们会继续这样做。该企业拥有强大的竞争优势。我们的投资组合中会有五六只占80%仓位的股票。

<!--en-->
My biggest position now, which I will not name, gets huge ROC and has a big shareholder in it. They plow their earnings back into buying stock. We are confident that they will continue to do that. There is a moat around the business. We will have five or six things that are 80% of the portfolio.

我最初是“烟蒂股”投资者，专注于净资产值低于股价的企业。*格雷厄姆*认为，若企业售价低于其净资产值，平均而言你会获得不错收益。*伯克希尔·哈撒韦*原本是一家纺织制造商，资本回报率很低，但他以低于净资产的价格购入了它。然而，如果企业正在消耗资本，其清算价值就会下降。除非你清算企业，否则就只能困在持续贬值的劣质企业中。

<!--en-->
I started as a cigar butt investor with net/nets. *Graham* said that if the business is selling below net liquid assets, then on average you will do well. *Berkshire Hathaway* was a textile manufacturer which was earning low ROC, but he bought it below liquid assets. However, if the business is dissipating capital, then the liquidating value will decline. Unless you liquidate the business, you are stuck with a poor business that is losing value.

**这就是为什么你不应购买经济模式糟糕的企业。** 如今他宁愿花8美元买下价值10美元且能增长到12美元的企业，也不愿花6美元买下价值10美元却会跌至8美元的企业。

<!--en-->
**That is why you should not buy a business with poor economics.** He now would rather pay $8 for a business worth $10 that is growing to $12 instead of paying $6 worth $10 that is going down to $8.

## 投资组合管理

<!--en-->
*PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT*

*巴菲特*不看重贝塔系数。**风险等同于资本的永久性损失。** 我不在乎*美国运通*的股价是否下跌，只要能恢复至正常盈利水平即可。如果我们正处于盈利峰值，我才会担心能否回到正常盈利状态。

<!--en-->
*Buffett* ignores Beta. **Risk is permanent loss of capital.** I don't care if the price goes down for *AXP*, if I can get back to normalized earnings. If we are at peak earnings, then I would be worried about reaching normalized earnings.

我关注风险与回报的比例。如果我判断错误，*美国运通*股价为80美元而当前股价为55美元，那么从55美元到80美元之间仍有很大盈利空间。

<!--en-->
I look at risk/reward. If I am wrong and *AXP* is $80 and the stock is $55 now. There is a lot of room between $55 and $80 or $35 to make money.

我的持仓集中但不杠杆。走进一个城镇，买入你能找到的最佳企业。挑选五家价格合理的优质企业，每家投入20%资金。而不是像指数化投资那样把钱分散投给镇上所有企业。如果一两家企业表现不佳，但只要另外两三家表现出色，整体仍会盈利。波动性是个愚蠢的指标。如果你至少持有三到五年，结果通常会不错。

<!--en-->
I am concentrated but not leveraged. Walk into a town and buy the best businesses you can find. Pick five good business at decent prices and put 20% in each. Instead of indexing by putting money in all the businesses in town. If one or two businesses doesn't work out, but the other two or three do very well. Volatility is a stupid metric. If you have a three to five year horizon at a minimum, you will do OK.

我错过了一些大机会——从2美元涨到12美元再到0美元。我在1美元时卖出，因此只损失了一半资金。有些年份我亏损5%，另一些年份则盈利100%。**要寻找非对称性回报。** 对于*美国运通*，我以55美元买入，赌它上涨至85美元（我的持有成本为5美元），预期涨幅达30%或50%——即5美元亏损换来25美元盈利，回报比为5:1。如果我对其估值有信心且企业运营良好，那么股价的波动就无需在意。但如果你持有时限为3到5年，那情况会更好。

<!--en-->
I have missed some huge things--$2 to $12 to $0. I got out at $1.00 so I only lost half my money. Some years I lose 5% and other years I make 100%. **Look for asymmetric rewards.** With *AXP*, I am betting $0 or $5 (whatever is my cost of carry) at $55 and have expected upside of $30 or 50%--$5 down and $25 up or 5 to 1 return. If I feel confident of my valuation, and the business does well so how the business bounces around just ignore it. But if you are in a 3 to 5 year horizon then you are in good shape.

再次强调，*巴菲特*拥有巨额资本，因此他的可选范围更小。他必须长期持有资产。相比你，他的选股范围更为有限。**规模较小时，发现未被发掘机会的可能性更大。** 我最喜欢的持有期限是“永远”，但他曾表示希望自己在可口可乐价值达到峰值2.5倍时卖掉它。我可能会用80美分的东西去换50美分的东西。这种情况现在不会发生在*巴菲特*身上。

<!--en-->
Once again, *Buffett* has huge amounts of capital, so his universe is much smaller. He must hold for a long period of time. He has a more limited universe in which to pick from than you. **There are more opportunities to find the unknown when you are smaller.**
My favorite period is forever, but he did say he wished he had sold *Coke* when it was worth 2.5 times its worth. I may sell 80 cent dollars to buy 50 cent dollars. That doesn't happen to *Buffett* now.

*巴菲特*在内布拉斯加州奥马哈经营保险公司具有优势，因为他可以投资股票。如果你没有相应的资产负债表和应对波动的信心，就无法做到这一点。

<!--en-->
*Buffett* has advantages operating an insurance company in Omaha, NE because he can invest in equities. If you don't have the balance sheet and the confidence to not worry about volatility.
