## 格林布拉特课程#6

<!--en-->
*Greenblatt Class #6*

2005年3月16日 LEAPS：乔尔在贝尔斯登的期权交易日子。那时的期权市场不如现在高效。如果能创造出一种情形：借贷成本为10%，却能获得12%的收益——那就是2%的无风险价差。我当时在进行远期转换操作。+ 整个夏天我都在交易期权。

<!--en-->
March 16, 2005
LEAPS:
Joel's Option Trading Days at Bear Stearns
Options were not as efficient back then as they are now. If I could create a situation if our borrowing cost was 10% and make 12%--it was a risk-less spread at 2%. I was doing forward conversions.
+
I spent the whole summer trading options.

看待*看涨期权*的另一种方式是：它类似于持有100股股票加上一份看跌期权。（1份看跌期权对应100股股票。）看跌期权的价格按每股计算。若看跌期权价格为3.70美元，总成本则为370美元。

<!--en-->
Another way to look at a *Call* is it is similar to owning 100 shares and 1 put. 100 shares of stock and 1 put (1 put has 100 shares). The put price is expressed on a per share basis. A put price of $3.70 costs $370.

持有*看涨期权*相当于买入股票加上一份看跌期权。为什么呢？一旦我以50美元行权价买入看跌期权，股价低于50美元时我就不会亏损。我需为以50美元买入的股票支付利息成本。这与以9美元买入*看涨期权*的经济效应完全相同，唯一的区别只是利息因素。

<!--en-->
The equivalent of owning a *Call* is like buying a stock and a put. Why is that? Once I own a put at $50 strike price, I can't lose money below $50. I have to lay out $$ for the interest cost of owning the stock at $50. That is the same as owning the *Call* at $9. The economics are exactly the same other than the interest difference.

股息发放：你必须调整股息因素，因为如果你持有股票，就能获得股息；而如果你持有的是看涨期权，则无法获得股息。

<!--en-->
Dividend Issue: You have to adjust for dividends because if you own the stock you are getting dividends and if you own the *Call* you are not getting dividends.

看涨期权赋予你以50美元价格购买股票的权利，同时保证在股价低于50美元时不会蒙受损失。因此，我持有股票并买入了看跌期权。哥伦比亚大学商学院的188期特殊情境投资课程中提到：我在整个夏天于贝尔斯登公司所做的就是买入股票和看跌期权，同时卖出看涨期权——以此获利。我执行的正是“正向套利”操作。

<!--en-->
The *Call* gives you the right to own stock at $50 and the right not to lose money below $50. So here I own the stock and I bought the put.
188
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
So what I was doing all summer at *Bear Stearns* was to buy the stock and a put while selling the *Call* --and make money. I was executing *forward conversions*.

如果我以50美元买入股票，以3.70美元买入看跌期权（这等同于持有看涨期权），再以9美元的价格卖出看涨期权——这就是套利行为。

<!--en-->
If I bought the stock at $50 and the put at $3.70 (identical to owning a *Call*) and I sell the *Call* at $9--this is an *arbitrage*.

我以56.65美元买入股票，并以9.00美元的价格卖出将于1月7日到期的看涨期权。

<!--en-->
I bought the stock at $56.65 and sold a *Call* for 9.00 which will expire Jan. 07.

## 套利或正向套利

<!--en-->
*Arbitrage or Forward Conversions*

### 如果股价达到60美元或以上。

<!--en-->
If the stock is at $60 or above.

因此，整个头寸的成本为56.55美元，而60美元与56.55美元之间的差额为3.45美元；此外还需考虑将56.55美元资金占用两年的成本——两年利息为3.45美元。若用56.55美元减去9美元（看涨期权价值），则交易成本为47.55美元。现在，我持有了股票和看跌期权，同时卖出了看涨期权。当股价为60美元时，47.55美元的价值是多少呢？

<!--en-->
So whole position is $56.55 and $60 = $3.45 and I have the cost of laying out the $56.55 for two years. $3.45 in interest for two years. If I put this down $56.55 minus $9 (*Call*) = $47.55 is the cost of the trade. Now, I own a stock and I own a put and I sold a *Call*. The stock is at $60. How much is this $47.55 worth with the stock is at $60?

我投入了47.55美元，两年后将收回50美元。

<!--en-->
I laid out $47.55 and I get $50 two years later.

### 如果股价为40美元或更低。

<!--en-->
If the stock is at $40 or below.

若到期时股价为40美元会怎样呢？你将持有价值为40美元的股票，以及价值10美元的看跌期权（因为股票价格为40美元时，行权价为50美元的看跌期权可带来10美元收益）。此时看涨期权的价值为零。

<!--en-->
What happens if the stock is at $40 at expiration? Own the stock at $40 and a put that is worth $10 (put stock at $50 when the stock is trading at $40 for a difference of $10). The *Call* is worth $0.

如果股价为50美元，该交易的价值就是50美元。因为看跌期权和看涨期权均一文不值，而你持有的股票价值正好为50美元。

<!--en-->
What if the stock is at $50, the trade is worth $50. Because the put and the *Call* are worthless and I own the stock at $50.

我以47.55美元建立该交易，无论股价如何变动，都能收回50美元。差额为2.45美元，因此成本为2.45美元/47.55美元=5.2%；折算为两年的年化利率则为2.7%。这一利率恰好等于该交易期间的无风险利率。

<!--en-->
I put trade on at $47.55 I collect $50 no matter what happens to the stock price. The difference is $2.45, so the cost is $2.45/$47.55 = 5.2% and annualized over two years is 2.7%. This rate equates to the risk-free rate for the amount of time of the trade.

哎呀，如果我（贝尔斯登的交易员）能以3%的利率借款，却能获得5%的收益，那这简直是无风险获利。

<!--en-->
Gee, if I (a trader at Bear Stearns) could borrow money at 3% and I can make 5%, it is risk-less.

**关键在于：把买入看涨期权视为等同于买入附带看跌期权的股票。**两者并无区别。投资时，你必须清楚自己在做什么。

<!--en-->
**The key is thinking of buying a call as the same thing as buying a stock with a put attached.**
There is no difference. When you are investing, you want to know what you are doing.

当我买入远月期权时，本质上就是买入带有保护机制的股票。价格差异主要源于股息及已支付的利息，但其定价是合理的。*这是一种廉价的借款方式。*看涨期权中隐含的借贷成本实际上就等于无风险利率；你几乎是以无风险利率来借款的。

<!--en-->
When I buy a *Leap*, I am basically buying a stock with protection. The difference in any price has to do with dividends and any interest that is paid out, but it is fairly priced. *It is a cheap way to borrow money.* The implied borrowing costs in the *Call* will really be the risk free rate. You will be borrowing close to the risk-free rate.

波动性会影响看跌期权的价值。如果股价波动剧烈，看跌期权的价格就不会那么便宜。

<!--en-->
The volatility will come into what is the put worth? If the stock can vary widely, then the put won't be priced so cheaply.

不必担心波动性或任何复杂因素。记住：当你买入看涨期权时——你实际上是在买入股票和看跌期权（即保护机制）。

<!--en-->
Don't worry about volatility or any complicated stuff. Remember that when you buy a *Call*--you are buying a stock and a put (protection).

## 关于美国运通公司（AXP）的基本面分析。

<!--en-->
*The fundamentals regarding American Express (AXP).*

### 构建投资逻辑。

<!--en-->
*Constructing a thesis.*

2005年9月，他们将分拆其财务顾问业务。一位分析师预测其每股收益将为56美分，并给出了16倍的估值倍数，因此其价值约为8至9美元。假设其股价为9美元，那么你购买另一项业务（我感兴趣的部分）的价格就是43.85美元。

<!--en-->
In Sept. 2005, they will spin off the financial advisory business. An analyst said it would earn 56 cents and he gave it a 16 multiple, so it is worth $8 or $9. Let's say it is at $9, so you are buying the other business (which I am interested in) at $43.85.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：让我们为*AXP*构建一份投资论点。分析师预计该公司今年的每股收益约为2.50美元。该公司宣称其盈利将以每年12%至15%的速度增长，这意味着2007年的每股收益将达到3.20美元。由于期权将在两年后到期，那么2007年1月时2007年预期收益的市盈率是多少呢？

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Let's construct a thesis for *AXP*. Analyst estimates were roughly $2.50 for this year. The company is telling you that they will grow earnings at 12% to 15% per year. This works out to $3.20 in earnings per share in 2007. Since the options expire in two years, in Jan 2007 what is the multiple of earnings in 2007?

现在的问题是：信用卡的赔付率是否低于正常水平，或者它们的利差是否高于正常水平？它们获得的利润是否超出了正常水平？还是说这种情况现在已成为正常的盈利水平？我们可以争论这3.20美元的每股收益能否达到3美元；我认为它将会是3.20美元。

<!--en-->
The question now is: are loss ratios in credit cards lower than normal or are their spreads larger than normal? Are they making more than normal profits? Or is this situation now normal earnings? We can quibble if this $3.20 EPS could turn into $3. I will argue that it will be $3.20.

当我们去分析这件事时——这不包括美国运通银行，它每年盈利约0.10美元，且不属于高倍数业务——所以归根结底我给它估值为1美元。

<!--en-->
When we went to analyze this thing--and this excludes the American Express Bank which earns about a $0.10 and is not a high multiple business--so I give that a $1 at the end of the day.

那么问题来了：这3.20美元到底值多少呢？请记住，当20年期政府债券收益率低于6%时，我们会以6%作为安全底线，然后将我们对*AXP*的投资与之对比。我们该给这3.20美元赋予多大的估值倍数呢？这是一家相当不错的企业。实际上，当他们通过分拆财务顾问业务来套现后，就不再需要为该部门投入资金了，届时他们的股本回报率将会接近40%。它虽不及*穆迪*或*可口可乐*那样出色——但确实是一家好企业。该行业没有天然的市场准入壁垒。美国运通公司会随着经济的发展而壮大。只要经济持续增长，*AXP*就能实现无止境的增长；其业务没有天然的终点。只要金融世界持续扩张且*穆迪*能保住市场份额，*穆迪*就会继续发展。

<!--en-->
So the question is what is that $3.20 worth? Remember when the 20 year govt. bond is below 6%, we will use 6% as a safety net, then we compare our investment in *AXP* to this. What multiple should we place on the $3.20? This is a pretty good business. Actually when they suck out money from spinning off the financial advisors, they won't have to spend money anymore on that division, their returns on equity will approach 40% at that time. Not quite *Moody's* or not quite *Coke*--but a good business. There are no natural barriers to entry. Amex will grow with the economy. *AXP* has unending growth as long as the economy grows. There is no natural end to their business. As long as the financial world grows and *Moody's* can retain share, *Moody's* will grow.

他们可以通过股票回购或派发股息来返还现金——去年他们通过回购和股息返还了87%的现金。这让我想起了可口可乐/穆迪那种情况：穆迪可以返还100%的资本同时仍能实现增长，而可口可乐只需用80%的资本就能做到同样的事。可口可乐需要将20%的资本重新投资于业务以实现增长。我认为他们（美国运通）目前声称会返还65%的现金，实际却支付了87%，未来他们或许还能提高到75%或80%。这是一家不错的多业务公司。**问题在于具体的倍数是多少，而这一点目前更像是<u>艺术</u>而非科学。** 见识过诸多情况后，我宁愿选择美国运通那5%的盈利增长率（该公司增速为12%至15%），也不愿要6%的债券收益。我当然会选择前者。

<!--en-->
They can do stock repurchases or through dividends--last year they returned 87% of cash through buybacks and dividends. That reminded me of a *Coke/Moody's* type of situation. *Moody's* could return 100% of their capital and still grow while *Coke* could do the same with 80% of their capital. *Coke* needed to reinvest 20% in their business to grow. I am thinking they (*AXP*) are saying 65% and they are paying out 87% while they could do 75% or 80% in the future. This is a decent multiple business. **The question is how much of a multiple and that is more <u>art</u> than science at this point.**
Having seen a lot of things, would I rather have a 5% on AXP earnings that it is growing 12% to 15% or a 6% bond. I would rather have the 5%.

保守估计的市盈率22倍乘以2007年的3.20美元，得出70.40美元。接着我们还能从银行获得1美元。此外，通过分拆还能获得9美元。

<!--en-->
A conservative P/E of 22 x $3.20 in 2007 = $70.40
Then we have $1 from the bank. Then we have $9 from the spin-off.

分拆预计将于2005年9月进行。但我们购买的是2007年1月的期权。那么分拆后，我在这两家独立公司中的期权会怎样呢？你将拥有这两家公司——即以50美元的价格购买分拆公司和AXP的权利。如果你购买行权价为50美元的看涨期权，你将获得<u>股</u>。

<!--en-->
The spin-off is supposed to happen in Sept. 2005. But we are buying options for Jan 2007. So what happens to my options with the two separate companies post spin-off? You get both of those companies--the right to buy the spin-off and AXP at $50. If you buy the $50 *Call* you get <u>each</u> share.

我更喜欢哪种风险/回报呢？我认为它两年后的价值为9美元。为了实现两年后3.20美元的盈利增长，公司会发放股息并进行股票回购。再加上另外2美元，两年后总价值将达到82.40美元。以9.00美元买入的1月7日看涨期权，其价值现为32.40美元（82.40美元 - 50.00美元）。

<!--en-->
Which risk/reward do I like better? I value it $9 in two years. To spend to get to this earnings growth of $3.20 in two years you will collect dividends and buybacks. Add another $2. $82.40 in two years. The Jan 07 *Calls* bought at $9.00 are worth $32.40 ($82.40 - $50.00).

如果你以52.40美元的价格买入股票，两年后以82.40美元卖出，那么你将获利30美元，即两年内的回报率为55%，年化收益率为25%。而通过期权交易，你的收益可达300%。

<!--en-->
If you own the stock at $52.40 and sell in two years at $82.40. So you make $30 or 55% return over two years or 25% annualized. The options you will make 300%.

如果价格为70美元，你每年可获得14.5%的收益；但这些期权的价值将达到20美元，即盈利11美元，相当于100%的回报率。

<!--en-->
At $70 then you would make 14.5% a year, but the options would be worth $20 or a profit of $11 or 100% return.

市场走势向下，市场不会给出溢价。你必须把利息成本算进去。

<!--en-->
The market turns down and the market will not pay a multiple. You have to include your interest carry.

构建一个<u>决策树</u>，但我设定其价值为30美元的概率为30%，价值70美元的概率为20%，价值60美元的概率为25%，价值50美元的概率也为25%。对于这9.00美元的*通话费用*而言，其期望值为20美元。

<!--en-->
Do a <u>decision tree</u>, but I give it a 30% chance of it being worth $30 and I give it a 20% of being worth $70 and give it a 25% of being $60 or 25% for $50. An expected value of $20 for these $9.00 *Calls*.

你不会像购买股票那样大量买入这些*看涨期权*，但它能为你提供<u>更高的杠杆作用</u>以及更大的风险/回报潜力。对于股票而言，你无法确切知晓其风险与回报——比如股价可能跌至30美元。

<!--en-->
You would not buy as much of these *Calls* as a stock, but it gives you an opportunity to <u>get more</u> leverage and a greater risk/reward. With the stock you don't know your risk reward exactly--the stock could be at $30.

在这里，你可以确定自己的损失不会超过9.00美元。买入股票与买入看跌期权之间并无本质区别。哥伦比亚大学商学院开设的190门特殊情境投资课程指出：我看待LEAP的方式——持有LEAP就等于同时买入股票并持有看跌期权。花费52美元来支付利息，与支付9美元的看涨期权费用，这两者之间有何区别呢？在这里，我支付的金额比该看涨期权的内在价值高出6.15美元。请注意：为了借入52.85美元以及另外9美元，我在22个月内需支付6.15美元的利息。换句话说，总成本为61.85美元，相当于每年4.8%的利息率。

<!--en-->
Here with options you know your loss is no more than $9.00. Buying a stock and buying a put is the only difference.
190
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The way I choose to look at a LEAP - owning a LEAP is buying the stock and owning the put. What is the difference between interest cost in laying out the $52 or paying the interest cost of the $9 *Call*? Here I am paying $6.15 above the intrinsic value of the *Call*. Look I am paying $6.15 in interest over 22 months to borrow $52.85 and $9. Or.......$61.85 or 4.8% per year.

我正在支付6.15美元，这相当于两年期间14%的资金成本（14%/2 = 7%）。因此，我的实际借款成本为7%。所以，与其说我是以无风险利率借款并购买看跌期权来获得LEAP，不如说干脆忽略这个看跌期权吧。让我们把看跌期权的成本**计入**我的利息成本中。

<!--en-->
I am paying $6.15, which is 14% cost of money over two years (14%/2 = 7%). So my effective borrowing cost is 7%. So instead of saying I am borrowing money at the risk free rate and buying a put to get my LEAP. What I am saying is forget the put. Let us **add** the cost of the put to my interest cost.

我购买这只股票与购买这种LEAP期权之间的区别在于：今天我无需支付52.85美元以及相应的利息，只需额外支付6.15美元（全部为利息）。作为交换，我所获得的看跌期权以及实际借款成本并非每年3%，而是每年7%。也就是说，我以7%的利率借款，但损失不会超过这个数额。本质上，我是以7%的利率借款，却拥有一笔无追索权的贷款。**换句话说，如果交易不成功，我只需支付利息，而无需偿还本金。**实际上，我购买了看跌期权。可以说，他们以7%的利率向我放贷，无论结果如何我都需支付利息；但如果事情不如预期，我无需偿还贷款。这听起来确实是个更划算的交易——你支付高额利息，却无需偿还本金。

<!--en-->
The difference between my buying this stock and this LEAP is that today--instead of laying out $52.85 today and paying the interest on that--I am paying an additional $6.15 (all interest). And what I get in exchange for the put and my effective borrowing cost is not 3% per year but 7% per year. So I get to borrow at 7%, but I can't lose any more money than this. I am basically borrowing at 7% but I have a non-recourse loan. **In other words, if it doesn't work out, I owe the interest, but I don't have to pay the loan back.**
In effect, I buy the put. I say look, they are lending me money at 7%, but I have to pay the interest no matter what, but if things don't work out, I don't have to pay the loan back. That sounds like a better deal. You pay high interest rates but you don't owe the loan.

## 重新阅读关于LEAPS的章节。

<!--en-->
*Reread the chapter on LEAPS.*

你需要预先支付利息成本。你支付的是所购资产价值与利息之间的差额——看跌期权为你提供的是一笔无追索权贷款；我的利率并非无风险利率3%，而是7%。假设我将投资组合中8%的资金投入这些LEAP期权。我会根据自己愿意承受的损失程度来判断：两年内损失8%，即每年4%。这样我就不会一次性失去所有资金。

<!--en-->
You pay your interest costs up front. You are paying the difference between the value of what you are buying (all interest)-- what that put is giving you is a non-recourse loan-- and my interest rate instead of being the risk free rate of 3%, I pay 7%. Say I put 8% of my portfolio into these leaps. I judge by how much I am willing to lose. 8% over two years or 4% a year. I won't lose it all at once.

听着，如果我遇到这类机会且它们并不常见，我会尽量充分利用。我认为，如果我这么做，预期收益能达到20美元；倘若我擅长预测市场走势，那么进行6次、8次或10次这样的交易，时间跨度为五年，只要预期收益能覆盖成本的100%，我就承受得起一些损失——前提是**我具备出色的预测能力**。我已经从事这类交易有一段时间了。

<!--en-->
Listen, if I have these opportunities and they don't come along very much, I will try to take as much as I can of them. And I think if I did this and my expected value is $20 and I am any good at this at handicapping horses then if I do 6 or 8 or 10 of these and I have a horizon of five years and my expected value is 100% over what I am paying, then I can afford to lose a few--as long as **I am good at handicapping**. I have been doing this awhile.

我想知道的是：与以52.85美元的价格购买股票相比，当股价涨至70美元时我能获得X%的收益（无论其中的风险回报如何）。或者我能否采用这种方式下注？又或者我能否部分购买股票、部分购买LEAP期权？这是一种不同的风险/回报模式，也是值得尝试的替代方案。

<!--en-->
I would like to know as opposed to buying the stock at $52.85 and when the stock goes to $70 and I make x percent with whatever implicit risk reward is there. Or can I take my bet this way or could I take partial stock and partial leaps. It is a different risk/reward. It is a different alternative that is worth working at.

我不确定自己的判断是否正确，但我觉得如果选择10个这样的标的，我大概能猜对8个或7个。AXP的市盈率25倍是合理的。

<!--en-->
I don't know if I am right, but I think if I looked at 10 of these, I would get 8 of them right or 7 of them right. There is a case for 25 P/E for AXP.

我将6%的债券收益率与投资机会进行比较。我可能会采用14%的收益率；或者经济下行、消费者购买力下降，再加上不良信贷和损失准备金的影响。你的损失不会超过9美元。在LEAP交易中，我每年会损失一些7%的利息，但不会遭受股票本身的损失。这就是我看待问题的角度。

<!--en-->
I am comparing the 6 bond yield to the opportunity. I might use 14 or the economy turns down and the consumer drops dead besides bad credit and loss reserves. You can't lose more than $9. In my leaps I would lose some of my 7% interest a year and won't have a stock loss. That is the way I choose to look at it.

## 牛市价差策略

<!--en-->
*BULL SPREAD*

期权还有另一种**选择**：你不必过于激进。你以9美元的价格买入行权价为50的看涨期权，再以6.20美元的价格卖出行权价为55的看涨期权，净成本为2.80美元。由于股票价值为55美元，因此行权价为50的看涨期权价值应为55美元或5美元；而行权价为55的看涨期权到期后将一文不值。利润为5美元 + 6.20美元 - 9美元，即11.20美元 - 9美元 = 2.20美元。简而言之，你投入2.80美元，就能获得2.20美元的净利润，资本回报率达79%。你为之支付的2.80美元差价，在股价高于55美元时能为你带来5美元的利润。你的盈亏平衡点为52.80美元。因此，即便股价涨幅有限，你也能创造出各种有趣的风险/回报情境。利用期权可以设计出许多有趣的风险/回报结构。

<!--en-->
There is another **choice** in options. You don't want to be as aggressive. You bought these 50's at 9 and sell the 55s for $6.20 for a net $2.80 cost. The stock is worth $55 so the 50 *Call* is worth 55 or $5 and the *Call* at 55 expires worthless. Profit is $5 + $6.20 - $9 or $11.20 - $9 = $2.20. In short, you laid out $2.80 to make $2.20 net profit for a 79% return on your capital. The spread you paid $2.80 for you will make $5 on any stock price above $55. Your break-even is at $52.80. So you can create all sorts of interesting risk reward situations even if the stock doesn't go very far. There a lot of things you can do to with options to create interesting risk/reward situations.

## 西尔斯公司

<!--en-->
*SEARS*

## 哥伦比亚大学商学院开设的191期特殊情境投资课程中有一讲是关于*西尔斯*的。*迪恩·威特（DW）*和*好事达*被分拆出去。该交易于9月宣布，而*迈克尔·普莱斯*早在7月就指出：西尔斯将分拆出西尔斯公司和好事达公司。一旦好事达和DW被分拆出来，通过买入西尔斯股票并卖空这两家公司股票，你就可以用每股35美元的价格获得剩下的西尔斯百货业务。该业务每股销售额达9美元，其交易价格仅为销售额的6%（5/90）。相比之下，*杰西潘尼*的交易价格相当于每美元销售额60美分——高出10倍。原本5美元就能打造出一个价值50美元的西尔斯；到了9月，这一价值已升至30美元，于是我卖出了股票。随后股价更是涨至50美元。这里就是催化剂所在；这不仅仅是一笔LEAP交易——这就是整个投资逻辑。9月将有分拆发生，一旦子公司被分拆，人们便会有新的公司可供审视，情况也会被重新评估。那家公司的特质是什么？你可能会说事情并非如此简单，但西尔斯的规模确实相当庞大。我可以保证，自那以后我多次采用类似策略。世事难料，也许这次(*AXP*)并不会成功。**如果你有强烈的看法且判断正确，利用LEAP期权就能创造出极具吸引力的风险/回报机会。它是你 arsenal 中一件不错的武器。**

<!--en-->
191 Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School There was a lecture on *Sears*. *Dean Witter (DW)* and *Allstate* spun-off. The deal was announced in Sept. and *Michael Price* said in July--Sears is spinning off Sears and *Allstate*. Once they spin off *All State* and *DW*, by buying Sears and shorting those two companies, you could create the rest of *Sears* the department store for $35 per share. The department had $9 per share in sales. It was trading at 6% of sales (5/90). When we looked at *JC Penny*, it was trading at 60 cents per dollar of sales--10 times higher. That $5 you could create Sears for $5 and it was worth $50. By Sept. the $5 had moved to $30, then I sold my stock. Then the stock moved to $50. Here we have the catalyst; it is not just a LEAP--that is the thesis anyway. There is a spin-off coming in Sept. Once the subsidiary is spun off, people will have a new company too look at. Things will be reassessed. What are the attributes of that company? You say it doesn't work that way, but Sears was pretty darn big. I can guarantee you I have done this many, many times since that time. And so stuff happens. It may not make a ton of sense. This (*AXP*) may not work out. **With Leaps you can create a very exciting risk reward play if you have a strong opinion, and you are right. It is a nice weapon to have in your arsenal.**

乔尔·格林布拉特所著《你可以成为股市天才》一书中对LEAPS的讨论（页码：213-220、236和242）。

<!--en-->
Discussion of LEAPS in Book, *You Can Be a Stock Market Genius* by Joel Greenblatt (pgs: 213-220, 236, and 242).

## LEAPS（长期股权预期证券）。

<!--en-->
*LEAPS (Long-term Equity Anticipation Securities).*

这是一种创建自己版本的“残股”的方法。这种情况具有许多与投资重组后公司的杠杆股权类似的风险/回报特征。

<!--en-->
This is a way to create your own version of a *stub* stock. A situation that has many of the risk/reward characteristics of an investment in the leveraged equity of a recapitalized company.

*看涨期权*仅仅赋予持有人在限定时间内以指定价格购买股票的权利，而非义务。例如，一份6月份到期、行权价为每股140美元的IBM看涨期权，赋予持有人在6月份到期前以140美元/股的价格购买IBM股票的权利。假设在4月份——即6月份到期前两个月——IBM的股价为148美元。此时，这些看涨期权的价值会高于其内在价值8美元（148美元股价减去140美元行权价），其交易价格更可能接近11.375美元。

<!--en-->
A *Call* is merely the right, but not the obligation--to buy a stock at a specified price for a limited period of time. A June *Call* to buy IBM at $140 per share gives the owner of the *Call* the right to buy IBM at $140 per share until the *Call* expires in June. Let's assume that IBM is trading at $148 in April, two months prior to June expiration. In April, these *Calls* are worth more than the intrinsic value of $8 (148 price - $140 Strike Price). They're more likely to be trading closer to $11.375.

为什么呢？首先，看涨期权持有人无需在接下来两个月内支付140美元，却仍能享有截至6月份股票的所有增值收益。为补偿这一点，这140美元在到期前两个月所能产生的利息应反映在看涨期权的价格中。这种被称为“推定利率”的机制，将看涨期权买方在这两个月内无需支付的资金所产生的利息也计入期权价格。

<!--en-->
Why? First, the owner of the *Calls* doesn't have to lay out $140 for another two months, yet he is entitled to all of the stock's appreciation until June. To compensate for this, the amount of interest that could have been earned on the $140 for the two months until expiration should be reflected in the price of the *Call*. This is *Called* imputed interest rate which is the rate for the amount of money the *Call* buyer didn't have to lay out for the two months is also included in the *Call* price.

正因如此，看涨期权的价格从8美元——即其内在价值——上升至约9.40美元——即包含买方无需支付的140美元所产生的利息后的期权价值。但我之前说过该看涨期权应交易于约11.375美元。那么，已计算的9.40美元与实际价格11.375美元之间近2美元的差异从何而来呢？显然，持有看涨期权还有另一项好处——确实存在这样的好处。

<!--en-->
That is how we move from a *Call* price of $8--the intrinsic value of the *Call*--to approximately $9.40--the value of the *Call* including the interest on the $140 the buyer of the *Call* did not have to lay out. But I said the *Call* should trade at approximately at $11.375. What accounts for the nearly $2 difference between the $9.40 already figured and the actual price of $11.375? Clearly there has to be another benefit to owning *Calls*--and there is.

看涨期权买方最多只会损失投资于该期权的金额。如果IBM股价跌至每股80美元，看涨期权买方仅损失11.375美元，而持有每股140美元IBM股票的股东则会损失60美元。这部分差额大约相当于2美元。因此，如果你在购买看涨期权时支付了这2美元的“保护费”，那么你的成本9.40美元就会趋近于11.375美元。为承担股价低于140美元所带来的风险而支付的2美元，实际上等同于看跌期权的成本。

<!--en-->
The buyer for the *Call* can only lose the amount of money invested in the *Call*. If IBM falls to $80 per share, the *Call* buyer only loses $11.375 while the owner of IBM at $140 would lose $60. This is probably worth about $2. So, if you pay the $2 in "protection money" as part of the purchase price of the *Calls*, then your cost of $9.40 moves closer to $11.375. The $2 cost for assuming the risk below $140 is actually the same as the cost of the put option.

**购买看涨期权就像借钱买股票，但带有保护作用。** 看涨期权的价格包含了你的*借贷成本*以及“保护”费用——所以你并非免费获得任何东西，但你确实在利用它来**放大对某只股票未来表现的押注**。同时，你在该押注中可能遭受的损失上限也被限制在看涨期权的价格之内。

<!--en-->
**Buying calls is like borrowing money to buy stock, but with protection.**
The price of the *Call* includes your *borrowing costs* and the cost of your "protection"--so you are not getting anything for free, but you are **leveraging your bet** on the future performance of a particular stock. You are also limiting the amount you can lose on the bet to the price of the *Call*.

持有看涨期权与持有“残股”并无太大区别。

<!--en-->
Owning a *Call* isn't too much different from owning a *stub* stock.

**残股示例：** 一家股价为36美元的公司通过向股东派发30美元进行资本重组，结果产生了股价为6美元的杠杆残股，这种残股会放大标的公司价值的变化。在某种情况下，该公司盈利仅增长20%，却导致残股价格上涨80%。

<!--en-->
**STUB EXAMPLE:** The company with a $36 stock recapitalized by distributing $30 to its shareholders, the result was a leveraged stub stock at $6 that magnified changes in the value of the underlying company. There,a relatively modest 20-percent increase in earnings resulted, in one scenario, in an 80-percent gain on the stub stock's price.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：另一方面，如果该公司破产，残股持有人仅会损失投资于残股的金额，而无需承担公司为完成重组所借的30美元债务。**残股没有到期日，其存续期无限，这与有到期日的期权不同。**

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
On the other hand, if the company declared bankruptcy, an owner of the stub stock was only at risk for the amount invested in the stub, not for the $30 of debt taken on by the company to complete the recap. **Stubs** have unlimited life unlike options which have expiration dates.

LEAPS属于长期期权，可在到期前两年半内购买。此外，两年半的时间往往足以让许多原本被低估的股票重新受到市场青睐。**持有超过一年的长期收益**也是投资LEAPS的另一优势。

<!--en-->
LEAPS, which are long-term options, can be purchased up to two and a half years before they expire. Additionally, two and a half years is often enough time for many just plain cheap stocks either to be discovered or regain popularity. **Long-term gains** are another advantage of holding investments past one year.

投资LEAPS将是你研究工作的副产品。能够将某只股票的风险/回报与通过相关LEAPS投资所获得的机会进行比较，会为你提供另一个不错的投资选择。**结束** 1998年6月8日，星期一 《危险游戏》：“电锯阿尔”邓拉普去年是否操纵了Sunbeam的盈利数据？**作者：乔纳森·R·莱恩** 阿尔伯特·邓拉普常说起1996年亲信们如何警告他：接手小型家电制造商Sunbeam Corp.的最高职位很可能成为他的“越南战场”。有一段时间，这位60岁的西点军校毕业生似乎证明了那些预言家的错误。作为90年代企业裁员的典型代表，他实现了华尔街所青睐的大规模裁员和激进的成本削减措施。他解雇或出售了Sunbeam旗下12,000名员工中的一半，共计关闭或出售了该公司114家工厂、办事处和仓库中的约80家。

<!--en-->
Investing in LEAPS will come about as a by-product of your research efforts. Being able to compare the risk/reward of a stock with the opportunities available through an investment in the related LEAPS will provide you with another good investment choice.
**END**
MONDAY, JUNE 8, 1998
Dangerous Games
*Did "Chainsaw Al" Dunlap manufacture Sunbeam's earnings last year?*
**By JONATHAN R. LAING**
Albert Dunlap likes to tell how confidants warned him in 1996 that taking the top job at the small-appliance maker Sunbeam Corp. would likely be his Vietnam. For a time, the 60-year-old West Point graduate seemingly proved the Cassandras wrong. As the poster boy of 'Nineties-style corporate cost-cutting, he delivered exactly the huge body counts and punishing air strikes that Wall Street loved. He dumped half of Sunbeam's 12,000 employees by either laying them off or selling the operations where they worked. In all, he shuttered or sold about 80 of Sunbeam's 114 plants, offices and warehouses.

Sunbeam的销售额和盈利随之上升，其股价也从1996年7月邓拉普接手时的每股12.50美元，涨至今年3月初的53美元高点。

<!--en-->
Sunbeam's sales and earnings responded, and so did its stock price, rising from $12.50 a share the day Dunlap took over in July 1996 to a high of 53 in early March of this year.

但上个月，Sunbeam遭遇了命运的逆转——这对邓拉普而言，犹如1968年越南战争中的塔特攻势对美国军队造成的冲击一般突然且惨痛。在几次关于营收可能不及预期的轻微警告之后，Sunbeam公布第一季度亏损4460万美元，销售额更是下降了3.6%，这一消息令华尔街震惊不已。转眼间，Sunbeam的降本增效神话破灭了，“电锯阿尔”邓拉普作为股东价值最大化大师的形象也随之崩塌。如今，Sunbeam的股价较峰值已下跌超过50%，最近跌至22美元。

<!--en-->
But last month Sunbeam suffered a reversal of fortune that was as sudden and traumatic for Dunlap as the Viet Congo's Tat offensive was to U.S. forces in 1968. After several mild warnings of a possible revenue disappointment, Sunbeam shocked Wall Street by reporting a loss of $44.6 million for the first quarter on a sales decline of 3.6%. In a trice, the Sunbeam cost-cutting story was dead, along with "Chainsaw Al" Dunlap's image as the supreme maximize of shareholder value. Now Sunbeam stock has fallen more than 50% from its peak, to a recent 22.

同样出人意料的是，原本被视作轻而易举就能完成的“最后一搏”——邓拉普作为企业扭亏专家的收山之作——却变成了一场艰难的马拉松。他为Sunbeam制定的增长计划彻底泡汤，该计划依赖于一些看似吸引人的新产品，如软冰淇淋机、高档烤架、家用净水器和空气净化器。然而，许多新产品在市场上遭遇惨败，或存在严重的质量问题。此外，Sunbeam还面临各种生产、质量和交付方面的难题。公司最近宣布关闭两家位于墨西哥的制造厂，涉及约2800名工人，理由是这些工厂表现糟糕。数十名关键高管——也就是邓拉普几个月前所称的“梦之队”成员——纷纷离职。现在，他还要面对长达一年甚至更久的痛苦重组过程，以便将Sunbeam与近期收购的企业整合在一起，包括露营设备制造商Coleman Co.、烟雾探测器生产商First Alert以及以Mr. Coffee系列家电闻名的Signature Brands USA。这些收购将使这家已经摇摇欲坠的公司规模翻倍。这里或许不是越南战场，但肯定也不是堪萨斯州，托托。

<!--en-->
And just as suddenly, what was supposed to be an easy sprint, Dunlap's last hurrah as a corporate turnaround artist, has turned into a grinding marathon. Lying in tatters is his growth scenario for Sunbeam, based on supposedly sexy new offerings such as soft-ice cream makers, fancy grills, home water purifiers and air-filter appliances. Many of the new products have bombed in the marketplace or run into serious quality problems. Moreover, Sunbeam has run into all manner of production, quality and delivery problems. It recently announced the closing of two Mexican manufacturing facilities with some 2,800 workers, citing the facilities' lamentable performance. Dozens of key executives, members of what Dunlap just months ago called his Dream Team, are bailing out. And now he faces another year or more of the wrenching restructuring that's needed to meld Sunbeam with its recently announced acquisitions, including the camping-equipment maker Coleman Co., the smoke-detector producer First Alert and Signature Brands USA, best known for its Mr. Coffee line of appliances. These acquisitions will double the size of a company whose wheels are coming off. This may not be Vietnam, but it sure isn't Kansas, Toto.

Sunbeam拒绝就公司问题接受《巴伦周刊》的采访。从某些方面看，邓拉普似乎已经变成了电影《现代启示录》中的库尔茨上校的现代版：他越来越脱离Sunbeam的残酷现实，对朋友和敌人都充满猜疑。例如，三周前在纽约举行的一次Sunbeam与金融界人士的会议上，邓拉普与PaineWebber分析师安德鲁·肖尔发生了激烈争执，此事至今仍在华尔街传为佳话。肖尔竟敢提出几个被邓拉普视为无礼的问题，邓拉普怒吼道：“你这个混蛋！如果你想对付我，我会加倍回击你。”

<!--en-->
Sunbeam declined to discuss the company's problems with *Barron's*. In some ways, Dunlap seems to have morphed into a latter-day Colonel Kurtz of the movie Apocalypse Now, increasingly out of touch with the grim realities of Sunbeam's situation and suspicious of friend and foe alike. For example, Wall Street is still buzzing over a confrontation that Dunlap had with PaineWebber analyst Andrew Shore at a Sunbeam meeting with the financial community in New York three weeks ago. Shore had the temerity to ask several questions that Dunlap deemed impertinent, and Dunlap snarled, "You sonof a bitch. If you want to come after me, I'll come after you twice as hard."

哥伦比亚大学商学院的“特殊情境投资课程”指出，肖尔是4月份首位下调Sunbeam股票评级的主要分析师，当时有关第一季度业绩惨淡的消息开始流传。他至今仍对那次事件耿耿于怀。“在我看来，阿尔是美国最被高估的首席执行官，”他抱怨道，“他不过是个只会说空话、毫无实质内容的恶霸罢了。”

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Shore, the first major analyst to downgrade Sunbeam's stock in April when word began to circulate of a possible first-quarter earnings debacle, is still upset over the incident. "As far as I'm concerned, Al is the most over-rated CEO in America," he grouses. "He's nothing but a bully who speaks in sound bites and completely lacks substance."

尽管Sunbeam近期命运多舛，但别指望阿尔·邓拉普会很快陷入贫困。虽然Sunbeam股价的暴跌抹去了公司大多数高管所持期权的价值，但邓拉普所拥有的巨额期权和股票赠予仍价值约7000万美元——这一数字虽较股价高峰时的3亿多美元有所缩水，但仍相当可观。此外，邓拉普在2月份谈妥了一份新合同，将其年度基本薪资翻倍至200万美元。根据优厚福利待遇，Sunbeam甚至为邓拉普及其妻子支付从佛罗里达州（Sunbeam总部所在地）到费城的一等舱机票费用，以便邓拉普能去看私人牙医，保持最新安装的牙桥舒适且洁白。豪华轿车接送服务以及在四季酒店的过夜费用也包含在内。这一切竟出自这位自诩为股东价值捍卫者之口。

<!--en-->
Despite Sunbeam's latest reversal of fortune, don't expect Al Dunlap to be headed for the poorhouse any time soon. Though the swoon in Sunbeam shares has vaporized the value of the options held by most of the company's executives and managers, Dunlap's huge option and stock grants are still worth about $70 million, down from a peak value of over $300 million when the stock was at its high. Moreover, in February Dunlap negotiated a new contract, doubling his annual base salary to $2 million. Under a rich benefits package, Sunbeam even foots the bill for Dunlap and his wife's first-class air fare from Florida, where Sunbeam is headquartered, to Philadelphia so that Dunlap can visit his personal dentist to keep his latest bridge comfy and pearly white. Limo charges and overnights at the Four Seasons hotel are included as well. All this from the self-styled champion of shareholder value.

我们对Sunbeam目前的困境并不感到意外。去年我们曾在一篇封面文章《小心，阿尔》（6月16日刊）中，对邓拉普在低利润、竞争激烈的小家电行业中的增长目标持怀疑态度。我们还指出了Sunbeam宣称的业绩与现实之间的巨大差距。我们特别注意到Sunbeam的会计手段——该公司似乎通过会计魔术，将1996年高达3.37亿美元（税前）的巨额重组费用，神奇地转化为了1997年令人瞩目的销售和盈利反弹。但这一切都无济于事。华尔街依然对Sunbeam的盈利表现津津乐道，其股价也从文章发表时的37美元继续上涨。

<!--en-->
We can't say we are surprised by Sunbeam's current woes. In a cover story last year entitled "Careful, Al" (June 16), we cast a skeptical eye at Dunlap's growth objectives in the low-margin, cutthroat small-appliance industry. We also pointed out the yawning gap between Sunbeam's performance claims and reality. We took special note of Sunbeam's accounting gimmickry, which appeared to have transmogrified through accounting wizardry the company's monster 1996 restructuring charge ($337 million before taxes) into 1997's eye-popping sales and earnings rebound. But to no avail. Wall Street remained impressed by Sunbeam's earnings, and the stock continued to rise from a price of 37 at the time of the story.

在邓拉普的领导下，Sunbeam的财务报表简直就像一场高能物理实验——时间和空间似乎在此融合、扭曲。它们简直就是一座名副其实的“云室”。收入和成本如同带电离子一般，几乎难以察觉地在损益表和资产负债表之间来回移动；而等到季度末公布业绩时，这些离子的痕迹早已消散无踪。此外，还有一些其他会计操纵和虚报的迹象，包括在产品实际发货或收到付款之前就提前确认销售收入和相关利润。在特定严格条件下，提前确认销售和收益确实可以符合会计准则。

<!--en-->
Sunbeam's financials under Dunlap look like an exercise in high-energy physics, in which time and space seem to fuse and bend. They are a veritable cloud chamber. Income and costs move almost imperceptibly back and forth between the income statement and balance sheet like charged ions, whose vapor trail has long since dissipated by the end of any quarter, when results are reported. There are also some signs of other accounting shenanigans and puffery, including sales and related profits booked in periods before the goods were actually shipped or payment received. Booking sales and earnings in advance can comply with accounting regulations under certain strict circumstances.

“我们度过了令人惊叹的一年，”邓拉普在Sunbeam最近发布的1997年年度报告中得意地宣称。当年公司实现净利润1.094亿美元，即每股1.41美元，销售额达到12亿美元。Sunbeam有充分的动机在1997年大展拳脚。邓拉普及其团队坚信自己能像1995年重组Scott Paper公司时那样，为公司找到买家——当时邓拉普成功将Scott Paper以90亿美元的价格卖给金佰利公司。去年下半年，他们公开四处推销Sunbeam，但始终没有收到收购要约。不断上涨的股价使公司估值过高，而潜在买家也因金佰利收购Scott Paper后所经历的噩梦而却步。

<!--en-->
"We had an amazing year," Dunlap crowed in Sunbeam's recently released 1997 annual report, taking an impromptu victory lap for the profit of $109.4 million, or $1.41 a share, on sales of $1.2 billion. Sunbeam had every incentive to try to shoot the lights out in 1997. Dunlap and crew were convinced they would be able to attract a buyer for the company just as they had done in the second year of their restructuring of Scott Paper in 1995, when Dunlap managed to fob Scott off on Kimberly-Clark for $9 billion. They openly shopped Sunbeam around in the second half of last year, but the offer never came. The rising stock price made the company too expensive, and would-be buyers were also deterred by the nightmares Kimberly-Clark experienced after buying Scott.

然而遗憾的是，Sunbeam所谓“突破性年份”所产生的盈利似乎大多是人为制造的。至少，在仔细研读该公司最新发布的10-K报表后，再加上一些公司内部人士的帮助，我们得出了这一结论。

<!--en-->
Yet, sad to say, the earnings from Sunbeam's supposed breakthrough year appear to be largely manufactured. That, at least, is our conclusion after close perusal of the company's recently released 10-K, with a little help from some people close to the company.

首先，1996年重组期间，Sunbeam将约9000万美元的存货价值减记为零，这些存货涉及已停产的产品线以及其他质量完好的商品。即便Sunbeam在1997年出售这些商品时能收回一半的价值（有报道称实际情况甚至更好），这一项也能占到去年1.094亿美元净利润的三分之一左右。

<!--en-->
Start with the fact that in the 1996 restructuring, Sunbeam chose to write down to zero some $90 million of its inventory for product lines being discontinued and other perfectly good items. Even if Sunbeam realized just 50 cents on the dollar by selling these goods in 1997 (in some cases, they reportedly did even better), that would account for about a third of last year's net income of $109.4 million.

要想发现更多此类“小把戏”，必须查看1997年的年末资产负债表。人们会注意到，预付费用及其他流动资产从1996年的4040万美元骤降至1997年的1720万美元，减少了2320万美元。据一位前Sunbeam财务人员透露，这并无玄机可言：由于1996年的巨额重组开支导致那一年毫无建树，因此Sunbeam尽可能提前支付所有费用，从广告和包装成本到保险费及各种存货费用无一例外。结果是：1997年的费用支出被显著压低，且这种压低显得极不自然。仅此一项，可能就在1997年为公司创造了约1500万美元的额外税后利润。

<!--en-->
One has to go to the 1997 year-end balance sheet to detect more of mother's little helpers. One notes a striking $23.2 million drop, from $40.4 million in 1996 to $17.2 million in 1997, in pre-paid expenses and other current assets. There's no mystery here, according to a former Sunbeam financial type. The huge restructuring charge in 1996 made it a lost year anyway, so Sunbeam pre-paid everything it could, ranging from advertising and packaging costs to insurance premiums and various inventory expenses. The result: Costs expensed for 1997 were reduced markedly, if unnaturally. This artifice alone probably yielded an additional $15 million or so in 1997 after-tax income.

为何Sunbeam的“其他流动负债”在1997年突然减少了1810万美元，而“其他长期负债”也减少了1900万美元？据公司内部人士称，答案很简单：1996年重组期间计提的各种产品保修准备金及其他项目，在1997年被悉数动用，从而可能为当年额外创造约2500万美元的净利润。

<!--en-->
Why did Sunbeam's "Other Current Liabilities" mysteriously drop by $18.1 million and "Other Long-Term Liabilities" fallby $19 million in 1997? The answer is simple, according to folks close to the company. Various reserves for product warranties and other items that were set aside during Sunbeam's giant 1996 restructuring were drained down in 1997, creating perhaps an additional $25 million or so in additional net income for the year.

除此之外，作为1996年重组开支的一部分，Sunbeam将其不动产、厂房、设备及商标的价值减少了9200万美元。虽然其中部分开支涉及即将出售的资产，但大部分仍与持续经营相关。这使得Sunbeam在1997年损益表上的折旧及摊销费用减少了近900万美元，进而又产生了约600万美元的额外税后利润。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
On top of all that, as part of the 1996 restructuring charge, Sunbeam reduced the value of its property, plant, equipment and trademarks by $92 million. Though some of these charges applied to assets Sunbeam was selling off, the bulk of the charge related to ongoing operations. This allowed Sunbeam to lower its depreciation and amortization expense on the 1997 income statement by nearly $9 million. That would create about $6 million of additional after-tax income.

奇怪的是，Sunbeam资产负债表上的不动产、厂房及设备净值在1997年反而从上一年的2.2亿美元上升至2.41亿美元。这很可能表明，产品开发、新包装以及某些广告营销活动所需的费用被资本化了，直接计入资产负债表，而非像以往那样在发生时即计入费用。通过这种方式，费用可以从1997年转移到未来年份，借助多年分摊的折旧机制逐步消化。否则，为何Sunbeam的广告及促销费用会从1996年的7150万美元骤降至去年的5640万美元呢？尤其是考虑到Sunbeam在1997年还推出了声势浩大的全国性电视广告活动以促进新产品销售。仅这一项广告费用的缩减，就为Sunbeam在1997年贡献了约1000万美元的利润。

<!--en-->
Oddly enough, the figure for net property, plant and equipment on Sunbeam's balance sheet still rose during 1997, to $241 million from $220 million the year before. This is likely an indication that such costs as product development, new packaging and some advertising and marketing initiatives were capitalized or put straight on the balance sheet instead of being expensed in the year they were incurred, as was the previous practice. In this manner, expenses could have been shifted from 1997 into future years, when they can be burned off at a slower, more decorous pace afforded by multi-year depreciation schedules. Why else would Sunbeam's advertising and promotion expense drop by some $15 million, from $71.5 million in 1996 to $56.4 million last year? Particularly when Sunbeam trotted out a splashy national television ad campaign in 1997 to boost consumer demand for its new products. This advertising shortfall alone contributed another $10 million to Sunbeam's 1997 profits.

该公司还因坏账准备和现金折扣减少了64%而受益良多：从1996年的2340万美元降至1997年的840万美元。尽管去年Sunbeam的销售额增长了19%，但这一数字仍出现了下降。1997年对这笔坏账准备的利用，很可能使净利润额外增加了约1000万美元。

<!--en-->
The company also got a nice boost from a 64% drop in its allowance for doubtful accounts and cash discounts, from $23.4 million in 1996 to $8.4 million in 1997. And this decline occurred despite a 19% rise in Sunbeam's sales last year. The milking of this bad debt reserve in 1997 likely puffed net income by an additional $10 million or so.

另一个谜团是：为何1997年Sunbeam的存货竟激增了约40%，即9300万美元？很有可能，Sunbeam通过操纵存货来美化损益表。企业通过全负荷运转并囤积存货，可以将固定间接费用从损益表转移到资产负债表上；这些费用会作为存货价值的一部分被保留下来，直到存货售出为止。为保守起见，我们假设这种存货积累对Sunbeam利润的促进作用约为1000万美元。

<!--en-->
Then there's the mystery of why Sunbeam's inventories exploded by some 40%, or $93 million, during 1997. Quite possibly, Sunbeam was playing games with its inventories to help the income statement. By running plants flat out and building inventories, a company can shift fixed overhead costs from the income statement to the balance sheet where they remain ensconced as part of the value of the inventory until such time as the inventory is sold. To be conservative, let's assume this inventory buildup might have helped Sunbeam's profits to the tune of, say, $10 million.

此外，有诸多迹象表明Sunbeam在1997年尽可能多地确认销售收入，以推高营收和利润。这种操纵行为早在去年年初便已开始：1996年底本已属于业绩不佳的一年，销售却被推迟至1997年。同样，《华尔街日报》也报道了1997年发生的几起“存货虚增”事件：Sunbeam要么向客户发送超出订单量的商品，要么在订单取消后仍继续发货。不过这些都属于企业为了美化季度业绩而常有的轻微违规行为。况且，Sunbeam当时给出的合理借口是：第一季度因计算机系统整合出现故障，导致公司一度无法掌握准确信息。

<!--en-->
Lastly, there are more than superficial indications that Sunbeam jammed as many sales as it could into 1997 to pump both the top and bottom lines. The revenue games began innocently enough early last year. Sales were apparently delayed in late 1996, a lost year anyway, and rammed into 1997. Likewise, *The Wall Street Journal* reported several instances of "inventory stuffing" during 1997, in which Sunbeam either sent more goods than had been ordered by customers or shipped goods even after an order had been canceled. But these are comparatively venial sins that companies engage in all the time to make a quarter's results look better. Besides, Sunbeam gave the plausible excuse at the time that glitches in a computer system consolidation in the first quarter had them flying blind for a time.

但随着1997年推进以及来自华尔街的业绩压力日益增大，Sunbeam开始越来越随意地调整销售条款以夸大当期业绩。例如，最新的10-K报告显示：去年第四季度，Sunbeam通过一项“提前购买”计划确认了约5000万美元的烤架销售收入；该计划允许零售商将付款时间推迟长达六个月。此外，其中约3500万美元被归类为“开票交货”销售，这些商品甚至从未离开Sunbeam的仓库。

<!--en-->
But as 1997 dragged on and the pressure to perform for Wall Street intensified, Sunbeam began to take greater and greater liberties with sales terms to puff current results. The latest 10-K, for example, discloses that in the fourth quarter of last year Sunbeam recorded some $50 million in sales of cooking grills under an "early buy" program that allowed retailers to delay payment for the items as long as six months. Moreover, some $35 million of these "early buys" were categorized "bill and hold" sales and never even left Sunbeam's warehouses.

据家电行业多位人士称，Sunbeam在其他产品线上也采用了开票交货的交易方式。例如第二季度，Sunbeam记录了一笔销售额，并将价值约1000万美元的毛毯“运送”到其位于密西西比州哈蒂斯堡配送中心附近租用的仓库中。这些货物为沃尔玛存放了数周之久。该公司还以极为宽松的付款条件向几家全国性小型家电分销商输送了数百万美元的商品，以至于令人怀疑这些交易是否真正发生。了解Sunbeam商业运作的人士称，在某些情况下，该公司虽将商品所有权转移给分销商，却不仅允许其延迟付款，甚至还会向分销商支付相当于仓储费的款项。这些消息来源还指出，有时分销商有权将商品退回给Sunbeam且无需承担任何损失。

<!--en-->
Sunbeam engaged in bill-and-hold transactions in other product lines, too, according to a number of people in the appliance industry. In the second quarter, for example, Sunbeam booked a sale and "shipped" some $10 million of blankets to a warehouse it had rented in Mississippi near its Hattiesburg distribution center. They were held there for some weeks for Wal-Mart. The company also pumped millions of dollars of goods into several national small-appliance distributors on such easy payment terms as to call into question whether a sale ever took place. Some with knowledge of Sunbeam's business practices say the appliance maker in some instances transferred title for the goods to distributors but then agreed to not only delay payment but actually pay the distributors what amounted to a storage charge for taking the goods. These sources also said that in some cases distributors also had the right to return the items to Sunbeam without suffering any loss.

各类可疑销售究竟为1997年的净利润增添了多少？外界无从确知。但根据Sunbeam的应收账款——即未收回的客户账款——在1997年增长了38%（即8200万美元）这一事实，我们可以做出合理推测：可疑销售可能使1997年净利润增加了多达800万美元。

<!--en-->
How much did various types of questionable sales add to 1997's net income? No outsider can know for sure. But we can make an educated guess based on the fact that Sunbeam's receivables, or unpaid customer accounts, jumped by 38%, or$82 million, in 1997. Taking into account Sunbeam's profit margins, it seems that questionable sales could have boosted 1997 net income by as much as $8 million.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程我们绝不可能知晓Sunbeam利用过往重组费用和未来销售来虚增当期收益的所有手段。“剖析阿尔·邓拉普”是一项艰巨的任务。但为了省去读者们的麻烦，我们估算出1997年人为虚增的利润约为1.2亿美元，而该公司实际公布的利润仅为1.094亿美元。因此，人们不禁要问：尽管邓拉普声称通过重组节省了约2.25亿美元成本，Sunbeam的实际经营业务究竟是否盈利？

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
We by no means are privy to all Sunbeam's techniques for harvesting current earnings from past restructuring charges and future sales. Deconstructing Al Dunlap is a daunting task. But to save our gentle readers the effort, our total estimate of artificial profit boosters in 1997 came to around $120 million compared with the $109.4 million profit the company actually reported. Thus, one is left to wonder whether Sunbeam made anything at all from its actual operations, despite Dunlap's claim to have realized some $225 million in cost savings as a result of his restructuring prowess.

我们对Sunbeam当前财务状况的悲观看法，在最新的10-K报告中该公司的合并现金流量表上得到了进一步证实。这些数字自然更难被人为调节，因为它们反映了1997年期间流入和流出公司的实际现金情况。而这份报表所呈现的画面并不乐观：尽管1997年净利润达到了令人瞩目的1.094亿美元，但扣除当年存货和应收账款的大幅增加后，Sunbeam的经营活动现金流仍为负820万美元。若不是1997年最后一周出售了5900万美元的应收账款，这一经营现金流赤字甚至会扩大到6720万美元。再加上5830万美元的资本支出，Sunbeam的自由现金流赤字便超过了1.25亿美元。

<!--en-->
Our dour view of Sunbeam's current financial health is only confirmed by the company's consolidated statement of cash flow in the latest 10-K. These numbers, of course, are harder to finesse because they track the actual cash that flowed in and out of the company during 1997. And the statement doesn't paint a pretty picture. Despite 1997's eye-catching $109.4 million net profit, Sunbeam still suffered negative cash flow from operations of $8.2 million, after taking into account the explosion in Sunbeam's inventory and accounts receivable during the year. And that operating cash flow deficit would have been an even larger $67.2 million if not for the sale of $59 million in receivables in the last week of 1997. After capital expenditures of $58.3 million is thrown into the equation, Sunbeam's free cash flow deficit amounts to more than $125 million.

Sunbeam第一季度业绩的惨淡表现，再次表明该公司状况堪忧。尽管管理层在4月份仍声称第一季度销售额将轻松超越1997年同期水平，但实际销售额却下降了4%。更令Dunlap的支持者震惊的是，今年第一季度公司亏损4460万美元，而去年同期还盈利690万美元。诚然，第一季度亏损中的3680万美元属于非经常性费用，主要是Dunlap在2月份谈成的一项丰厚薪酬方案所致。但Sunbeam 780万美元的经营亏损，明显反映出一旦1996年的重组费用耗尽后，公司真正的盈利能力究竟如何。

<!--en-->
Sunbeam's first-quarter earnings debacle is yet another sign of a company that's in anything but the pink of health. Despite management assertions into April that Sunbeam's first-quarter sales would finish comfortably ahead of those for the first quarter of 1997, they ended up declining 4%. Even more shocking to Dunlap's fans was the $44.6 million loss in the March quarter compared with a profit in the year-earlier period of $6.9 million. Sure, $36.8 million of that first-quarter loss was the result of nonrecurring charges, mostly a handsome new pay package Dunlap managed to negotiate in February. But the operating loss Sunbeam suffered of $7.8 million was a clear sign of its true earnings power once the tank from the 1996 restructuring charge had run dry.

Dunlap为该公司糟糕的第一季度业绩找了一堆借口：他提到前任第三号高管在4月份被Chainsaw解雇前与大型零售商签订的糟糕交易、厄尔尼诺现象对烧烤炉销售造成的负面影响等等。

<!--en-->
Dunlap trotted out a whole raft of excuses for the company's lamentable first-quarter performance. He cited dumb deals his former No. 3 executive had made with major retailers before Chainsaw fired him in April, the effect of bad weather on grill sales caused by El Nino, and so forth.

无论原因如何，第一季度的灾难并非源于Sunbeam在提升业绩方面缺乏努力。该公司录得了2900万美元的额外“先买后付”式烧烤炉销售额。事实上，如今在密苏里州Neosho的烧烤炉工厂周边仓库中堆积的烧烤炉数量之多，以至于公司不得不租赁俄克拉荷马州附近的仓储空间。谁知道这些烧烤炉中有多少最终能上架销售呢？

<!--en-->
Whatever the case, the first-quarter disaster wasn't the result of any lack of effort on Sunbeam's part to pump up the results. The company recorded $29 million of additional "buy now, pay later" grill sales. In fact, the company is now holding so many grills in various warehouses around its Neosho, Missouri, grill plant that it has had to lease warehouse space in nearby Oklahoma. Who knows how many of these grills will ever make it to the selling floor?

Sunbeam还将季度结算日延长了三天，从3月28日延至3月31日。此举使公司能够额外计入2000万美元的销售额，其中包括日常运营产生的销售额以及收购Coleman后两天所产生的销售额（收购于3月30日完成）。但这一切都无济于事：Sunbeam的销售额仍比去年的2.535亿美元少了900万美元。

<!--en-->
Sunbeam also extended its quarter by three days, from March 28 to March 31. This allowed the company to book an extra $20 million in sales both from ongoing Sunbeam operations and two days of sales from Coleman (its acquisition closed on March 30). But to no avail. Sunbeam still fell $9 million short of last year's sales of $253.5 million.

有报道称，Sunbeam试图强迫供应商“修改”各类商品和服务的发票，以便正式减少自身所欠款项。条件是供应商可以在第一季度结束后提交的发票中补回这笔被减免的金额及利息。一位Sunbeam财务官员否认了“修改发票”的指控，并将采购部门的行为描述为供应商与寻求折扣的企业之间常见的讨价还价过程。

<!--en-->
Reports are rife that Sunbeam tried to strong-arm suppliers into "rebutting" their invoices for various goods and services so that Sunbeam would officially owe less money. The proviso was that the suppliers would be allowed to add back the amount forgone, plus interest, in invoices submitted after the first quarter had ended. A Sunbeam financial official denies the "rebutting" charge and characterizes the activity by the company's procurement department as the normal give-and-take that goes on between suppliers and companies seeking rebates.

不过，一家中国供应商的负责人并不这么看。在接受《巴伦周刊》采访时，该负责人承认自己于3月底给Sunbeam寄去了一张50万美元的支票，相当于他与该公司年度业务额的5%。“我之所以寄支票而不是开新发票，是因为接到电话时我们并没有未结发票，”他解释道，“我们认为如果Sunbeam将这笔款项计入账目，我们的贡献就会被直接反映到净利润中。不过我也不清楚后来发生了什么。”

<!--en-->
But that's not the understanding held by an official at one China-based supplier. When contacted by Barron's, this official readily acknowledged that he had sent Sunbeam a check for $500,000, or 5% of the business he does annually with the company, in late March. "The only reason I sent them a check rather than a new invoice is that we had no invoices outstanding at the time we received the call," he explained. "We figure our contribution dropped right down to the bottom line if Sunbeam actually booked it. I don't know what happened, though."

预计在接下来的几个季度里，近期对Coleman、First Alert和Mr. Coffee的收购将有助于稳定Sunbeam的财务表现。为了整合这些新收购单位，Sunbeam将承担3.9亿美元（税前）的巨额重组费用，这正好为该公司操纵盈利数据提供了充足空间。该公司甚至预测今年每股收益将达到1美元，明年达到2美元——当然，这都是未计非经常性项目前的数字。

<!--en-->
For the next few quarters, expect the recent acquisition of Coleman, First Alert and Mr. Coffee to restore a measure of calm to Sunbeam's financial performance. The giant restructuring charges that Sunbeam is taking to integrate the new units, at $390 million before taxes, will give the company plenty of fodder with which to play earnings games. Thecompany is even forecasting earnings of $1 a share this year and $2 next year -- before extraordinary items, naturally.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：但邓拉普在Sunbeam公司的日子可能屈指可数了。这家本已陷入困境的公司如今还要背负20亿美元的新增债务，其有形净资产更是为负8亿美元。他的敌人——包括心灰意冷的股东、愤怒的证券分析师以及愤愤不平的前员工——数量不断增加，且正逐渐逼近位于德尔雷比奇的公司总部。当然，一旦情势危急，邓拉普随时可以借助大楼的平屋顶乘直升机逃离。只希望他记得带上那面美国国旗。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
But Dunlap's days at Sunbeam may be numbered. The already-ailing company now has to struggle under $2 billion of additional debt and a negative tangible net worth of $800 million. And his enemies, including disenchanted shareholders, angry securities analysts, and bitter former employees, are growing in number and circling ever closer to the company's headquarters in Delray Beach. Of course, Dunlap could always escape by using the building's flat roof to chopper out, should it come to that. One can only hope he'll remember to take the American flag with him.

## 格林布拉特课程第7讲

<!--en-->
*Greenblatt Class #7*

2005年3月30日

<!--en-->
March 30, 2005

## 以21倍预期收益的价格买入*MCO*股票，或者……

<!--en-->
Buying *MCO* at 21x Forward Earnings or

我们如何从*巴菲特*收购*可口可乐*的交易中吸取教训：笔记：*John Chew*；教授***乔尔·格林布拉特***；引言：

<!--en-->
How We Learned from *Buffett's* Purchase of *Coca-Cola*
Notes: *John Chew*
Professor ***Joel Greenblatt*** Introduction:

由来自*Gotham Partners*的我的合伙人***罗伯特·戈尔茨坦***进行讲解。他跟随我已有15或16年之久。他是一位杰出的投资者。

<!--en-->
Presentation by ***Robert Goldstein***, my partner from *Gotham Partners*. He has been with me for the last 15 or 16 years. He is a brilliant investor.

他将讲述我们作为价值投资者，为何会对某些公司支付比以往更高的价格。我们根据资产的实际价值而非低股价/账面价值或低市盈率来重新定义“价值”。这在某种程度上引发了与我们讨论*Amex*时类似的议题。这算是你工具箱中的又一种工具/手段：为优质公司支付合理的价格。你不必一辈子都这么做。我认为这样做更难，因为容错空间更小。**如果你打算支付高价，最好能透彻了解该业务，并明白它为何值得更高的估值。** 这很难做到，因为你很容易犯错。这个例子清楚地表明，当你试图确定某笔盈利流的合理倍数时，*资本回报率*的重要性不言而喻。

<!--en-->
He will talk about how we are value investors but we also are paying a lot more than we were accustomed for some company. *Redefining value* based on what it is worth rather than low price/book or low P/E. And it sort of opens up a similar discussion to what we talked about with *Amex* to some degree. It is sort of another tool/arrow in your quiver or in your arsenal. To pay a decent price for a good company. You do not have to go through life doing that. I think it is harder to do, because you have less room for error. **If you are going to pay up, you better understand the business and know why it should be worth more.** It is hard to do because you can screw up. This example certainly shows how important *returns on capital* are when you are trying to figure out a fair multiple for that earnings stream.

总结：投入资本的回报率是关键，但什么样的倍数才算公平？由于必须真正理解企业本质，因此购买优秀企业时的容错空间更小。

<!--en-->
Summary: Return on Invested Capital is key, but what multiple is fair? There is less room for error in buying great businesses since you must really understand the business.

*Rob*将分析一家我们曾支付高价收购的公司。课程的后半部分我们将探讨筛选技巧。***罗伯特·戈尔茨坦（RG）：*** 我们在*穆迪（MCO）*从*邓白氏*分拆出来后对其进行了研究，当时其股价相当于21倍预期收益。这种卓越性是否已被市场定价？

<!--en-->
*Rob* will go through an analysis of a company where we paid up.
The second half of the class we will go through screening techniques
***Robert Goldstein (RG):*** We were looking at *Moody's (MCO)* business after it's spin-off from *Dun & Bradstreet*, but it was priced at 21x forward earnings. Was the greatness priced in?

**为了解答这个问题，我们选择将我们可能收购的*穆迪*与*巴菲特收购可口可乐*的案例进行比较。**（这是对两个不同行业公司的创造性对比。）*巴菲特*于1988年开始买入*可口可乐*股票。他意识到通过收购一家优秀企业就能大赚一笔。1988年，*巴菲特*向*可口可乐*股票投资了6.5亿美元，支付的价格是过去收益的15倍。12年后，他的投资额增长了10倍。显然，他深知自己在做什么。那么问题来了：为什么*可口可乐*是一家优秀的企业？它处于成长期，资本回报率高，且拥有极其持久的竞争优势——五年后你仍能看到*可口可乐*及其优势，这与你最初购买该公司时并无二致。

<!--en-->
**To help answer that question we chose to compare our potential purchase of *Moody's* with *Buffett's purchase of Coke*.** *(This is a creative comparison of two companies in separate industries).*
*Buffett* began buying *Coke* in 1988. *Buffett* figured out that by buying a great business, he could make a fortune. In 1988, *Buffett* invested $650 million in *Coke* stock. He paid 15 times trailing earnings. 12 years later he was up 10 times his initial investment. Obviously, he knew what he was doing. The question then is why *Coke* is a great business? It was growing, it had high returns on capital and it had a very long lasting competitive advantage so five years down the road you are still going to have *Coke* and its advantages—the same as when you initially bought the company.

简单介绍一下背景：最初*穆迪*的收入来源于购买其评级服务的债券投资者。到了20世纪70年代，评级行业发生了巨大变化：评级公司开始向发行方和投资者同时收费。这对*穆迪*而言意义重大，因为这意味着评级机构获得了巨大的影响力，它们可以向希望发行债务的公司收费，否则这些公司将面临更高的市场借贷成本。

<!--en-->
To give you a little bit of history: originally *Moody's* revenue came from bond investors who paid for *Moody's* ratings. Then the rating industry changed dramatically in the 1970s because the rating companies began to charge issuers as well as investors. And this was a huge deal for *Moody's* because it meant that rating agencieshad gained so much clout, they could charge companies who wished to issue debt or else they would face higher borrowing costs in the market.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：如今*穆迪*和*标普*在评级行业中各占约40%的市场份额。企业通常会从两家评级机构获得评级。由于评级在资本市场中至关重要，发行债务的公司会同时从这两家公司获取评级，以免过度依赖单一评级机构。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Today *Moody's* and *S&P* both have about 40% of the rating industry. Frequently companies get ratings from both rating agencies. Since ratings are very important in the capital market, companies issuing debt will get ratings from both companies since these companies do not want to be dependent upon one rating agency.

<table><thead><tr><th><i>MCO</i>2000财年</th><th>营收增长率</th><th>营业利润增长率</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>19年间的增长率</td><td>15%</td><td>17%</td></tr><tr><td colspan="3">19年间仅有1年出现营收下滑。表现极为稳定。</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th><i>MCO</i>'s 2000 FY</th><th>Revenue Growth Rate</th><th>Operating Profit Growth Rate</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Growth rate for 19 years</td><td>15%</td><td>17%</td></tr><tr><td colspan="3">In 19 years only 1 year of decline in revenue. Very stable.</td></tr></tbody></table>

过去的成功是否等于未来的成功？有时是，有时不是。考虑到其漫长的时间跨度，*MCO*的增长率堪称惊人。

<!--en-->
Does past success = future success? Sometimes it does and sometimes it doesn't. *MCO's* growth rate is phenomenal considering its long time period.

看看*市场份额的稳定性*。过去25年间，全球公共债务市场迅速扩张。本质上来说，债务市场出现了去中介化现象：银行放贷减少，因此企业转向在公开市场上发行更多债券，从而需要更多的信用评级。抵押贷款、汽车贷款等证券化产品增多——金融市场不断演变。但市场份额并未发生太大变化——主要由*穆迪*和*标普*主导。我们得出的结论是，*MCO*的增长势头有望持续。欧洲和亚洲市场的崛起将为其提供未来增长动力，且竞争压力较小。

<!--en-->
Look at the *market share stability*. The global public debt market grew rapidly over the past 25 years. Basically what was happening was that there was disintermediation in the debt markets. Banks were doing less lending so companies were moving to issue more debt in the public markets, therefore they needed more ratings. You had more securitizations for mortgage loans, car loans—the financial markets were evolving. The market share had not changed much—it was predominantly *Moody's* and *S&P*. It was our conclusion that *MCO's* growth was likely to continue. Europe and Asia emergence can provide future growth. Less competitive pressure.

很容易理解为何该领域会有巨大的未来增长空间且竞争压力不大。两家评级机构都需要付费才能提供服务。由于信誉至关重要，外人几乎不可能进入这一行业。无论该业务多么盈利或发展多快，竞争对手都难以获得客户首席财务官的信任，也难以轻易进入市场。这就像向黑手党交保护费一样。

<!--en-->
It was easy to understand there would be a lot of future growth and not much competitive pressure. Both rating agencies had to be paid. It was very unlikely someone could enter the business because you need credibility. No matter how profitable the business or fast it was growing, a competitor could not obtain the confidence of the customer's CFO nor enter the market easily. It is like paying the Mafia.

1999年12月，*邓白氏*宣布将拆分为两家公司。当时*D&B*的股价为每股27美元，投资者将获得0.5股*MCO*股票。即便在最糟糕的情况下，假设1股D&B股票价值15美元，那么这0.5股的价值就是每股7.5美元。实际上相当于每股支付24美元。当时我预计*穆迪*在2000年的每股收益将达到0.95美元。

<!--en-->
In December 1999, *Dun & Bradstreet* announced that they would split into two businesses. *D&B* was selling for $27 a share and you were going to get ½ a share of *MCO* and we assume in a worse case scenario that one share of D&B was worth $15 so the half share was at $7.5 per share. You were effectively paying $24 a share. At the time, I expected *Moody's* to earn $0.95 per share in 2000.

***乔尔·格林布拉特：*** 当时我们根本无法确定*D&B*的股价会如何变动，因此我们采用的7.50美元这一数字相当保守；我们认为这就是我们支付价格的最坏情况。

<!--en-->
***Joel Greenblatt:*** At the time we had no idea where *D&B* would trade, so the $7.50 we were using was very conservative, so we thought this was a worst case of what we were paying.

这意味着按照0.95美元的每股收益计算，我们支付的价格相当于21倍预测收益。这一数值远高于*巴菲特*购买*可口可乐*时所支付的4.5至5美元——他购买*可口可乐*时的市盈率为13至15倍。

<!--en-->
This meant that at a $0.95 EPS we were paying 21x forward earnings. Much more than *Buffett* paid $4.5 to $5 for *Coke*—he paid 13x–15x for *Coke*.

***乔尔·格林布拉特：*** 这对我们而言是个全新的投资对象。我们从未见过像*MCO*这样优秀的企业：拥有19年的持续增长记录且无需再投入资金。于是我们向大师*巴菲特*取经，挑选了他曾成功投资过的标的（*KO*）。乍一看，从图表中我们能看到这些。我们获得的交易条件能与1988年巴菲特购买*可口可乐*时相提并论吗？乍看之下似乎并非如此。哥伦比亚大学商学院198期特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
***Joel Greenblatt:*** This was a new animal for us. We had never seen a business (*MCO*) this good with a 19-year growth rate and no need to reinvest money. So we went back to the Master, *Buffett*, and picked something (*KO*) that worked out well for him. So at first blush, if you looked at (the chart), this is what we saw. Were we getting as good a deal as *Buffett* did buying *Coke* in 1988? At first blush it does not look that way.

*可口可乐*将其投资资本的80%返还给股东，其市盈率从13倍升至40倍。其中三分之一的收益来自市盈率的扩张。

<!--en-->
*Coke* returned 80% of its invested capital return to shareholders and the P/E expanded from 13 to 40. 1/3 of the gain came from P/E expansion.

*沃伦·巴菲特*以5美元的价格购入*可口可乐*，12年后股价涨至58美元（不含所收股息）。截至2000年6月，4.75美元的股息按6%的收益率计算，可带来6美元的股息收入。12年间股价从5美元涨至64美元（即58美元+6美元）。不计税收因素，年化收益率高达23%。

<!--en-->
*Warren Buffett* paid $5 for *Coke* and in 12 years it went to $58 (not including dividends received). Investment at June 2000: $4.75 in dividends x 6% rate of return = $6 in dividends by June of 2000. $5 to $64 or ($58+ $6) in 12 years. Leave taxes out so you get a 23% CAGR.

他最初投入的5美元在12年后变成了64美元。这引出了下一个问题：为什么*可口可乐*的表现如此出色？

<!--en-->
His initial outlay of $5 turned into $64 in 12 years. That brings us to the next question—why did *Coke* do so well?

答案：*可口可乐*的净资产收益率在很长一段时间内都居高不下。

<!--en-->
Answer: *Coke*'s ROE was high for a very long time.
