股票回购使每股收益每年增长15%。可口可乐的管理层将20%的盈利重新投资于业务以实现这一增长，他们通过股息或股票回购将每投入一美元中的80%返还给股东。这正是其回报如此优异的重要原因。此外，市盈率从13倍升至40倍——市盈率的扩张导致了股价涨幅的三分之一。

<!--en-->
Share buybacks help grow the EPS by 15% a year. *Coke*'s management invested 20% of their earnings back into the business to produce that growth and they returned 80% of each dollar invested in the firm of dividends or share repurchases. That had a lot to do with why the return was so good. In addition, the P/E multiple went from 13 xs to 40 xs—the P/E expansion caused 1/3 of the price gain.

由于可口可乐在强大品牌、分销渠道、优秀管理及公司治理方面的竞争优势，未来10年前景同样看好。这也是投资者愿意为该公司股票支付高溢价的部分原因。

<!--en-->
The next 10 years looked good as well due to *Coke*'s competitive advantages of strong brand, distribution, good management and corporate governance. This is in part what made investors pay up for the stock.

让我们暂时回到MCO的话题上。我们对增长的假设是：MCO的营业利润增长率为17%，尽管这一增长率很高，但表现却十分稳定。

<!--en-->
Let's go back to *MCO* for a moment. Our assumptions for growth? *MCO*'s 17% operating income growth which, despite this high growth rate, was very stable.

**学生：** 在这19年间你可能会看到许多趋势变化——或许最后一年增长有所放缓？哥伦比亚大学商学院199期特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
**Student:** You might see a lot of trends within those 19 years—perhaps growth in trailing off in the last year?
199
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**RG：** 实际上，增长非常*稳定*。

<!--en-->
**RG:** Actually the growth was very *stable*.

**学生：** 先假设没有增长，然后再重新设定增长假设？

<!--en-->
**Student:** Assume no growth and then back into a growth assumption?

**RG：** 这其实*并无定论*。我们假定12%的增长率，是因为推动其增长的因素依然存在。尽管MCO每年的增长率超过17%，但管理层还是要求我们把增长预期下调至12%。

<!--en-->
**RG:** There really is *no science* to it. We assumed 12% growth rate because many of the factors that drove their growth were still in place. Even though *MCO* had grown annually at over 17%, management basically had us lower our growth assumptions to 12%.

我们试图选择一个自己感到放心且认为相当保守的增长假设，然后判断其是否仍具合理性。**没有任何事物能永远保持12%的增长。**因此我们假设未来5到10年内增长率为12%。

<!--en-->
We try to pick something (growth assumptions) that we feel comfortable with and we think is very conservative and then see if it still makes sense. **Nothing grows for 12% forever.** So we assumed 12% for the next 5 years to 10 years.

我们认为MCO的增长动力仍然存在。我们力求做到*极为保守*：未来5到10年保持12%的增长率。公共金融市场发展与银行贷款情况也是考虑因素。我们假设亚洲市场和欧洲市场能为MCO提供额外的增长机会。这家企业将伴随全球经济增长而发展。

<!--en-->
We felt *MCO*'s growth factors were still in place. We try to be very *conservative*. 12% growth for 5 to 10 years. Public financial markets growing vs. bank lending. We assumed Asia's market and Europe's market was a source of additional growth opportunities for *MCO*. This business will grow with global growth.

资本需求极少——几乎无需额外资本。MCO本质上就是一群坐在房间里使用电脑的人而已。

<!--en-->
Capital needs were minimal—no real capital needs. *MCO* was basically some guys in a room with computers.

**MCO无需资本即可实现增长这一特点，对我们愿意为它支付的金额有何影响呢？**可口可乐的营业利润增长率为12%。可口可乐每投入一美元便向股东返还0.80美元。

<!--en-->
**How does *MCO*'s no need for capital to grow figure into how much more we would be willing to pay for *MCO*?**
*Coke* was growing its operating earnings 12%. *Coke* sent back $0.80 to shareholders for every dollar invested.

MCO每投入一美元可返还1美元甚至更多。可口可乐返还0.80美元，而MCO则返还1.00美元，即多出25%。

<!--en-->
*MCO* could send back $1 or more for every dollar invested. $0.80 for KO vs. $1.00 for *MCO* returned or 25% more.

现在我们来关注MCO的资本回报率。由于其几乎不占用资本（仅涉及桌椅和电脑），其资本回报率实际上是无限的。

<!--en-->
Now we focus on *MCO*'s ROC. It's ROC was infinite because they use almost no capital (chairs, desks and computers).

**你愿意为MCO支付比巴菲特购买可口可乐时更高的价格吗？** 盈利等于自由现金流，且无需资本支出。对于可口可乐而言，有20%的利润需留存于企业内，因此它通过股票回购和股息向股东返还相当于每美元80美分的数额。

<!--en-->
**How much more could you pay for *MCO* than *Buffett* paid for his *Coke*?**
Earnings = Free cash flow with no capex needs. With *Coke* 20 cents had to be retained in the business so they repaid shareholders through share buybacks and dividends the equivalent of 80 cents of every dollar.

每1美元的*MCO*价值比*Coke*的1美元高出25%。作为*MCO*的股东，你的现金流将比持有*Coke*时高出25%。

<!--en-->
Every $1 of *MCO* is worth 25% more than *Coke*'s $1. Your cash flow as a *MCO* shareholder will be 25% higher than *Coke*'s.

若要让*Coke*实现每年12%的增长，其投资规模需比*MCO*多出25%。当*Coke*报告每股1美元的盈利时，对你而言其实际价值仅相当于从*MCO*获得的80美分。一旦增长放缓至5%，*MCO*仍能让你每投入1美元收回1美元；而*Coke*则只能让你收回90美分。为何增长放缓时你只能收回90美分？因为用于增长的资本支出减少了。

<!--en-->
For *Coke* to grow 12% a year, it has to invest 25% more than *MCO*. When *Coke* reports a $1 per share in earnings that is really only worth 80 cents to you compared to the dollar you get back from *MCO*. Down the road when growth slows, so say when growth slows to 5%, with *MCO* you will still get back $1 for each $1 invested. With *Coke* you will get back 90 cents on each dollar. Why would you get 90 cents back when growth slows? Because of *less* growth capex.

假设增长率为5%、资本回报率为50%，则可得出10%的再投资率。套用公式“增长率/ROC=再投资率”：$5%/50\% = 10\%$。因此，那25%的差异最终会缩小至10%到11%。

<!--en-->
Take a growth rate of 5% and a 50% return on capital gets me a 10% reinvestment rate. Plug into a formula of growth rate/ROC = reinvestment rate: $5%/50\% = 10\%$. So that 25% disparity will shrink to 10% to 11% at some point.

*巴菲特*买入时的市盈率为13倍，但我们愿意多付15%，即13倍乘以1.15，等于*MCO*的市盈率为15倍——因为从长期看，*MCO*的盈利价值对我们而言要高出15%。

<!--en-->
*Buffett* paid 13 times earnings but we are willing to pay 15% more so 13x multiplied by 1.15 = 15x earnings for *MCO* because *MCO*'s earnings are worth 15% more long term to us.

我们愿意支付15倍的预期盈利来取得与*巴菲特*相同的投资结果；这一数值远远低于21倍的市盈率。

<!--en-->
We can pay 15 times forward earnings to get the same result that *Buffett* got based on that different ROC which is a long way off from 21x earnings.

*MCO*于9月上市，我们则在12月开始研究它。*巴菲特*也是买家。我们仍需弄清楚自己在做什么。*巴菲特*绝不会允许管理层滥用股东的资本。

<!--en-->
*MCO* came public in September and we looked at it in December. *Buffett* was a buyer. We still had to understand what we are doing. *Buffett* won't allow management to be stupid with the shareholder's capital.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：我们买入公司的门槛比他更高。我们选择的并非大盘股，而是其他标的。对他而言15%的回报率或许不错，但我们的门槛可能设定为20%。我们早就知道这是一家具备强大经济特性和进入壁垒的特许经营类企业（即WEB业务）。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Our hurdle for buying companies is much higher than his. We pick and choose other than large caps. 15% return might be great for him, but our hurdle might be 20%. We did know it was a *WEB* business with these numbers (a franchise-like business with strong economics and barriers to entry).

***MCO***是一家具有可重复性和增长潜力的服务型企业——关键问题在于**可重复性与增长前景**。值得称赞的是它无需大量资本投入。数据就是事实；关键在于团队和商业模式能否维持这些数据的增长或稳定。

<!--en-->
***MCO*** is a service business with repeatable business and growth—the key question to answer is **repeatability and growth prospects**. Good for them not to have to use much capital. The numbers are the numbers. How good are the people and the franchise to keep those numbers growing or stable.

1988年*巴菲特*买入*Coke*时，利率比现在高出40%。如果*巴菲特*支付的股价比5美元高出40%，那么*Coke*的买入价将是每股7美元。如此一来，他的年化收益率将从23%降至20%。

<!--en-->
Interest rates were 40% higher when *Buffett* bought *Coke* in 1988. If *Buffett* paid 40% more than $5, then he would have paid $7 per share for *Coke*. Then he would have earned 20% CAGR vs. 23%.

对比30年期国债收益率：过去为9%，如今为6%。剔除利率下降对业绩的影响后，市盈率可视为盈利收益率。1988年至2000年间利率较高。**这一点至关重要：利率从9%降至6%，降幅达40%；因此2000年时未来盈利的价值便增加了40%。**若调整后市盈率为15（而*Coke*为13，因*MCO*的盈利价值更高），再乘以1.4（鉴于2000年较低的利率水平），结果便是21倍。*巴菲特*的投资表现会如何呢？股价从5美元涨至46美元（而*Coke*则为64美元）。将*KO*的估值下调30%，便得到70美分的价值。

<!--en-->
Compare a 30 year T-bond yield (9%) then to now (6%). Remove the drop in interest rate to adjust performance. P/E as an earnings yield. During 1988 – 2000 Interest rates were higher. **This was key because interest rates fell from 9% to 6%, a 40% decline. So, in 2000 the future earnings would be worth 40% more.**
If our adjusted P/E is 15 (vs. 13 for *Coke* because *MCO*'s earnings are worth more) and you multiplied that by 1.4 (because of the lower interest rates now prevailing in 2000) you get 21x. How would *Buffett* have done? $5 to $46 (vs. $64). Knock *KO* down by 30% to get a 70 cents dollar.

10年期国债收益率为6%。养老基金期望从股票中获得的回报率为2%至8%——任选其一即可。

<!--en-->
A 6% 10-year T-bond. What Pension Funds expect to earn in stock--2% to 8%--pick a number.

*巴菲特*的投资收益得益于利率下降。让我们把利率因素排除在外：他的回报率从23%降至20%，现在我们假定最低回报率为16%。再给予最终结果30%的折扣，最终结果为70美分，即70% × 64 = 45。

<!--en-->
*Buffett*'s investment rose because of the interest rate drop. So let's take the drop in interest rates out of the equation. *Buffett*'s return drops from 23% to 20%, now we assume 16% minimum return. We take 30% discount to the end result gets you 70 cents on the dollar to 70% x 64 = 45.

在当前的利率环境下，你所损失的正是未来股票回报率的预期值。如果我们以最低的6%债券收益率为基准，并假设人们长期在养老基金中期望获得8%的年回报率，那么正如*Rob*所说：如果*WEB*没有受益于利率下降，其年化回报率将是20%而非23%。

<!--en-->
Part of what you lose in this interest rate environment. Expectations on future stock returns are lower. So if we take our minimum 6 percent bond and say people over time in their pension funds expect to earn 8% a year. So here *Rob* said if *WEB* didn't have the benefit of interest rates falling, he would have returned 20% a year instead of 23%.

我们为*MCO*支付溢价，因此不会指望利率走势对我们有利。我们设定的年化回报率为16%。

<!--en-->
We are paying a premium for what we are paying for *MCO*, so we are not going to assume interest rates will go our way. We will make 16% a year.

***乔尔·格林布拉特（JG）：***我是这样看的：假设三年或五年后事态如预期发展，公司每年盈利增长12%，同时回购股票，人们也会认为这是一家好企业。**三年后，如果*MCO*的定价能使年化回报率达到8%，股价可能会翻倍。由于众人都能看到同样的机会，你可能在两年内就拿到其中50%的收益。我们甚至可能因股价快速上涨而提前获得回报，进而实现**估值扩张**，而且这一过程有时相当迅速。**人们可能会问：如果想在未来几年获得X价值的资产，我需要付出多少成本才能确保每年8%的回报率？这就是实现**估值扩张**的方式。**

<!--en-->
***Joel Greenblatt (JG):*** I look at it this way: let us go three years out or five years out and say the story plays out as expected. The company earns grows 12% a year, they are buying back their stock and people see that it is a good business. **Well, in three years if they price *MCO* to return 8% a year, so the stock may double. You may collect 50% of that in two years' time because everyone sees what you see. We may get paid **upfront** by a faster rise in the stock due to a big multiple bump.**
People may say what do I have to pay to get 8% a year if it is going to be worth X in a few years? That is how you get your **multiple expansion** and sometimes fairly quickly.

如果你分析得当，市场通常能给出正确的定价。如果我预计该公司十年内年化收益率能达到16%，那么三年内我的平均年化收益率可能高达40%。如果市场要求的折现率为8%，我的大部分收益可能会在短期内实现。

<!--en-->
Mr. Market usually gets it right if you have done your analysis correctly. If in 10 years, I believe it will earn 16% a year, then in three years I may be averaging 40% per year. A big chunk of my return may come in the near term if the market charges a 8% discount rate.

实际上，这就是*MCO*所经历的情况。它的市盈率从21倍升至30倍，之后年回报率便降至8%。股价并不会以线性方式变动。

<!--en-->
In effect that is what happened to *MCO*'s. It went from a 21x multiple to a 30x multiple then the return drops to 8% a year after that. The stock price will not move in a linear fashion.

不知您是否记得我们研究*Duff & Phelps*时曾设定了三种增长情景。然而我们**仍然**低估了其增长率。实际上，*MCO*产品的应用场景出现了爆发式增长；不过当时它仅占据了市场的一小部分份额，你自然能预见到这一趋势会持续下去。随后几年里，其盈利增长率达到了30%至40%。这种情形在分拆上市的公司中很常见，它们往往能高效运作。做出这些预测其实很复杂，有时也会出错。

<!--en-->
I don't know if you remember when we looked a *Duff & Phelps* and we had three scenarios of growth. Yet we **still** undershot the growth rate. There was in effect an explosion in the different uses for *MCO*'s product, but you knew the trend was going your way; they had only penetrated a small percentage of the market. The trend in earnings grew 30% to 40% for a few years. This happens with a spin-off where they do things efficiently. It is complicated to make these assumptions and sometimes you are wrong.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：坦率地说，我们以21美元买入，以35-36美元卖出。在我们最乐观的情景中，该股股价可达70美元。其中一种较为合理的情景预计时间为三年，而股价也确实达到了那个水平。但我们并未持有——没理由做错事。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
Frankly, we bought it at $21 and sold it at $35-$36. In our good scenario we had a $70 stock. One of our reasonable scenarios was three years. The stock did go there. We didn't hold it—any reason to do the wrong thing.

*RG*今天提出的观点中有许多重要之处。**不仅要看公司的盈利多少，还要看它能留存多少以及能否维持其增长率。** 关于增长与ROIC——需审视为维持增长所需的资本投入。

<!--en-->
There are so many important points in what *RG* brought up today. **It is not only important how much a company earns but how much you get to keep and still get your growth rate.** Growth and ROIC --- examine the capital investment requirements to grow.

显然，*Coke*为了维持其增长率，必须将20%的现金流重新投入业务；但*MCO*的业务模式更佳，无需再追加投资，因此这些盈利的价值更高。**这是一种非常重要的看待世界的方式。** 你可以算出16%的年回报率——这相当不错，但算不上卓越。但如果你放眼全局，认为它在三四年后能达到这样的盈利水平，且届时基于ROC和盈利增长能获得合理的市盈率，那么我就能获得惊人的回报率。

<!--en-->
Obviously, *Coke* had to put 20% of their cash flows back into their business to maintain their growth rate, but *MCO* even had a better business where they did not have to reinvest anything and those earnings were worth more. **This is a very important way of looking at the world.** You can do all your calculations and say 16% annual returns—that is pretty good—not great. But if you look at the world, this is what I think it is going to earn in three or four years, and if it gets a fair multiple at that time based on ROC and earnings growth, I could get an astronomical rate of return.

*MCO*是一家独特的、非常出色的企业。如果我们能将其与*S&P*单独对比，或许就会这么做。但我们的大部分收益并非来自可比分析；这只是一种参照。要么是因为可比公司股价更高，从而说明这是更好的投资，你便想弄明白为何该股票未能达到那些可比水平；

<!--en-->
*MCO* was a unique business, a considerably great business. If we could have compared this to *S&P* as a stand alone, I guess we would have done that. But most of our money is *not* made on comparable analysis; it is a check. Either the comparables are trading much higher and this is a better investment and you want to know *why* your stock is not trading at those comparable levels.

要么是整个行业估值过低，你偶然发现这一点，或经过分析后认定它是其中最便宜的，或者你最看好它的业务模式，因而愿意支付稍高的价格。所以这是多种因素的综合结果。通常我们不会基于大宗商品或油价进行主题性投资。

<!--en-->
Or all of the industry is trading too low and either you stumble across or you did the analysis and this is the cheapest of the bunch or you like their business the best. And you are willing to pay up a little bit. So it is a *combination* of factors. Usually we are finding a situation where we — we don't make thematic investments based on the price of commodities or oil.

**这是我们首次为一家公司支付21倍的 normalized earnings 对价。** 这算是一种警钟长鸣。我们实在不想再这样做。但让我们做个练习，看看是否能为其找到合理依据——毕竟它确实奏效。一旦某种做法行之有效，就很难改变。显然，许多表现优异的公司都会遭遇此类情况：它们因执着于核心业务而未能察觉竞争者的崛起，最终措手不及。

<!--en-->
**This was the first time we paid 21 times normalized earnings for a company.** This was sort of a wake-up call. We really don't want to do this. But let us do this exercise to see if we can justify this because it works. If you are doing something that works, it is very hard to do something different. Obviously this can happen to a lot of companies that are doing well. They don't see the competition coming because they want to hold onto their core business. They get blind-sided.

在这种特定情况下，总有多种赚钱途径。我向您传授的是我们的方法，但这*并非*唯一的赚钱之道。我认为这是一种可行的方法。如果您有更好的办法，那也很好。我们一直都有机会投资廉价资产，也就是我所说的“价格稍高的优质企业”。这只是另一种可供比较的选项，也是您工具箱中的*另一件武器*。

<!--en-->
In this particular case there is always money to be made in many different ways. Just because I am teaching you the way we do it, it is *not* the only way to make money. It is a way that I think works. If you have something better to do, that is fine. We have always had an opportunity to invest in cheap stuff. In what I call a good business at a little higher price. This is something more to compare and *another weapon* in your arsenal.

投身于优秀企业、目睹诸多利好随之而来后，再去购买那些“烟蒂股”确实很有诱惑力。那样也能赚不少钱。但这属于另一种游戏。*巴菲特*已无法再玩这种游戏了。

<!--en-->
It is very seductive to be in great businesses and see a lot of good things flying off of that to then go and buy cigar butts after that. There is plenty of money to be made at that. It is a bit of a little different game. *Buffett* can't play in that anymore.

假设企业能延续现有模式，几乎等同于一种*盲目相信*。您打算如何在未来取得那些卓越成果？他们将如何运用资本？像*MCO*这样的公司，可预测性并不强。

<!--en-->
It is almost taking a *leap of faith* to assume that the business will continue as it has. What is your plan to get those great results in the future? What will they do with the capital? With something like *MCO* there are not many calls you can make.

分析的一部分是了解行业背景、阅读分析师报告。**大多数人会认为这是一家好公司，但估值合理。** 三年后，*MCO*的预期市盈率可能达到30-35倍。出于与我要求长期债券收益率不低于6%相同的理由，我不会给任何公司30倍的normalized earnings市盈率。30倍对应3.3%的回报率——对于所承担的风险而言，这个回报太低了。

<!--en-->
Part of the analysis is taking a background of the industry. Read analyst reports. **Most people would have said a good business but fairly valued.** In three years from now, *MCO* could be at 30x – 35xs prospective earnings. There is no business I would give a 30x multiple to on normalized earnings for the same reason I would never use less than a 6% yield on a long term bond. 30x would be 3.3% return—a return too low for the risk.

我们原本期望的增长率超过12%，但为保守起见采用了这一数值。你常能听到很多聪明人的见解，但我们并不那么聪明。我们花了半小时回顾那些售出后价格翻番的股票，犯了不少错误。能犯各种错误却仍能赚钱，这倒是件好事。

<!--en-->
We were hoping for more growth than 12% but used that for a conservative rate. You hear a lot of smart people, but we are not that smart. We spent ½ hour going over stuff we sold that subsequently doubled. We made a lot of errors. It is good to make a lot of different errors and still make money.

我们关注*MCO*是因为它属于头号分拆股。人们都在等着看这种情况发生。**我不想在人们等待的*心理原因*上浪费太多时间。** 21倍的估值看起来并不那么诱人。其实它的表现相当不错。问题在于*巴菲特*早就入手了，而我们却在5个月后才买入。无论如何我们都会关注分拆股。所以我想说：如果你看到某只股票估值为21倍，只要这家企业足够优秀，就值得考虑。

<!--en-->
We looked at *MCO* because it was a spin-off number 1. People wait to see it happen. **I don't want to waste too much time on the *psychological reasons* people wait.** 21x doesn't look that enticing. How good thisactually was. The question would be that *Buffett* filed on it and yet we bought it 5 months later. We look at spin offs anyway. So I would say that if you see something at 21x then look at it if the business is exceptional.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**学生：** 您多久会转向更优质的企业？

<!--en-->
**Student:** How often do you migrate to higher quality businesses?

## 投资组合管理

<!--en-->
*Portfolio Management*

**JG：** 这样的机会很少出现。**我们会持有5到8只证券，时间为1至5年。** 我们可能一年只需要找到一个合适的标的。比如我们可能只会持有*美国运通*几周时间。*AXP*与*可口可乐*类似，在某些方面甚至更优。

<!--en-->
**JG:** Everything comes up rarely. **We hold 5 to 8 securities for a year to 2-5 years.** We may only need to find *one* idea a year. We may do *American Express* for a few weeks. *AXP* is similar to *Coke* and it may be better in some ways.

目前，小盘股市场在2003年上涨了50%到100%，2004年又继续上涨。**如今大部分价值都集中在规模较大、业绩优良的公司中。** 当小盘股市场暴跌，我能以6倍市盈率买入零售股时，我不会挑剔，就会出手。现在，一些优质公司正是绝佳的买入机会。

<!--en-->
Right now, the market for small cap stock was up 50% to 100% in 2003 and it was up again in 2004. **Most of the values are in bigger, good companies right now.** When the small cap market gets killed and I can buy retailers at 6x earnings, then I am not picky, I will go do that. Right now some of these better companies are where some of the better deals are.

我不会将两者相互比较。我的投资决策取决于我先发现哪个标的。只要价格足够低、能满足我的要求即可。毕竟世界很大，选择很多。更重要的是你了解什么、擅长什么——也就是你的能力圈。

<!--en-->
I am not measuring one against another. It (my interest/investment) depends upon which I found first. What is cheap enough to meet the hurdle. Basically it is a big world out there, there is plenty to choose from. It is more what you know and what you feel competent in. Your circle of competence.

**想想这有多强大吧——知道某事物的*真实价值*是非常强大的。这些信息几乎就是*一切*。** 你能够展望未来三四年，而不必担心接下来一两年的情况，也不必在意别人的表现。这就是投资的精髓所在。

<!--en-->
**Think how powerful that is—knowing what something is *worth* is very powerful. That information is *almost everything*.** And you have the ability to look ahead three or four years and not worry about the next year or two. And not worry about how other people are doing. That is the whole ball game.

**你们现在都足够聪明，能够做估值工作，也知道何时自己掌握了关键信息——这时就需要*实践*了。** 你们现在很聪明，但缺乏经验。必须经历实践的磨练才能不断进步。可以说我们在所从事的领域持续进步。我们仍然会犯很多错，但能有所改进就是好事；只不过犯错的类型有所不同。随着不断学习，我们的选择也会更多。**你永远都在学习，也永远都在进步。** 当你以为自己已经掌握了一切时，其实并没有。要预期自己正确的次数多于错误的次数。*休息结束*

<!--en-->
**You are all smart enough now to do valuation work. And know when you know it and that is where *practice* comes in.** You are smart enough now, but you don't have the experience. And you need to go through the school of hard knocks and you will keep getting better. I would say we keep getting better at what we are doing. We still make tons of mistakes, so it is good that we got better, but we make different ones. It gives us more to choose from as we keep learning. **You always keep learning and you always get better.** When you think you have it knocked, you don't. Expect to be right more than you are wrong.
*Back from break*

**乔尔·格林布拉特：** 你无法从教科书里找到关于*穆迪*的这种分析，我们花了很长时间才形成这种思路。*罗布*和我希望自己能早点拥有这些宝贵见解。如有不明白之处，请随时提问。本次讲座到此结束。

<!--en-->
**Joel Greenblatt:** You can't get this analysis of *Moody's* from a text book and it took us a long time to think this way. *Rob* and I wished we had this good stuff. Ask questions if you don't understand this.

## 其他来源的补充笔记

<!--en-->
*Additional Notes from other sources*

摘自罗伯特·哈格斯特朗所著的《巴菲特之道》：**巴菲特为何在1988年购买*可口可乐*？** 1988年巴菲特首次购入*可口可乐*时，人们问道：“*可口可乐*的价值何在？”当时该公司的市盈率为15倍，现金流倍数为12倍——分别比市场平均水平高出30%和50%。巴菲特以5倍账面价值的价格买入一家盈利收益率为6.6%的公司，而当时长期利率高达9%。他之所以愿意这么做，是因为*可口可乐*拥有非凡的*经济商誉*。该公司资本投入较少却能产生31%的净资产收益率。巴菲特指出，价格并不能反映价值。***可口可乐*的价值取决于其整个经营周期内预计产生的所有者收益总和，并按适当利率折现。** 1988年，*可口可乐*的所有者收益达到8.28亿美元。当时30年期国债（无风险利率）的收益率约为9%。将*可口可乐*1988年的所有者收益按9%折现后，其内在价值约为92亿美元。巴菲特购买*可口可乐*时，其市场价值为148亿美元（溢价65%），这意味着他可能买贵了。

<!--en-->
From *The Essential *Buffett* by Robert Hagstrom: **Why *Buffett* purchased *Coke* in 1988**
When *Buffett* first purchased *Coke* in 1988, people asked: **“Where is the value in *Coke*?”** The company's price was 15 times earnings and 12 times cash flow – 30% and 50% premiums to the market average. *Buffett* paid five times book value for a company with a 6.6% earnings yield during a time of 9% long-term interest rates. He was willing to do that because of *Coke's* extraordinary level of *economic goodwill*. The company was earning 31 percent ROE while employing relatively little capital investment. *Buffett* explained that price tells us nothing about value. **The value of *Coke* is determined by the total owner earnings expected to occur over the life of the business, discounted at an appropriate interest rate.**
In 1988, owner earnings of *Coke* equaled $828 million. The 30 year Treasury bond (the risk-free rate) traded near a 9 percent yield. *Coke's* 1988 owner earnings, discounted by 9%, would produce an intrinsic value of $9.2 billion. When *Buffett* purchased *Coke*, the market value was $14.8 billion (a 65% premium), suggesting that *Buffett* might have overpaid for the company.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：**不过，如果一家公司无需额外资本就能增加所有者收益，那么就应该用无风险收益率与所有者收益预期增长率之间的差额来折现所有者收益。** 如果*可口可乐*能长期保持5%的平均盈利增长率，那么8.28亿美元/(9%的无风险收益率 – 5%的长期盈利增长率) = 207亿美元，四舍五入即为210亿美元。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
**However, when a company is able to grow owner earnings without the need for additional capital, it is appropriate to discount owner earnings by the difference between the risk-free rate of return and the expected growth of owner earnings.**
If *Coke* were able to grow its earnings on average 5% for a long, long time then $828 million/(9% alternative rate of return – 5% long term average growth rate in earnings) = $20.7 billion or round up to $21 billion.

因此，即便巴菲特是以148亿美元的价格购买*可口可乐*，其内在价值也达到了210亿美元或更高——也就是说，巴菲特实际上获得了比保守估算的*可口可乐*内在价值低40%的折扣。

<!--en-->
So if *Buffett* purchased *Coke* at a $14.8 billion value its intrinsic value was $21 billion or higher-- or *Buffett* was getting a 40% discount to a conservative appraisal of *Coke*'s intrinsic value.

## 留存资本回报率

<!--en-->
*Return on retained capital*

摘自《巴菲特之道》：沃伦可能会这样推理：1994年，如果他以21.95美元的价格购买可口可乐公司的股票，而该股票每股盈利为0.98美元，那么实际上他获得的初始税后投资回报率将达到4.5%（0.98美元 ÷ 21.95美元 = 4.5%）。而且这一回报率还会进一步上升，因为可口可乐的每股盈利正以每年17.2%至18.4%的复合增长率增长。

<!--en-->
From *Buffettology*: *Warren* could reason that in 1994, if he paid $21.95 for a share of *Coca-Cola* stock that had per share earnings of $0.98 a share, he would in effect be getting an initial after-corporate-tax return on his investment of 4.5% ($0.98 / $21.95 = 4.5%). And this rate of return would expand because *Coke*'s per share earnings were growing at an annual compounding rate of 17.2% to 18.4% a year.

沃伦认为，只有当可以合理预期管理层能够比股东更有效地运用这些未分配盈余时，公司才应保留这些盈余。

<!--en-->
*Warren* believes that a company should retain unrestricted earnings only if it is reasonable to project that the management would be able to do a better job investing those unrestricted earnings than would be the shareholders.

**作为投资者，我们该如何衡量一家公司及其管理层有效配置未分配盈余的能力呢？** 资本配置能力与管理效率究竟如何？

<!--en-->
**How do we as investors measure a company and its management's ability to profitably allocate unrestricted earnings?** What is the management skill in allocating capital and management effectiveness?

我们会取某一段时间内企业留存的每股盈利数据，然后将其与同期每股盈利的增长额进行比较。

<!--en-->
We take the per share earnings retained by a business for a certain period of time, then compare it to any increase in per share earnings that occurred during this same period.

1983年，可口可乐的每股盈利为0.17美元。这意味着截至1983年底投资于可口可乐的所有资本在当年为股东创造了0.17美元的每股收益。从1983年底到1993年底，可口可乐在这十年间的每股总盈利达到了4.44美元。其中，可口可乐在1983年至1993年间支付的股息总额为每股1.89美元。这意味着从1983年到1994年的十年间，可口可乐留存的盈利为每股2.55美元（4.44美元 - 1.89美元 = 2.55美元）。

<!--en-->
In 1983 *Coke* made $0.17 a share. This means that all the capital invested in *Coke* up until the end of 1983 produced for its owners $0.17 a share in 1983. Now between the end of 1983 and the end of 1993, *Coke* had total earnings for this ten year period of $4.44 per share. Of that $4.44, *Coke* paid out in dividends during 1983-1993: a total of $1.89 a share. This means that for the ten-year period between 1983 and 1994, *Coke* had retained earnings of $2.55 a share ($4.44 - $1.89 = $2.55).

因此，从1983年到1993年底，可口可乐总共赚取了每股4.44美元的盈利，其中每股1.89美元用于支付股息，另有每股2.55美元被保留下来充实资本基础。

<!--en-->
So between 1983 and the end of 1993, *Coke* earned a total of $4.44 a share, paid out in dividends a total of $1.89 a share, and retained to its capital base a total of $2.55 a share.

在1983年至1993年期间，可口可乐的每股盈利从0.17美元上升至0.84美元。我们可以将1983年的0.17美元盈利归因于截至1983年底投资于可口可乐的所有资本。我们也可以认为，从1983年的每股0.17美元增长到1993年的每股0.84美元，得益于可口可乐管理层出色地运用了1983年至1993年间留存的每股2.55美元盈利。

<!--en-->
During 1983-1993 *Coke*'s per share earnings rose from $0.17 a share to $0.84 a share. We can attribute the 1983 earnings of $0.17 to all the capital invested in *Coke* up to the end of 1983. We can also argue that the increase in earnings from $0.17 a share in 1983 to $0.84 a share in 1993 was caused by *Coke*'s management doing an excellent job of utilizing the $2.55 a share in earnings that *Coke* retained between 1983 – 1993.

如果我们用1993年的每股盈利0.84美元减去1983年的每股盈利0.17美元，得到0.67美元。因此可以说，1983年至1993年间留存的每股2.55美元盈利在1993年产生了0.67美元的额外收益。这意味着这2.55美元的留存盈利在1993年创造了0.67美元的收益，总回报率为26.2%（0.67美元 ÷ 2.55美元 = 26.2%）。

<!--en-->
If we subtract the 1983 per share earnings of $0.17 from the 1993 per share earnings of $0.84, to get $0.67. Thus, we can say that the $2.55 a share that was retained between 1983 and 1993 produced $0.67 in additional income for 1993. This means that the $2.55 in retained earnings earned $0.67 in 1993 for a total return of 26.2% ($0.67 / $2.55 = 26.2%).

可口可乐的管理层在1993年对1983年至1993年间留存的每股2.55美元股权创造了26.2%的回报率。***结束*** 哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
*Coke*'s management earned a 26.2% return in 1993 on the $2.55 a share in equity that *Coke* retained from 1983-93.
***END***
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

## 股票筛选与创意生成：

<!--en-->
*Stock Screening and Generating Ideas:*

我本想在课堂上晚些时候讨论股票筛选的话题。昨天我在《华尔街日报》上发现了这条消息：

<!--en-->
I wanted to talk about stock screening later in the class. I found this yesterday in the *Wall Street Journal*:

纽文公司分拆：纽文投资股价下跌8%；圣保罗公司将出售控股权。道琼斯新闻专线，2005年3月28日下午1:56。作者：安吉拉·普鲁伊特，道琼斯新闻专线，纽约报道——纽文投资公司（JNC）的股票在周一盘中交易时下跌8.1%，原因是该公司计划成为一家完全独立且公开上市的公司。

<!--en-->
*Nuveen* Spin-off
*Nuveen* Invest down 8%; St. Paul to Sell Controlling Stake
DOW JONES NEWSWIRES *March 28, 2005 1:56 p.m.* By Angela Pruitt Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES
NEW YORK -- *Nuveen Investments Inc.* (JNC) shares fell 8.1% in mid-day trading Monday following news of plans to make the asset manager a fully independent and publicly traded firm.

纽文的母公司圣保罗旅行者公司（STA）于周五宣布，将通过二次发行的方式出售其持有的纽文控股权。截至3月初，这家财产及意外险保险公司拥有纽文约78%的已发行有表决权证券。

<!--en-->
*Nuveen*'s parent company, *St. Paul Travelers Cos.* (STA) announced Friday that it will implement a three-part plan to sell its controlling stake in *Nuveen* in a secondary offering. The property-and-casualty insurer owned about 78% of *Nuveen*'s outstanding voting securities as of early March.

纽文股票当日下跌3.08美元，收于34.92美元，成交量为766,800股，而日均成交量仅为111,000股。圣保罗公司的股价则上涨15美分，即0.4%，达到36.41美元。

<!--en-->
*Nuveen* shares recently were down $3.08 at $34.92 on volume of 766,800, compared with average daily volume of 111,000. St. Paul shares were up 15 cents, or 0.4%, at $36.41.

圣保罗公司的这一策略并不出人意料，因为市场分析师此前就预计该公司会通过二次发行或出售给第三方买家的方式来处置股权。不过，投资者似乎更倾向于相信会有另一家机构出资收购纽文。

<!--en-->
*St. Paul's* strategy was not unexpected as market analysts anticipated that some sort of secondary offering or sale to a third-party buyer would be the routes taken. However, investors appeared to have stacked more of their chips on the probability that another institution would cough up the money to buy *Nuveen*.

“我认为股价下跌的原因是市场原本期望有人会收购它，”位于弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔的SNL金融公司研究员约翰·伦纳德说。

<!--en-->
"I think the reason the shares are down is because the market was expecting someone to buy them out," said *John Leonard*, a research analyst at *SNL Financial* in Charlottesville, Va.

“我认为由于优质资产管理公司的股价通常较高，因此市场不愿在高位买入纽文，”他说。

<!--en-->
"I think there was a reluctance to buy (*Nuveen*) at the top of the market given that *quality asset managers are trading at premium prices*," he said.

*Nuveen*称，*St. Paul Travelers*将在二次发行中出售3960万股该公司股票，占已发行股份总数的42%。根据计划，*Nuveen*还将以二次发行的价格从*St. Paul Travelers*手中回购价值6亿美元的股票。

<!--en-->
*Nuveen* said *St. Paul Travelers* will sell 39.6 million of the company's shares, or 42% of total shares outstanding, in a secondary offering. Under the plan, *Nuveen* also will buy back $600 million of its shares from *St. Paul Travelers* at the price of the secondary offering.

*St. Paul Travelers*于1月底宣布，正在考虑出售其持有的*Nuveen*股份，该部分股份价值约30亿美元。**此举旨在筹集现金，以弥补与石棉储备相关的9.22亿美元开支。**分析师指出，由于大量*Nuveen*股票即将涌入市场，**供应方面的担忧可能也会对*Nuveen*的股价造成压力。***Nuveen*是封闭式基金的最大发行商，管理资产规模达1150亿美元。该公司1月份公布的2004年第四季度总销售额为81亿美元，较去年同期增长99%。此外，*Nuveen*第四季度的净利润同比增长15%。

<!--en-->
*St. Paul Travelers* announced in late January that it was reviewing options to sell its *Nuveen* stake, valued at about $3 billion. **The move is aimed at raising cash after a $922 million charge related to its asbestos reserves.**
Given the hefty float of *Nuveen*'s shares set to be unleashed on the market, **supply concerns also may be getting the best of *Nuveen*'s stock, analysts said.**
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
*Nuveen* is the largest issuer of closed-end funds and has $115 billion in total assets under management. The company in January reported $8.1 billion in gross sales for the fourth quarter of 2004, a 99% increase over the prior year. In addition, *Nuveen*'s fourth-quarter net income jumped 15% over the same period a year earlier.

*Keefe Bruyette & Woods*的分析师*Jim Johnson*表示：“通过此次二次发行，*Nuveen*可能会受益，因为其流通股数量将增加，且能获得华尔街更多的研究覆盖。”他补充道，投资者或许以为会有第三方买家介入，或者会爆发针对*Nuveen*的竞购战。

<!--en-->
"*Nuveen* might be better off because they will have...higher float (and) more research coverage from Wall Street," said *Jim Johnson*, an analyst at *Keefe Bruyette & Woods* of the secondary offering. He added that investors probably thought a third-party buyer would swoop in or that a bidding war for *Nuveen* would unfold.

Johnson称：“*Nuveen*是一家优质公司。”

<!--en-->
"*Nuveen* is a high-quality company," Johnson said.

*Leonard*和*Johnson*均未持有*Nuveen*股票，且他们所在的公司也不为该公司的投资银行业务提供服务。

<!--en-->
Neither *Leonard* nor *Johnson* owns *Nuveen* shares, and their firms don't do investment banking work for the company.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/49da3c42e0a3be94909bce6f1dac5545.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=51cdab2ecfdd2ae500cb7d013660ec6863585145b37e426d2906544977c5527b)

### 潜在机会：急售的卖家

<!--en-->
*Potential Opportunity: A motivated seller*

这篇文章中能引起特殊情境投资者兴趣的是什么？是一个*急售的卖家*。没错，就是急售的卖家。*St. Paul*为了筹集现金而急于出售9.22亿股股票。他们之所以这么做，是因为其在保险业务上出了差错。

<!--en-->
What would interest a special situations investor in this article? A *motivated seller*. Right, a motivated seller. *St Paul* wants to sell to raise cash by selling 922 million shares. Right away these guys are blowing out of this because they screwed up in their insurance business.

股价下跌可能是因为大量股票同时上市出售，因此作为价值投资者，我们或许能以此获得低价——有可能。该公司将回购由St. Paul持有的6亿美元股票；当前股价约为34.25美元左右，相当于回购1750万股。也许他们会利用债务来杠杆运作这家优质公司——前提是其确实便宜的话。还有别的吗？哥伦比亚大学商学院的206期特殊情境投资课程。$42.50的收购价可作为交易的基准价格。或许这就是他人愿意支付的价格。或者说，该资产虽已挂牌出售却无人问津。传统上，*Nuveen*主要发行封闭式债券基金，这是一种宝贵的收入来源。失去这种类似年金的收入流是难以接受的。

<!--en-->
It may be going down because there will a lot of stock for sale all at the same time, so we may get a good price as a value investor--possible. The company is going to buy back $600 million of the stock that is held by St Paul, so the stock is at $34.25 and change so they are buying back 17.5 million shares. Perhaps this will have debt to leverage a good company. If indeed it is cheap. Anything else?
206
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
$42.50 buyout price is the baseline price for a sale. Maybe that is a baseline for what someone would pay. Or gee the thing was for sale and no one would buy it. Traditionally they sell closed-end bond funds that is a valuable income stream. It is tough to lose that income stream—an annuity-like business.

该公司80%的流通股此前由一家大型保险公司持有，而该公司在业内并不算重要。这或许会引起管理层的重视。股价已从34美元跌至7或8美元，因此现在更便宜了。卖方因非业务相关原因而急于抛售。公司正在回购股票，以此调整资本结构；管理层或许对此乐见其成。他们（管理层）将持有多少股份呢？

<!--en-->
80% of your float has been owned by a big insurance company where it was not considered important as far as size. That might get management focused. The stock dropped $7 or $8 to $34 so it is cheaper than it was. The seller is a motivated seller for non business related reasons for this business. The company is buying back stock, so they are changing the capitalization of the company to create that. Management is perhaps happy to do that. How much will they (mgt.) own?

## 管理层

<!--en-->
*Management*

华尔街往往给高管支付过高薪酬，这一点令人担忧。在管理类公司中，由于业务所需资本不多，高管们每晚回家后便独吞所有利润。因此我想看看他们的股权结构究竟如何。其他公司也曾出现过这种情况。这是一家价值30亿美元的公司，管理层可能会从中牟利，但我们仍能从中发掘出大量价值。

<!--en-->
Wall Street tends to overpay people a lot, so I would worry about that. In management companies where your resources—there is not much capital in these business—go home every night, mgt. ends up taking all the profit for them. So I would like to see how their shares are bread and buttered. That has happened at other companies. This is a $3 billion dollar company so management can be piggy and there is still a lot of value left for us.

## 分析

<!--en-->
*Analysis*

我查阅了招股说明书并快速浏览了一下。我大概看了二三十份此类文件。我深知这类业务回报率高；我们曾因其他原因持有过一只封闭式基金。

<!--en-->
So what I did was, I took out the prospectus—read this. So anyway, I did a quick and dirty. I may look at 20 or 30 of these. I happen to know these are high return businesses, we used to own a closed end fund (this) for other reasons.

简要分析如下：EBIT为254，企业价值(EV)为3349，因此EV/EBIT比率为13.5倍。ROIC超过100%。看来这是一家极具价值的特许经营型企业。我进一步研究了该业务的构成情况。

<!--en-->
The quick and dirty: EBIT was $254 and EV is $3349 so 13.5x EV/EBIT. ROIC was over 100%. So it looked like a valuable franchise. I was looking at the break down of what the business looks like.

他们管理的资产规模达到1150亿美元，但其中500亿美元属于交易所交易基金（ETF）。这确实是一块大业务，但其盈利水平如何呢？这些资金与封闭式基金相比是否同样有价值？共同基金的管理规模仅为127亿美元，因此500亿+127亿后，剩下370亿美元用于管理账户或零售业务。另有156亿美元用于机构管理账户。可见各类业务的特性各不相同。**需要分别剖析每项业务。**我想逐一分析它们：每种业务的客户粘性、估值倍数以及现金流特征都有所差异。这些业务的表现是否不尽如人意呢？管理账户的业务可能较为分散，但这未必是坏事。我想看看那500亿美元的ETF业务究竟有多赚钱；如果盈利可观，他们或许能进一步扩张该业务。

<!--en-->
They have $115 billion assets under management, but included in that $50 billion is in Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs). That is a big business but how profitable is that business. Are those dollars as valuable as the closed-end funds? Mutual funds—there is only 12.7 billion, so you have $50 + $12.7 then you have $37 billion in managed accounts or retail. And you have $15.6 billion in managed institutional accounts. So each of those businesses is a little bit different. **Break out each business.** I want to go through each one of these. Each one has a little different stickiness to it; each one has a little different multiple to it. Cash-flow characteristics for each. Do they stink at what they are doing? Managed accounts might be pretty diffuse which is good. I want to see how profitable are the ETF funds—$50 billion. If it is profitable, they may be able to expand that business.

相对于高管薪酬而言，公司似乎并不会持有大量股票。首席执行官年薪为600万美元；假设他拥有100万股的期权，那么600万美元的薪资对应3600万美元的股票价值。他们认为自身拥有强大的平台，尤其在ETF等快速增长领域占据有利位置。

<!--en-->
It didn't seem like mgt was going to own much stock relative to their salaries. The CEO earned $6 million a year. So let us say he had an option on million shares. $6 million in salary vs. $36 million in stock. They think they have a great platform and they are well-positioned in rapidly growing segments especially in ETF.

他们将扩大营销与分销渠道。

<!--en-->
They will expand their marketing and distribution.

独立运营可能会成为**催化剂**式事件。他们有望使盈利增速超过过去四年的12%~13%；这一表现虽已不错，但市场环境也功不可没。我之所以做出上述判断，是因为13.5倍EBIT估值看似偏高，但未来几年EBIT可能增长30%，届时估值将降至10倍，而该业务的资本回报率高达100%。鉴于此次事件带来的**高溢价**，我不会立刻否定其投资价值。

<!--en-->
Going independent may be a **catalytic** event. They may be able to make earnings explode more than 12% to 13% a year over the last four years which is pretty good, but the market has been good as well. I would make all those assessments, because 13.5x EBIT may look expensive, but EBIT may grow 30% over the next few years. Then you are down to 10x EBIT in a business that is earning 100% return on capital. I wouldn't write it off right way because of the pretty **high price**, because of this event.

以上只是分析的**开端**。如果EV/EBIT比率为10倍，我会直接买入股票再问后续问题；但13倍的话，我则会提出诸多疑问，很可能不会购买。不过我还是会完成分析，以确定是否值得投资。阅读本文后，我已初步形成了**投资逻辑**。

<!--en-->
So that is the **beginning** of an analysis. If this was at 10x EV/EBIT, I would be buying the stock and asking questions later, but at 13xs I am asking a lot of questions and probably not buying the thing. But I will go through the analysis and look to see whether I should or not. Already there is a **thesis** built from reading the article.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：我的分析与我们对*AXP*的分析类似。*AXP*拥有两项业务：一项业务净资产收益率高，另一项则较低。我想进一步研究这一点。此外，近期市场走势较弱，这类资产极易受到冲击。这些公司急需资金；*St Paul*只想促成这笔交易。一旦进入这一阶段，就会有庞大的支持团队（*投资银行家*）推动交易完成。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
My analysis is not dissimilar to our analysis of *AXP*. *AXP* has two businesses: one business has a high ROE and the other a low ROE. OK, I want to look at that. Also, the market is kind of weak lately, so this is the kind of thing that could really get crushed. These guys really need the money. *St Paul* just wants to get the deal done. Once you are at this phase, there is a big cheering squad (*investment bankers*) to get this deal done.

我们可能会看到股价在此基础上下跌6至7美元。

<!--en-->
We may see the stock down another $6 or $7 from here.

## *美国运通（AXP）*

<!--en-->
*American Express (AXP)*

对*AXP*的看法如下：通常我买入股票后，股价反而会下跌。其次，若我的估值基于三到四年的周期，短期波动便无关紧要。**关键在于我对三年后正常化盈利水平的预测。**这需要考虑到账户损失率低于常态、信贷利差高于常态等因素。我对此进行了详细分析。目前该数值比正常水平高出20美分，但该领域的支出也高出50美分；传统上他们会削减这方面的开支——因此这并非决定性因素。

<!--en-->
The thinking on *AXP* is this: usually when I buy the stock, it goes down. Number two is this: if I am truly taking a three or four year horizon in my valuation, then what is happening in the short term does not matter. **What matters is what I think normalized earnings will be three years from now.** Which should take into account the fact that account if loss ratios are lower than usual, income credit spreads are bigger than usual. There are a lot of things that go into that. I analyze that. They are 20 cents above normal, but they are also 50 cents above normal in spending in this area. So, they traditionally cut back in this area—it is not a big factor.

**你必须区分哪些因素重要，哪些不重要。**事实证明，若着眼于三四年后的正常化盈利，许多因素并不重要。就像我之前提到的*Amex*——无论我是否买入，都无关紧要。我们与*穆迪*共同完成的这项分析非常重要：该资产在3到5年后应价值X美元；但如果有人在我的期权到期前一年或两年察觉到机会，我就能提前获得大部分资金，而非等待8%的预期回报。

<!--en-->
**You have to decide what is material and what is not.** It turns out a lot of stuff is not material, if you are looking out normalized earnings three or four years. Like I said before about *Amex*—whether I bought them or not, it does not matter. This analysis is very important that we did with *Moody's*. It should be worth in 3 to 5 years, X dollars, but if someone wakes up in the next year or two before my leaps expire, I will get most of that money upfront instead of the expected return of 8%.

持有LEAP的风险在于：确实无法准确预测未来22个月内市场会给*AXP*定何种价格。但我们可以合理预估三年到五年后的估值。持有股票能带来一种确定性：无论何时发生，它都在掌控之中。若你持有期限为22个月的LEAP，而市场变幻莫测，你就处于风险之中——这实际上是一种风险/收益博弈。

<!--en-->
**The risk in the LEAP is that there really is no intelligent way to know where the market will price *AXP* in the next 22 months.** There is an intelligent way to know where the market will value *AXP* in three to five years. By owning a stock, you have that comfort level of whenever it happens it happens. If you are in a LEAP with a 22 month expiration and this market can do anything, you are in a window of risk. You are making a risk/reward bet.

如果我财力允许且期权到期，我会续购另一批LEAP。**这是一种廉价的融资方式。**这就是解读财报的一种方式。我试图向你们展示一些显而易见的事实：那些“有效市场理论”的支持者会声称信息早已反映在股价中，所以20美元钞票不会留在地上没人捡——但现实并非如此。

<!--en-->
If I have the wherewithal and my options expire, I will (could) re-up and buy another set of LEAPs. **It is a cheap way to borrow money.**
That is one way to read the paper. I am trying to show you even obvious stuff. The *efficient marketeers* would have you believe, it is already in the paper so the twenty dollar bill is not there because someone would have picked it up. This is the way it really works.

### 股票筛选

<!--en-->
*Stock Screens*

所以我就为了好玩做个股票筛选。这是从*Multex*上获取的。这套筛选工具每年收费1500美元，由*Reuters*出售。也许它用起来会稍微方便些。每年只需几百美元就能获得的优秀筛选工具来自*AAII.com*、*Powerinvester.com*、*Smartmoney.com*；这类网页版筛选工具很多，它们都使用*Reuters*的数据。

<!--en-->
So I will do a stock screen just for fun. This is off of *Multex*. This screening package cost $1500 a year—it is sold by *Reuters*. And maybe it is a little easier to use. A great screening package for a cost of a couple hundred dollars a year is from *AAII.com*, *Powerinvester.com*, *Smartmoney.com*, there are a lot of web screening packages. They all use the *Reuters'* data.

我确实使用了这类筛选工具，但它并不值那个价钱。使用*Reuters*的数据时需要注意一点：其质量并非很好，有时数据并不准确。我的建议是：如果找到价格极其低廉的工具，可以将其作为第一步来使用。

<!--en-->
I use the screening package but it is not worth the money. One thing you want to be careful with the *Reuters'* Data is that it is not that good. Sometimes the data is not accurate. All I am saying is that if you get something super cheap, use that as a first step.

*Compustat*是一款很棒的产品。但请把股票筛选当作一种“创意生成器”来使用。

<!--en-->
*Compustat* is a great product. But use stock screens as an *idea generator*.

上个季度的每股账面价值。我们不用EV/EBIT指标，而是采用简单的过去12个月滚动市盈率。将其除以有形账面价值。为什么我要把ROE乘以BV/有形账面价值呢？其实我是在夸大ROE的数值，因为ROE是基于报表中的账面价值计算的；我想强调的是，我真正关注的是ROE与有形账面价值之间的关系。请使用*独特的*筛选标准！哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程 结束

<!--en-->
Book Value per share last quarter. Instead of doing EV/EBIT we will do simple trailing P/E trailing twelve months. Divide that by tangible book value. Why did I multiply ROE by BV/Tangible BV? I am goosing up the ROE because ROE is based on reported book and I am trying to say I really care about looking at ROE and tangible book value.
Use *unique* screening criteria!
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
END

*Corinthian College*: An attractive price to earnings and cash flow. The company is being sued because some students can't transfer their credits. We believe that the company will be exonerated because there is no evidence of wrong doing. Every student signs a binding arbitration.

增长势头已放缓。历史上20%的利润率水平并不可持续。市场对此感到恐慌，但这种担忧并无根据。目前增长放缓且利润率受压，资本支出暂时较高。其市值140亿美元，销售额10亿美元。企业价值低于市值。每股收益增长20%，营收增长15%。去年资本支出较多，因此自由现金流将会跃升。我们对自由现金流的定义为：EBITDA减去资本支出、营运资本变动及税费；或者也可理解为税后EBIT。自由现金流达1亿美元。按7%至8%的加权平均资本成本计算，其价值约为30美元。EV/EBIT比率为8.5，ROE高达35%；用于资本再投资的资金占80%至90%，维持性资本支出占20%，ROIC为20%。管理层只需开设分校即可。还有更多门店扩张空间。具备增长潜力且需要加大投入。整理好你的陈述要点。*Peter Lynch曾用三分钟计时器来听取分析师的陈述。* *Joel Greenblatt*：提供全局视角：

## Linda Greenblatt关于零售企业投资的讲座，以及对Ann Taylor Stores (ANN)的零售分析

*Linda Greenblatt's Lecture on Investing in Retail Companies and a Retail Analysis of Ann Taylor Stores (ANN)*

Joel Greenblatt教授（“JG”）：

Prof. Joel Greenblatt ("JG"):

今天我们有位特别嘉宾——*Linda Greenblatt女士*，她过去10年间管理着Saddle Rock Partners对冲基金，业绩出色。她几乎只投资于零售股及部分消费类股票。凭借对自身擅长领域的专注，她取得了惊人的回报。换句话说，她的能力圈无需过于宽泛。十年间她构建了一个回报丰厚的投资组合。这表明你不必掌握太多不同的知识。去年她在课堂上推荐的股票是*Abercrombie (ANF)*，其股价从25美元涨至58美元。哥伦比亚大学商学院第210期特殊情境投资课程

Linda Greenblatt将介绍她当前的投资思路、评估方法以及她目前的看法。

<!--en-->
Linda Greenblatt will discuss her current idea, how to evaluate it, and what her thoughts are now.

### Linda Greenblatt (“LG”):

我将简单介绍一下我的从业起点以及为何选择进入零售业。我真心想为自己找到一个合适的“细分领域”——一个我能产生共鸣的领域。我喜欢消费品行业。**我喜欢购物。** 我专注于那些容易理解的公司：你可以亲自去店里触摸、感受并了解产品，从而掌握顾客的需求并获得他们的反馈。在我看来，这是较容易理解和分析的行业之一。我对零售业的另一大喜爱之处在于能获取大量信息，而且这些信息每月都会更新，比如同店销售额（SSS）——即开业至少十二个月以上的门店的销售额。

<!--en-->
I will talk a little bit about how I started and why I went into retail. I really wanted to find a *niche* for myself. Something I could relate to. I like the consumer sector. **I like to shop.** I focused on those companies easy to understand where you could get out there, touch, feel and understand. I could get the customers' understanding and get their feedback. So it is one of the easier sectors, in my opinion to understand and analyze. Another thing I really like about retail is that you are getting a lot of info and it comes out on a monthly basis, for example, like same store sales (SSS)--Store sales of stores that have been opened for at least twelve months.

与其他行业每季度才公布数据不同，零售业每月都会发布大量信息，这有利有弊。其弊端在于会导致该行业出现极大的波动性，但这也是它的优势所在——因为这样你就有机会在商品被低估时买入。**当人们频繁交易这些商品时，你就能趁机入手。** 如果你具备价值导向和长期视角——我所说的长期是指一到两年，因为大多数人只关注未来几个月的数据。如果你能退一步看清全局，往往会发现很多机会。

<!--en-->
Unlike other industries where you are getting numbers on a quarterly basis. You are getting a ton of information coming out of these companies on a monthly basis, which is good and bad. It is bad because it creates tremendous volatility in this sector, but that is the reason it is good. Because you get the opportunity to buy things when they are unfairly cheap. **You get to buy things when people are often trading them.** If you have a value orientation and a longer term orientation—when I say longer-term I mean one to two years because people are mostly focused on the next months' numbers. If you can take a step back and see the big picture, there often a lot of opportunities out there.

正因如此，很多人“讨厌”这个行业。我无法预测下一个热门趋势是什么，也不知道*Abercrombie (ANF)*的春季系列是否受欢迎。**但这并不重要，这正是它的妙处所在。** 你其实无需去深究“管理层是否选对了牛仔裙款式”，重要的是他们是否懂得如何经营业务、能否创造良好的资本回报。就算他们这次没做好又怎样？下个季节你还有机会。而且在此期间公司绝不会倒闭。

<!--en-->
And a lot of people *hate* this sector for that reason. I can't analyze what the next hot trend is. I don't know whether *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)*'s Spring line looks good. **And that doesn't matter and that is the beauty of it.** You really don't have to understand, “Whether management get the right denim skirt doesn't matter, what you have to get right is if management knows how to run a business, are they generating good returns on capital? And if they miss so what? I get another chance next season. And they certainly are not going under in the meantime.

以*Abercrombie (ANF)*为例，看看它的股票走势图就会发现：一年前买入的人到现在已经翻了一番。从业务本质上讲，并没有发生什么重大变化——无论是经营模式还是客户群体都没变。虽然管理层有所变动，但在我看来这并不重要。过去一年半时间里，该公司的同店销售额（SSS）持续为负，整个行业的人都只盯着这一指标，却忽略了其他重要方面。

<!--en-->
So *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* is a case in point if you look at their stock chart and you can go back a year ago you could have doubled your money between then and now. I can't say that a lot has happened in the business fundamentally that has changed from what kind of business they are running or who their customers was. There was a management change but in my opinion it was not significant, but what was happening for a good year and a half prior is that they were generating negative same store sales (SSS) and negative comp store sales. People throughout the industry could not focus on what type of business they were running.

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程指出：该公司的EBIT利润率接近20%，在同行中名列前茅。但所有人却只关心其下一期同店销售额是否为负。在2002-2003年，如果你能退一步思考：虽然同店销售额为负，或许存在商品陈列问题，但该公司整体运营良好；只要能稳定住这一指标——尽管此前数据分别为负9%、负5%、负9%——一旦情况好转，人们就会惊叹：“哇，这家公司真不错！”于是大家不再只关注SSS，而是开始重视其实际经营状况。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
And they were generating EBIT margins close to 20%, amongst the highest in their peer group. And all anybody could focus on was on whether their next comp stores sales was negative. In 2002-2003, you could have taken a step back and said, I recognize that comp store sales are negative, perhaps there are merchandising issues here, but I can see they run a good business and if they could stabilize that comp, if they could just generate at the bottom of those comp numbers—they were running negative 9, negative 5, negative 9, but once they could stabilize their comps, people thought, “Oh wow, look at this business!” This is a great business and all of a sudden people were not just focused on the SSS but on what the actual business was doing.

下面这篇文章采访了一位负责零售股研究的基金经理，他的观点与许多人对零售股的看法以及卖方分析师的普遍看法极为相似。他大致说道：

<!--en-->
This article (included below) interviewing a money manager who covers retail stocks and his quote is very similar to how a lot of people think about retail stocks and how most or all of the sell side thinks about retail stocks. Basically he said:

我会派人去门店和商场查看商品折扣幅度以及收银台前的排队长度。如果我认为公司业绩会超出预期，我就买入股票；反之则做空。就是这么简单。

<!--en-->
I have my people visit stores and malls to see how much the items are marked down and how long the lines are at the registers. I'll buy a stock if I think the company is going to beat numbers and short it if it is going to miss numbers. It is that simple.

### 投资：《零售业的王者》 《财富》杂志，2005年3月22日星期二

<!--en-->
*INVESTING: King of the Retail Jungle FORTUNE Tuesday, March 22, 2005*

对冲基金经理*David Berman*凭借像耐心捕食者般的思维而获利。

<!--en-->
Hedge fund manager *David Berman* profits by thinking like a patient predator.

“我曾是和我一样的人的受害者，”对冲基金经理兼前会计师大卫·伯曼说。“每次我买入股票时，总有人比我更聪明，他们会卖出；每次我卖出时，又有人比我更聪明，他们会买入。”因此，1997年当他成立公司来管理自己的资金时，伯曼决定专注于一个行业并深耕细作。他的选择是零售业。这位家具制造商之子花了一年时间走访购物中心，最终开发出一种定制指数——DeeBee（取自大卫·伯曼的名字），用于对比美国零售商的销售额与库存情况。他的专业化策略取得了成效：伯曼称，过去八年里扣除费用后，他的平均回报率达到了17%，且仅有三个月出现亏损。如今，他通过德班资本管理着超过1亿美元的资产。这家对冲基金以他在南非的家乡命名，于2001年成立。他的投资原则之一是：如果价格不合适，他宁愿不买入。《财富》杂志的朱莉·施洛瑟从开普敦（他每年在此度过三个月）致电伯曼，与他探讨了零售业最新的强劲销售数据、为何这些数据未必对股价有利，以及投资者能从鳄鱼身上学到什么。

<!--en-->
"I used to be a victim of people like me," says hedge fund manager and onetime accountant *David Berman*. "Every time I bought a stock, someone smarter than me was selling it. Every time I sold, someone smarter was buying." So when he formed a firm to manage his own money in 1997, *Berman* decided to focus on a single sector and master it. His choice? Retail. This son of a furniture maker spent a year walking malls and eventually developed a custom index—the DeeBee (as in *David Berman*)—to compare sales vs. inventories at U.S. retailers. His specialization strategy has paid off: Berman says he has averaged a return of 17% after fees over the past eight years with only three down months. He now manages more than $100 million through Durban Capital, a hedge fund he named for his hometown in South Africa and launched in 2001. A big part of his formula is that he's willing not to buy if prices aren't right. FORTUNE's Julie Schlosser phoned Berman in Cape Town (where he spends three months every year) to chat about the sector's latest batch of strong sales reports, why they don't necessarily bode well for stocks, and what investors can learn from crocodiles.

## 尽管假日销售表现平平，但标普500零售指数在过去一年中仍上涨了11%。零售商能在2005年继续超出预期吗？

<!--en-->
*Despite lackluster holiday sales, the S&P 500 retailing index is up 11% for the past year. Can retailers keep beating expectations in 2005?*

二月让所有人，包括零售商在内，都感到意外。它也让我吃惊。关于原因有多种说法：或许退税情况比人们预想的要好；时尚潮流也相当不错；我认为天气也是一个积极因素——二月全国气温比往常高出约四度。但在很大程度上，每年这个时候零售板块的走势会受到宏观经济因素的影响。

<!--en-->
February surprised everybody, retailers included. It surprised me. There are a bunch of theories why. Perhaps tax refunds are better than people thought they'd be. Fashions are pretty good. And I think weather has been a positive factor. It was about four degrees warmer than usual across the country in February. But to a large degree, during this time of year the retail group gets moved for macro reasons.

## 哪些宏观经济因素会影响零售商？

<!--en-->
*Which macro factors affect retailers?*

有时零售销售最好的月份，恰恰是股市最差的月份。如果某月零售业绩出色，利率会怎样？它们会上升。这对零售商而言并非好事。现在可能正是如此。美联储未能有效放缓经济，但债券收益率会承担这一任务。格林斯潘在加息方面收效甚微，但长期趋势已超出他的控制范围。利率已经升至42%以上；房贷利率可能也会随之上涨，从而拖累经济。我虽非债券专家，但鉴于当前经济势头强劲，这些收益率很可能还会继续攀升——至少人们是这么认为的。

<!--en-->
Sometimes the best months for retail sales have been the worst months for stocks. If it is the best month for retail, what happens to interest rates? They go up. And that's not good for retailers. You may have that now. The Fed hasn't been able to slow the economy down, but bond yields are going to do the job. Greenspan has been very ineffective with raising rates. But the long range is out of hiscontrol. The rates have gone up to over 42%. Home loans may start going higher, and that will slow things down. I'm not a bond expert, but those yields may well go higher because this economy is really rocking. Or at least people think it's rocking.

哥伦比亚大学商学院特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

## 如何判断一只股票是否具有投资价值？

<!--en-->
*How do you figure out if a stock is a good value?*

我坚持认为，自己不够聪明，也没人能真正确定合理的市盈率应该是多少。我的任务是弄清楚每股收益应该是多少。我注重事实依据。这就是为什么我会测量库存数据。我派人前往商店和购物中心，查看商品打折幅度以及收银台前的排队长度。如果我认为一家公司能超出预期，我就会买入其股票；反之，如果预计其业绩不佳，我则会做空。就是这么简单。

<!--en-->
I maintain that I am not smart enough, and I don't think anyone really is, to know what the P/E should be. My job is to understand what the EPS [earnings per share] should be. I look for facts. That's why I measure inventories. I have my people visit stores and malls to see how much the items are marked down and how long the lines are at the registers. I'll buy a stock if I think the company is going to beat numbers and short it if it is going to miss numbers. It is that simple.

## 您的DeeBee指数衡量的是销售增长与库存增长的关系。您是否据此来预测公司能否超出华尔街的收益预期？

<!--en-->
*Your DeeBee index measures sales growth vs. inventory growth. Is that how you predict whether a company will beat Wall Street's earnings estimates?*

我们会对美国所有上市零售商进行汇总分析，这类公司将近300家。多年来我们每季度都会进行此项工作。从个体层面看，这能让我们清楚了解哪些公司因库存管理得当而有望表现优异，哪些公司则可能达不到预期。它还能帮助我们预判该行业的未来盈利能力，以及经济的潜在强度——因为零售业往往领先于其他行业。库存耗尽意味着什么？这意味着零售商将加快订货节奏，进而带动下游经济繁荣。虽然这项工作量大，但对我们而言非常值得。

<!--en-->
We summarize every publicly held retailer in America. That's almost 300 companies. We've been doing this quarterly for many years. On an individual level, it gives us a great sense of which companies are going to do well because their inventories are well controlled and which ones have potential for missing numbers. It gives us a sense of the profitability of the group going forward. And it also gives us a sense of the future strength of the economy, because retail leads the way. If inventories are depleted what does that mean? It means retailers are going to be ordering faster, and that means the back end of the economy is going to do well. It is a lot of work, but it is really worth it to us.

## 您所说的“鳄鱼策略”是什么意思？

<!--en-->
*What do you mean when you say you use a "Crocodile Approach"?*

就是要耐心等待合适的机会。鳄鱼可以两年不吃东西，它的腿很短，行动缓慢，只会潜伏在河床边。如果猎物不来，它就整天睡觉。你要像鳄鱼一样，等待猎物自己送上门来，而不是急于去追捕。你要等那只大斑马出现，然后一口将其吞下。基于这种理念，我从不惧怕持有大量现金。持有现金就不会亏钱，这也是我很少出现亏损月份的原因。我从不使用杠杆。事实上，一些投资者可能会对此不满，但直到最近，我同时用于多头和空头投资的资金很少超过50%——也就是说，我有一半资金是现金。我承认这个比例偏低，需要提高。但这正是“鳄鱼策略”的体现。

<!--en-->
Just wait and be patient for the right opportunities. The crocodile can go for almost two years without eating food. It has very small legs and can't go very fast. It waits by the riverbed. If its prey doesn't come, it just sleeps all day. You want to be like the crocodile and wait for the prey to come to you. You don't want to rush off to the prey. You want to wait for the big zebra and grab him and eat it up. With that in mind, I've never been afraid to build up a big cash position. You can't lose money if you're in cash. That's why I don't have many down months. I've never used leverage. In fact, some of my investors will be upset with me, but until recently I rarely had much more than 50% of my money invested—both long and short—at one time. That means I am half in cash. I recognize that is too low. It needs to increase. But it's because of the Crocodile Approach.

上个月，*梅西百货*和*布鲁明戴尔百货*的母公司——*联合百货公司*，以及*安·泰勒百货*(ANN)宣布了收购*梅百货公司*的计划。这是否意味着百货商店真的正在走向衰落？

<!--en-->
Last month *Federated Department Stores*, parent of *Macy's* and *Bloomingdale's*, *Ann Taylor Stores* (ANN) announced plans to acquire *May Department Stores*. Is it a sign that the department stores are truly dying?

哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程：此次并购是*沃尔玛*影响力的体现。根据我们的数据，沃尔玛占上市公司零售销售额的21%（不含汽车类），约占总销售额的8%。在美国，几乎每十笔销售中就有一笔是在沃尔玛完成的。这彻底改变了零售业格局。结果就是百货商店被严重挤压，它们不得不拼命挣扎以保持竞争力。这可能只是零售业格局的自然演变；百货商店模式正在缓慢衰退。

<!--en-->
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
The merger is a function of *Wal-Mart's* power. *Wal-Mart* by our numbers has 21% of the sales of publicly held retailers, excluding autos. And roughly 8% of total sales. Almost one in every ten sales in America is done in *Wal-Mart*. That has totally changed the retail landscape. As a result the department stores are really being squeezed. They're having to scramble to stay competitive. It is probably just a natural evolution of the retail landscape. There is just a slow deterioration in the department store mode.

## DeeBee指数目前评级最高的股票是什么？

<!--en-->
*What is the DeeBee index's top-rated stock right now?*

我可以告诉你我股票清单中表现不错的个股，但它们的市盈率可能已经很高。排名首位的是*美国鹰牌服饰*(AEOS, $29)。该公司刚刚公布的销售额增长了37%，而存货仅增长14%。这对未来的利润率和盈利是个好兆头。不过，这一利好已大部分反映在股价中。我持有该股，但一直在减持。美国鹰牌拥有出色的管理团队；过去几年他们加强了员工队伍，最近还为即将推出的新概念店招募了一些优秀人才，这将为其带来新的增长点。他们现在正全速前进。诺德斯特龙(JWN, $55)的表现也不错，销售额增长9%，存货仅增长2%，在百货商店类别中堪称最佳。问题是这些业绩早已被计入股价。记住：业绩超出预期与股价表现并非同一回事。

<!--en-->
I can tell you who is good on my inventory list but they might already have a high P/E. At the top is *American Eagle Outfitters* (AEOS, $29). It just reported sales up 37% while inventories are up only 14%. That bodes well for future margins and profits. But a large amount of that is reflected in stock price. I own it, but I've been reducing my position. American *Eagle* has got great management. They've beefed up their staff over the last couple of years. They just hired some good people for a new concept that they will be announcing soon. It will give them another leg of growth. They are firing on all cylinders. Nordstrom (JWN, $55) also had good results, with sales up 9% and inventory up only 2%. That's the best in the department store category. The problem is that those results are already factored into the stock price. Remember, the concept of who is going to beat earnings and the stock price are two different things.

## 所以那只鳄鱼并不会冲出去捕食斑马吗？

<!--en-->
*So the crocodile isn't running out to snap up zebras?*

我确实担心零售业已经经历了一段好时光。今年许多公司的存货增速超过了销售额，很难找到值得长期持有的股票。我正处于观望状态，耐心等待机会。

<!--en-->
I am really concerned that the retail group has had a nice run. Many companies are looking worse this year in terms of inventory growing faster than sales. It's hard to find good longs. I'm in sleeping mode, waiting patiently for opportunities.

## 琳达·格林布拉特(LG)继续说道……

<!--en-->
*Linda Greenblatt (LG) continued.........*

我要告诉你们，这就是你们的机会。就这么简单。无论公司是否未达到预期业绩，都有很多人这么做，这造成了巨大的波动，也为你们带来了诸多机会。随便翻开任何分析师报告，尤其是一年前的*Abercrombie (ANF)*相关报告，你会发现华尔街分析师们都在谈论*Abercrombie (ANF)*的核心业务无法再像过去那样实现两位数的同店销售增长；或者他们只关注三四月份门店的表象，却忽略了公司的实际运营状况和门店效率。实际上，该公司的增长并不来自核心业务，而是来自其第二大业务——*Hollister*，这一业务已成为其重要的增长引擎。

<!--en-->
And I say to you that is your opportunity. It is that simple. There are so many people out there doing that whether they miss their numbers or not. It creates so much volatility and so much opportunity for you. And you will read any analyst report, particularly a year ago in *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)*, they (Wall Street Analysts) talked about the *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* core business and the fact that it couldn't generate double digit SSS as they had in the past. Or analysts will focus on what the stores looked like in March and April. As opposed to what the company was doing and how productive their store base was. But they had tremendous growth—not so much in their core business—but in their *Hollister* business which is their secondary business, which has been a great growth vehicle for them.

如果你能看清方向，这里同样存在巨大的机会。哥伦比亚大学商学院的特殊情况投资课程。

<!--en-->
Once again tremendous opportunity here if you are looking at the right stuff.
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School

**学生：** *Abercrombie (ANF)*的企业价值/息税前利润倍数是多少？

<!--en-->
**Student:** What was the EV/EBIT multiple for *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)*?

琳达·格林布拉特(LG)：当时该数值为7倍，但我们的目标是10倍至11倍的企业价值/息税前利润。税后ROIC则高达十几个百分点。

<!--en-->
Linda Greenblatt (LG) – it was at 7x but our target was 10x - 11x EV/EBIT. ROIC was high teens after-tax.

美国鹰牌服饰（“Eagle” AEOS）

<!--en-->
American *Eagle* Outfitters ("*Eagle*" AEOS)

**学生：**这个品牌发生了什么变化？*AEOS*调整了商品策略，现在它更偏向冲浪风格而非传统风格。

<!--en-->
**Student:** What has happened with this brand? *AEOS* changed their merchandising. Now they are more surf oriented than conservative.

LG：他们确实存在商品策略方面的问题，难以确定自身定位。他们面临着两端的挤压：高端市场有*Abercrombie (ANF)*，吸引那些想穿*Abercrombie (ANF)*品牌的年轻人；低端市场则受到*Aeropostale (ARO)*的冲击，后者价格更低且模仿了*Eagle*的很多设计。*Eagle*虽然找到了自己的细分市场，但为了改善商品供应，他们也重组了商品团队。当*Abercrombie (ANF)*同时宣布要向更高端市场转型时，*Eagle*更是得到了竞争对手的“帮助”。*Eagle*试图聚焦高中生客户群；而*Abercrombie (ANF)*则通过提高定价向更成熟、更高端的市场迈进。因此，*Eagle*有几点优势助力其发展。

<!--en-->
LG: They definitely were having merchandising issues and they were really having trouble finding what their identity was. They were being squeezed at both ends. *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* was at the higher end—the kids who wanted to shop *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* and wanted the *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* brand. While on the lower end, they were being hurt by *Aeropostale (ARO)* where they couldn't compete with those prices and *ARO* was knocking off a lot of what *Eagle* was doing. *Eagle* had defined a niche for itself, but they were also shook up their merchandise team in order to improve their merchandise offering. They also had some little help from their competitors when *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* simultaneously announced that they wished to go more upscale. *Eagle* has tried to focus on the high school customer. *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* has gone a little older and a little bit higher end by putting in higher price points. So *Eagle* had a couple of things working in their favor.

大约一年前，当*Eagle*的股价在13美元到15美元之间时，人们基本上已经抛弃了它，认为它再也无法翻身。如果观察那段时间的数据，会发现其EBIT利润率已降至8%左右。当时，或许会吸引你的是：EBIT利润率仅为8%，而两年前这一数字还曾达到12%。正如你在上一张幻灯片中看到的，*ABERCROMBIE (ANF)*的利润率则在18%到19%之间。如果他们能找准方向，这里其实存在巨大机遇。当时该股股价仅为收益的8倍。人们早已对它失去信心；其同店销售也呈负增长。但6-8-12个月后，你会发现股价已经翻倍——在过去2.5年里，股价从5美元涨到了30美元。在此期间，他们改善了商品结构，且部分竞争对手退出竞争，使他们无需正面交锋。此外，人们开始注意到：一只在2003年市盈率仅为8倍的股票，如今市盈率已接近17倍——这意味着盈利倍数扩张超过了100%。

<!--en-->
About a year ago you would see, when *Eagle*'s price was at $13 to $15, people basically had written them off and had decided that they were never going to regain their footing. What happened during that time, if you looked at EBIT margins, those margins were headed down to the 8% range. At the time if you had looked at it, what might have been attractive to you is that the EBIT margins were trading in the 8% range and two years before the EBIT margin had been in the 12% range. *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* as you might have remembered from the last slide was in the 18% to 19% range. There could be a lot of opportunity here if they could just get it right. Basically the common stock was trading at 8 times earnings. People had written them off; they had negative comps. Skip forward 6-8-12 months later, you can see the stock has doubled. It has gone from $5 to $30 over the past 2.5 years. And what has happened during that time, they have improve their merchandise and some of their competitors have moved away so they are not competing head on. But the other thing people started to take notice and a stock that was trading at 8xs back in 2003 is now trading closer to 17xs—or over a 100% earnings multiple expansion.

哥伦比亚大学商学院215期特殊情境投资课程：实际情况是，他们收购了一家加拿大连锁店，但刚收购就搞砸了，最终将其注销。如果你留意底部的门店数量数据，会发现市场已趋于饱和。他们声称能开设多达1000家门店，但现有的购物中心数量有限。因此他们确实需要新的增长引擎——尽管如此，即便没有新的增长引擎，该股市盈率仍高达18倍至20倍。

<!--en-->
215
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
LG: What happened was they bought a Canadian chain and basically blew it the moment they bought it. So they wrote it off. If you notice in the store count which is on the bottom line—they are pretty saturated. If you ask them, they say they can open up to a 1000 stores, but there are only so many malls that exist. So they really needed a new growth vehicle—having said that, the stock is still trading at 18x to 20xs, in spite of no new growth vehicle.

JG：为什么它的市盈率如此之高？

<!--en-->
JG: Why is it trading at such a high multiple?

LG：因为他们创造了出色的同店销售业绩（SSS）。关键在于，当这些股票受青睐时，人们往往关注错了重点。

<!--en-->
LG: Because they are generating great comps (SSS). The point being that when these stocks are in favor, people focus on the wrong thing.

学生：在这个案例中，关键在于准确把握商品销售趋势。那么，难道不需要对未来同店销售的增长做出预测吗？

<!--en-->
Student: What you had to get right in this story was to get the merchandising sales trend correctly. So are you not having to guess on future growth in SSS?

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/a0739afad783f61e988a5ad5bc5c29a0.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a3ad252f7c98bff9adabd11e97c17f8df01df138272b7aa2875573bbbe35d0d1)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/a0739afad783f61e988a5ad5bc5c29a0.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T065618Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a3ad252f7c98bff9adabd11e97c17f8df01df138272b7aa2875573bbbe35d0d1)

LG：原因在于管理层意识到了自身问题，并重组了商品团队。此外，他们明白自己在竞争中处于劣势。不过，这家公司确实拥有稳定的客户群；他们开始专注于特定客户群体。此前他们涉足范围过广：既瞄准20岁的年轻人，又瞄准15岁的青少年，导致焦点分散，这很大程度上是因为商品团队无法精准定位客户。哥伦比亚大学商学院216期特殊情境投资课程：答案是——我并不确定他们一定能成功，但当时他们的EBIT利润率仅为8%，而几年前这一数字还曾达到12%；其最接近的竞争对手（ANF）利润率更是高达19%。在我看来，这就是机遇所在——毕竟他们此前做的一切都是错的，却仍能维持8%的EBIT利润率。如果他们制定了一套五步改进计划——哪怕只落实其中两三点，也必然存在巨大的上涨空间。正如我所说，另一个对他们有利的因素是行业外的外部环境。

<!--en-->
LG: It is the fact that they (management) recognized that they had issues; they shook up their merchandising team. Plus they knew they were having a hard time competing. What you have here, though, is a company that definitely has a customer base. Definitely what you were starting to see is they were going to focus on a particular customer. What happened is that they were all over the board. They were focusing on the 20 year old kid, on the 15 year old kid and they really couldn't get their focus down and that was largely in part to their merchants were not being able to target their customer well.
216
Special Situation Investing Classes at Columbia University Business School
So the answer is—I didn't know for sure they were going to get it right, but they were at an 8% EBIT margin and a couple of years earlier they had 12% margins when they had run things just a little bit better and their closest competitor (ANF) was at 19% margins. This smells like opportunity to me, because actually they did everything wrong and they ran an 8% EBIT margin. So if they laid out a five step program to improve—well if they get two or three of those points right, there is certainly a big upside opportunity there. And, as I said, another thing went in their favor was an external factor in their industry.

JG：让我补充一点。*Rich Pzena*曾说过，低ROE的公司会做出改变：解雇管理层、关闭工厂。他们会采取行动，因为现状行不通（董事会或新管理层会做出调整以改善经营或止损）。零售业正是如此。**当时该股的市盈率因盈利低迷而处于低位。**他们此前表现糟糕，但仍能盈利，并未倒闭，且资产负债表强劲。所以问题在于：零售业的有趣之处在于，如果春季商品不受欢迎，秋季或冬季可能会好转。只要买入价格足够低廉，他们无需在短时间内就扭转局面。你看，股价从5美元涨到了30美元。

<!--en-->
JG: Let me add to that. When *Rich Pzena* was here, he said low ROE companies make changes: they fire management, they close factories. They do stuff because it is not working (The Board of Directors or new management make changes to improve or stop losses). That is what happens here in retail. **Here it was trading at a low multiple of depressed earnings.** They were doing everything wrong, but they were still earning some money. They were not going out of business and they had a strong balance sheet. So the question was—the great thing about retail is that if Spring stinks (their merchandise assortment of customer acceptance), then Fall will be better or Winter. So if you buy them cheap enough, they didn't have to get it right in this short of period of time. You see it went from $5 to $30.

如果你有两到三年的投资视野，就会想：瞧，我的马还在赛道上奔跑，比赛仍在继续。公司仍在运营，不会倒闭。这个季度表现不佳，但下个季度可能会好转。也许我们会聘请这个人；也许他们确实具备实现目标的能力。

<!--en-->
If you have a two to three year horizon and you say look I still have a pony on the track and it still is running and the race is still going on. I am still in business; I am not going out of business. This season stinks, but next season won't. Maybe we will hire this guy; maybe they have the platform to really do it.

如果你去年圣诞节走进他们的门店，会发现他们连商品都卖不出去。如果他们继续表现如此糟糕，却仍能赚到一些钱，且你看到其股票估值倍数较低，那情况还能更糟吗？**或者他们能做对几件事？** 一旦他们做对了几件事，人们就会开始重视起来。届时，基于更高的盈利基础，该股票估值倍数可能会升至10到12倍。毕竟之前的盈利水平实在太低了。这样一来，你的投资回报就能从5美元涨到10美元，这可是相当不错的收益。（你既能从盈利从低谷回升至正常水平中获益，又能因其他投资者信心增强而获得估值倍数扩张带来的双重好处。）如果你追求的是5到10美元的投资回报，就没必要指望它能涨到30美元。

<!--en-->
If you had walked into their stores last Christmas and they couldn't give stuff away. And if they continue to be this bad and they still are generating some money and you could see that the stock is trading at a low multiple, then can it get any worse? **Or they could get a few things right?** And if they get a few things right, then people will start to sit up and take notice. Then the stock can trade at a greater multiple—10 to 12 xs—off a greater earnings base. Because these were incredibly depressed earnings. Then all of a sudden you get your returns from $5 to $10 which is a pretty good return. *(You are getting a double upside from both an increase from depressed earnings to normalized earnings and a multiple expansion as other investors gain confidence).* If you are playing for a $5 to $10 return, you don't have to be playing for a return of $5 to $30.

JG：琳达曾谈到她持有的*ABERCROMBIE (ANF)*股票，她以25美元的价格买入，基于类似的逻辑，如今该股股价已达58美元。她在40多美元时抛售，这仍是相当不错的回报（80%以上）。在这里，你可能会认为（与AEOS观点一致）该股略显高估。目前经营状况不错，但增长前景有限，且估值已达17到18倍，所以你可能等不到那时。哥伦比亚大学商学院217期特殊情境投资课程

<!--en-->
JG: When Linda was talking about *ABERCROMBIE (ANF)* which she did own, she bought at $25 on sort of on a similar thesis and now it is at $58. She sold out in the mid-$40s, which is still a pretty good return (80%+). Here you might argue (with AEOS) this is slightly overvalued. Things are going well, there are not a lot of growth prospects and it is trading at 17xs - 18xs so you probably don't last till then.
